v: The vision[^1] of Isaiah[^2] son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.[^3]
חֲזוֹן֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֧הוּ יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃
Hear, you heavens, and listen, you earth, for Yahweh[^4] has spoken:[^5] I raised children[^6] and brought them up, but they have rebelled against me.
שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּ֑ר בָּנִים֙ גִּדַּ֣לְתִּי וְרוֹמַ֔מְתִּי וְהֵ֖ם פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's feeding trough, but Israel does not know; my people do not understand.
יָדַ֥ע שׁוֹר֙ קֹנֵ֔הוּ וַחֲמ֖וֹר אֵב֣וּס בְּעָלָ֑יו יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע עַמִּ֖י לֹ֥א הִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃

Woe to[^7] the sinful nation, a people weighed down with guilt, offspring of evildoers, children who act corruptly! They have abandoned Yahweh; they have despised the Holy One of Israel;[^8] they have turned their backs on him.[^9]
ה֣וֹי ׀ גּ֣וֹי חֹטֵ֗א עַ֚ם כֶּ֣בֶד עָוֺ֔ן זֶ֣רַע מְרֵעִ֔ים בָּנִ֖ים מַשְׁחִיתִ֑ים עָזְב֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה נִֽאֲצ֛וּ אֶת־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נָזֹ֥רוּ אָחֽוֹר׃
Why will you be beaten again?[^10] Why do you keep on rebelling? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart is faint.
עַ֣ל מֶ֥ה תֻכּ֛וּ ע֖וֹד תּוֹסִ֣יפוּ סָרָ֑ה כָּל־רֹ֣אשׁ לָחֳלִ֔י וְכָל־לֵבָ֖ב דַּוָּֽי׃
From the sole of the foot to the head there is nothing sound in it: only wounds and welts and open sores. They have not been cleaned or bandaged, or soothed with oil.
מִכַּף־רֶ֤גֶל וְעַד־רֹאשׁ֙ אֵֽין־בּ֣וֹ מְתֹ֔ם פֶּ֥צַע וְחַבּוּרָ֖ה וּמַכָּ֣ה טְרִיָּ֑ה לֹא־זֹ֙רוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֻבָּ֔שׁוּ וְלֹ֥א רֻכְּכָ֖ה בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃
Your land is a desolation; your cities are burned with fire. As for your fields, foreigners devour them before your eyes. It is desolate, as when foreigners overthrow a land.[^11]
אַרְצְכֶ֣ם שְׁמָמָ֔ה עָרֵיכֶ֖ם שְׂרֻפ֣וֹת אֵ֑שׁ אַדְמַתְכֶ֗ם לְנֶגְדְּכֶם֙ זָרִים֙ אֹכְלִ֣ים אֹתָ֔הּ וּשְׁמָמָ֖ה כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֥ת זָרִֽים׃
Daughter Zion[^12] is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a city under siege.[^13]
וְנוֹתְרָ֥ה בַת־צִיּ֖וֹן כְּסֻכָּ֣ה בְכָ֑רֶם כִּמְלוּנָ֥ה בְמִקְשָׁ֖ה כְּעִ֥יר נְצוּרָֽה׃
If Yahweh of Armies[^14] had not left us a few survivors,[^15] we would have been like Sodom; we would have resembled Gomorrah.
לוּלֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הוֹתִ֥יר לָ֛נוּ שָׂרִ֖יד כִּמְעָ֑ט כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ׃ ס
Hear the word of Yahweh, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the instruction[^16] of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם הַאֲזִ֛ינוּ תּוֹרַ֥ת אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה׃

What are all your sacrifices to me? says Yahweh. I have had more than enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened animals. I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls, of lambs and of goats.
לָמָּה־לִּ֤י רֹב־זִבְחֵיכֶם֙ יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׂבַ֛עְתִּי עֹל֥וֹת אֵילִ֖ים וְחֵ֣לֶב מְרִיאִ֑ים וְדַ֨ם פָּרִ֧ים וּכְבָשִׂ֛ים וְעַתּוּדִ֖ים לֹ֥א חָפָֽצְתִּי׃
When you come to appear before me,[^17] who asked you to do this, to trample my courts?
כִּ֣י תָבֹ֔אוּ לֵרָא֖וֹת פָּנָ֑י מִי־בִקֵּ֥שׁ זֹ֛את מִיֶּדְכֶ֖ם רְמֹ֥ס חֲצֵרָֽי׃
Stop bringing worthless offerings![^18] Your incense is detestable to me. New moons and Sabbaths, the calling of assemblies: I cannot bear wickedness together with a solemn assembly.[^19]
לֹ֣א תוֹסִ֗יפוּ הָבִיא֙ מִנְחַת־שָׁ֔וְא קְטֹ֧רֶת תּוֹעֵבָ֛ה הִ֖יא לִ֑י חֹ֤דֶשׁ וְשַׁבָּת֙ קְרֹ֣א מִקְרָ֔א לֹא־אוּכַ֥ל אָ֖וֶן וַעֲצָרָֽה׃
Your new moons and your appointed festivals I hate with all my being.[^20] They have become a burden to me; I am tired of carrying them.
חָדְשֵׁיכֶ֤ם וּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם֙ שָׂנְאָ֣ה נַפְשִׁ֔י הָי֥וּ עָלַ֖י לָטֹ֑רַח נִלְאֵ֖יתִי נְשֹֽׂא׃
When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide my eyes from you. Even when you pray and pray, I am not listening. Your hands are full of blood.
וּבְפָרִשְׂכֶ֣ם כַּפֵּיכֶ֗ם אַעְלִ֤ים עֵינַי֙ מִכֶּ֔ם גַּ֛ם כִּֽי־תַרְבּ֥וּ תְפִלָּ֖ה אֵינֶ֣נִּי שֹׁמֵ֑עַ יְדֵיכֶ֖ם דָּמִ֥ים מָלֵֽאוּ׃
Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean. Take your evil deeds out of my sight. Stop doing evil.
רַחֲצוּ֙ הִזַּכּ֔וּ הָסִ֛ירוּ רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם מִנֶּ֣גֶד עֵינָ֑י חִדְל֖וּ הָרֵֽעַ׃
Learn to do good. Seek justice; correct the oppressor.[^21] Defend the rights of the fatherless;[^22] plead the widow's case.
לִמְד֥וּ הֵיטֵ֛ב דִּרְשׁ֥וּ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט אַשְּׁר֣וּ חָמ֑וֹץ שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה׃ ס
Come now, let us settle this,[^23] says Yahweh. Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow. Though they are red as crimson, they will become like wool.[^24]
לְכוּ־נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה אִם־יִֽהְי֨וּ חֲטָאֵיכֶ֤ם כַּשָּׁנִים֙ כַּשֶּׁ֣לֶג יַלְבִּ֔ינוּ אִם־יַאְדִּ֥ימוּ כַתּוֹלָ֖ע כַּצֶּ֥מֶר יִהְיֽוּ׃
If you are willing and obey, you will eat the good things of the land.
אִם־תֹּאב֖וּ וּשְׁמַעְתֶּ֑ם ט֥וּב הָאָ֖רֶץ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃
But if you refuse and rebel, you will be eaten by the sword.[^25] For the mouth of Yahweh has spoken.
וְאִם־תְּמָאֲנ֖וּ וּמְרִיתֶ֑ם חֶ֣רֶב תְּאֻכְּל֔וּ כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ ס
How[^26] the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice; righteousness lived in her, but now murderers.
אֵיכָה֙ הָיְתָ֣ה לְזוֹנָ֔ה קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה מְלֵאֲתִ֣י מִשְׁפָּ֗ט צֶ֛דֶק יָלִ֥ין בָּ֖הּ וְעַתָּ֥ה מְרַצְּחִֽים׃
Your silver has become dross; your best wine[^27] is watered down.
כַּסְפֵּ֖ךְ הָיָ֣ה לְסִיגִ֑ים סָבְאֵ֖ךְ מָה֥וּל בַּמָּֽיִם׃

Your rulers are rebels[^28] and companions of thieves. Every one of them loves a bribe and chases after gifts. They do not defend the rights of the fatherless, and the widow's case never comes before them.
שָׂרַ֣יִךְ סוֹרְרִ֗ים וְחַבְרֵי֙ גַּנָּבִ֔ים כֻּלּוֹ֙ אֹהֵ֣ב שֹׁ֔חַד וְרֹדֵ֖ף שַׁלְמֹנִ֑ים יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה לֹֽא־יָב֥וֹא אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ פ
Therefore the Lord[^29] Yahweh of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel,[^30] declares: Ah,[^31] I will get relief from my adversaries and take revenge on my enemies!
לָכֵ֗ן נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲבִ֖יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ה֚וֹי אֶנָּחֵ֣ם מִצָּרַ֔י וְאִנָּקְמָ֖ה מֵאוֹיְבָֽי׃
I will turn my hand against you. I will smelt away your dross as with lye and remove all your impurities.[^32]
וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה יָדִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וְאֶצְרֹ֥ף כַּבֹּ֖ר סִיגָ֑יִךְ וְאָסִ֖ירָה כָּל־בְּדִילָֽיִךְ׃
I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After that you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.
וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה שֹׁפְטַ֙יִךְ֙ כְּבָרִ֣אשֹׁנָ֔ה וְיֹעֲצַ֖יִךְ כְּבַתְּחִלָּ֑ה אַחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן יִקָּ֤רֵא לָךְ֙ עִ֣יר הַצֶּ֔דֶק קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה׃
Zion will be redeemed by justice, and those in her who turn back,[^33] by righteousness.
צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה וְשָׁבֶ֖יהָ בִּצְדָקָֽה׃
But rebels and sinners will be crushed together, and those who abandon Yahweh will come to an end.
וְשֶׁ֧בֶר פֹּשְׁעִ֛ים וְחַטָּאִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וְעֹזְבֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה יִכְלֽוּ׃
For you[^34] will be ashamed of the sacred oaks[^35] that you delighted in, and you will blush for the gardens that you chose.
כִּ֣י יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ מֵאֵילִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲמַדְתֶּ֑ם וְתַ֨חְפְּר֔וּ מֵהַגַּנּ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּחַרְתֶּֽם׃
For you will be like an oak whose leaves are withering, like a garden that has no water.
כִּ֣י תִֽהְי֔וּ כְּאֵלָ֖ה נֹבֶ֣לֶת עָלֶ֑הָ וּֽכְגַנָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־מַ֖יִם אֵ֥ין לָֽהּ׃
The strong one will become tinder,[^36] and his work a spark.[^37] Both of them will burn together, with no one to put out the fire.
וְהָיָ֤ה הֶחָסֹן֙ לִנְעֹ֔רֶת וּפֹעֲל֖וֹ לְנִיצ֑וֹץ וּבָעֲר֧וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם יַחְדָּ֖ו וְאֵ֥ין מְכַבֶּֽה׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *chazon*, a revelation that a prophet "saw". The word gives its name to the whole book.
n.2: Hebrew *Yesha'yahu*, "Yahweh saves".
n.3: These kings reigned in the eighth century BC. Isaiah's call came in the year Uzziah died (6:1), about 740 BC, and his last dated words are from Hezekiah's reign (chapters 36–39), about 701 BC.
n.4: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.5: In Isaiah's poetry the words of the prophet and the words of Yahweh alternate, often with no marked change of speaker. As in Deuteronomy 32, Yahweh's words in the poems are not put in quotation marks.
n.6: Literally "sons". Also in verse 4.
n.7: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning for the dead ("Alas!", 1 Kings 13:30). The prophets use it to announce disaster, and in that sense it is translated "Woe to" throughout this book.
n.8: A title of God found often in Isaiah and only rarely elsewhere (2 Kings 19:22; Psalm 71:22): the holy God who has bound himself to Israel.
n.9: Literally "they are estranged backward".
n.10: Or "Where can you be beaten again?" The body is already wounded everywhere (verse 6).
n.11: Literally "like an overthrow by foreigners". *Overthrow* is the word used for the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:25; Deuteronomy 29:22, 29:23 in most English Bibles), which are named in verses 9 and 10.
n.12: A poetic name for Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman.
n.13: Or "like a guarded city", a watchman's post left standing alone.
n.14: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. The title is used often in Isaiah. Also in verse 24.
n.15: Literally "a survivor, a little". Or "If Yahweh of Armies had not left us survivors, we would soon have been like Sodom". Romans 9:29 quotes this verse from the Greek Septuagint, which reads "offspring" (literally "seed").
n.16: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching, law".
n.17: Literally "to be seen at my face". The same consonants could be read "to see my face".
n.18: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute", in Leviticus a grain offering. Literally "offerings of emptiness".
n.19: Hebrew *atsarah*, a festive gathering for worship.
n.20: Hebrew *nephesh*, "soul, self". Literally "my soul hates them".
n.21: Or "set the oppressed free" or "lead the oppressed". The word translated *oppressor*, Hebrew *chamots*, is found only here. The Septuagint reads "rescue the one who is wronged".
n.22: Literally "judge the orphan". Also in verse 23.
n.23: Or "let us argue it out". The verb is a term from the law court. Traditionally "let us reason together".
n.24: Or "If your sins are like scarlet, can they be as white as snow? If they are red as crimson, can they become like wool?"
n.25: The same verb as *eat* in verse 19: they will either eat the land's good things or be eaten by the sword.
n.26: Hebrew *ekhah*, the opening cry of a funeral song, as in Lamentations 1:1.
n.27: Hebrew *sove*, "drink", probably fine wine or beer.
n.28: A play on words: *sarayikh sorerim*, "your rulers are rebels".
n.29: Hebrew *ha-adon*, "the Lord", a title, not the name Yahweh.
n.30: Hebrew *avir yisra'el*, found only here. Compare "the Mighty One of Jacob" (Genesis 49:24; Isaiah 49:26).
n.31: Hebrew *hoy*, the word translated "Woe to" in verse 4. Here it is a cry of grim resolve. *Get relief* is literally "comfort myself".
n.32: Hebrew *bedil*, tin or lead, metals separated from silver when it is refined.
n.33: Or "her captives who return". Hebrew *shavim* can mean those who repent or those who come back.
n.34: Literally "they". The Hebrew moves from "they" to "you" within the verse.
n.35: Or "terebinths". Large trees, and the gardens around them, were places of worship for other gods (57:5; 65:3).
n.36: Hebrew *ne'oret*, the coarse fibers left from beating flax, which catch fire at once.
n.37: Or "its maker". If the "work" is an idol, its maker and the idol burn together.

v: This is the word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַֽׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אָמ֑וֹץ עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
In the days to come,[^1] the mountain of Yahweh's[^2] house will be established as the highest of the mountains;[^3] it will be raised above the hills, and all the nations will stream to it.[^4]
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֗ים נָכ֨וֹן יִֽהְיֶ֜ה הַ֤ר בֵּית־יְהוָה֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הֶהָרִ֔ים וְנִשָּׂ֖א מִגְּבָע֑וֹת וְנָהֲר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

Many peoples will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob, so that he may teach us his ways and we may walk in his paths." For instruction[^5] will go out from Zion, and the word of Yahweh from Jerusalem.

וְֽהָלְכ֞וּ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים וְאָמְרוּ֙ לְכ֣וּ ׀ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה אֶל־הַר־יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־בֵּית֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹרֵ֙נוּ֙ מִדְּרָכָ֔יו וְנֵלְכָ֖ה בְּאֹרְחֹתָ֑יו כִּ֤י מִצִיּוֹן֙ תֵּצֵ֣א תוֹרָ֔ה וּדְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה מִירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃

He will judge between the nations and settle disputes for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares[^6] and their spears into pruning knives. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will not learn war anymore.

וְשָׁפַט֙ בֵּ֣ין הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְהוֹכִ֖יחַ לְעַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְכִתְּת֨וּ חַרְבוֹתָ֜ם לְאִתִּ֗ים וַחֲנִיתֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ לְמַזְמֵר֔וֹת לֹא־יִשָּׂ֨א ג֤וֹי אֶל־גּוֹי֙ חֶ֔רֶב וְלֹא־יִלְמְד֥וּ ע֖וֹד מִלְחָמָֽה׃ פ
House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of Yahweh!
בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה בְּא֥וֹר יְהוָֽה׃

For you have abandoned your people, the house of Jacob, because they are full of things from the east[^7] and of fortune-tellers like the Philistines, and they strike hands with the children of foreigners.[^8]
כִּ֣י נָטַ֗שְׁתָּה עַמְּךָ֙ בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב כִּ֤י מָלְאוּ֙ מִקֶּ֔דֶם וְעֹֽנְנִ֖ים כַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וּבְיַלְדֵ֥י נָכְרִ֖ים יַשְׂפִּֽיקוּ׃
Their land is filled with silver and gold, and there is no end to their treasures. Their land is filled with horses, and there is no end to their chariots.
וַתִּמָּלֵ֤א אַרְצוֹ֙ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב וְאֵ֥ין קֵ֖צֶה לְאֹצְרֹתָ֑יו וַתִּמָּלֵ֤א אַרְצוֹ֙ סוּסִ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין קֵ֖צֶה לְמַרְכְּבֹתָֽיו׃
Their land is filled with idols.[^9] They bow down to the work of their hands, to what their own fingers have made.
וַתִּמָּלֵ֥א אַרְצ֖וֹ אֱלִילִ֑ים לְמַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יָדָיו֙ יִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֔וּ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשׂ֖וּ אֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו׃
So humankind is brought low, and everyone is humbled. Do not forgive them![^10]
וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל־אִ֑ישׁ וְאַל־תִּשָּׂ֖א לָהֶֽם׃
Go into the rock and hide in the dust from the terror of Yahweh and from the splendor of his majesty.[^11]
בּ֣וֹא בַצּ֔וּר וְהִטָּמֵ֖ן בֶּֽעָפָ֑ר מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר גְּאֹנֽוֹ׃
The proud eyes of humankind will be brought low, and human arrogance will be humbled. Yahweh alone will be exalted on that day.
עֵינֵ֞י גַּבְה֤וּת אָדָם֙ שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃ ס
For Yahweh of Armies[^12] has a day against all that is proud and lofty, against all that is lifted up, and it will be brought low,
כִּ֣י י֞וֹם לַיהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת עַ֥ל כָּל־גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם וְעַ֖ל כָּל־נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל׃
against all the cedars of Lebanon, high and lifted up, and against all the oaks of Bashan,
וְעַל֙ כָּל־אַרְזֵ֣י הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן הָרָמִ֖ים וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל כָּל־אַלּוֹנֵ֥י הַבָּשָֽׁן׃
against all the high mountains and against all the lofty hills,
וְעַ֖ל כָּל־הֶהָרִ֣ים הָרָמִ֑ים וְעַ֖ל כָּל־הַגְּבָע֥וֹת הַנִּשָּׂאֽוֹת׃
against every high tower and against every fortified wall,
וְעַ֖ל כָּל־מִגְדָּ֣ל גָּבֹ֑הַ וְעַ֖ל כָּל־חוֹמָ֥ה בְצוּרָֽה׃
against all the ships of Tarshish[^13] and against all the beautiful vessels.[^14]
וְעַ֖ל כָּל־אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ וְעַ֖ל כָּל־שְׂכִיּ֥וֹת הַחֶמְדָּֽה׃
Human pride will be humbled, and human arrogance brought low. Yahweh alone will be exalted on that day,
וְשַׁח֙ גַּבְה֣וּת הָאָדָ֔ם וְשָׁפֵ֖ל ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃
and the idols will vanish completely.
וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף׃
People will go into caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, from the terror of Yahweh and from the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to make the earth tremble.[^15]
וּבָ֙אוּ֙ בִּמְעָר֣וֹת צֻרִ֔ים וּבִמְחִלּ֖וֹת עָפָ֑ר מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
On that day people will throw away to the moles[^16] and the bats their idols of silver and their idols of gold, which they made for themselves to worship,
בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ יַשְׁלִ֣יךְ הָאָדָ֔ם אֵ֚ת אֱלִילֵ֣י כַסְפּ֔וֹ וְאֵ֖ת אֱלִילֵ֣י זְהָב֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָֽשׂוּ־לוֹ֙ לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֔ת לַחְפֹּ֥ר פֵּר֖וֹת וְלָעֲטַלֵּפִֽים׃
and go into the clefts of the rocks and the crevices of the cliffs, from the terror of Yahweh and from the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to make the earth tremble.
לָבוֹא֙ בְּנִקְר֣וֹת הַצֻּרִ֔ים וּבִסְעִפֵ֖י הַסְּלָעִ֑ים מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Stop trusting in human beings, who have only a breath in their nostrils. For what are they worth?[^17]
חִדְל֤וּ לָכֶם֙ מִן־הָ֣אָדָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְשָׁמָ֖ה בְּאַפּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־בַמֶּ֥ה נֶחְשָׁ֖ב הֽוּא׃ פ

n.1: Literally "at the end of the days". Verses 2–4 are found also in Micah 4:1–3, with small differences.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "at the head of the mountains".
n.4: Or "will flow to it", like a river.
n.5: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching, law".
n.6: Hebrew *ittim*, probably iron plow points or hoes. Joel 4:10 (3:10 in most English Bibles) turns the image around: "Beat your plowshares into swords."
n.7: Literally "they are full from the east", perhaps of practices of divination from the east. The Hebrew is difficult.
n.8: Perhaps "they make deals with foreigners". The meaning of the verb is uncertain.
n.9: Hebrew *elilim*, "worthless things, nothings", a word that sounds like *elohim*, "gods". Isaiah uses it often for idols.
n.10: Literally "Do not lift them up". Or "You cannot raise them up".
n.11: The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a), the oldest complete manuscript of Isaiah, does not have the last words of verse 9 ("Do not forgive them!") or verse 10.
n.12: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.13: Large seagoing ships, of the kind that sailed to Tarshish, a distant port in the west, perhaps in Spain.
n.14: Hebrew *sekhiyyot*, a word found only here. Perhaps "beautiful craft" or "fine images".
n.15: A play on words: *la'arots ha'arets*, "to make the earth tremble". Also in verse 21.
n.16: Hebrew *lachpor perot*, found only here, perhaps "to the burrowers": moles, rats or shrews.
n.17: The Septuagint does not have this verse.

v: For look, the Lord[^1] Yahweh of Armies[^2] is about to take away from Jerusalem and from Judah every support and supply,[^3] all supply of bread and all supply of water:
כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת מֵסִ֤יר מִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ וּמִ֣יהוּדָ֔ה מַשְׁעֵ֖ן וּמַשְׁעֵנָ֑ה כֹּ֚ל מִשְׁעַן־לֶ֔חֶם וְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁעַן־מָֽיִם׃
the warrior and the soldier, the judge and the prophet, the diviner and the elder,
גִּבּ֖וֹר וְאִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֑ה שׁוֹפֵ֥ט וְנָבִ֖יא וְקֹסֵ֥ם וְזָקֵֽן׃
the commander of fifty and the man of rank, the counselor, the skilled craftsman[^4] and the expert in charms.
שַׂר־חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וּנְשׂ֣וּא פָנִ֑ים וְיוֹעֵ֛ץ וַחֲכַ֥ם חֲרָשִׁ֖ים וּנְב֥וֹן לָֽחַשׁ׃
I will make boys their rulers, and the reckless[^5] will govern them.
וְנָתַתִּ֥י נְעָרִ֖ים שָׂרֵיהֶ֑ם וְתַעֲלוּלִ֖ים יִמְשְׁלוּ־בָֽם׃
The people will oppress one another, each one his neighbor. The young will be insolent to the old, and the nobody to the honored.
וְנִגַּ֣שׂ הָעָ֔ם אִ֥ישׁ בְּאִ֖ישׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֑הוּ יִרְהֲב֗וּ הַנַּ֙עַר֙ בַּזָּקֵ֔ן וְהַנִּקְלֶ֖ה בַּנִּכְבָּֽד׃
A man will take hold of his brother in his father's house and say, "You have a cloak; you be our ruler! Take charge of this heap of ruins!"[^6]
כִּֽי־יִתְפֹּ֨שׂ אִ֤ישׁ בְּאָחִיו֙ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו שִׂמְלָ֣ה לְכָ֔ה קָצִ֖ין תִּֽהְיֶה־לָּ֑נוּ וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את תַּ֥חַת יָדֶֽךָ׃
On that day he will cry out, "I will not be a healer![^7] There is no bread and no cloak in my house. Do not make me ruler of the people."
יִשָּׂא֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֤וּא ׀ לֵאמֹר֙ לֹא־אֶהְיֶ֣ה חֹבֵ֔שׁ וּבְבֵיתִ֕י אֵ֥ין לֶ֖חֶם וְאֵ֣ין שִׂמְלָ֑ה לֹ֥א תְשִׂימֻ֖נִי קְצִ֥ין עָֽם׃
For Jerusalem has stumbled, and Judah has fallen, because their words and their deeds are against Yahweh, defying his glorious presence.[^8]
כִּ֤י כָשְׁלָה֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וִיהוּדָ֖ה נָפָ֑ל כִּֽי־לְשׁוֹנָ֤ם וּמַֽעַלְלֵיהֶם֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה לַמְר֖וֹת עֵנֵ֥י כְבוֹדֽוֹ׃
The look on their faces testifies against them.[^9] They parade their sin like Sodom; they do not hide it. Woe to them![^10] They have brought disaster on themselves.
הַכָּרַ֤ת פְּנֵיהֶם֙ עָ֣נְתָה בָּ֔ם וְחַטָּאתָ֛ם כִּסְדֹ֥ם הִגִּ֖ידוּ לֹ֣א כִחֵ֑דוּ א֣וֹי לְנַפְשָׁ֔ם כִּֽי־גָמְל֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם רָעָֽה׃
Tell the righteous that it will go well with them, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
אִמְר֥וּ צַדִּ֖יק כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּֽי־פְרִ֥י מַעַלְלֵיהֶ֖ם יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
Woe to the wicked! It will go badly with them, for they will be paid back for what their hands have done.
א֖וֹי לְרָשָׁ֣ע רָ֑ע כִּֽי־גְמ֥וּל יָדָ֖יו יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לּֽוֹ׃
My people! Children are their oppressors,[^11] and women rule over them.[^12] My people, your guides lead you astray; they have erased the path you should walk.[^13]
עַמִּי֙ נֹגְשָׂ֣יו מְעוֹלֵ֔ל וְנָשִׁ֖ים מָ֣שְׁלוּ ב֑וֹ עַמִּי֙ מְאַשְּׁרֶ֣יךָ מַתְעִ֔ים וְדֶ֥רֶךְ אֹֽרְחֹתֶ֖יךָ בִּלֵּֽעוּ׃ ס
Yahweh takes his place to bring charges; he stands to judge the peoples.[^14]
נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים׃
Yahweh enters into judgment with the elders and leaders of his people: It is you who have stripped the vineyard bare.[^15] What you have stolen from the poor is in your houses.
יְהוָה֙ בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט יָב֔וֹא עִם־זִקְנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹ וְשָׂרָ֑יו וְאַתֶּם֙ בִּֽעַרְתֶּ֣ם הַכֶּ֔רֶם גְּזֵלַ֥ת הֶֽעָנִ֖י בְּבָתֵּיכֶֽם׃
What do you mean by crushing my people and grinding the faces of the poor? declares the Lord Yahweh of Armies.
*מלכם **מַה[q] **לָּכֶם֙ תְּדַכְּא֣וּ עַמִּ֔י וּפְנֵ֥י עֲנִיִּ֖ים תִּטְחָ֑נוּ נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ ס
Yahweh said: Because the daughters of Zion are proud and walk with outstretched necks, flirting with their eyes, tripping along with mincing steps, jingling the bangles on their feet,
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה יַ֚עַן כִּ֤י גָֽבְהוּ֙ בְּנ֣וֹת צִיּ֔וֹן וַתֵּלַ֙כְנָה֙ *נטוות **נְטוּי֣וֹת גָּר֔וֹן וּֽמְשַׂקְּר֖וֹת עֵינָ֑יִם הָל֤וֹךְ וְטָפֹף֙ תֵּלַ֔כְנָה וּבְרַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם תְּעַכַּֽסְנָה׃
the Lord will cover the heads of the daughters of Zion with scabs, and Yahweh will lay bare their foreheads.[^16]
וְשִׂפַּ֣ח אֲדֹנָ֔י קָדְקֹ֖ד בְּנ֣וֹת צִיּ֑וֹן וַיהוָ֖ה פָּתְהֵ֥ן יְעָרֶֽה׃ ס
On that day the Lord will take away their finery:[^17] the anklets, the headbands, the crescent ornaments,
בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יָסִ֣יר אֲדֹנָ֗י אֵ֣ת תִּפְאֶ֧רֶת הָעֲכָסִ֛ים וְהַשְּׁבִיסִ֖ים וְהַשַּׂהֲרֹנִֽים׃
the pendants, the bracelets, the veils,
הַנְּטִיפ֥וֹת וְהַשֵּׁיר֖וֹת וְהָֽרְעָלֽוֹת׃
the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume boxes,[^18] the amulets,
הַפְּאֵרִ֤ים וְהַצְּעָדוֹת֙ וְהַקִּשֻּׁרִ֔ים וּבָתֵּ֥י הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ וְהַלְּחָשִֽׁים׃
the signet rings, the nose rings,
הַטַּבָּע֖וֹת וְנִזְמֵ֥י הָאָֽף׃
the festal robes, the capes, the shawls, the purses,
הַמַּֽחֲלָצוֹת֙ וְהַמַּ֣עֲטָפ֔וֹת וְהַמִּטְפָּח֖וֹת וְהָחֲרִיטִֽים׃
the mirrors,[^19] the linen garments, the turbans and the veils.
וְהַגִּלְיֹנִים֙ וְהַסְּדִינִ֔ים וְהַצְּנִיפ֖וֹת וְהָרְדִידִֽים׃
Instead of perfume there will be rot; instead of a sash, a rope; instead of well-set hair, baldness; instead of a rich robe, a wrapping of sackcloth; instead of beauty, branding.[^20]
וְהָיָה֩ תַ֨חַת בֹּ֜שֶׂם מַ֣ק יִֽהְיֶ֗ה וְתַ֨חַת חֲגוֹרָ֤ה נִקְפָּה֙ וְתַ֨חַת מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה מִקְשֶׁה֙ קָרְחָ֔ה וְתַ֥חַת פְּתִיגִ֖יל מַחֲגֹ֣רֶת שָׂ֑ק כִּי־תַ֖חַת יֹֽפִי׃
Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.[^21]
מְתַ֖יִךְ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֑לוּ וּגְבוּרָתֵ֖ךְ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
Her gates will lament and mourn; stripped bare, she will sit on the ground.
וְאָנ֥וּ וְאָבְל֖וּ פְּתָחֶ֑יהָ וְנִקָּ֖תָה לָאָ֥רֶץ תֵּשֵֽׁב׃

n.1: Hebrew *ha-adon*, "the Lord", a title, not the name Yahweh. "The Lord" in verses 17 and 18 is *Adonai*.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verse 15.
n.3: Hebrew *mash'en u-mash'enah*, the masculine and feminine forms of the same word, "staff": every kind of support.
n.4: Or "the expert in magic arts".
n.5: Hebrew *ta'alulim*, perhaps "caprice, whims", or "infants".
n.6: Literally "and this ruin will be under your hand".
n.7: Literally "a binder of wounds".
n.8: Literally "rebelling against the eyes of his glory".
n.9: Or "Their partiality testifies against them". The Hebrew phrase can mean "regard for faces", that is, favoritism in judgment.
n.10: Hebrew *oy*, a cry of distress close in meaning to *hoy* (1:4). Literally "Woe to their souls!"
n.11: Or "a child is their oppressor". The Hebrew word may also mean "one who gleans": "their oppressors strip them bare".
n.12: The same consonants can be read "creditors" (*noshim*) instead of "women" (*nashim*), as the Septuagint understood them.
n.13: Literally "they have swallowed up the way of your paths".
n.14: The Septuagint reads "his people".
n.15: Literally "burned" or "grazed bare".
n.16: Or "their private parts". The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
n.17: Many of the words in verses 18–23 are rare, and some of the items cannot be identified with certainty.
n.18: Literally "houses of the *nephesh*", probably small bottles of perfume worn at the throat.
n.19: Or "the papyrus garments", perhaps "the see-through garments".
n.20: The Hebrew is short and abrupt: "for instead of beauty, branding". The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) reads "for instead of beauty, shame".
n.21: *Your* is feminine singular: Zion is addressed as a woman.

v: On that day seven women will take hold of one man and say, "We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes; only let us be called by your name. Take away our disgrace!"[^1]
וְהֶחֱזִיקוּ֩ שֶׁ֨בַע נָשִׁ֜ים בְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֗ד בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לַחְמֵ֣נוּ נֹאכֵ֔ל וְשִׂמְלָתֵ֖נוּ נִלְבָּ֑שׁ רַ֗ק יִקָּרֵ֤א שִׁמְךָ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ אֱסֹ֖ף חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ׃ ס
On that day the branch[^2] of Yahweh[^3] will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and splendor of the survivors of Israel.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ צֶ֣מַח יְהוָ֔ה לִצְבִ֖י וּלְכָב֑וֹד וּפְרִ֤י הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ לְגָא֣וֹן וּלְתִפְאֶ֔רֶת לִפְלֵיטַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Whoever is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone in Jerusalem who is recorded for life.[^4]
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ הַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר בְּצִיּ֗וֹן וְהַנּוֹתָר֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם קָד֖וֹשׁ יֵאָ֣מֶר ל֑וֹ כָּל־הַכָּת֥וּב לַחַיִּ֖ים בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
When the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and rinsed the bloodstains of Jerusalem from within her by a spirit[^5] of judgment and a spirit of burning,
אִ֣ם ׀ רָחַ֣ץ אֲדֹנָ֗י אֵ֚ת צֹאַ֣ת בְּנוֹת־צִיּ֔וֹן וְאֶת־דְּמֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם יָדִ֣יחַ מִקִּרְבָּ֑הּ בְּר֥וּחַ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּבְר֥וּחַ בָּעֵֽר׃

then Yahweh will create over the whole site of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day, and smoke and the glow of a flaming fire by night.[^6] For over all the glory there will be a canopy.[^7]
וּבָרָ֣א יְהוָ֡ה עַל֩ כָּל־מְכ֨וֹן הַר־צִיּ֜וֹן וְעַל־מִקְרָאֶ֗הָ עָנָ֤ן ׀ יוֹמָם֙ וְעָשָׁ֔ן וְנֹ֛גַהּ אֵ֥שׁ לֶהָבָ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה כִּ֥י עַל־כָּל־כָּב֖וֹד חֻפָּֽה׃
It will be a shelter, a shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from storm and rain.
וְסֻכָּ֛ה תִּהְיֶ֥ה לְצֵל־יוֹמָ֖ם מֵחֹ֑רֶב וּלְמַחְסֶה֙ וּלְמִסְתּ֔וֹר מִזֶּ֖רֶם וּמִמָּטָֽר׃ פ

n.1: The shame of being unmarried and childless. So many men will have died in war (3:25) that women will plead for the protection of a husband's name.
n.2: Hebrew *tsemach*, "sprout, growth". Here it may be the new growth of the land, matching "the fruit of the land". In Jeremiah 23:5; 33:15 and Zechariah 3:8; 6:12, "the Branch" is a title of a coming king of David's line, and many later readers took it so here: the Aramaic Targum reads "the anointed one (Messiah) of Yahweh".
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: Literally "everyone written for life", that is, entered in the register of the living.
n.5: Or "wind" or "breath". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.6: The cloud and the fire recall the pillar that led Israel through the wilderness (Exodus 13:21–22).
n.7: Hebrew *chuppah*, a covering or canopy, the word later used for the canopy over a bride and groom (Psalm 19:6, 19:5 in most English Bibles; Joel 2:16).

v: Let me sing for my beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard:[^1] My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.[^2]
אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ לִֽידִידִ֔י שִׁירַ֥ת דּוֹדִ֖י לְכַרְמ֑וֹ כֶּ֛רֶם הָיָ֥ה לִֽידִידִ֖י בְּקֶ֥רֶן בֶּן־שָֽׁמֶן׃

He dug it up and cleared it of stones, and planted it with choice vines.[^3] He built a watchtower in the middle of it and also cut out a winepress in it. He waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced rotten grapes.[^4]
וַֽיְעַזְּקֵ֣הוּ וַֽיְסַקְּלֵ֗הוּ וַיִּטָּעֵ֙הוּ֙ שֹׂרֵ֔ק וַיִּ֤בֶן מִגְדָּל֙ בְּתוֹכ֔וֹ וְגַם־יֶ֖קֶב חָצֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ וַיְקַ֛ו לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עֲנָבִ֖ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בְּאֻשִֽׁים׃
So now, you who live in Jerusalem and you people of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
וְעַתָּ֛ה יוֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֑ה שִׁפְטוּ־נָ֕א בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין כַּרְמִֽי׃
What more could I have done for my vineyard that I have not done in it? When I waited for it to produce grapes, why did it produce rotten grapes?
מַה־לַּעֲשׂ֥וֹת עוֹד֙ לְכַרְמִ֔י וְלֹ֥א עָשִׂ֖יתִי בּ֑וֹ מַדּ֧וּעַ קִוֵּ֛יתִי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עֲנָבִ֖ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ בְּאֻשִֽׁים׃
Now let me tell you what I am going to do to my vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be grazed bare; I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled.
וְעַתָּה֙ אוֹדִֽיעָה־נָּ֣א אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֖ה לְכַרְמִ֑י הָסֵ֤ר מְשׂוּכָּתוֹ֙ וְהָיָ֣ה לְבָעֵ֔ר פָּרֹ֥ץ גְּדֵר֖וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְמִרְמָֽס׃
I will make it a wasteland. It will not be pruned or hoed, and briers and thorns will grow up there. I will also command the clouds not to rain on it.
וַאֲשִׁיתֵ֣הוּ בָתָ֗ה לֹ֤א יִזָּמֵר֙ וְלֹ֣א יֵעָדֵ֔ר וְעָלָ֥ה שָׁמִ֖יר וָשָׁ֑יִת וְעַ֤ל הֶעָבִים֙ אֲצַוֶּ֔ה מֵהַמְטִ֥יר עָלָ֖יו מָטָֽר׃

For the vineyard of Yahweh[^5] of Armies is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the planting he delighted in. He waited for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard an outcry.[^6]
כִּ֣י כֶ֜רֶם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה נְטַ֖ע שַׁעֲשׁוּעָ֑יו וַיְקַ֤ו לְמִשְׁפָּט֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִשְׂפָּ֔ח לִצְדָקָ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה צְעָקָֽה׃ ס
Woe to[^7] those who join house to house and add field to field, until there is no room left, and you are left to live alone in the middle of the land!
ה֗וֹי מַגִּיעֵ֥י בַ֙יִת֙ בְּבַ֔יִת שָׂדֶ֥ה בְשָׂדֶ֖ה יַקְרִ֑יבוּ עַ֚ד אֶ֣פֶס מָק֔וֹם וְהֽוּשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם לְבַדְּכֶ֖ם בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Yahweh of Armies has sworn in my hearing:[^8] Many houses will surely become desolate, large and fine houses, with no one living in them.
בְּאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־לֹ֞א בָּתִּ֤ים רַבִּים֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה יִֽהְי֔וּ גְּדֹלִ֥ים וְטוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃
For ten acres[^9] of vineyard will produce only one bath,[^10] and a homer of seed will produce only an ephah.[^11]
כִּ֗י עֲשֶׂ֙רֶת֙ צִמְדֵּי־כֶ֔רֶם יַעֲשׂ֖וּ בַּ֣ת אֶחָ֑ת וְזֶ֥רַע חֹ֖מֶר יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֵיפָֽה׃ פ
Woe to those who rise early in the morning to chase after beer, who stay up late at night till wine sets them on fire!
ה֛וֹי מַשְׁכִּימֵ֥י בַבֹּ֖קֶר שֵׁכָ֣ר יִרְדֹּ֑פוּ מְאַחֲרֵ֣י בַנֶּ֔שֶׁף יַ֖יִן יַדְלִיקֵֽם׃
They have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, and wine at their feasts, but they pay no attention to the deeds of Yahweh, and they do not see the work of his hands.
וְהָיָ֨ה כִנּ֜וֹר וָנֶ֗בֶל תֹּ֧ף וְחָלִ֛יל וָיַ֖יִן מִשְׁתֵּיהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֨ת פֹּ֤עַל יְהוָה֙ לֹ֣א יַבִּ֔יטוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדָ֖יו לֹ֥א רָאֽוּ׃
Therefore my people go into exile for lack of knowledge.[^12] Their nobles are starving,[^13] and their masses are parched with thirst.
לָכֵ֛ן גָּלָ֥ה עַמִּ֖י מִבְּלִי־דָ֑עַת וּכְבוֹדוֹ֙ מְתֵ֣י רָעָ֔ב וַהֲמוֹנ֖וֹ צִחֵ֥ה צָמָֽא׃
Therefore Sheol[^14] has opened its throat wide[^15] and opened its mouth beyond measure. Down go her splendor and her masses, her noisy crowd and all who revel in her.[^16]
לָכֵ֗ן הִרְחִ֤יבָה שְּׁאוֹל֙ נַפְשָׁ֔הּ וּפָעֲרָ֥ה פִ֖יהָ לִבְלִי־חֹ֑ק וְיָרַ֨ד הֲדָרָ֧הּ וַהֲמוֹנָ֛הּ וּשְׁאוֹנָ֖הּ וְעָלֵ֥ז בָּֽהּ׃
So humankind is brought low, and everyone is humbled, and the eyes of the proud are humbled.
וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל־אִ֑ישׁ וְעֵינֵ֥י גְבֹהִ֖ים תִּשְׁפַּֽלְנָה׃
But Yahweh of Armies is exalted by justice, and the holy God shows himself holy by righteousness.
וַיִּגְבַּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וְהָאֵל֙ הַקָּד֔וֹשׁ נִקְדָּ֖שׁ בִּצְדָקָֽה׃
Lambs will graze there as in their own pasture, and strangers will eat among the ruins of the rich.[^17]
וְרָע֥וּ כְבָשִׂ֖ים כְּדָבְרָ֑ם וְחָרְב֥וֹת מֵחִ֖ים גָּרִ֥ים יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
Woe to those who drag guilt along with cords of falsehood, and sin as if with cart ropes,
ה֛וֹי מֹשְׁכֵ֥י הֶֽעָוֺ֖ן בְּחַבְלֵ֣י הַשָּׁ֑וְא וְכַעֲב֥וֹת הָעֲגָלָ֖ה חַטָּאָֽה׃
who say, "Let him hurry; let him be quick with his work, so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come near and come true, so that we may know it!"
הָאֹמְרִ֗ים יְמַהֵ֧ר ׀ יָחִ֛ישָׁה מַעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ לְמַ֣עַן נִרְאֶ֑ה וְתִקְרַ֣ב וְתָב֗וֹאָה עֲצַ֛ת קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְנֵדָֽעָה׃ ס
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who make darkness light and light darkness, who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
ה֣וֹי הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לָרַ֛ע ט֖וֹב וְלַטּ֣וֹב רָ֑ע שָׂמִ֨ים חֹ֤שֶׁךְ לְאוֹר֙ וְא֣וֹר לְחֹ֔שֶׁךְ שָׂמִ֥ים מַ֛ר לְמָת֖וֹק וּמָת֥וֹק לְמָֽר׃ ס
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight!
ה֖וֹי חֲכָמִ֣ים בְּעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם וְנֶ֥גֶד פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם נְבֹנִֽים׃
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine, and champions at mixing strong drinks,
ה֕וֹי גִּבּוֹרִ֖ים לִשְׁתּ֣וֹת יָ֑יִן וְאַנְשֵׁי־חַ֖יִל לִמְסֹ֥ךְ שֵׁכָֽר׃
who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deny justice to the innocent!
מַצְדִּיקֵ֥י רָשָׁ֖ע עֵ֣קֶב שֹׁ֑חַד וְצִדְקַ֥ת צַדִּיקִ֖ים יָסִ֥ירוּ מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃ ס

Therefore, as a tongue of fire devours straw and dry grass sinks down in the flame, their root will be like rot, and their blossom will blow away like dust. For they have rejected the instruction[^18] of Yahweh of Armies and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

לָכֵן֩ כֶּאֱכֹ֨ל קַ֜שׁ לְשׁ֣וֹן אֵ֗שׁ וַחֲשַׁ֤שׁ לֶֽהָבָה֙ יִרְפֶּ֔ה שָׁרְשָׁם֙ כַּמָּ֣ק יִֽהְיֶ֔ה וּפִרְחָ֖ם כָּאָבָ֣ק יַעֲלֶ֑ה כִּ֣י מָאֲס֗וּ אֵ֚ת תּוֹרַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְאֵ֛ת אִמְרַ֥ת קְדֽוֹשׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִאֵֽצוּ׃

That is why the anger of Yahweh burns against his people. He has stretched out his hand against them and struck them down. The mountains shook, and their corpses were like garbage in the middle of the streets. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.[^19]

עַל־כֵּ֡ן חָרָה֩ אַף־יְהוָ֨ה בְּעַמּ֜וֹ וַיֵּ֣ט יָד֧וֹ עָלָ֣יו וַיַּכֵּ֗הוּ וַֽיִּרְגְּזוּ֙ הֶֽהָרִ֔ים וַתְּהִ֧י נִבְלָתָ֛ם כַּסּוּחָ֖ה בְּקֶ֣רֶב חוּצ֑וֹת בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃
He will raise a signal flag for the nations far away and whistle for them[^20] from the ends of the earth. And look, swiftly, speedily they come!
וְנָֽשָׂא־נֵ֤ס לַגּוֹיִם֙ מֵרָח֔וֹק וְשָׁ֥רַק ל֖וֹ מִקְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה מְהֵרָ֖ה קַ֥ל יָבֽוֹא׃
None of them is weary, and none stumbles; none slumbers or sleeps. Not a belt is loose at the waist, not a sandal strap is broken.
אֵין־עָיֵ֤ף וְאֵין־כּוֹשֵׁל֙ בּ֔וֹ לֹ֥א יָנ֖וּם וְלֹ֣א יִישָׁ֑ן וְלֹ֤א נִפְתַּח֙ אֵז֣וֹר חֲלָצָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א נִתַּ֖ק שְׂר֥וֹךְ נְעָלָֽיו׃
Their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are strung. Their horses' hooves seem like flint, and their chariot wheels like a whirlwind.
אֲשֶׁ֤ר חִצָּיו֙ שְׁנוּנִ֔ים וְכָל־קַשְּׁתֹתָ֖יו דְּרֻכ֑וֹת פַּרְס֤וֹת סוּסָיו֙ כַּצַּ֣ר נֶחְשָׁ֔בוּ וְגַלְגִּלָּ֖יו כַּסּוּפָֽה׃
Their roar is like a lion's; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey and carry it off, and no one can rescue it.
שְׁאָגָ֥ה ל֖וֹ כַּלָּבִ֑יא *ושאג **יִשְׁאַ֨ג כַּכְּפִירִ֤ים וְיִנְהֹם֙ וְיֹאחֵ֣ז טֶ֔רֶף וְיַפְלִ֖יט וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּֽיל׃
On that day they will growl over it like the growling of the sea. If anyone looks at the land, there is darkness and distress, and the light is darkened by its clouds.
וְיִנְהֹ֥ם עָלָ֛יו בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כְּנַהֲמַת־יָ֑ם וְנִבַּ֤ט לָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וְהִנֵּה־חֹ֔שֶׁךְ צַ֣ר וָא֔וֹר חָשַׁ֖ךְ בַּעֲרִיפֶֽיהָ׃ פ

n.1: Or "my love song about his vineyard". Hebrew *dod*, "beloved", is the word used in the Song of Songs. The prophet sings as the friend of the vineyard's owner, who is revealed in verse 7.
n.2: Literally "on a horn, a son of oil".
n.3: Hebrew *soreq*, a choice variety of red grape (Jeremiah 2:21).
n.4: Hebrew *be'ushim*, "stinking things": sour, rotten or wild grapes. Also in verse 4.
n.5: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.6: A play on words that English cannot reproduce: he waited for *mishpat*, "justice", but saw *mispach*; for *tsedaqah*, "righteousness", but heard *tse'aqah*, the cry of the oppressed (Exodus 3:7, 9). *Mispach* is found only here; it probably means "bloodshed" or "lawlessness".
n.7: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning, used by the prophets to announce disaster (see 1:4). It begins six woes in this chapter (verses 8, 11, 18, 20, 21 and 22).
n.8: Literally "In my ears, Yahweh of Armies". The verb "has sworn" is not in the Hebrew but is implied by the oath that follows.
n.9: Literally "ten yokes": the land that ten teams of oxen could plow in a day.
n.10: A bath was about 6 gallons (22 liters).
n.11: A homer was ten ephahs (Ezekiel 45:11), probably about 220 liters (6 bushels). The harvest will be only a tenth of the seed sown.
n.12: Or "without knowing it".
n.13: Literally "Their glory are men of hunger". The same consonants can be read "dead from hunger".
n.14: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead, pictured here as a monster with an open mouth.
n.15: Hebrew *nephesh*, here "throat, appetite".
n.16: *Her*: Jerusalem's.
n.17: Literally "the fat ones". The Septuagint reads "lambs" instead of "strangers". The meaning of the verse is uncertain.
n.18: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching, law".
n.19: This refrain returns in 9:11, 16 and 20 (9:12, 17 and 21 in most English Bibles) and in 10:4.
n.20: Literally "for it". The invader is singular in the Hebrew of verses 26–30, a single nation pictured as one army.

v: In the year that King Uzziah died,[^1] I saw the Lord[^2] sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the hem of his robe filled the temple.[^3]
בִּשְׁנַת־מוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וָאֶרְאֶ֧ה אֶת־אֲדֹנָ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֖א רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֑א וְשׁוּלָ֖יו מְלֵאִ֥ים אֶת־הַהֵיכָֽל׃
Seraphim[^4] stood above him. Each had six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet,[^5] and with two he flew.
שְׂרָפִ֨ים עֹמְדִ֤ים ׀ מִמַּ֙עַל֙ ל֔וֹ שֵׁ֧שׁ כְּנָפַ֛יִם שֵׁ֥שׁ כְּנָפַ֖יִם לְאֶחָ֑ד בִּשְׁתַּ֣יִם ׀ יְכַסֶּ֣ה פָנָ֗יו וּבִשְׁתַּ֛יִם יְכַסֶּ֥ה רַגְלָ֖יו וּבִשְׁתַּ֥יִם יְעוֹפֵֽף׃
And they called to one another: "Holy, holy, holy is Yahweh of Armies![^6] The whole earth is full of his glory."[^7]
וְקָרָ֨א זֶ֤ה אֶל־זֶה֙ וְאָמַ֔ר קָד֧וֹשׁ ׀ קָד֛וֹשׁ קָד֖וֹשׁ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת מְלֹ֥א כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃
The doorposts and thresholds[^8] shook at the sound of the one who called, and the house was filled with smoke.
וַיָּנֻ֙עוּ֙ אַמּ֣וֹת הַסִּפִּ֔ים מִקּ֖וֹל הַקּוֹרֵ֑א וְהַבַּ֖יִת יִמָּלֵ֥א עָשָֽׁן׃
Then I said, "Woe is me! I am ruined![^9] For I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips, and my eyes have seen the King, Yahweh of Armies!"
וָאֹמַ֞ר אֽוֹי־לִ֣י כִֽי־נִדְמֵ֗יתִי כִּ֣י אִ֤ישׁ טְמֵֽא־שְׂפָתַ֙יִם֙ אָנֹ֔כִי וּבְתוֹךְ֙ עַם־טְמֵ֣א שְׂפָתַ֔יִם אָנֹכִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֑ב כִּ֗י אֶת־הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת רָא֥וּ עֵינָֽי׃
Then one of the seraphim flew to me, holding in his hand a glowing coal[^10] that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
וַיָּ֣עָף אֵלַ֗י אֶחָד֙ מִן־הַשְּׂרָפִ֔ים וּבְיָד֖וֹ רִצְפָּ֑ה בְּמֶ֨לְקַחַ֔יִם לָקַ֖ח מֵעַ֥ל הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
He touched my mouth with it and said, "See, this has touched your lips. Your guilt is taken away, and your sin is atoned for."[^11]
וַיַּגַּ֣ע עַל־פִּ֔י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה נָגַ֥ע זֶ֖ה עַל־שְׂפָתֶ֑יךָ וְסָ֣ר עֲוֺנֶ֔ךָ וְחַטָּאתְךָ֖ תְּכֻפָּֽר׃
Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send? Who will go for us?"[^12] And I said, "Here I am. Send me!"
וָאֶשְׁמַ֞ע אֶת־ק֤וֹל אֲדֹנָי֙ אֹמֵ֔ר אֶת־מִ֥י אֶשְׁלַ֖ח וּמִ֣י יֵֽלֶךְ־לָ֑נוּ וָאֹמַ֖ר הִנְנִ֥י שְׁלָחֵֽנִי׃
He said, "Go, and say to this people: 'Keep on hearing, but do not understand; keep on seeing, but do not perceive.'
וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֵ֥ךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֙וֹעַ֙ וְאַל־תָּבִ֔ינוּ וּרְא֥וּ רָא֖וֹ וְאַל־תֵּדָֽעוּ׃

Make the heart of this people dull,[^13] make their ears heavy and shut their eyes, so that they may not see with their eyes, hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn back and be healed."[^14]
הַשְׁמֵן֙ לֵב־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאָזְנָ֥יו הַכְבֵּ֖ד וְעֵינָ֣יו הָשַׁ֑ע פֶּן־יִרְאֶ֨ה בְעֵינָ֜יו וּבְאָזְנָ֣יו יִשְׁמָ֗ע וּלְבָב֥וֹ יָבִ֛ין וָשָׁ֖ב וְרָ֥פָא לֽוֹ׃
Then I said, "How long, Lord?" And he answered, "Until cities lie in ruins with no one living in them, and houses with no people, and the land is left utterly desolate,
וָאֹמַ֕ר עַד־מָתַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י וַיֹּ֡אמֶר עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר֩ אִם־שָׁא֨וּ עָרִ֜ים מֵאֵ֣ין יוֹשֵׁ֗ב וּבָתִּים֙ מֵאֵ֣ין אָדָ֔ם וְהָאֲדָמָ֖ה תִּשָּׁאֶ֥ה שְׁמָמָֽה׃
until Yahweh sends the people far away, and the deserted places are many in the middle of the land.
וְרִחַ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־הָאָדָ֑ם וְרַבָּ֥ה הָעֲזוּבָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Even if a tenth remains in it, it will be burned again,[^15] like a terebinth or an oak whose stump remains when it is cut down.[^16] The holy seed is its stump."[^17]
וְע֥וֹד בָּהּ֙ עֲשִׂ֣רִיָּ֔ה וְשָׁ֖בָה וְהָיְתָ֣ה לְבָעֵ֑ר כָּאֵלָ֣ה וְכָאַלּ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֤ר בְּשַׁלֶּ֙כֶת֙ מַצֶּ֣בֶת בָּ֔ם זֶ֥רַע קֹ֖דֶשׁ מַצַּבְתָּֽהּ׃ פ

n.1: About 740 BC.
n.2: Hebrew *Adonai*, "the Lord", not the name Yahweh. Also in verses 8 and 11.
n.3: Hebrew *heikhal*, the main hall of the temple, or a palace.
n.4: Hebrew *seraphim*, probably "burning ones". The same word is used of the venomous snakes in the wilderness (Numbers 21:6) and of a "flying serpent" in Isaiah 14:29 and 30:6. Here they are winged beings that attend the throne of God.
n.5: Perhaps their bodies. "Feet" is sometimes a polite word for the private parts (7:20).
n.6: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verse 5.
n.7: Or "His glory is the fullness of the whole earth". The threefold "holy" is echoed in Revelation 4:8, and this verse is sung in Jewish and Christian worship (the *Kedushah* and the *Sanctus*).
n.8: Literally "the foundations of the thresholds", perhaps the pivots on which the doors turned.
n.9: Or "I am silenced". Hebrew *nidmeti*.
n.10: Or "a hot stone".
n.11: Hebrew *kipper*, "atone, make atonement", the word used for the removal of sin by sacrifice.
n.12: The plural may include the heavenly beings around the throne (compare 1 Kings 22:19–22).
n.13: Literally "fat".
n.14: Verses 9–10 are quoted in Matthew 13:14–15; Mark 4:12; Luke 8:10; John 12:40 and Acts 28:26–27, mostly from the Greek Septuagint, which turns the commands into a description: "You will indeed hear but never understand … For the heart of this people has grown dull."
n.15: Or "it will be laid waste again".
n.16: Or "when it is felled". Hebrew *shalleket*, found also in 1 Chronicles 26:16 as the name of a temple gate.
n.17: The Septuagint does not have this sentence.

v: In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, marched up to Jerusalem to wage war against it, but they could not conquer it.[^1]

וַיְהִ֡י בִּימֵ֣י אָ֠חָז בֶּן־יוֹתָ֨ם בֶּן־עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה עָלָ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־אֲ֠רָם וּפֶ֨קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה עָלֶ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יָכֹ֖ל לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם עָלֶֽיהָ׃
When the house of David was told, "Aram has joined forces with Ephraim,"[^2] the heart of Ahaz and the hearts of his people shook, as the trees of the forest shake in the wind.
וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לְבֵ֤ית דָּוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נָ֥חָֽה אֲרָ֖ם עַל־אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיָּ֤נַע לְבָבוֹ֙ וּלְבַ֣ב עַמּ֔וֹ כְּנ֥וֹעַ עֲצֵי־יַ֖עַר מִפְּנֵי־רֽוּחַ׃
Then Yahweh[^3] said to Isaiah, "Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub,[^4] at the end of the channel of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field.[^5]
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶֽל־יְשַׁעְיָהוּ֒ צֵא־נָא֙ לִקְרַ֣את אָחָ֔ז אַתָּ֕ה וּשְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בְּנֶ֑ךָ אֶל־קְצֵ֗ה תְּעָלַת֙ הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הָעֶלְיוֹנָ֔ה אֶל־מְסִלַּ֖ת שְׂדֵ֥ה כוֹבֵֽס׃

Say to him, 'Be careful, keep calm, and do not be afraid. Do not lose heart because of these two smoldering stubs of firewood, because of the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.[^6]
וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵ֠לָיו הִשָּׁמֵ֨ר וְהַשְׁקֵ֜ט אַל־תִּירָ֗א וּלְבָבְךָ֙ אַל־יֵרַ֔ךְ מִשְּׁנֵ֨י זַנְב֧וֹת הָאוּדִ֛ים הָעֲשֵׁנִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה בָּחֳרִי־אַ֛ף רְצִ֥ין וַאֲרָ֖ם וּבֶן־רְמַלְיָֽהוּ׃
Aram, with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted evil against you. They have said:
יַ֗עַן כִּֽי־יָעַ֥ץ עָלֶ֛יךָ אֲרָ֖ם רָעָ֑ה אֶפְרַ֥יִם וּבֶן־רְמַלְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃
Let us invade Judah and terrify it, and break it open for ourselves, and make the son of Tabeel[^7] king in it.
נַעֲלֶ֤ה בִֽיהוּדָה֙ וּנְקִיצֶ֔נָּה וְנַבְקִעֶ֖נָּה אֵלֵ֑ינוּ וְנַמְלִ֥יךְ מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ אֵ֖ת בֶּן־טָֽבְאַֽל׃ ס
This is what the Lord Yahweh says: It will not stand; it will not happen.
כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה לֹ֥א תָק֖וּם וְלֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶֽה׃
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered and will no longer be a people.
כִּ֣י רֹ֤אשׁ אֲרָם֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וְרֹ֥אשׁ דַּמֶּ֖שֶׂק רְצִ֑ין וּבְע֗וֹד שִׁשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה יֵחַ֥ת אֶפְרַ֖יִם מֵעָֽם׃
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in faith, you will not stand firm at all.'"[^8]
וְרֹ֤אשׁ אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וְרֹ֥אשׁ שֹׁמְר֖וֹן בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֑הוּ אִ֚ם לֹ֣א תַאֲמִ֔ינוּ כִּ֖י לֹ֥א תֵאָמֵֽנוּ׃ ס
Again Yahweh spoke to Ahaz:
וַיּ֣וֹסֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל־אָחָ֖ז לֵאמֹֽר׃
"Ask Yahweh your God for a sign, whether as deep as Sheol or as high as the heavens above."[^9]
שְׁאַל־לְךָ֣ א֔וֹת מֵעִ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ הַעְמֵ֣ק שְׁאָ֔לָה א֖וֹ הַגְבֵּ֥הַּ לְמָֽעְלָה׃
But Ahaz said, "I will not ask. I will not put Yahweh to the test."
וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָחָ֑ז לֹא־אֶשְׁאַ֥ל וְלֹֽא־אֲנַסֶּ֖ה אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
Then Isaiah[^10] said, "Listen now, house of David! Is it not enough for you to wear out the patience of people, that you wear out the patience of my God too?
וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֖א בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֑ד הַמְעַ֤ט מִכֶּם֙ הַלְא֣וֹת אֲנָשִׁ֔ים כִּ֥י תַלְא֖וּ גַּ֥ם אֶת־אֱלֹהָֽי׃
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: Look, the young woman[^11] is pregnant and will give birth to a son,[^12] and she will call him Immanuel.[^13]
לָ֠כֵן יִתֵּ֨ן אֲדֹנָ֥י ה֛וּא לָכֶ֖ם א֑וֹת הִנֵּ֣ה הָעַלְמָ֗ה הָרָה֙ וְיֹלֶ֣דֶת בֵּ֔ן וְקָרָ֥את שְׁמ֖וֹ עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל׃
He will eat curds and honey by the time he knows how to reject evil and choose good.[^14]
חֶמְאָ֥ה וּדְבַ֖שׁ יֹאכֵ֑ל לְדַעְתּ֛וֹ מָא֥וֹס בָּרָ֖ע וּבָח֥וֹר בַּטּֽוֹב׃
For before the boy knows how to reject evil and choose good, the land whose two kings you dread will be abandoned.
כִּ֠י בְּטֶ֨רֶם יֵדַ֥ע הַנַּ֛עַר מָאֹ֥ס בָּרָ֖ע וּבָחֹ֣ר בַּטּ֑וֹב תֵּעָזֵ֤ב הָאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתָּ֣ה קָ֔ץ מִפְּנֵ֖י שְׁנֵ֥י מְלָכֶֽיהָ׃
Yahweh will bring on you, on your people and on your father's house days such as have not come since the day Ephraim broke away from Judah:[^15] the king of Assyria."
יָבִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה עָלֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל־עַמְּךָ֮ וְעַל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִיךָ֒ יָמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־בָ֔אוּ לְמִיּ֥וֹם סוּר־אֶפְרַ֖יִם מֵעַ֣ל יְהוּדָ֑ה אֵ֖ת מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃ פ
On that day Yahweh will whistle for the fly that is at the far end of the streams of Egypt and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ לַזְּב֔וּב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּקְצֵ֖ה יְאֹרֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלַ֨דְּבוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אַשּֽׁוּר׃
They will all come and settle in the steep ravines and in the clefts of the rocks, on all the thornbushes and on all the watering places.[^16]
וּבָ֨אוּ וְנָח֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ בְּנַחֲלֵ֣י הַבַּתּ֔וֹת וּבִנְקִיקֵ֖י הַסְּלָעִ֑ים וּבְכֹל֙ הַנַּ֣עֲצוּצִ֔ים וּבְכֹ֖ל הַנַּהֲלֹלִֽים׃
On that day the Lord will shave with a razor hired from beyond the River,[^17] with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet,[^18] and it will sweep away the beard as well.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יְגַלַּ֣ח אֲדֹנָי֩ בְּתַ֨עַר הַשְּׂכִירָ֜ה בְּעֶבְרֵ֤י נָהָר֙ בְּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר אֶת־הָרֹ֖אשׁ וְשַׂ֣עַר הָרַגְלָ֑יִם וְגַ֥ם אֶת־הַזָּקָ֖ן תִּסְפֶּֽה׃ ס
On that day a man will keep alive a young cow and two sheep.
וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא יְחַיֶּה־אִ֛ישׁ עֶגְלַ֥ת בָּקָ֖ר וּשְׁתֵּי־צֹֽאן׃
Because they give so much milk, he will eat curds. Everyone who is left in the land will eat curds and honey.
וְהָיָ֗ה מֵרֹ֛ב עֲשׂ֥וֹת חָלָ֖ב יֹאכַ֣ל חֶמְאָ֑ה כִּֽי־חֶמְאָ֤ה וּדְבַשׁ֙ יֹאכֵ֔ל כָּל־הַנּוֹתָ֖ר בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
On that day every place where there used to be a thousand vines, worth a thousand shekels of silver,[^19] will become briers and thorns.
וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִֽהְיֶ֣ה כָל־מָק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִֽהְיֶה־שָּׁ֛ם אֶ֥לֶף גֶּ֖פֶן בְּאֶ֣לֶף כָּ֑סֶף לַשָּׁמִ֥יר וְלַשַּׁ֖יִת יִֽהְיֶֽה׃
People will go there with bow and arrows, for all the land will be briers and thorns.
בַּחִצִּ֥ים וּבַקֶּ֖שֶׁת יָ֣בוֹא שָׁ֑מָּה כִּי־שָׁמִ֥יר וָשַׁ֖יִת תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה כָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
As for all the hills that used to be dug with a hoe, you will not go there for fear of the briers and thorns. They will become a place where cattle are let loose and sheep trample.
וְכֹ֣ל הֶהָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּמַּעְדֵּר֙ יֵעָ֣דֵר֔וּן לֹֽא־תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה יִרְאַ֖ת שָׁמִ֣יר וָשָׁ֑יִת וְהָיָה֙ לְמִשְׁלַ֣ח שׁ֔וֹר וּלְמִרְמַ֖ס שֶֽׂה׃ פ

n.1: Literally "but he could not fight against it". Aram, the kingdom of the Arameans with its capital at Damascus, and Israel, the northern kingdom, attacked Judah in about 734 BC (2 Kings 16:5).
n.2: Literally "Aram has settled on Ephraim". *Ephraim*, the largest tribe of the north, stands for the northern kingdom of Israel.
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: *Shear-jashub* means "A remnant will return" (10:20–22).
n.5: Traditionally "the Fuller's Field", where cloth was washed and bleached (36:2).
n.6: Pekah. Isaiah does not use his name, perhaps in contempt.
n.7: Hebrew *Tav'al*. The name is probably Tabeel, "God is good". The vowels of the Hebrew text may make it sound like "good-for-nothing".
n.8: A play on words: *im lo ta'aminu ki lo te'amenu*. Both verbs come from the root *aman*, "be firm, be sure", the root of *amen*. The promise to David was that his house would be made firm (2 Samuel 7:16). *You* is plural, addressed to the house of David.
n.9: The vowel points read "make it deep, ask" (*she'alah*). The same consonants read as *she'olah*, "deep as Sheol", match "high above" in the next line, and that reading is followed here. *Sheol* is the realm of the dead.
n.10: Literally "he".
n.11: Hebrew *almah*, "young woman", a girl old enough to marry. It is used of Rebekah (Genesis 24:43) and of Moses' sister (Exodus 2:8). The word does not in itself say whether she is a virgin; the more specific word for that is *betulah*. With the article, "the young woman" is someone the hearers knew of, perhaps the king's wife or the prophet's. The Greek Septuagint translated *almah* here as *parthenos*, "virgin", and Matthew 1:23 quotes the Septuagint in telling of the birth of Jesus.
n.12: Or "will become pregnant and give birth to a son". The Hebrew has no verb, only the adjective "pregnant", and the time depends on the context.
n.13: *Immanuel* means "God is with us" (8:8, 10). The Septuagint reads "you will call", and Matthew 1:23 reads "they will call".
n.14: Or "so that he will know how to reject evil and choose good". *Curds and honey* are the food of a land where no crops are grown and herds graze freely (verses 21–22).
n.15: When the northern tribes broke away from the house of David after Solomon's death (1 Kings 12).
n.16: Hebrew *nahalolim*, a word found only here. Perhaps "watering holes" or "pastures".
n.17: The Euphrates.
n.18: "The hair of the feet" probably means the hair of the body, including the private parts. Shaving a man's beard was a deep humiliation (2 Samuel 10:4–5).
n.19: A shekel is about 2/5 ounce (11.5 grams), so a thousand shekels is about 25 pounds (11.5 kg).

v: Yahweh[^1] said to me, "Take a large tablet[^2] and write on it in ordinary letters:[^3] Belonging to Maher-shalal-hash-baz."[^4]
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י קַח־לְךָ֖ גִּלָּי֣וֹן גָּד֑וֹל וּכְתֹ֤ב עָלָיו֙ בְּחֶ֣רֶט אֱנ֔וֹשׁ לְמַהֵ֥ר שָׁלָ֖ל חָ֥שׁ בַּֽז׃
So I took reliable witnesses to testify for me,[^5] Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.
וְאָעִ֣ידָה לִּ֔י עֵדִ֖ים נֶאֱמָנִ֑ים אֵ֚ת אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְאֶת־זְכַרְיָ֖הוּ בֶּ֥ן יְבֶרֶכְיָֽהוּ׃
Then I went to the prophetess,[^6] and she conceived and gave birth to a son. Yahweh said to me, "Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
וָאֶקְרַב֙ אֶל־הַנְּבִיאָ֔ה וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י קְרָ֣א שְׁמ֔וֹ מַהֵ֥ר שָׁלָ֖ל חָ֥שׁ בַּֽז׃
For before the boy knows how to say 'My father' or 'My mother,' the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off before the king of Assyria."
כִּ֗י בְּטֶ֙רֶם֙ יֵדַ֣ע הַנַּ֔עַר קְרֹ֖א אָבִ֣י וְאִמִּ֑י יִשָּׂ֣א ׀ אֶת־חֵ֣יל דַּמֶּ֗שֶׂק וְאֵת֙ שְׁלַ֣ל שֹׁמְר֔וֹן לִפְנֵ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃ ס
Yahweh spoke to me again:
וַיֹּ֣סֶף יְהוָ֔ה דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד לֵאמֹֽר׃
"Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah[^7] and rejoices over Rezin and the son of Remaliah,[^8]
יַ֗עַן כִּ֤י מָאַס֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֵ֚ת מֵ֣י הַשִּׁלֹ֔חַ הַהֹלְכִ֖ים לְאַ֑[t]ט וּמְשׂ֥וֹשׂ אֶת־רְצִ֖ין וּבֶן־רְמַלְיָֽהוּ׃

therefore, look, the Lord is bringing up against them the waters of the River,[^9] mighty and many, the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will rise over all its channels and overflow all its banks.
וְלָכֵ֡ן הִנֵּ֣ה אֲדֹנָי֩ מַעֲלֶ֨ה עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת־מֵ֣י הַנָּהָ֗ר הָעֲצוּמִים֙ וְהָ֣רַבִּ֔ים אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר וְאֶת־כָּל־כְּבוֹד֑וֹ וְעָלָה֙ עַל־כָּל־אֲפִיקָ֔יו וְהָלַ֖ךְ עַל־כָּל־גְּדוֹתָֽיו׃
It will sweep on into Judah, flood it and pass through, reaching up to the neck. Its outspread wings will fill the breadth of your land, Immanuel!"[^10]
וְחָלַ֤ף בִּֽיהוּדָה֙ שָׁטַ֣ף וְעָבַ֔ר עַד־צַוָּ֖אר יַגִּ֑יעַ וְהָיָה֙ מֻטּ֣וֹת כְּנָפָ֔יו מְלֹ֥א רֹֽחַב־אַרְצְךָ֖ עִמָּ֥נוּ אֵֽל׃ ס
Raise the war cry,[^11] you peoples, and be shattered! Listen, all you distant lands! Arm yourselves, and be shattered! Arm yourselves, and be shattered!
רֹ֤עוּ עַמִּים֙ וָחֹ֔תּוּ וְהַֽאֲזִ֔ינוּ כֹּ֖ל מֶרְחַקֵּי־אָ֑רֶץ הִתְאַזְּר֣וּ וָחֹ֔תּוּ הִֽתְאַזְּר֖וּ וָחֹֽתּוּ׃
Make your plans, but they will come to nothing! Give your orders, but they will not stand! For God is with us.[^12]
עֻ֥צוּ עֵצָ֖ה וְתֻפָ֑ר דַּבְּר֤וּ דָבָר֙ וְלֹ֣א יָק֔וּם כִּ֥י עִמָּ֖נוּ אֵֽל׃ ס
For this is what Yahweh said to me, with his strong hand on me,[^13] when he warned me not to walk in the way of this people:
כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י כְּחֶזְקַ֣ת הַיָּ֑ד וְיִסְּרֵ֕נִי מִלֶּ֛כֶת בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
"Do not call conspiracy[^14] all that this people calls conspiracy. Do not fear what they fear, and do not dread it.
לֹא־תֹאמְר֣וּן קֶ֔שֶׁר לְכֹ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־יֹאמַ֛ר הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה קָ֑שֶׁר וְאֶת־מוֹרָא֥וֹ לֹֽא־תִֽירְא֖וּ וְלֹ֥א תַעֲרִֽיצוּ׃
Yahweh of Armies:[^15] he is the one you must regard as holy. He is the one you must fear; he is the one you must dread.[^16]
אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֹת֣וֹ תַקְדִּ֑ישׁוּ וְה֥וּא מוֹרַאֲכֶ֖ם וְה֥וּא מֽ͏ַעֲרִֽצְכֶֽם׃
He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel he will be a stone that makes people stumble and a rock that makes them fall, and for those who live in Jerusalem a trap and a snare.[^17]
וְהָיָ֖ה לְמִקְדָּ֑שׁ וּלְאֶ֣בֶן נֶ֠גֶף וּלְצ֨וּר מִכְשׁ֜וֹל לִשְׁנֵ֨י בָתֵּ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְפַ֣ח וּלְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ לְיוֹשֵׁ֖ב יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Many among them will stumble; they will fall and be broken, they will be snared and captured."
וְכָ֥שְׁלוּ בָ֖ם רַבִּ֑ים וְנָפְל֣וּ וְנִשְׁבָּ֔רוּ וְנוֹקְשׁ֖וּ וְנִלְכָּֽדוּ׃ ס
Bind up the testimony; seal the instruction among my disciples.[^18]
צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה בְּלִמֻּדָֽי׃
I will wait for Yahweh, who is hiding his face from the house of Jacob. I will put my hope in him.
וְחִכִּ֙יתִי֙ לַיהוָ֔ה הַמַּסְתִּ֥יר פָּנָ֖יו מִבֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְקִוֵּ֖יתִֽי־לֽוֹ׃
Here am I, and the children Yahweh has given me. We are signs and portents in Israel from Yahweh of Armies, who dwells on Mount Zion.[^19]
הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י וְהַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָֽתַן־לִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְאֹת֥וֹת וּלְמוֹפְתִ֖ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מֵעִם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הַשֹּׁכֵ֖ן בְּהַ֥ר צִיּֽוֹן׃ ס

When people say to you, "Consult the spirits of the dead and the spiritists,[^20] who chirp and mutter," should not a people consult their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?[^21]
וְכִֽי־יֹאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֗ם דִּרְשׁ֤וּ אֶל־הָאֹבוֹת֙ וְאֶל־הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֔ים הַֽמְצַפְצְפִ֖ים וְהַמַּהְגִּ֑ים הֲלוֹא־עַם֙ אֶל־אֱלֹהָ֣יו יִדְרֹ֔שׁ בְּעַ֥ד הַחַיִּ֖ים אֶל־הַמֵּתִֽים׃
To the instruction and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, there is no dawn for them.[^22]
לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה אִם־לֹ֤א יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵֽין־ל֖וֹ שָֽׁחַר׃
They will pass through the land,[^23] hard-pressed and hungry. When they are hungry, they will become enraged, and they will curse their king and their God[^24] as they look upward.
וְעָ֥בַר בָּ֖הּ נִקְשֶׁ֣ה וְרָעֵ֑ב וְהָיָ֨ה כִֽי־יִרְעַ֜ב וְהִתְקַצַּ֗ף וְקִלֵּ֧ל בְּמַלְכּ֛וֹ וּבֵאלֹהָ֖יו וּפָנָ֥ה לְמָֽעְלָה׃
Then they will look to the earth, and see only distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish, and they will be driven into thick darkness.
וְאֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ יַבִּ֑יט וְהִנֵּ֨ה צָרָ֤ה וַחֲשֵׁכָה֙ מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה וַאֲפֵלָ֖ה מְנֻדָּֽח׃

Yet there will be no more gloom for the land that was in anguish.[^25] In the past he brought shame on the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future he will bring glory to the way of the sea, the land beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.[^26]
כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ כָּעֵ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן הֵקַ֞ל אַ֤רְצָה זְבֻלוּן֙ וְאַ֣רְצָה נַפְתָּלִ֔י וְהָאַחֲר֖וֹן הִכְבִּ֑יד דֶּ֤רֶךְ הַיָּם֙ עֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן גְּלִ֖יל הַגּוֹיִֽם׃

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Or "scroll". Hebrew *gillayon*, perhaps a smooth sheet or board for writing.
n.3: Literally "with a man's stylus", that is, in writing everyone can read.
n.4: *Maher-shalal-hash-baz* means "Quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil".
n.5: Or "And I will take reliable witnesses to testify for me", as Yahweh's words. Uriah may be the priest of 2 Kings 16:10–16.
n.6: Isaiah's wife.
n.7: A channel that carried water from the Gihon spring to a pool in Jerusalem (John 9:7, "Siloam"). Its quiet waters stand for trust in Yahweh's protection, against the flood of verses 7–8.
n.8: Literally "and rejoicing with Rezin". The Hebrew is difficult; *this people* may be Judah or the northern kingdom.
n.9: The Euphrates.
n.10: *Immanuel* means "God is with us" (7:14).
n.11: Hebrew *ro'u*, perhaps "be broken" or "make an uproar". The Septuagint reads "Know".
n.12: Hebrew *immanu el*, the name *Immanuel* (verse 8; 7:14).
n.13: Literally "with strength of the hand", the hand of Yahweh on the prophet.
n.14: *You* is plural in verses 12–13: the prophet and those who follow him.
n.15: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verse 18.
n.16: Verses 12–13 are echoed in 1 Peter 3:14–15, following the Septuagint.
n.17: Romans 9:33 and 1 Peter 2:8 combine this verse with 28:16.
n.18: Hebrew *te'udah*, a solemn, witnessed message; *torah*, "instruction" (also in verse 20). The speaker may be Isaiah or Yahweh.
n.19: Hebrews 2:13 quotes verses 17–18 from the Septuagint. Isaiah's sons' names were signs: Shear-jashub (7:3), Maher-shalal-hash-baz (verse 3), and perhaps Immanuel (7:14).
n.20: Hebrew *ovot* and *yidde'onim*, those who claim to speak with the dead (Leviticus 19:31; 1 Samuel 28:3–9).
n.21: Or, as the words of those who consult the dead: "Should not a people consult their gods, the dead on behalf of the living?" Hebrew *elohim* can mean "God" or "gods", and is used of the spirit of the dead Samuel in 1 Samuel 28:13.
n.22: Or "it is because there is no dawn for them". The meaning of the line is uncertain.
n.25: Verse 23 is 9:1 in most English Bibles, and 9:1–20 are 9:2–21. The first line of this verse is difficult; literally "For there is no gloom to her who is in distress".
n.26: Or "the district of the nations". Hebrew *galil* means "circle, region". These northern lands were the first to be taken by Assyria (2 Kings 15:29). Matthew 4:15–16 quotes this verse and 9:1 (9:1–2 in most English Bibles).

v: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. On those who lived in the land of deep darkness[^1] a light has shone.
הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ רָא֖וּ א֣וֹר גָּד֑וֹל יֹשְׁבֵי֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ צַלְמָ֔וֶת א֖וֹר נָגַ֥הּ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
You have made the nation great; you have increased its joy.[^2] They rejoice before you as people rejoice at harvest, as warriors rejoice when they divide the plunder.
הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי *לא **ל֖וֹ הִגְדַּ֣לְתָּ הַשִּׂמְחָ֑ה שָׂמְח֤וּ לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ כְּשִׂמְחַ֣ת בַּקָּצִ֔יר כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגִ֖ילוּ בְּחַלְּקָ֥ם שָׁלָֽל׃
For the yoke that weighed them down, the bar across their shoulders, the rod of their oppressor, you have shattered, as on the day of Midian.[^3]
כִּ֣י ׀ אֶת־עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗וֹ וְאֵת֙ מַטֵּ֣ה שִׁכְמ֔וֹ שֵׁ֖בֶט הַנֹּגֵ֣שׂ בּ֑וֹ הַחִתֹּ֖תָ כְּי֥וֹם מִדְיָֽן׃
For every boot of the warrior that tramped in the battle,[^4] and every garment rolled in blood, will be burned as fuel for the fire.
כִּ֤י כָל־סְאוֹן֙ סֹאֵ֣ן בְּרַ֔עַשׁ וְשִׂמְלָ֖ה מְגוֹלָלָ֣ה בְדָמִ֑ים וְהָיְתָ֥ה לִשְׂרֵפָ֖ה מַאֲכֹ֥לֶת אֵֽשׁ׃

For a child has been born to us, a son has been given to us, and the government will be on his shoulder. His name will be called[^5] Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.[^6]
כִּי־יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד־לָ֗נוּ בֵּ֚ן נִתַּן־לָ֔נוּ וַתְּהִ֥י הַמִּשְׂרָ֖ה עַל־שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמ֜וֹ פֶּ֠לֶא יוֹעֵץ֙ אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר אֲבִיעַ֖ד שַׂר־שָׁלֽוֹם׃

His government will grow,[^7] and there will be no end to peace, on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and uphold it with justice and righteousness from now on and forever. The zeal of Yahweh[^8] of Armies will do this.

*לם[c]*רבה **לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה הַמִּשְׂרָ֜ה וּלְשָׁל֣וֹם אֵֽין־קֵ֗ץ עַל־כִּסֵּ֤א דָוִד֙ וְעַל־מַמְלַכְתּ֔וֹ לְהָכִ֤ין אֹתָהּ֙ וּֽלְסַעֲדָ֔הּ בְּמִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּבִצְדָקָ֑ה מֵעַתָּה֙ וְעַד־עוֹלָ֔ם קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה־זֹּֽאת׃ ס
The Lord has sent a word against Jacob, and it has fallen on Israel.
דָּבָ֛ר שָׁלַ֥ח אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּיַעֲקֹ֑ב וְנָפַ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
All the people will know it, Ephraim and those who live in Samaria, who say in their pride and arrogance of heart,
וְיָדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם כֻּלּ֔וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם וְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב שֹׁמְר֑וֹן בְּגַאֲוָ֛ה וּבְגֹ֥דֶל לֵבָ֖ב לֵאמֹֽר׃
"The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with dressed stone. The sycamore-figs have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place."
לְבֵנִ֥ים נָפָ֖לוּ וְגָזִ֣ית נִבְנֶ֑ה שִׁקְמִ֣ים גֻּדָּ֔עוּ וַאֲרָזִ֖ים נַחֲלִֽיף׃
So Yahweh has raised up the adversaries of Rezin against him[^9] and stirred up his enemies:
וַיְשַׂגֵּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־צָרֵ֥י רְצִ֖ין עָלָ֑יו וְאֶת־אֹיְבָ֖יו יְסַכְסֵֽךְ׃
Aram from the east and the Philistines from the west[^10] have devoured Israel with open mouth. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.[^11]
אֲרָ֣ם מִקֶּ֗דֶם וּפְלִשְׁתִּים֙ מֵֽאָח֔וֹר וַיֹּאכְל֥וּ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּכָל־פֶּ֑ה בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃
But the people have not turned back to him who struck them, nor have they sought Yahweh of Armies.
וְהָעָ֥ם לֹא־שָׁ֖ב עַד־הַמַּכֵּ֑הוּ וְאֶת־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֹ֥א דָרָֽשׁוּ׃ ס
So Yahweh cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed,[^12] in a single day.
וַיַּכְרֵ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֗ל רֹ֧אשׁ וְזָנָ֛ב כִּפָּ֥ה וְאַגְמ֖וֹן י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃
The elder and the man of rank are the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
זָקֵ֥ן וּנְשׂוּא־פָנִ֖ים ה֣וּא הָרֹ֑אשׁ וְנָבִ֥יא מֽוֹרֶה־שֶּׁ֖קֶר ה֥וּא הַזָּנָֽב׃
Those who guide this people lead them astray, and those who are guided are swallowed up.[^13]
וַיִּֽהְי֛וּ מְאַשְּׁרֵ֥י הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה מַתְעִ֑ים וּמְאֻשָּׁרָ֖יו מְבֻלָּעִֽים׃

That is why the Lord takes no pleasure in their young men and has no compassion on their fatherless and widows, for everyone is godless and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.

עַל־כֵּ֨ן עַל־בַּחוּרָ֜יו לֹֽא־יִשְׂמַ֣ח ׀ אֲדֹנָ֗י וְאֶת־יְתֹמָ֤יו וְאֶת־אַלְמְנֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔ם כִּ֤י כֻלּוֹ֙ חָנֵ֣ף וּמֵרַ֔ע וְכָל־פֶּ֖ה דֹּבֵ֣ר נְבָלָ֑ה בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃
For wickedness burns like a fire; it devours briers and thorns. It sets the thickets of the forest ablaze, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.
כִּֽי־בָעֲרָ֤ה כָאֵשׁ֙ רִשְׁעָ֔ה שָׁמִ֥יר וָשַׁ֖יִת תֹּאכֵ֑ל וַתִּצַּת֙ בְּסִֽבְכֵ֣י הַיַּ֔עַר וַיִּֽתְאַבְּכ֖וּ גֵּא֥וּת עָשָֽׁן׃
By the fury of Yahweh of Armies the land is scorched,[^14] and the people are like fuel for the fire. No one spares his brother.
בְּעֶבְרַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת נֶעְתַּ֣ם אָ֑רֶץ וַיְהִ֤י הָעָם֙ כְּמַאֲכֹ֣לֶת אֵ֔שׁ אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֖יו לֹ֥א יַחְמֹֽלוּ׃
They slice meat on the right but are still hungry; they eat on the left but are not satisfied. Each of them devours the flesh of his own arm.[^15]
וַיִּגְזֹ֤ר עַל־יָמִין֙ וְרָעֵ֔ב וַיֹּ֥אכַל עַל־שְׂמֹ֖אול וְלֹ֣א שָׂבֵ֑עוּ אִ֥ישׁ בְּשַׂר־זְרֹע֖וֹ יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אֶת־אֶפְרַ֗יִם וְאֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ אֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יַחְדָּ֥ו הֵ֖מָּה עַל־יְהוּדָ֑ה בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃ ס

n.1: Verses 1–20 are 9:2–21 in most English Bibles. *Deep darkness* is Hebrew *tsalmavet*, traditionally "the shadow of death" (Psalm 23:4). Matthew 4:15–16 quotes this verse with 8:23 (9:1–2 in most English Bibles).
n.2: The Hebrew text is written "you have not increased the joy" but read "you have increased its joy". The two words sound the same (*lo*).
n.3: When Gideon defeated Midian with a small band (Judges 7; Isaiah 10:26).
n.4: Hebrew *se'on*, a word found only here, probably the boot of a soldier. Literally "every boot of one who tramps with noise".
n.5: Or "has been called". The verbs in this verse are in the past tense in Hebrew: either a birth that has just happened, or the future described as if it had already taken place. Literally "and he has called his name", that is, "one has named him".
n.6: Hebrew *pele yo'ets el gibbor avi'ad sar-shalom*. Each name is made of two words: "a wonder of a counselor", "a mighty God" or "God the warrior" (*el gibbor*, used of God in 10:21), "a father forever", "a prince of peace". In the ancient Near East a king could be given throne names at his crowning. Some read the words as one long name in the form of a sentence, like the names of Isaiah's sons (7:3; 8:3), describing God who gives the child. In Jewish interpretation the child was often taken to be King Hezekiah, while the Aramaic Targum takes the first names as names of God, who names the child "the anointed one (Messiah), in whose days peace will increase". Christian tradition reads the names as titles of Jesus the Messiah. The Septuagint reads "and his name is called Messenger of Great Counsel".
n.7: Literally "to the increase of the government". The Hebrew text is written as two words, *lm rbh*, the first ending in the final form of the letter *mem*, but read as one word, *lemarbeh*, "to the increase".
n.8: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.9: *Him* is Israel. Rezin of Aram was Israel's ally (7:1), but now the enemies of both are sent against them. The Hebrew is difficult.
n.10: Literally "from in front … from behind": a person faced east to name the directions.
n.11: This refrain first appears in 5:25 and returns in verses 16 and 20 and in 10:4.
n.12: The top and bottom of society, as verse 14 explains.
n.13: A play on words: *me'ashrim*, "those who guide", and *me'ushar*, "those who are guided" (3:12).
n.14: Hebrew *ne'tam*, a word found only here. Perhaps "is burned" or "is shaken".
n.15: That is, his own kin, as verse 20 shows.

v: Woe to[^1] those who make unjust laws,[^2] and to the writers who keep writing oppression,
ה֥וֹי הַחֹֽקְקִ֖ים חִקְקֵי־אָ֑וֶן וּֽמְכַתְּבִ֥ים עָמָ֖ל כִּתֵּֽבוּ׃
to deprive the poor of justice and rob the needy among my people of their rights, so that widows become their plunder and they prey on the fatherless!
לְהַטּ֤וֹת מִדִּין֙ דַּלִּ֔ים וְלִגְזֹ֕ל מִשְׁפַּ֖ט עֲנִיֵּ֣י עַמִּ֑י לִהְי֤וֹת אַלְמָנוֹת֙ שְׁלָלָ֔ם וְאֶת־יְתוֹמִ֖ים יָבֹֽזּוּ׃
What will you do on the day of reckoning,[^3] when ruin comes from far away? To whom will you run for help, and where will you leave your wealth?[^4]
וּמַֽה־תַּעֲשׂוּ֙ לְי֣וֹם פְּקֻדָּ֔ה וּלְשׁוֹאָ֖ה מִמֶּרְחָ֣ק תָּב֑וֹא עַל־מִי֙ תָּנ֣וּסוּ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה וְאָ֥נָה תַעַזְב֖וּ כְּבוֹדְכֶֽם׃
Nothing will be left but to crouch among the prisoners or to fall among the slain. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.[^5]
בִּלְתִּ֤י כָרַע֙ תַּ֣חַת אַסִּ֔יר וְתַ֥חַת הֲרוּגִ֖ים יִפֹּ֑לוּ בְּכָל־זֹאת֙ לֹא־שָׁ֣ב אַפּ֔וֹ וְע֖וֹד יָד֥וֹ נְטוּיָֽה׃ ס
Woe to Assyria, the rod of my anger! The club in their hand is my fury.
ה֥וֹי אַשּׁ֖וּר שֵׁ֣בֶט אַפִּ֑י וּמַטֶּה־ה֥וּא בְיָדָ֖ם זַעְמִֽי׃
I send him against a godless nation; I command him to go against the people who provoke my wrath,[^6] to take spoil and seize plunder, and to trample them like mud in the streets.
בְּג֤וֹי חָנֵף֙ אֲשַׁלְּחֶ֔נּוּ וְעַל־עַ֥ם עֶבְרָתִ֖י אֲצַוֶּ֑נּוּ לִשְׁלֹ֤ל שָׁלָל֙ וְלָבֹ֣ז בַּ֔ז *ולשימו **וּלְשׂוּמ֥וֹ מִרְמָ֖ס כְּחֹ֥מֶר חוּצֽוֹת׃
But this is not what he intends; this is not what he has in mind. His purpose is to destroy, to cut off nations, and not a few.
וְהוּא֙ לֹא־כֵ֣ן יְדַמֶּ֔ה וּלְבָב֖וֹ לֹא־כֵ֣ן יַחְשֹׁ֑ב כִּ֚י לְהַשְׁמִ֣יד בִּלְבָב֔וֹ וּלְהַכְרִ֥ית גּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א מְעָֽט׃
For he says, "Are not my commanders all kings?
כִּ֖י יֹאמַ֑ר הֲלֹ֥א שָׂרַ֛י יַחְדָּ֖ו מְלָכִֽים׃
Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?[^7]
הֲלֹ֥א כְּכַרְכְּמִ֖ישׁ כַּלְנ֑וֹ אִם־לֹ֤א כְאַרְפַּד֙ חֲמָ֔ת אִם־לֹ֥א כְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
As my hand has reached the kingdoms of the idols,[^8] whose images were greater than those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ מָצְאָ֣ה יָדִ֔י לְמַמְלְכֹ֖ת הָאֱלִ֑יל וּפְסִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם מִירֽוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם וּמִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן׃
shall I not do to Jerusalem and her images as I have done to Samaria and her idols?"
הֲלֹ֗א כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֛יתִי לְשֹׁמְר֖וֹן וְלֶאֱלִילֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה לִירוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם וְלַעֲצַבֶּֽיהָ׃ ס
When the Lord has finished all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the king of Assyria's proud heart and the haughty look in his eyes.[^9]
וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יְבַצַּ֤ע אֲדֹנָי֙ אֶת־כָּל־מֽ͏ַעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ בְּהַ֥ר צִיּ֖וֹן וּבִירוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם אֶפְקֹ֗ד עַל־פְּרִי־גֹ֙דֶל֙ לְבַ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֔וּר וְעַל־תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת ר֥וּם עֵינָֽיו׃

For he says: "By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I have understanding. I have removed the boundaries of peoples and plundered their treasures; like a mighty one I have brought down those who sat on thrones.[^10]
כִּ֣י אָמַ֗ר בְּכֹ֤חַ יָדִי֙ עָשִׂ֔יתִי וּבְחָכְמָתִ֖י כִּ֣י נְבֻנ֑וֹתִי וְאָסִ֣יר ׀ גְּבוּלֹ֣ת עַמִּ֗ים *ועתידתיהם **וַעֲתוּדֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ שׁוֹשֵׂ֔תִי וְאוֹרִ֥יד כַּאבִּ֖יר יוֹשְׁבִֽים׃
My hand has found the wealth of the peoples like a nest, and as one gathers abandoned eggs, I have gathered all the earth. Not one flapped a wing or opened its mouth to chirp."
וַתִּמְצָ֨א כַקֵּ֤ן ׀ יָדִי֙ לְחֵ֣יל הָֽעַמִּ֔ים וְכֶאֱסֹף֙ בֵּיצִ֣ים עֲזֻב֔וֹת כָּל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲנִ֣י אָסָ֑פְתִּי וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ נֹדֵ֣ד כָּנָ֔ף וּפֹצֶ֥ה פֶ֖ה וּמְצַפְצֵֽף׃

Does the ax boast over the one who chops with it? Does the saw make itself greater than the one who saws with it? As if a rod could wield the one who lifts it, or a staff could lift the one who is not wood!
הֲיִתְפָּאֵר֙ הַגַּרְזֶ֔ן עַ֖ל הַחֹצֵ֣ב בּ֑וֹ אִם־יִתְגַּדֵּ֤ל הַמַּשּׂוֹר֙ עַל־מְנִיפ֔וֹ כְּהָנִ֥יף שֵׁ֙בֶט֙ וְאֶת־מְרִימָ֔יו כְּהָרִ֥ים מַטֶּ֖ה לֹא־עֵֽץ׃
Therefore the Lord[^11] Yahweh of Armies[^12] will send a wasting disease among his stout warriors, and under his glory a fire will be kindled, burning like a fire.
לָ֠כֵן יְשַׁלַּ֨ח הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּמִשְׁמַנָּ֖יו רָז֑וֹן וְתַ֧חַת כְּבֹד֛וֹ יֵקַ֥ד יְקֹ֖ד כִּיק֥וֹד אֵֽשׁ׃
The light of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One a flame. It will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in a single day.
וְהָיָ֤ה אֽוֹר־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְאֵ֔שׁ וּקְדוֹשׁ֖וֹ לְלֶהָבָ֑ה וּבָעֲרָ֗ה וְאָֽכְלָ֛ה שִׁית֥וֹ וּשְׁמִיר֖וֹ בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃
The glory of his forest and his fruitful land[^13] it will destroy, both soul and body,[^14] and it will be as when a sick man wastes away.[^15]
וּכְב֤וֹד יַעְרוֹ֙ וְכַרְמִלּ֔וֹ מִנֶּ֥פֶשׁ וְעַד־בָּשָׂ֖ר יְכַלֶּ֑ה וְהָיָ֖ה כִּמְסֹ֥ס נֹסֵֽס׃
The trees left in his forest will be so few that a child could write them down.
וּשְׁאָ֥ר עֵ֛ץ יַעְר֖וֹ מִסְפָּ֣ר יִֽהְי֑וּ וְנַ֖עַר יִכְתְּבֵֽם׃ פ
On that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer lean on the one who struck them, but will truly lean on Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel.
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא לֹֽא־יוֹסִ֨יף ע֜וֹד שְׁאָ֤ר יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפְלֵיטַ֣ת בֵּֽית־יַעֲקֹ֔ב לְהִשָּׁעֵ֖ן עַל־מַכֵּ֑הוּ וְנִשְׁעַ֗ן עַל־יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּאֱמֶֽת׃
A remnant will return,[^16] the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.[^17]
שְׁאָ֥ר יָשׁ֖וּב שְׁאָ֣ר יַעֲקֹ֑ב אֶל־אֵ֖ל גִּבּֽוֹר׃
For even if your people, Israel, were like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. Destruction has been decreed, overflowing with righteousness.[^18]
כִּ֣י אִם־יִהְיֶ֞ה עַמְּךָ֤ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כְּח֣וֹל הַיָּ֔ם שְׁאָ֖ר יָשׁ֣וּב בּ֑וֹ כִּלָּי֥וֹן חָר֖וּץ שׁוֹטֵ֥ף צְדָקָֽה׃
For the Lord Yahweh of Armies will carry out the destruction he has decreed in the middle of all the earth.[^19]
כִּ֥י כָלָ֖ה וְנֶחֱרָצָ֑ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת עֹשֶׂ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃ ס
Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh of Armies says: My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of Assyria, though he strikes you with a rod and lifts up his staff against you, as Egypt did.[^20]
לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ צְבָא֔וֹת אַל־תִּירָ֥א עַמִּ֛י יֹשֵׁ֥ב צִיּ֖וֹן מֵֽאַשּׁ֑וּר בַּשֵּׁ֣בֶט יַכֶּ֔כָּה וּמַטֵּ֥הוּ יִשָּֽׂא־עָלֶ֖יךָ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
For in a very little while my fury will come to an end, and my anger will turn to their destruction.
כִּי־ע֖וֹד מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֑ר וְכָ֣לָה זַ֔עַם וְאַפִּ֖י עַל־תַּבְלִיתָֽם׃
Yahweh of Armies will raise a whip against him, as when he struck Midian at the rock of Oreb.[^21] His staff will be over the sea, and he will lift it up as he did in Egypt.[^22]
וְעוֹרֵ֨ר עָלָ֜יו יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ שׁ֔וֹט כְּמַכַּ֥ת מִדְיָ֖ן בְּצ֣וּר עוֹרֵ֑ב וּמַטֵּ֙הוּ֙ עַל־הַיָּ֔ם וּנְשָׂא֖וֹ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
On that day his burden will be lifted from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke will be broken because of fatness.[^23]
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יָס֤וּר סֻבֳּלוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל שִׁכְמֶ֔ךָ וְעֻלּ֖וֹ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֑ךָ וְחֻבַּ֥ל עֹ֖ל מִפְּנֵי־שָֽׁמֶן׃
He has come to Aiath; he has passed through Migron; at Michmash he leaves his baggage.[^24]
בָּ֥א עַל־עַיַּ֖ת עָבַ֣ר בְּמִגְר֑וֹן לְמִכְמָ֖שׂ יַפְקִ֥יד כֵּלָֽיו׃
They have crossed the pass: "Geba is our camp for the night!" Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
עָֽבְרוּ֙ מַעְבָּרָ֔ה גֶּ֖בַע מָל֣וֹן לָ֑נוּ חָֽרְדָה֙ הָֽרָמָ֔ה גִּבְעַ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל נָֽסָה׃
Cry aloud, Daughter Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth![^25]
צַהֲלִ֥י קוֹלֵ֖ךְ בַּת־גַּלִּ֑ים הַקְשִׁ֥יבִי לַ֖יְשָׁה עֲנִיָּ֥ה עֲנָתֽוֹת׃
Madmenah is in flight; the people of Gebim take refuge.
נָדְדָ֖ה מַדְמֵנָ֑ה יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הַגֵּבִ֖ים הֵעִֽיזוּ׃
This very day he will halt at Nob. He shakes his fist at the mount of Daughter Zion,[^26] the hill of Jerusalem.
ע֥וֹד הַיּ֖וֹם בְּנֹ֣ב לַֽעֲמֹ֑ד יְנֹפֵ֤ף יָדוֹ֙ הַ֣ר *בית־**בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן גִּבְעַ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ ס
Look, the Lord Yahweh of Armies will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The tallest trees will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.
הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת מְסָעֵ֥ף פֻּארָ֖ה בְּמַעֲרָצָ֑ה וְרָמֵ֤י הַקּוֹמָה֙ גְּדוּעִ֔ים וְהַגְּבֹהִ֖ים יִשְׁפָּֽלוּ׃
He will cut down the thickets of the forest with an ax,[^27] and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.[^28]
וְנִקַּ֛ף סִֽבְכֵ֥י הַיַּ֖עַר בַּבַּרְזֶ֑ל וְהַלְּבָנ֖וֹן בְּאַדִּ֥יר יִפּֽוֹל׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning, used by the prophets to announce disaster (see 1:4). Also in verse 5.
n.2: Literally "who decree decrees of wickedness".
n.3: Literally "the day of visitation", when God comes to call to account.
n.4: Literally "your glory".
n.5: The refrain of 5:25 and 9:11, 16 and 20 (9:12, 17 and 21 in most English Bibles).
n.6: Literally "the people of my fury".
n.7: Cities of Syria and northern Mesopotamia that Assyria conquered in the eighth century BC. Samaria fell in 722 BC.
n.8: Hebrew *elil*, "worthless thing" (see 2:8). Also in verse 11.
n.9: Yahweh speaks of himself as *the Lord* and then as *I*.
n.10: Or "I have brought down the inhabitants". Hebrew *yoshevim* means both "those who sit" and "those who live".
n.11: Hebrew *ha-adon*, "the Lord", a title, not the name Yahweh. Also in verse 33. "The Lord" in verses 12, 23 and 24 is *Adonai*.
n.12: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.13: Hebrew *karmel*, "garden land, orchard".
n.14: Literally "from *nephesh* to flesh", that is, completely.
n.15: Hebrew *kimsos noses*, words found only here. Perhaps "as a standard-bearer faints".
n.16: Hebrew *she'ar yashuv*, the name of Isaiah's son Shear-jashub (7:3). *Return* can also mean "turn back" to God.
n.17: Hebrew *el gibbor*, the title given to the child in 9:5 (9:6 in most English Bibles).
n.18: Romans 9:27–28 quotes verses 22–23 from the Septuagint.
n.19: Or "of all the land".
n.20: Literally "in the way of Egypt", as Egypt oppressed Israel before the exodus.
n.21: Where the Midianite leader Oreb was killed (Judges 7:25).
n.22: As Moses' staff was raised over the Red Sea (Exodus 14:16).
n.23: Or "because of the oil". The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain: perhaps the ox has grown too fat for the yoke.
