n.24: Verses 28–32 trace an enemy army marching on Jerusalem from the north. The towns all lie within about 10 miles (16 km) of the city.
n.25: A play on words: *aniyyah anatot*, "poor Anathoth". *Gallim* sounds like "waves", and *Laishah* like "lion".
n.26: The Hebrew text is written "the house of Zion" but read "Daughter Zion".
n.28: Or "by a mighty one". *Lebanon*, with its great cedars, stands for the proud army of Assyria.

v: A shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse,[^1] and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.[^2]
וְיָצָ֥א חֹ֖טֶר מִגֵּ֣זַע יִשָׁ֑י וְנֵ֖צֶר מִשָּׁרָשָׁ֥יו יִפְרֶֽה׃
The Spirit of Yahweh[^3] will rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.[^4]
וְנָחָ֥ה עָלָ֖יו ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֑ה ר֧וּחַ חָכְמָ֣ה וּבִינָ֗ה ר֤וּחַ עֵצָה֙ וּגְבוּרָ֔ה ר֥וּחַ דַּ֖עַת וְיִרְאַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃
His delight will be in the fear of Yahweh.[^5] He will not judge by what his eyes see, or decide by what his ears hear.
וַהֲרִיח֖וֹ בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־לְמַרְאֵ֤ה עֵינָיו֙ יִשְׁפּ֔וֹט וְלֹֽא־לְמִשְׁמַ֥ע אָזְנָ֖יו יוֹכִֽיחַ׃

He will judge the poor with righteousness and decide with fairness for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will put the wicked to death.[^6]
וְשָׁפַ֤ט בְּצֶ֙דֶק֙ דַּלִּ֔ים וְהוֹכִ֥יחַ בְּמִישׁ֖וֹר לְעַנְוֵי־אָ֑רֶץ וְהִֽכָּה־אֶ֙רֶץ֙ בְּשֵׁ֣בֶט פִּ֔יו וּבְר֥וּחַ שְׂפָתָ֖יו יָמִ֥ית רָשָֽׁע׃
Righteousness will be the belt around his waist, and faithfulness the belt around his hips.
וְהָ֥יָה צֶ֖דֶק אֵז֣וֹר מָתְנָ֑יו וְהָאֱמוּנָ֖ה אֵז֥וֹר חֲלָצָֽיו׃
The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat. The calf and the young lion and the fattened calf will be together, and a little child will lead them.
וְגָ֤ר זְאֵב֙ עִם־כֶּ֔בֶשׂ וְנָמֵ֖ר עִם־גְּדִ֣י יִרְבָּ֑ץ וְעֵ֨גֶל וּכְפִ֤יר וּמְרִיא֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו וְנַ֥עַר קָטֹ֖ן נֹהֵ֥ג בָּֽם׃
The cow and the bear will graze; their young will lie down together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox.
וּפָרָ֤ה וָדֹב֙ תִּרְעֶ֔ינָה יַחְדָּ֖ו יִרְבְּצ֣וּ יַלְדֵיהֶ֑ן וְאַרְיֵ֖ה כַּבָּקָ֥ר יֹֽאכַל־תֶּֽבֶן׃
The nursing child will play over the hole of the cobra, and the weaned child will put his hand into the viper's den.
וְשִֽׁעֲשַׁ֥ע יוֹנֵ֖ק עַל־חֻ֣ר פָּ֑תֶן וְעַל֙ מְאוּרַ֣ת צִפְעוֹנִ֔י גָּמ֖וּל יָד֥וֹ הָדָֽה׃
They will not harm or destroy on all my holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea.[^7]
לֹֽא־יָרֵ֥עוּ וְלֹֽא־יַשְׁחִ֖יתוּ בְּכָל־הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֑י כִּֽי־מָלְאָ֣ה הָאָ֗רֶץ דֵּעָה֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה כַּמַּ֖יִם לַיָּ֥ם מְכַסִּֽים׃ פ
On that day the root of Jesse will stand as a signal for the peoples. The nations will seek him, and his resting place will be glorious.[^8]
וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ יִשַׁ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֹמֵד֙ לְנֵ֣ס עַמִּ֔ים אֵלָ֖יו גּוֹיִ֣ם יִדְרֹ֑שׁוּ וְהָיְתָ֥ה מְנֻחָת֖וֹ כָּבֽוֹד׃ פ

On that day the Lord will reach out his hand a second time to reclaim the remnant of his people that is left, from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath and from the coastlands of the sea.[^9]

וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י ׀ שֵׁנִית֙ יָד֔וֹ לִקְנ֖וֹת אֶת־שְׁאָ֣ר עַמּ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִשָּׁאֵר֩ מֵאַשּׁ֨וּר וּמִמִּצְרַ֜יִם וּמִפַּתְר֣וֹס וּמִכּ֗וּשׁ וּמֵעֵילָ֤ם וּמִשִּׁנְעָר֙ וּמֵ֣חֲמָ֔ת וּמֵאִיֵּ֖י הַיָּֽם׃
He will raise a signal flag for the nations and gather the outcasts of Israel; he will bring together the scattered people of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
וְנָשָׂ֥א נֵס֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְאָסַ֖ף נִדְחֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּנְפֻצ֤וֹת יְהוּדָה֙ יְקַבֵּ֔ץ מֵאַרְבַּ֖ע כַּנְפ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
The jealousy of Ephraim will depart, and the adversaries of Judah will be cut off. Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah, and Judah will not be hostile to Ephraim.[^10]
וְסָ֙רָה֙ קִנְאַ֣ת אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְצֹרְרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יִכָּרֵ֑תוּ אֶפְרַ֙יִ[t]ם֙ לֹֽא־יְקַנֵּ֣א אֶת־יְהוּדָ֔ה וִֽיהוּדָ֖ה לֹֽא־יָצֹ֥ר אֶת־אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

They will swoop down on the slopes of the Philistines to the west;[^11] together they will plunder the people of the east. They will lay their hands on Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will obey them.
וְעָפ֨וּ בְכָתֵ֤ף פְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ יָ֔מָּה יַחְדָּ֖ו יָבֹ֣זּוּ אֶת־בְּנֵי־קֶ֑דֶם אֱד֤וֹם וּמוֹאָב֙ מִשְׁל֣וֹח יָדָ֔ם וּבְנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן מִשְׁמַעְתָּֽם׃

Yahweh will utterly destroy[^12] the gulf of the Sea of Egypt.[^13] With his scorching wind[^14] he will wave his hand over the River[^15] and split it into seven streams, so that people can cross it in sandals.
וְהֶחֱרִ֣ים יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֚ת לְשׁ֣וֹן יָם־מִצְרַ֔יִם וְהֵנִ֥יף יָד֛וֹ עַל־הַנָּהָ֖ר בַּעְיָ֣ם רוּח֑וֹ וְהִכָּ֙הוּ֙ לְשִׁבְעָ֣ה נְחָלִ֔ים וְהִדְרִ֖יךְ בַּנְּעָלִֽים׃
There will be a highway for the remnant of his people that is left from Assyria, as there was for Israel on the day they came up from the land of Egypt.
וְהָיְתָ֣ה מְסִלָּ֔ה לִשְׁאָ֣ר עַמּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִשָּׁאֵ֖ר מֵֽאַשּׁ֑וּר כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר הָֽיְתָה֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּי֥וֹם עֲלֹת֖וֹ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

n.1: Jesse was the father of King David (1 Samuel 16). The *stump* suggests a family tree that has been cut down (compare 6:13; 10:33–34).
n.2: Hebrew *netser*, "branch, shoot". Matthew 2:23, "He will be called a Nazarene", is often thought to echo this word. Both Jewish and Christian interpreters have read verses 1–10 of the Messiah: the Aramaic Targum begins "A king will come out from the sons of Jesse, and the anointed one (Messiah) will grow up from his sons' sons". The Septuagint reads "and a flower will come up from the root".
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: Or "the Spirit of wisdom … the Spirit of counsel … the Spirit of knowledge". Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, wind, breath". The Septuagint translates "the fear of Yahweh" here as "godliness", and "the fear of Yahweh" in verse 3 as "the fear of God", so that it lists seven qualities. This became the basis of the traditional "seven gifts of the Holy Spirit".
n.5: Literally "his smelling", that is, his enjoyment, as of a pleasing fragrance.
n.6: Or "the spirit of his lips". Hebrew *ruach*. 2 Thessalonians 2:8 echoes this line.
n.7: Habakkuk 2:14 repeats the second half of this verse, and Isaiah 65:25 repeats parts of verses 6–9.
n.8: Literally "his resting place will be glory". Romans 15:12 quotes this verse from the Septuagint: "The root of Jesse will come, the one who rises to rule the nations; in him the nations will hope."
n.9: *Pathros* is southern (Upper) Egypt; *Cush*, the region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia); *Elam*, a kingdom east of Babylonia, in what is now southwestern Iran; *Shinar*, Babylonia; *Hamath*, a city in Syria; *the coastlands* are the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean.
n.10: *Ephraim*, the northern kingdom, and *Judah*, the southern kingdom, had been enemies since they divided (7:17).
n.11: Literally "on the shoulder of the Philistines", the low hills toward the coast.
n.12: Hebrew *hecherim*, "devote to destruction".
n.13: Literally "the tongue of the Sea of Egypt", probably the Gulf of Suez on the Red Sea.
n.14: Hebrew *ba'yam*, a word found only here. Perhaps "scorching" or "mighty". Or "With the might of his breath".
n.15: The Euphrates.

v: On that day you will say,[^1] "I will praise you, Yahweh.[^2] Though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away, and you comfort me.[^3]
וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אוֹדְךָ֣ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אָנַ֖פְתָּ בִּ֑י יָשֹׁ֥ב אַפְּךָ֖ וּֽתְנַחֲמֵֽנִי׃
Look, God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For Yah, Yahweh, is my strength and my song;[^4] he has become my salvation."
הִנֵּ֨ה אֵ֧ל יְשׁוּעָתִ֛י אֶבְטַ֖ח וְלֹ֣א אֶפְחָ֑ד כִּֽי־עָזִּ֤י וְזִמְרָת֙ יָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיְהִי־לִ֖י לִֽישׁוּעָֽה׃
With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.[^5]
וּשְׁאַבְתֶּם־מַ֖יִם בְּשָׂשׂ֑וֹן מִמַּעַיְנֵ֖י הַיְשׁוּעָֽה׃
On that day you will say, "Give thanks to Yahweh; call on his name. Make known his deeds among the peoples; declare that his name is exalted.
וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֞ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא הוֹד֤וּ לַֽיהוָה֙ קִרְא֣וּ בִשְׁמ֔וֹ הוֹדִ֥יעוּ בָֽעַמִּ֖ים עֲלִֽילֹתָ֑יו הַזְכִּ֕ירוּ כִּ֥י נִשְׂגָּ֖ב שְׁמֽוֹ׃
Sing praises to Yahweh, for he has done glorious things; let this be known in all the earth.
זַמְּר֣וּ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י גֵא֖וּת עָשָׂ֑ה *מידעת **מוּדַ֥עַת זֹ֖את בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Shout aloud and sing for joy, you who live in Zion,[^6] for great among you is the Holy One of Israel."
צַהֲלִ֥י וָרֹ֖נִּי יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת צִיּ֑וֹן כִּֽי־גָד֥וֹל בְּקִרְבֵּ֖ךְ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ פ

n.1: *You* is singular in verse 1, and plural in verses 3–4: first one voice, then the whole people.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: Or "may your anger turn away, and may you comfort me".
n.4: Hebrew *Yah YHWH*. *Yah* is a short form of the name Yahweh. The line repeats Exodus 15:2 and Psalm 118:14. *My song* may also mean "my might".
n.5: Or "wells".
n.6: Literally "you inhabitant of Zion", feminine singular: Zion's people are addressed as a woman.

v: An oracle[^1] concerning Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
מַשָּׂ֖א בָּבֶ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אָמֽוֹץ׃
On a bare hill raise a signal flag! Shout to them; wave your hand for them to enter the gates of the nobles.
עַ֤ל הַר־נִשְׁפֶּה֙ שְֽׂאוּ־נֵ֔ס הָרִ֥ימוּ ק֖וֹל לָהֶ֑ם הָנִ֣יפוּ יָ֔ד וְיָבֹ֖אוּ פִּתְחֵ֥י נְדִיבִֽים׃
I myself have given orders to my consecrated ones;[^2] I have summoned my warriors to carry out my anger, those who exult in my triumph.[^3]
אֲנִ֥י צִוֵּ֖יתִי לִמְקֻדָּשָׁ֑י גַּ֣ם קָרָ֤אתִי גִבּוֹרַי֙ לְאַפִּ֔י עַלִּיזֵ֖י גַּאֲוָתִֽי׃
Listen! A tumult on the mountains, like that of a great people! Listen! An uproar of kingdoms, of nations gathering! Yahweh of Armies[^4] is mustering an army for battle.
ק֥וֹל הָמ֛וֹן בֶּֽהָרִ֖ים דְּמ֣וּת עַם־רָ֑ב ק֠וֹל שְׁא֞וֹן מַמְלְכ֤וֹת גּוֹיִם֙ נֶֽאֱסָפִ֔ים יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת מְפַקֵּ֖ד צְבָ֥א מִלְחָמָֽה׃
They come from a distant land, from the ends of the heavens, Yahweh and the weapons of his wrath, to destroy the whole earth.[^5]
בָּאִ֛ים מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָ֖ק מִקְצֵ֣ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם יְהוָה֙ וּכְלֵ֣י זַעְמ֔וֹ לְחַבֵּ֖ל כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Wail, for the day of Yahweh is near! It comes like destruction from the Almighty.[^6]
הֵילִ֕ילוּ כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב י֣וֹם יְהוָ֑ה כְּשֹׁ֖ד מִשַׁדַּ֥י יָבֽוֹא׃
Therefore all hands will go limp, and every human heart will melt.
עַל־כֵּ֖ן כָּל־יָדַ֣יִם תִּרְפֶּ֑ינָה וְכָל־לְבַ֥ב אֱנ֖וֹשׁ יִמָּס׃
They will be terrified. Pains and pangs will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor. They will look at one another in horror, their faces aflame.
וְֽנִבְהָ֓לוּ ׀ צִירִ֤ים וַֽחֲבָלִים֙ יֹֽאחֵז֔וּן כַּיּוֹלֵדָ֖ה יְחִיל֑וּן אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ יִתְמָ֔הוּ פְּנֵ֥י לְהָבִ֖ים פְּנֵיהֶֽם׃
Look, the day of Yahweh is coming, cruel, with fury and burning anger, to make the earth a desolation and to destroy its sinners from it.
הִנֵּ֤ה יוֹם־יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔א אַכְזָרִ֥י וְעֶבְרָ֖ה וַחֲר֣וֹן אָ֑ף לָשׂ֤וּם הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְחַטָּאֶ֖יהָ יַשְׁמִ֥יד מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
For the stars of the heavens and their constellations[^7] will not give their light. The sun will be dark when it rises, and the moon will not shed its light.[^8]
כִּֽי־כוֹכְבֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וּכְסִ֣ילֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א יָהֵ֖לּוּ אוֹרָ֑ם חָשַׁ֤ךְ הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ בְּצֵאת֔וֹ וְיָרֵ֖חַ לֹֽא־יַגִּ֥יהַ אוֹרֽוֹ׃
I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their guilt. I will put an end to the pride of the arrogant and bring low the haughtiness of tyrants.
וּפָקַדְתִּ֤י עַל־תֵּבֵל֙ רָעָ֔ה וְעַל־רְשָׁעִ֖ים עֲוֺנָ֑ם וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי֙ גְּא֣וֹן זֵדִ֔ים וְגַאֲוַ֥ת עָרִיצִ֖ים אַשְׁפִּֽיל׃
I will make human beings scarcer than fine gold, humankind scarcer than the gold of Ophir.[^9]
אוֹקִ֥יר אֱנ֖וֹשׁ מִפָּ֑ז וְאָדָ֖ם מִכֶּ֥תֶם אוֹפִֽיר׃
Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken from its place at the fury of Yahweh of Armies, on the day of his burning anger.
עַל־כֵּן֙ שָׁמַ֣יִם אַרְגִּ֔יז וְתִרְעַ֥שׁ הָאָ֖רֶץ מִמְּקוֹמָ֑הּ בְּעֶבְרַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּבְי֖וֹם חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃
Like a hunted gazelle, like sheep with no one to gather them, each will turn to his own people, each will flee to his own land.
וְהָיָה֙ כִּצְבִ֣י מֻדָּ֔ח וּכְצֹ֖אן וְאֵ֣ין מְקַבֵּ֑ץ אִ֤ישׁ אֶל־עַמּוֹ֙ יִפְנ֔וּ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶל־אַרְצ֖וֹ יָנֽוּסוּ׃
Whoever is found will be stabbed, and whoever is caught will fall by the sword.
כָּל־הַנִּמְצָ֖א יִדָּקֵ֑ר וְכָל־הַנִּסְפֶּ֖ה יִפּ֥וֹל בֶּחָֽרֶב׃
Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses will be plundered, and their wives raped.[^10]
וְעֹלְלֵיהֶ֥ם יְרֻטְּשׁ֖וּ לְעֵֽינֵיהֶ֑ם יִשַּׁ֙סּוּ֙ בָּֽתֵּיהֶ֔ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם *תשגלנה **תִּשָּׁכַֽבְנָה׃
Look, I am stirring up the Medes[^11] against them, who have no regard for silver and take no delight in gold.
הִנְנִ֛י מֵעִ֥יר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֶת־מָדָ֑י אֲשֶׁר־כֶּ֙סֶף֙ לֹ֣א יַחְשֹׁ֔בוּ וְזָהָ֖ב לֹ֥א יַחְפְּצוּ־בֽוֹ׃
Their bows will cut down the young men. They will have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eyes will not spare children.
וּקְשָׁת֖וֹת נְעָרִ֣ים תְּרַטַּ֑שְׁנָה וּפְרִי־בֶ֙טֶן֙ לֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ עַל־בָּנִ֖ים לֹֽא־תָח֥וּס עֵינָֽם׃
Babylon, the jewel of kingdoms, the glory and pride of the Chaldeans,[^12] will be like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them.
וְהָיְתָ֤ה בָבֶל֙ צְבִ֣י מַמְלָכ֔וֹת תִּפְאֶ֖רֶת גְּא֣וֹן כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֣ת אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־סְדֹ֖ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָֽה׃
It will never be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation. No Arab will pitch his tent there, and no shepherds will rest their flocks there.
לֹֽא־תֵשֵׁ֣ב לָנֶ֔צַח וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁכֹּ֖ן עַד־דּ֣וֹר וָד֑וֹר וְלֹֽא־יַהֵ֥ל שָׁם֙ עֲרָבִ֔י וְרֹעִ֖ים לֹא־יַרְבִּ֥צוּ שָֽׁם׃
But desert creatures will lie down there, and its houses will be full of howling creatures. Ostriches will live there, and wild goats will dance there.[^13]
וְרָבְצוּ־שָׁ֣ם צִיִּ֔ים וּמָלְא֥וּ בָתֵּיהֶ֖ם אֹחִ֑ים וְשָׁ֤כְנוּ שָׁם֙ בְּנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֔ה וּשְׂעִירִ֖ים יְרַקְּדוּ־שָֽׁם׃
Hyenas will howl in its fortresses,[^14] and jackals in its luxurious palaces. Its time is near, and its days will not be prolonged.
וְעָנָ֤ה אִיִּים֙ בְּאַלְמנוֹתָ֔יו וְתַנִּ֖ים בְּהֵ֣יכְלֵי עֹ֑נֶג וְקָר֤וֹב לָבוֹא֙ עִתָּ֔הּ וְיָמֶ֖יהָ לֹ֥א יִמָּשֵֽׁכוּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *massa*, from the verb "to lift up, carry": a message "lifted up" by the prophet, or a "burden" laid on a nation. Traditionally "the burden of Babylon". The word heads most of the oracles against the nations in chapters 13–23, and is translated "oracle" throughout.
n.2: Soldiers set apart for a holy war.
n.3: Or "my proudly exulting ones".
n.4: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Here Yahweh of Armies musters an army (*tseva*).
n.5: Or "the whole land".
n.6: A play on words: *shod*, "destruction", and *Shaddai*, "the Almighty", a title of God whose meaning is uncertain. The same line is found in Joel 1:15.
n.7: Hebrew *kesilim*, plural of *kesil*, the constellation Orion.
n.8: Compare Mark 13:24–25.
n.9: A land famous for its gold, perhaps in southern Arabia or East Africa (1 Kings 9:28).
n.10: The Hebrew text is written with a coarse word for sexual violation but read with a milder one, "lain with".
n.11: A people of what is now northwestern Iran. With the Persians they conquered Babylon in 539 BC.
n.12: The people of southern Babylonia, whose kings ruled the Babylonian empire.
n.13: Several of the animals in verses 21–22 cannot be identified with certainty. *Wild goats* (Hebrew *se'irim*, "hairy ones") may be goat-demons thought to haunt ruins (34:14; Leviticus 17:7).
n.14: Hebrew *almenotav*, literally "its widows", probably a form of *armenotav*, "its fortresses".

v: Yahweh[^1] will have compassion on Jacob and will again choose Israel and settle them in their own land. Foreigners will join them and attach themselves to the house of Jacob.
כִּי֩ יְרַחֵ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֗ב וּבָחַ֥ר עוֹד֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהִנִּיחָ֖ם עַל־אַדְמָתָ֑ם וְנִלְוָ֤ה הַגֵּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנִסְפְּח֖וּ עַל־בֵּ֥ית יַעֲקֹֽב׃

Peoples will take them and bring them to their own place, and the house of Israel will possess them as male and female servants in Yahweh's land. They will take captive those who took them captive, and rule over those who oppressed them.
וּלְקָח֣וּם עַמִּים֮ וֶהֱבִיא֣וּם אֶל־מְקוֹמָם֒ וְהִֽתְנַחֲל֣וּם בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַ֚ל אַדְמַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְלִשְׁפָח֑וֹת וְהָיוּ֙ שֹׁבִ֣ים לְשֹֽׁבֵיהֶ֔ם וְרָד֖וּ בְּנֹגְשֵׂיהֶֽם׃ ס
On the day Yahweh gives you rest from your pain and turmoil and from the hard labor forced on you,
וְהָיָ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם הָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ לְךָ֔ מֵֽעָצְבְּךָ֖ וּמֵרָגְזֶ֑ךָ וּמִן־הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַקָּשָׁ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֻבַּד־בָּֽךְ׃
you will take up this taunt[^2] against the king of Babylon: "How the oppressor has come to an end! How his fury has ended![^3]
וְנָשָׂ֜אתָ הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה עַל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְאָמָ֑רְתָּ אֵ֚יךְ שָׁבַ֣ת נֹגֵ֔שׂ שָׁבְתָ֖ה מַדְהֵבָֽה׃
Yahweh has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of rulers,
שָׁבַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה מַטֵּ֣ה רְשָׁעִ֑ים שֵׁ֖בֶט מֹשְׁלִֽים׃
that struck peoples in fury with blows that never stopped, that ruled nations in anger with relentless persecution.
מַכֶּ֤ה עַמִּים֙ בְּעֶבְרָ֔ה מַכַּ֖ת בִּלְתִּ֣י סָרָ֑ה רֹדֶ֤ה בָאַף֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם מֻרְדָּ֖ף בְּלִ֥י חָשָֽׂךְ׃
The whole earth is at rest and at peace; they break into song.
נָ֥חָה שָׁקְטָ֖ה כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ פָּצְח֖וּ רִנָּֽה׃
Even the junipers[^4] and the cedars of Lebanon rejoice over you: 'Since you were laid low, no woodcutter comes up against us.'
גַּם־בְּרוֹשִׁ֛ים שָׂמְח֥וּ לְךָ֖ אַרְזֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן מֵאָ֣ז שָׁכַ֔בְתָּ לֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֥ה הַכֹּרֵ֖ת עָלֵֽינוּ׃
Sheol[^5] below is stirred up to meet you when you come. It rouses the shades[^6] to greet you, all who were leaders[^7] of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
שְׁא֗וֹל מִתַּ֛חַת רָגְזָ֥ה לְךָ֖ לִקְרַ֣את בּוֹאֶ֑ךָ עוֹרֵ֨ר לְךָ֤ רְפָאִים֙ כָּל־עַתּ֣וּדֵי אָ֔רֶץ הֵקִים֙ מִכִּסְ[t]אוֹתָ֔ם כֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִֽם׃
All of them answer and say to you: 'You too have become as weak as we are! You have become like us!'
כֻּלָּ֣ם יַֽעֲנ֔וּ וְיֹאמְר֖וּ אֵלֶ֑יךָ גַּם־אַתָּ֛ה חֻלֵּ֥יתָ כָמ֖וֹנוּ אֵלֵ֥ינוּ נִמְשָֽׁלְתָּ׃
Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, with the music of your harps. Maggots are spread out as your bed, and worms are your covering.
הוּרַ֥ד שְׁא֛וֹל גְּאוֹנֶ֖ךָ הֶמְיַ֣ת נְבָלֶ֑יךָ תַּחְתֶּ֙יךָ֙ יֻצַּ֣ע רִמָּ֔ה וּמְכַסֶּ֖יךָ תּוֹלֵעָֽה׃
How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of the dawn![^8] How you have been cut down to the ground, you who laid the nations low!
אֵ֛יךְ נָפַ֥לְתָּ מִשָּׁמַ֖יִם הֵילֵ֣ל בֶּן־שָׁ֑חַר נִגְדַּ֣עְתָּ לָאָ֔רֶץ חוֹלֵ֖שׁ עַל־גּוֹיִֽם׃
You said in your heart, 'I will go up to heaven; above the stars of God I will set my throne on high. I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of the north.[^9]
וְאַתָּ֞ה אָמַ֤רְתָּ בִֽלְבָבְךָ֙ הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם אֶֽעֱלֶ֔ה מִמַּ֥עַל לְכֽוֹכְבֵי־אֵ֖ל אָרִ֣ים כִּסְאִ֑י וְאֵשֵׁ֥ב בְּהַר־מוֹעֵ֖ד בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י צָפֽוֹן׃
I will go up above the heights of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.'[^10]
אֶעֱלֶ֖ה עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵי עָ֑ב אֶדַּמֶּ֖ה לְעֶלְיֽוֹן׃
But you are brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the Pit.
אַ֧ךְ אֶל־שְׁא֛וֹל תּוּרָ֖ד אֶל־יַרְכְּתֵי־בֽוֹר׃
Those who see you will stare at you; they will look closely at you: 'Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms,
רֹאֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵלֶ֣יךָ יַשְׁגִּ֔יחוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ יִתְבּוֹנָ֑נוּ הֲזֶ֤ה הָאִישׁ֙ מַרְגִּ֣יז הָאָ֔רֶץ מַרְעִ֖ישׁ מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃
who made the world like a wilderness and overthrew its cities, who would not let his prisoners go home?'
שָׂ֥ם תֵּבֵ֛ל כַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְעָרָ֣יו הָרָ֑ס אֲסִירָ֖יו לֹא־פָ֥תַח בָּֽיְתָה׃
All the kings of the nations, all of them, lie in honor, each in his own tomb.[^11]
כָּל־מַלְכֵ֥י גוֹיִ֖ם כֻּלָּ֑ם שָׁכְב֥וּ בְכָב֖וֹד אִ֥ישׁ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ׃
But you are thrown out of your grave like a rejected branch,[^12] covered with the slain, those pierced by the sword, who go down to the stones of the Pit, like a corpse trampled underfoot.
וְאַתָּ֞ה הָשְׁלַ֤כְתָּ מִֽקִּבְרְךָ֙ כְּנֵ֣צֶר נִתְעָ֔ב לְב֥וּשׁ הֲרֻגִ֖ים מְטֹ֣עֲנֵי חָ֑רֶב יוֹרְדֵ֥י אֶל־אַבְנֵי־ב֖וֹר כְּפֶ֥גֶר מוּבָֽס׃
You will not join them in burial, for you have destroyed your land and killed your people. May the offspring of evildoers never be named again!
לֹֽא־תֵחַ֤ד אִתָּם֙ בִּקְבוּרָ֔ה כִּֽי־אַרְצְךָ֥ שִׁחַ֖תָּ עַמְּךָ֣ הָרָ֑גְתָּ לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵ֥א לְעוֹלָ֖ם זֶ֥רַע מְרֵעִֽים׃
Prepare a place to slaughter his sons for the guilt of their ancestors, so that they may not rise and possess the earth and fill the face of the world with cities."
הָכִ֧ינוּ לְבָנָ֛יו מַטְבֵּ֖חַ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן אֲבוֹתָ֑ם בַּל־יָקֻ֙מוּ֙ וְיָ֣רְשׁוּ אָ֔רֶץ וּמָלְא֥וּ פְנֵֽי־תֵבֵ֖ל עָרִֽים׃
I will rise up against them, declares Yahweh of Armies.[^13] I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and descendants, declares Yahweh.
וְקַמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְהִכְרַתִּ֨י לְבָבֶ֜ל שֵׁ֥ם וּשְׁאָ֛ר וְנִ֥ין וָנֶ֖כֶד נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
I will make it a place for owls[^14] and pools of water, and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction, declares Yahweh of Armies.
וְשַׂמְתִּ֛יהָ לְמוֹרַ֥שׁ קִפֹּ֖ד וְאַגְמֵי־מָ֑יִם וְטֵֽאטֵאתִ֙יהָ֙ בְּמַטְאֲטֵ֣א הַשְׁמֵ֔ד נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ פ
Yahweh of Armies has sworn: Surely, as I have planned, so it will be, and as I have purposed, so it will stand:
נִשְׁבַּ֛ע יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־לֹ֞א כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּמִּ֙יתִי֙ כֵּ֣ן הָיָ֔תָה וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָעַ֖צְתִּי הִ֥יא תָקֽוּם׃
I will break Assyria in my land and trample him on my mountains. His yoke will be removed from them, and his burden removed from their shoulder.
לִשְׁבֹּ֤ר אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּאַרְצִ֔י וְעַל־הָרַ֖י אֲבוּסֶ֑נּוּ וְסָ֤ר מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶם֙ עֻלּ֔וֹ וְסֻ֨בֳּל֔וֹ מֵעַ֥ל שִׁכְמ֖וֹ יָסֽוּר׃
This is the plan that is planned for the whole earth, and this is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.
זֹ֛את הָעֵצָ֥ה הַיְּעוּצָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְזֹ֛את הַיָּ֥ד הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃
For Yahweh of Armies has planned, and who can stop him? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?
כִּֽי־יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת יָעָ֖ץ וּמִ֣י יָפֵ֑ר וְיָד֥וֹ הַנְּטוּיָ֖ה וּֽמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃ פ
In the year King Ahaz died,[^15] this oracle[^16] came:
בִּשְׁנַת־מ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֑ז הָיָ֖ה הַמַּשָּׂ֥א הַזֶּֽה׃
Do not rejoice, all you Philistines,[^17] because the rod that struck you is broken. For from the root of the snake will come a viper, and its fruit will be a flying serpent.[^18]
אַֽל־תִּשְׂמְחִ֤י פְלֶ֙שֶׁת֙ כֻּלֵּ֔ךְ כִּ֥י נִשְׁבַּ֖ר שֵׁ֣בֶט מַכֵּ֑ךְ כִּֽי־מִשֹּׁ֤רֶשׁ נָחָשׁ֙ יֵ֣צֵא צֶ֔פַע וּפִרְי֖וֹ שָׂרָ֥ף מְעוֹפֵֽף׃
The firstborn of the poor will graze,[^19] and the needy will lie down in safety. But I will kill your root with famine, and it will slay your survivors.[^20]
וְרָעוּ֙ בְּכוֹרֵ֣י דַלִּ֔ים וְאֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים לָבֶ֣טַח יִרְבָּ֑צוּ וְהֵמַתִּ֤י בָֽרָעָב֙ שָׁרְשֵׁ֔ךְ וּשְׁאֵרִיתֵ֖ךְ יַהֲרֹֽג׃
Wail, you gate! Cry out, you city! Melt in fear, all you Philistines! For smoke comes from the north, and there is no straggler in its ranks.[^21]
הֵילִ֤ילִֽי שַׁ֙עַר֙ זַֽעֲקִי־עִ֔יר נָמ֖וֹג פְּלֶ֣שֶׁת כֻּלֵּ֑ךְ כִּ֤י מִצָּפוֹן֙ עָשָׁ֣ן בָּ֔א וְאֵ֥ין בּוֹדֵ֖ד בְּמוֹעָדָֽיו׃
What answer will be given to the messengers of the nation? That Yahweh has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people will find refuge.
וּמַֽה־יַּעֲנֶ֖ה מַלְאֲכֵי־ג֑וֹי כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ יִסַּ֣ד צִיּ֔וֹן וּבָ֥הּ יֶחֱס֖וּ עֲנִיֵּ֥י עַמּֽוֹ׃ ס

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *mashal*, "saying, proverb, taunt song". The song runs from here to verse 21.
n.3: Hebrew *madhevah*, a word found only here, of uncertain meaning. The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) reads *marhevah*, "onslaught" or "arrogance", which differs by one similar letter.
n.4: Or "cypresses". Hebrew *berosh*.
n.5: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.6: Hebrew *repha'im*, the spirits of the dead (26:14, 19).
n.7: Literally "he-goats", the leaders of the flock.
n.8: Hebrew *helel ben shachar*, "shining one, son of the dawn", probably the morning star, the planet Venus, which rises brightly before dawn and then fades in the light of the sun. The poem may draw on an old story of a heavenly being who tried to rise above the gods and was thrown down. The Septuagint translated *helel* as "the morning star", and the Latin Vulgate as *lucifer*, "light-bearer", its word for the morning star; from this came the traditional rendering "Lucifer" (as in the King James Version). Some early Christian writers applied the verse to the fall of Satan (compare Luke 10:18), and "Lucifer" became a name for him. In the poem the words are a taunt against the king of Babylon (verse 4).
n.9: Hebrew *yarkete tsafon*, "the far reaches of Zaphon". In Canaanite stories the gods met on Mount Zaphon in the north. Psalm 48:3 (48:2 in most English Bibles) uses the same words of Mount Zion.
n.10: Hebrew *Elyon*, a title of God.
n.11: Literally "in his house".
n.12: Hebrew *netser*, the word for the "branch" from the roots of Jesse in 11:1.
n.13: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.14: Hebrew *qippod*, perhaps a hedgehog or a kind of owl.
n.15: About 715 BC, though the date of Ahaz's death is uncertain.
n.16: Hebrew *massa*. See 13:1.
n.17: Literally "Philistia, all of you", the land addressed as a woman. Also in verse 31.
n.18: Hebrew *saraf*, the word used for the *seraphim* of 6:2.
n.19: That is, the poorest of the poor.
n.21: Literally "there is no one alone in his appointed places". The meaning is uncertain.

v: An oracle[^1] concerning Moab: Ar of Moab is devastated in a night, destroyed![^2] Kir of Moab is devastated in a night, destroyed!
מַשָּׂ֖א מוֹאָ֑ב כִּ֠י בְּלֵ֞יל שֻׁדַּ֨ד עָ֤ר מוֹאָב֙ נִדְמָ֔ה כִּ֗י בְּלֵ֛יל שֻׁדַּ֥ד קִיר־מוֹאָ֖ב נִדְמָֽה׃
Dibon goes up to its temple, to its high places, to weep.[^3] Over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. Every head is shaved bald, every beard cut off.[^4]
עָלָ֨ה הַבַּ֧יִת וְדִיבֹ֛ן הַבָּמ֖וֹת לְבֶ֑כִי עַל־נְב֞וֹ וְעַ֤ל מֵֽידְבָא֙ מוֹאָ֣ב יְיֵלִ֔יל בְּכָל־רֹאשָׁ֣יו קָרְחָ֔ה כָּל־זָקָ֖ן גְּרוּעָֽה׃
In its streets they wear sackcloth; on its rooftops and in its squares everyone wails, streaming with tears.
בְּחוּצֹתָ֖יו חָ֣גְרוּ שָׂ֑ק עַ֣ל גַּגּוֹתֶ֧יהָ וּבִרְחֹבֹתֶ֛יהָ כֻּלֹּ֥ה יְיֵלִ֖יל יֹרֵ֥ד בַּבֶּֽכִי׃
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voice is heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry out; his soul trembles within him.
וַתִּזְעַ֤ק חֶשְׁבּוֹן֙ וְאֶלְעָלֵ֔ה עַד־יַ֖הַץ נִשְׁמַ֣ע קוֹלָ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֗ן חֲלֻצֵ֤י מוֹאָב֙ יָרִ֔יעוּ נַפְשׁ֖וֹ יָ֥רְעָה לּֽוֹ׃
My heart cries out for Moab. Her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah.[^5] For they go up the ascent of Luhith weeping; on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of destruction.
לִבִּי֙ לְמוֹאָ֣ב יִזְעָ֔ק בְּרִיחֶ֕הָ עַד־צֹ֖עַר עֶגְלַ֣ת שְׁלִשִׁיָּ֑ה כִּ֣י ׀ מַעֲלֵ֣ה הַלּוּחִ֗ית בִּבְכִי֙ יַֽעֲלֶה־בּ֔וֹ כִּ֚י דֶּ֣רֶךְ חוֹרֹנַ֔יִם זַעֲקַת־שֶׁ֖בֶר יְעֹעֵֽרוּ׃
For the waters of Nimrim are a desolation; the grass is withered, the new growth is gone, and nothing green is left.
כִּֽי־מֵ֥י נִמְרִ֖ים מְשַׁמּ֣וֹת יִֽהְי֑וּ כִּֽי־יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ כָּ֣לָה דֶ֔שֶׁא יֶ֖רֶק לֹ֥א הָיָֽה׃
So they carry the wealth they have gained and stored up away over the Wadi of the Willows.[^6]
עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִתְרָ֣ה עָשָׂ֑ה וּפְקֻדָּתָ֔ם עַ֛ל נַ֥חַל הָעֲרָבִ֖ים יִשָּׂאֽוּם׃
For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab; her wailing reaches as far as Eglaim, her wailing as far as Beer-elim.
כִּֽי־הִקִּ֥יפָה הַזְּעָקָ֖ה אֶת־גְּב֣וּל מוֹאָ֑ב עַד־אֶגְלַ֙יִם֙ יִלְלָתָ֔הּ וּבְאֵ֥ר אֵילִ֖ים יִלְלָתָֽהּ׃
For the waters of Dimon[^7] are full of blood. Yet I will bring still more on Dimon: a lion for the survivors of Moab and for the remnant of the land.
כִּ֣י מֵ֤י דִימוֹן֙ מָ֣לְאוּ דָ֔ם כִּֽי־אָשִׁ֥ית עַל־דִּימ֖וֹן נוֹסָפ֑וֹת לִפְלֵיטַ֤ת מוֹאָב֙ אַרְיֵ֔ה וְלִשְׁאֵרִ֖ית אֲדָמָֽה׃

n.1: Hebrew *massa*. See 13:1. Much of chapters 15–16 is found also in Jeremiah 48.
n.2: Or "silenced". Ar and Kir were chief cities of Moab, east of the Dead Sea.
n.3: Literally "He goes up, the house and Dibon, the high places, to weep". The Hebrew is difficult; *the house* may be a temple or a place named Bayith.
n.4: Shaving the head and cutting the beard were signs of mourning.
n.5: Or "as far as Zoar, like a three-year-old heifer".
n.6: Or "the Wadi of the Poplars". Probably the Zered, the southern border of Moab.
n.7: Probably Dibon (verse 2), spelled to sound like *dam*, "blood". The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) and the Vulgate read "Dibon".

v: Send lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela, by way of the wilderness, to the mount of Daughter Zion.[^1]
שִׁלְחוּ־כַ֥ר מֹשֵֽׁל־אֶ֖רֶץ מִסֶּ֣לַע מִדְבָּ֑רָה אֶל־הַ֖ר בַּת־צִיּֽוֹן׃
Like fluttering birds, like a scattered nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon.[^2]
וְהָיָ֥ה כְעוֹף־נוֹדֵ֖ד קֵ֣ן מְשֻׁלָּ֑ח תִּֽהְיֶ֙ינָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת מוֹאָ֔ב מַעְבָּרֹ֖ת לְאַרְנֽוֹן׃
Give counsel; make a decision.[^3] Make your shade like night at high noon. Hide the outcasts; do not betray the fugitive.
*הביאו **הָבִ֤יאִי עֵצָה֙ עֲשׂ֣וּ פְלִילָ֔ה שִׁ֧יתִי כַלַּ֛יִל צִלֵּ֖ךְ בְּת֣וֹךְ צָהֳרָ֑יִם סַתְּרִי֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים נֹדֵ֖ד אַל־תְּגַלִּֽי׃
Let my outcasts from Moab stay with you;[^4] be a refuge for them from the destroyer. When the oppressor is no more and destruction has ceased, and the one who tramples has vanished from the land,
יָג֤וּרוּ בָךְ֙ נִדָּחַ֔י מוֹאָ֛ב הֱוִי־סֵ֥תֶר לָ֖מוֹ מִפְּנֵ֣י שׁוֹדֵ֑ד כִּֽי־אָפֵ֤ס הַמֵּץ֙ כָּ֣לָה שֹׁ֔ד תַּ֥מּוּ רֹמֵ֖ס מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
then a throne will be established in faithful love,[^5] and on it will sit in faithfulness, in the tent of David, one who judges and seeks justice and is quick to do what is right.
וְהוּכַ֤ן בַּחֶ֙סֶד֙ כִּסֵּ֔א וְיָשַׁ֥ב עָלָ֛יו בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת בְּאֹ֣הֶל דָּוִ֑ד שֹׁפֵ֛ט וְדֹרֵ֥שׁ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּמְהִ֥ר צֶֽדֶק׃
We have heard of the pride of Moab, how very proud he is, of his arrogance, his pride and his insolence; his boasting is empty.[^6]
שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ גְאוֹן־מוֹאָ֖ב גֵּ֣א מְאֹ֑ד גַּאֲוָת֧וֹ וּגְאוֹנ֛וֹ וְעֶבְרָת֖וֹ לֹא־כֵ֥ן בַּדָּֽיו׃ ס
Therefore Moab wails; all of them wail for Moab. Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth,[^7] utterly stricken.
לָכֵ֗ן יְיֵלִ֥יל מוֹאָ֛ב לְמוֹאָ֖ב כֻּלֹּ֣ה יְיֵלִ֑יל לַאֲשִׁישֵׁ֧י קִיר־חֲרֶ֛שֶׂת תֶּהְגּ֖וּ אַךְ־נְכָאִֽים׃

For the fields of Heshbon wither, and the vines of Sibmah, whose choice vines laid low the lords of the nations.[^8] They reached as far as Jazer and wandered into the wilderness; their shoots spread out and crossed the sea.
כִּ֣י שַׁדְמוֹת֩ חֶשְׁבּ֨וֹן אֻמְלָ֜ל גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֗ה בַּעֲלֵ֤י גוֹיִם֙ הָלְמ֣וּ שְׂרוּקֶּ֔יהָ עַד־יַעְזֵ֥ר נָגָ֖עוּ תָּ֣עוּ מִדְבָּ֑ר שְׁלֻ֣חוֹתֶ֔יהָ נִטְּשׁ֖וּ עָ֥בְרוּ יָֽם׃
So I weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vines of Sibmah. I drench you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, for the battle shout has fallen on your summer fruit and your harvest.[^9]
עַל־כֵּ֡ן אֶבְכֶּ֞ה בִּבְכִ֤י יַעְזֵר֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה אֲרַיָּ֙וֶךְ֙ דִּמְעָתִ֔י חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וְאֶלְעָלֵ֑ה כִּ֧י עַל־קֵיצֵ֛ךְ וְעַל־קְצִירֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד נָפָֽל׃
Joy and gladness are taken away from the fruitful field; in the vineyards no one sings or shouts. No one treads out wine in the presses; I have put an end to the shout.
וְנֶאֱסַ֨ף שִׂמְחָ֤ה וָגִיל֙ מִן־הַכַּרְמֶ֔ל וּבַכְּרָמִ֥ים לֹֽא־יְרֻנָּ֖ן לֹ֣א יְרֹעָ֑ע יַ֗יִן בַּיְקָבִ֛ים לֹֽא־יִדְרֹ֥ךְ הַדֹּרֵ֖ךְ הֵידָ֥ד הִשְׁבַּֽתִּי׃
Therefore my heart moans for Moab like a lyre, and my inmost being for Kir-heres.[^10]
עַל־כֵּן֙ מֵעַ֣י לְמוֹאָ֔ב כַּכִּנּ֖וֹר יֶֽהֱמ֑וּ וְקִרְבִּ֖י לְקִ֥יר חָֽרֶשׂ׃
When Moab appears and wears himself out on the high place,[^11] and comes to his sanctuary to pray, it will do him no good.[^12]
וְהָיָ֧ה כִֽי־נִרְאָ֛ה כִּֽי־נִלְאָ֥ה מוֹאָ֖ב עַל־הַבָּמָ֑ה וּבָ֧א אֶל־מִקְדָּשׁ֛וֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל וְלֹ֥א יוּכָֽל׃
This is the word that Yahweh[^13] spoke concerning Moab in the past.
זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־מוֹאָ֖ב מֵאָֽז׃

But now Yahweh has spoken: Within three years, counted as a hired worker counts them,[^14] the glory of Moab will be brought into contempt, with all its great crowd, and its survivors will be very few and feeble.
וְעַתָּ֗ה דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בְּשָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ כִּשְׁנֵ֣י שָׂכִ֔יר וְנִקְלָה֙ כְּב֣וֹד מוֹאָ֔ב בְּכֹ֖ל הֶהָמ֣וֹן הָרָ֑ב וּשְׁאָ֥ר מְעַ֛ט מִזְעָ֖ר ל֥וֹא כַבִּֽיר׃ ס

n.1: Moab had once paid lambs as tribute to the king of Israel (2 Kings 3:4). *Sela*, "the rock", is a place in Edom, perhaps Petra.
n.2: The river that runs into the Dead Sea from the east, the northern border of Moab.
n.3: Verses 3–5 are probably the plea of Moab's refugees to Zion.
n.4: Literally "my outcasts, Moab". The Septuagint reads "the outcasts of Moab".
n.5: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love.
n.6: Literally "his idle talk is not so".
n.7: Or "the men". Jeremiah 48:31 reads "the men of Kir-heres". Kir-hareseth and Kir-heres (verse 11) are probably Kir of Moab (15:1).
n.8: Or "the lords of the nations have struck down its choice vines". The wine of Sibmah may have been strong enough to overcome rulers.
n.9: Hebrew *hedad*, the shout of those treading grapes, here the shout of the enemy (Jeremiah 48:33). Also in verse 10.
n.10: Literally "my bowels", thought of as the seat of feeling.
n.11: A play on words: *nir'ah*, "appears", and *nil'ah*, "wears himself out".
n.12: Literally "and he will not be able".
n.13: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.14: Literally "like the years of a hired worker", who will not work a day beyond what he is paid for: exactly three years.

v: An oracle[^1] concerning Damascus: Look, Damascus will cease to be a city; it will become a heap of ruins.
מַשָּׂ֖א דַּמָּ֑שֶׂק הִנֵּ֤ה דַמֶּ֙שֶׂק֙ מוּסָ֣ר מֵעִ֔יר וְהָיְתָ֖ה מְעִ֥י מַפָּלָֽה׃
The cities of Aroer[^2] are abandoned; they will be for flocks, which will lie down with no one to frighten them.
עֲזֻב֖וֹת עָרֵ֣י עֲרֹעֵ֑ר לַעֲדָרִ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ינָה וְרָבְצ֖וּ וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃
The fortress will disappear from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus. The remnant of Aram will be like the glory of the Israelites, declares Yahweh of Armies.[^3]
וְנִשְׁבַּ֤ת מִבְצָר֙ מֵֽאֶפְרַ֔יִם וּמַמְלָכָ֥ה מִדַּמֶּ֖שֶׂק וּשְׁאָ֣ר אֲרָ֑ם כִּכְב֤וֹד בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יִֽהְי֔וּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ ס
On that day the glory of Jacob will fade, and the fat of his body will waste away.
וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִדַּ֖ל כְּב֣וֹד יַעֲקֹ֑ב וּמִשְׁמַ֥ן בְּשָׂר֖וֹ יֵרָזֶֽה׃
It will be as when a reaper gathers the standing grain and his arm harvests the ears, as when someone gleans ears of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.[^4]
וְהָיָ֗ה כֶּֽאֱסֹף֙ קָצִ֣יר קָמָ֔ה וּזְרֹע֖וֹ שִׁבֳּלִ֣ים יִקְצ֑וֹר וְהָיָ֛ה כִּמְלַקֵּ֥ט שִׁבֳּלִ֖ים בְּעֵ֥מֶק רְפָאִֽים׃
Gleanings will be left in it, as when an olive tree is beaten: two or three olives at the very top, four or five on its fruitful branches, declares Yahweh, the God of Israel.
וְנִשְׁאַר־בּ֤וֹ עֽוֹלֵלֹת֙ כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת שְׁנַ֧יִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֛ה גַּרְגְּרִ֖ים בְּרֹ֣אשׁ אָמִ֑יר אַרְבָּעָ֣ה חֲמִשָּׁ֗ה בִּסְעִפֶ֙יהָ֙ פֹּֽרִיָּ֔ה נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס
On that day people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will turn to the Holy One of Israel.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִשְׁעֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם עַל־עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ וְעֵינָ֕יו אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃
They will not look to the altars, the work of their hands, or regard what their fingers have made, the Asherah poles[^5] and the incense altars.[^6]
וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁעֶ֔ה אֶל־הַֽמִּזְבְּח֖וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדָ֑יו וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֤וּ אֶצְבְּעֹתָיו֙ לֹ֣א יִרְאֶ֔ה וְהָאֲשֵׁרִ֖ים וְהָחַמָּנִֽים׃
On that day their strong cities will be like the abandoned places of the woods and the hilltops,[^7] which they abandoned before the Israelites, and there will be desolation.
בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יִהְי֣וּ ׀ עָרֵ֣י מָעֻזּ֗וֹ כַּעֲזוּבַ֤ת הַחֹ֙רֶשׁ֙ וְהָ֣אָמִ֔יר אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָזְב֔וּ מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֖ה שְׁמָמָֽה׃
For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and have not remembered the Rock of your refuge. Therefore, though you plant pleasant plants[^8] and set out cuttings for a foreign god,[^9]
כִּ֤י שָׁכַ֙חַתְּ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׁעֵ֔ךְ וְצ֥וּר מָעֻזֵּ֖ךְ לֹ֣א זָכָ֑רְתְּ עַל־כֵּ֗ן תִּטְּעִי֙ נִטְעֵ֣י נַעֲמָנִ֔ים וּזְמֹ֥רַת זָ֖ר תִּזְרָעֶֽנּוּ׃
though on the day you plant them you make them grow, and in the morning you make your seed blossom, the harvest will vanish[^10] on the day of sickness and incurable pain.
בְּי֤וֹם נִטְעֵךְ֙ תְּשַׂגְשֵׂ֔גִי וּבַבֹּ֖קֶר זַרְעֵ֣ךְ תַּפְרִ֑יחִי נֵ֥ד קָצִ֛יר בְּי֥וֹם נַחֲלָ֖ה וּכְאֵ֥ב אָנֽוּשׁ׃ ס
Woe to[^11] the many peoples who roar, who roar like the roaring of the seas, and the nations who rage, who rage like the raging of mighty waters!
ה֗וֹי הֲמוֹן֙ עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים כַּהֲמ֥וֹת יַמִּ֖ים יֶהֱמָי֑וּן וּשְׁא֣וֹן לְאֻמִּ֔ים כִּשְׁא֛וֹן מַ֥יִם כַּבִּירִ֖ים יִשָּׁאֽוּן׃
The nations rage like the raging of many waters, but he rebukes them, and they flee far away, chased like chaff on the mountains before the wind, like whirling dust before a storm.
לְאֻמִּ֗ים כִּשְׁא֞וֹן מַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ יִשָּׁא֔וּן וְגָ֥עַר בּ֖וֹ וְנָ֣ס מִמֶּרְחָ֑ק וְרֻדַּ֗ף כְּמֹ֤ץ הָרִים֙ לִפְנֵי־ר֔וּחַ וּכְגַלְגַּ֖ל לִפְנֵ֥י סוּפָֽה׃
At evening, look, sudden terror! Before morning, they are gone. This is the portion of those who loot us, the lot of those who plunder us.
לְעֵ֥ת עֶ֙רֶב֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה בַלָּהָ֔ה בְּטֶ֥רֶם בֹּ֖קֶר אֵינֶ֑נּוּ זֶ֚ה חֵ֣לֶק שׁוֹסֵ֔ינוּ וְגוֹרָ֖ל לְבֹזְזֵֽינוּ׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *massa*. See 13:1. The oracle concerns both Damascus, capital of Aram, and its ally Ephraim, the northern kingdom of Israel (7:1–9).
n.2: Aroer is known as a town on the Arnon in Moab (Deuteronomy 2:36). The name here may stand for towns near Damascus. The Septuagint reads "abandoned forever".
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.4: A fertile valley southwest of Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:18).
n.5: Hebrew *asherim*: wooden poles or trees that were symbols of the goddess Asherah.
n.6: Hebrew *chammanim*, probably small altars for burning incense.
n.7: The Septuagint reads "like the abandoned places of the Amorites and the Hivites", peoples who lived in Canaan before Israel.
n.8: Hebrew *na'amanim*, "pleasant things". The word may refer to gardens planted in honor of a dying and rising god of fertility, whose title *na'aman*, "the pleasant one", was used of the god Adonis.
n.9: Literally "a stranger".
n.10: Or "the harvest will be a heap". The meaning of the Hebrew word *ned* here is uncertain.
n.11: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning, used by the prophets to announce disaster (see 1:4).

v: Woe to[^1] the land of whirring wings,[^2] beyond the rivers of Cush,[^3]
ה֥וֹי אֶ֖רֶץ צִלְצַ֣ל כְּנָפָ֑יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר מֵעֵ֖בֶר לְנַֽהֲרֵי־כֽוּשׁ׃

which sends envoys by sea, in papyrus boats over the waters! Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth-skinned,[^4] to a people feared far and wide,[^5] a nation strong and conquering,[^6] whose land the rivers divide.

הַשֹּׁלֵ֨חַ בַּיָּ֜ם צִירִ֗ים וּבִכְלֵי־גֹמֶא֮ עַל־פְּנֵי־מַיִם֒ לְכ֣וּ ׀ מַלְאָכִ֣ים קַלִּ֗ים אֶל־גּוֹי֙ מְמֻשָּׁ֣ךְ וּמוֹרָ֔ט אֶל־עַ֥ם נוֹרָ֖א מִן־ה֣וּא וָהָ֑לְאָה גּ֚וֹי קַו־קָ֣ו וּמְבוּסָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־בָּזְא֥וּ נְהָרִ֖ים אַרְצֽוֹ׃
All you inhabitants of the world, you who live on the earth, when a signal flag is raised on the mountains, you will see it; when a ram's horn is blown, you will hear it.
כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵ֖ל וְשֹׁ֣כְנֵי אָ֑רֶץ כִּנְשֹׂא־נֵ֤ס הָרִים֙ תִּרְא֔וּ וְכִתְקֹ֥עַ שׁוֹפָ֖ר תִּשְׁמָֽעוּ׃ ס
For this is what Yahweh[^7] has said to me: I will be still and look on from my dwelling place, like the shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י *אשקוטה **אֶשְׁקֳטָ֖ה וְאַבִּ֣יטָה בִמְכוֹנִ֑י כְּחֹ֥ם צַח֙ עֲלֵי־א֔וֹר כְּעָ֥ב טַ֖ל בְּחֹ֥ם קָצִֽיר׃
For before the harvest, when the blossom is over and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the shoots with pruning knives and lop off and clear away the spreading branches.
כִּֽי־לִפְנֵ֤י קָצִיר֙ כְּתָם־פֶּ֔רַח וּבֹ֥סֶר גֹּמֵ֖ל יִֽהְיֶ֣ה נִצָּ֑ה וְכָרַ֤ת הַזַּלְזַלִּים֙ בַּמַּזְמֵר֔וֹת וְאֶת־הַנְּטִישׁ֖וֹת הֵסִ֥יר הֵתַֽז׃
They will all be left to the birds of prey on the mountains and to the wild animals of the earth. The birds of prey will spend the summer on them, and all the wild animals of the earth the winter.
יֵעָזְב֤וּ יַחְדָּו֙ לְעֵ֣יט הָרִ֔ים וּֽלְבֶהֱמַ֖ת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְקָ֤ץ עָלָיו֙ הָעַ֔יִט וְכָל־בֶּהֱמַ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ עָלָ֥יו תֶּחֱרָֽף׃

At that time gifts will be brought to Yahweh of Armies[^8] from a people tall and smooth-skinned,[^9] from a people feared far and wide, a nation strong and conquering, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of Yahweh of Armies, Mount Zion.

בָּעֵת֩ הַהִ֨יא יֽוּבַל־שַׁ֜י לַיהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת עַ֚ם מְמֻשָּׁ֣ךְ וּמוֹרָ֔ט וּמֵעַ֥ם נוֹרָ֖א מִן־ה֣וּא וָהָ֑לְאָה גּ֣וֹי ׀ קַו־קָ֣ו וּמְבוּסָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּזְא֤וּ נְהָרִים֙ אַרְצ֔וֹ אֶל־מְק֛וֹם שֵׁם־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת הַר־צִיּֽוֹן׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning, used by the prophets to announce disaster (see 1:4).
n.2: Hebrew *tsiltsal kenafayim*, perhaps the buzzing of insects, or the sails of ships.
n.3: The region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia). In Isaiah's time its kings also ruled Egypt and sought allies against Assyria.
n.4: Literally "drawn out and polished". Also in verse 7.
n.5: Literally "from it and beyond".
n.6: Hebrew *qav-qav u-mevusah*, literally perhaps "line-line and trampling". The meaning is uncertain; perhaps "of strange speech".
n.7: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.8: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.9: Literally "a people tall and smooth-skinned, and from a people feared far and wide".

v: An oracle[^1] concerning Egypt: Look, Yahweh[^2] is riding on a swift cloud and is coming to Egypt. The idols of Egypt tremble before him, and the heart of Egypt melts within it.
מַשָּׂ֖א מִצְרָ֑יִם הִנֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה רֹכֵ֨ב עַל־עָ֥ב קַל֙ וּבָ֣א מִצְרַ֔יִם וְנָע֞וּ אֱלִילֵ֤י מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ מִפָּנָ֔יו וּלְבַ֥ב מִצְרַ֖יִם יִמַּ֥ס בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃
I will stir up Egyptian against Egyptian; they will fight, brother against brother and neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
וְסִכְסַכְתִּ֤י מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְנִלְחֲמ֥וּ אִישׁ־בְּאָחִ֖יו וְאִ֣ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֑הוּ עִ֣יר בְּעִ֔יר מַמְלָכָ֖ה בְּמַמְלָכָֽה׃
The spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it, and I will confuse its plans.[^3] They will consult the idols and the spirits of the dead,[^4] the mediums and the spiritists.
וְנָבְקָ֤ה רֽוּחַ־מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ וַעֲצָת֖וֹ אֲבַלֵּ֑עַ וְדָרְשׁ֤וּ אֶל־הָֽאֱלִילִים֙ וְאֶל־הָ֣אִטִּ֔ים וְאֶל־הָאֹב֖וֹת וְאֶל־הַיִּדְּעֹנִֽים׃
I will hand Egypt over to a cruel master,[^5] and a fierce king will rule over them, declares the Lord[^6] Yahweh of Armies.[^7]
וְסִכַּרְתִּי֙ אֶת־מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּיַ֖ד אֲדֹנִ֣ים קָשֶׁ֑ה וּמֶ֤לֶךְ עַז֙ יִמְשָׁל־בָּ֔ם נְאֻ֥ם הָאָד֖וֹן יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
The waters of the sea[^8] will dry up, and the river will be parched and dry.
וְנִשְּׁתוּ־מַ֖יִם מֵֽהַיָּ֑ם וְנָהָ֖ר יֶחֱרַ֥ב וְיָבֵֽשׁ׃
The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt[^9] will dwindle and dry up; reeds and rushes will wither.
וְהֶאֶזְנִ֣יחוּ נְהָר֔וֹת דָּלֲל֥וּ וְחָרְב֖וּ יְאֹרֵ֣י מָצ֑וֹר קָנֶ֥ה וָס֖וּף קָמֵֽלוּ׃
The plants along the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, and every sown field along the Nile will dry up, blow away and be no more.[^10]
עָר֥וֹת עַל־יְא֖וֹר עַל־פִּ֣י יְא֑וֹר וְכֹל֙ מִזְרַ֣ע יְא֔וֹר יִיבַ֥שׁ נִדַּ֖ף וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ׃
The fishermen will mourn and lament, all who cast hooks into the Nile; those who spread nets on the water will waste away.
וְאָנוּ֙ הַדַּיָּגִ֔ים וְאָ֣בְל֔וּ כָּל־מַשְׁלִיכֵ֥י בַיְא֖וֹר חַכָּ֑ה וּפֹרְשֵׂ֥י מִכְמֹ֛רֶת עַל־פְּנֵי־מַ֖יִם אֻמְלָֽלוּ׃
Those who work with combed flax will be dismayed, and the weavers of white cloth.[^11]
וּבֹ֛שׁוּ עֹבְדֵ֥י פִשְׁתִּ֖ים שְׂרִיק֑וֹת וְאֹרְגִ֖ים חוֹרָֽי׃
Her foundations[^12] will be crushed, and all who work for wages will be sick at heart.
וְהָי֥וּ שָׁתֹתֶ֖יהָ מְדֻכָּאִ֑ים כָּל־עֹ֥שֵׂי שֶׂ֖כֶר אַגְמֵי־נָֽפֶשׁ׃
The officials of Zoan[^13] are nothing but fools; the wise counselors of Pharaoh give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings"?
אַךְ־אֱוִלִים֙ שָׂ֣רֵי צֹ֔עַן חַכְמֵי֙ יֹעֲצֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה עֵצָ֖ה נִבְעָרָ֑ה אֵ֚יךְ תֹּאמְר֣וּ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה בֶּן־חֲכָמִ֥ים אֲנִ֖י בֶּן־מַלְכֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃
Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you and make known what Yahweh of Armies has planned against Egypt.
אַיָּם֙ אֵפ֣וֹא חֲכָמֶ֔יךָ וְיַגִּ֥ידוּ נָ֖א לָ֑ךְ וְיֵ֣דְע֔וּ מַה־יָּעַ֛ץ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת עַל־מִצְרָֽיִם׃
The officials of Zoan have become fools; the officials of Memphis[^14] are deceived. The cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
נֽוֹאֲלוּ֙ שָׂ֣רֵי צֹ֔עַן נִשְּׁא֖וּ שָׂ֣רֵי נֹ֑ף הִתְע֥וּ אֶת־מִצְרַ֖יִם פִּנַּ֥ת שְׁבָטֶֽיהָ׃
Yahweh has poured into her a spirit of confusion,[^15] and they make Egypt stagger in all she does, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.
יְהוָ֛ה מָסַ֥ךְ בְּקִרְבָּ֖הּ ר֣וּחַ עִוְעִ֑ים וְהִתְע֤וּ אֶת־מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בְּכָֽל־מַעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ כְּהִתָּע֥וֹת שִׁכּ֖וֹר בְּקִיאֽוֹ׃
There is nothing Egypt can do, head or tail, palm branch or reed.[^16]
וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְמִצְרַ֖יִם מַֽעֲשֶׂ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר יַעֲשֶׂ֛ה רֹ֥אשׁ וְזָנָ֖ב כִּפָּ֥ה וְאַגְמֽוֹן׃ ס
On that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble and be afraid before the hand that Yahweh of Armies raises against them.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִֽהְיֶ֥ה מִצְרַ֖יִם כַּנָּשִׁ֑ים וְחָרַ֣ד ׀ וּפָחַ֗ד מִפְּנֵי֙ תְּנוּפַת֙ יַד־יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ה֖וּא מֵנִ֥יף עָלָֽיו׃
The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Everyone to whom it is mentioned will be afraid because of the plan that Yahweh of Armies has planned against them.
וְ֠הָיְתָה אַדְמַ֨ת יְהוּדָ֤ה לְמִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לְחָגָּ֔א כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַזְכִּ֥יר אֹתָ֛הּ אֵלָ֖יו יִפְחָ֑ד מִפְּנֵ֗י עֲצַת֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ה֖וּא יוֹעֵ֥ץ עָלָֽיו׃ ס
On that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan[^17] and swear allegiance to Yahweh of Armies. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.[^18]
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יִהְיוּ֩ חָמֵ֨שׁ עָרִ֜ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם מְדַבְּרוֹת֙ שְׂפַ֣ת כְּנַ֔עַן וְנִשְׁבָּע֖וֹת לַיהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת עִ֣יר הַהֶ֔רֶס יֵאָמֵ֖ר לְאֶחָֽת׃ ס
On that day there will be an altar to Yahweh in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a standing stone[^19] to Yahweh at its border.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶ֤ה מִזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וּמַצֵּבָ֥ה אֵֽצֶל־גְּבוּלָ֖הּ לַֽיהוָֽה׃
It will be a sign and a witness to Yahweh of Armies in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to Yahweh because of their oppressors, he will send them a savior and defender,[^20] who will rescue them.
וְהָיָ֨ה לְא֥וֹת וּלְעֵ֛ד לַֽיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־יִצְעֲק֤וּ אֶל־יְהוָה֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י לֹֽחֲצִ֔ים וְיִשְׁלַ֥ח לָהֶ֛ם מוֹשִׁ֥יעַ וָרָ֖ב וְהִצִּילָֽם׃
Yahweh will make himself known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know Yahweh on that day. They will worship with sacrifice and grain offering,[^21] and make vows to Yahweh and keep them.
וְנוֹדַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לְמִצְרַ֔יִם וְיָדְע֥וּ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְעָֽבְדוּ֙ זֶ֣בַח וּמִנְחָ֔ה וְנָדְרוּ־נֵ֥דֶר לַֽיהוָ֖ה וְשִׁלֵּֽמוּ׃
Yahweh will strike Egypt, striking and healing. They will turn back to Yahweh, and he will listen to their pleas and heal them.
וְנָגַ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מִצְרַ֖יִם נָגֹ֣ף וְרָפ֑וֹא וְשָׁ֙בוּ֙ עַד־יְהוָ֔ה וְנֶעְתַּ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם וּרְפָאָֽם׃
On that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will come to Egypt and the Egyptians to Assyria, and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians.[^22]
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא תִּהְיֶ֨ה מְסִלָּ֤ה מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ אַשּׁ֔וּרָה וּבָֽא־אַשּׁ֥וּר בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם וּמִצְרַ֣יִם בְּאַשּׁ֑וּר וְעָבְד֥וּ מִצְרַ֖יִם אֶת־אַשּֽׁוּר׃ ס
On that day Israel will be the third, with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the middle of the earth.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִהְיֶ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ שְׁלִ֣ישִׁיָּ֔ה לְמִצְרַ֖יִם וּלְאַשּׁ֑וּר בְּרָכָ֖ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Yahweh of Armies will bless them,[^23] saying, "Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance."[^24]
אֲשֶׁ֧ר בֵּרֲכ֛וֹ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּר֨וּךְ עַמִּ֜י מִצְרַ֗יִם וּמַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יָדַי֙ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְנַחֲלָתִ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *massa*. See 13:1.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "swallow up".
n.4: Hebrew *ittim*, a word found only here, perhaps "mutterers" or "ghosts". The *mediums* and *spiritists* (*ovot* and *yidde'onim*) are those who claim to speak with the dead (8:19).
n.5: Literally "masters", a plural of majesty.
n.6: Hebrew *ha-adon*, "the Lord", a title, not the name Yahweh.
n.7: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.8: Here the Nile, whose broad waters could be called a sea.
n.9: Hebrew *Matsor*, a poetic name for Egypt.
n.10: The first word of the verse, Hebrew *arot*, is uncertain: perhaps "plants", "meadows" or "bare places".
n.11: Hebrew *chori*, a word found only here, probably "white cloth", that is, fine linen.
n.12: Hebrew *shatoteha*, perhaps "her pillars", the leaders of the land, or "her weavers".
n.13: Also called Tanis, a royal city in the Nile Delta.
n.14: Hebrew *Noph*, Memphis, the ancient capital of Egypt near modern Cairo.
n.15: Or "dizziness". Literally "a spirit of distortions".
n.16: The top and bottom of society (9:13–14, 9:14–15 in most English Bibles).
n.17: That is, Hebrew or a related language.
n.18: Hebrew *ir ha-heres*. Some Hebrew manuscripts, the Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) and the Vulgate read *ir ha-cheres*, "City of the Sun", that is, Heliopolis in Egypt. The Septuagint reads "City of Righteousness".
n.19: Hebrew *matsevah*, a standing stone, a pillar set up as a memorial or as an object of worship. The law forbade them in Israel (Deuteronomy 16:22).
n.20: Hebrew *rav*, "a great one" or "one who contends", that is, defends their cause.
n.21: Hebrew *minchah*, "gift, tribute", in Leviticus a grain offering.
n.22: Or "and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians". Hebrew *avad* means both "serve" and "worship".
n.23: Literally "him", the land or people of verse 24.
n.24: The Septuagint reads "Blessed be my people who are in Egypt and among the Assyrians, and Israel my inheritance".

v: In the year that the commander-in-chief,[^1] sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod and fought against it and captured it,[^2]
בִּשְׁנַ֨ת בֹּ֤א תַרְתָּן֙ אַשְׁדּ֔וֹדָה בִּשְׁלֹ֣ח אֹת֔וֹ סַֽרְג֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיִּלָּ֥חֶם בְּאַשְׁדּ֖וֹד וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃
at that time Yahweh[^3] spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz: "Go, take off the sackcloth from your waist and remove the sandals from your feet." And he did so, walking around stripped[^4] and barefoot.

בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָה֮ בְּיַ֣ד יְשַׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמוֹץ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ לֵ֗ךְ וּפִתַּחְתָּ֤ הַשַּׂק֙ מֵעַ֣ל מָתְנֶ֔יךָ וְנַעַלְךָ֥ תַחֲלֹ֖ץ מֵעַ֣ל רַגְלֶ֑יךָ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ כֵּ֔ן הָלֹ֖ךְ עָר֥וֹם וְיָחֵֽף׃ ס
Then Yahweh said, "Just as my servant Isaiah has walked stripped and barefoot for three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and Cush,[^5]
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלַ֛ךְ עַבְדִּ֥י יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ עָר֣וֹם וְיָחֵ֑ף שָׁלֹ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ א֣וֹת וּמוֹפֵ֔ת עַל־מִצְרַ֖יִם וְעַל־כּֽוּשׁ׃
so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, stripped and barefoot, with buttocks bared, to Egypt's shame.
כֵּ֣ן יִנְהַ֣ג מֶֽלֶךְ־אַ֠שּׁוּר אֶת־שְׁבִ֨י מִצְרַ֜יִם וְאֶת־גָּל֥וּת כּ֛וּשׁ נְעָרִ֥ים וּזְקֵנִ֖ים עָר֣וֹם וְיָחֵ֑ף וַחֲשׂוּפַ֥י שֵׁ֖ת עֶרְוַ֥ת מִצְרָֽיִם׃
They will be dismayed and ashamed because of Cush, their hope, and Egypt, their pride.
וְחַתּ֖וּ וָבֹ֑שׁוּ מִכּוּשׁ֙ מַבָּטָ֔ם וּמִן־מִצְרַ֖יִם תִּפְאַרְתָּֽם׃

On that day the people who live on this coast will say, 'Look, this is what has happened to those we hoped in, to whom we fled for help, to be rescued from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?'"
וְ֠אָמַר יֹשֵׁ֨ב הָאִ֣י הַזֶּה֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ הִנֵּה־כֹ֣ה מַבָּטֵ֗נוּ אֲשֶׁר־נַ֤סְנוּ שָׁם֙ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה לְהִ֨נָּצֵ֔ל מִפְּנֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְאֵ֖יךְ נִמָּלֵ֥ט אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *tartan*, an Assyrian title for the army's chief commander (2 Kings 18:17).
n.2: Ashdod, a Philistine city, rebelled against Assyria and was captured by Sargon II's army in 711 BC.
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: Hebrew *arom*, "naked", here probably wearing only a loincloth, like a prisoner of war. Also in verses 3–4.
n.5: The region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia), whose kings then ruled Egypt.

v: An oracle[^1] concerning the wilderness of the sea:[^2] Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev,[^3] it comes from the wilderness, from a terrifying land.
מַשָּׂ֖א מִדְבַּר־יָ֑ם כְּסוּפ֤וֹת בַּנֶּ֙גֶב֙ לַֽחֲלֹ֔ף מִמִּדְבָּ֣ר בָּ֔א מֵאֶ֖רֶץ נוֹרָאָֽה׃
A harsh vision has been shown to me: the traitor betrays, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media![^4] I put an end to all the groaning she caused.[^5]
חָז֥וּת קָשָׁ֖ה הֻגַּד־לִ֑י הַבּוֹגֵ֤ד ׀ בּוֹגֵד֙ וְהַשּׁוֹדֵ֣ד ׀ שׁוֹדֵ֔ד עֲלִ֤י עֵילָם֙ צוּרִ֣י מָדַ֔י כָּל־אַנְחָתָ֖ה הִשְׁבַּֽתִּי׃
Therefore my body[^6] is filled with anguish; pains have seized me like the pains of a woman in labor. I am bent double by what I hear; I am terrified by what I see.
עַל־כֵּ֗ן מָלְא֤וּ מָתְנַי֙ חַלְחָלָ֔ה צִירִ֣ים אֲחָז֔וּנִי כְּצִירֵ֖י יֽוֹלֵדָ֑ה נַעֲוֵ֣יתִי מִשְּׁמֹ֔עַ נִבְהַ֖לְתִּי מֵרְאֽוֹת׃
My mind reels; horror overwhelms me. The twilight I longed for has become a terror to me.
תָּעָ֣ה לְבָבִ֔י פַּלָּצ֖וּת בִּֽעֲתָ֑תְנִי אֵ֚ת נֶ֣שֶׁף חִשְׁקִ֔י שָׂ֥ם לִ֖י לַחֲרָדָֽה׃
They set the table, they spread the rugs,[^7] they eat, they drink! Get up, you officers, oil the shields!
עָרֹ֧ךְ הַשֻּׁלְחָ֛ן צָפֹ֥ה הַצָּפִ֖ית אָכ֣וֹל שָׁתֹ֑ה ק֥וּמוּ הַשָּׂרִ֖ים מִשְׁח֥וּ מָגֵֽן׃ פ
For this is what the Lord said to me: "Go, post a lookout; let him report what he sees.
כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י לֵ֚ךְ הַעֲמֵ֣ד הַֽמְצַפֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִרְאֶ֖ה יַגִּֽיד׃
When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, let him pay attention, close attention."
וְרָ֣אָה רֶ֗כֶב צֶ֚מֶד פָּֽרָשִׁ֔ים רֶ֥כֶב חֲמ֖וֹר רֶ֣כֶב גָּמָ֑ל וְהִקְשִׁ֥יב קֶ֖שֶׁב רַב־קָֽשֶׁב׃
Then he called out like a lion:[^8] "Lord,[^9] I stand on the watchtower continually by day, and I am stationed at my post every night.
וַיִּקְרָ֖א אַרְיֵ֑ה עַל־מִצְפֶּ֣ה ׀ אֲדֹנָ֗י אָנֹכִ֞י עֹמֵ֤ד תָּמִיד֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וְעַל־מִ֨שְׁמַרְתִּ֔י אָנֹכִ֥י נִצָּ֖ב כָּל־הַלֵּילֽוֹת׃
Look, here comes a man in a chariot, with horsemen in pairs!" Then he answered, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All the images of her gods lie shattered on the ground!"[^10]
וְהִנֵּה־זֶ֥ה בָא֙ רֶ֣כֶב אִ֔ישׁ צֶ֖מֶד פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּ֣עַן וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָפְלָ֤ה נָֽפְלָה֙ בָּבֶ֔ל וְכָל־פְּסִילֵ֥י אֱלֹהֶ֖יהָ שִׁבַּ֥ר לָאָֽרֶץ׃
My people, threshed and winnowed on my threshing floor,[^11] what I have heard from Yahweh of Armies,[^12] the God of Israel, I have told you.
מְדֻשָׁתִ֖י וּבֶן־גָּרְנִ֑י אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי מֵאֵ֨ת יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הִגַּ֥דְתִּי לָכֶֽם׃ ס
An oracle concerning Dumah:[^13] Someone calls to me from Seir, "Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?"
מַשָּׂ֖א דּוּמָ֑ה אֵלַי֙ קֹרֵ֣א מִשֵּׂעִ֔יר שֹׁמֵר֙ מַה־מִלַּ֔יְלָה שֹׁמֵ֖ר מַה־מִלֵּֽיל׃
The watchman says, "Morning is coming, but also the night. If you want to ask, ask; come back again."[^14]
אָמַ֣ר שֹׁמֵ֔ר אָתָ֥ה בֹ֖קֶר וְגַם־לָ֑יְלָה אִם־תִּבְעָי֥וּן בְּעָ֖יוּ שֻׁ֥בוּ אֵתָֽיוּ׃ ס
An oracle concerning Arabia:[^15] You caravans of Dedanites, who camp in the thickets of Arabia,
מַשָּׂ֖א בַּעְרָ֑ב בַּיַּ֤עַר בַּעְרַב֙ תָּלִ֔ינוּ אֹֽרְח֖וֹת דְּדָנִֽים׃
bring water to meet the thirsty! You who live in the land of Tema, meet the fugitives with bread.
לִקְרַ֥את צָמֵ֖א הֵתָ֣יוּ מָ֑יִם יֹשְׁבֵי֙ אֶ֣רֶץ תֵּימָ֔א בְּלַחְמ֖וֹ קִדְּמ֥וּ נֹדֵֽד׃
For they have fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.
כִּֽי־מִפְּנֵ֥י חֲרָב֖וֹת נָדָ֑דוּ מִפְּנֵ֣י ׀ חֶ֣רֶב נְטוּשָׁ֗ה וּמִפְּנֵי֙ קֶ֣שֶׁת דְּרוּכָ֔ה וּמִפְּנֵ֖י כֹּ֥בֶד מִלְחָמָֽה׃ ס
For this is what the Lord said to me: "Within one year, counted as a hired worker counts it,[^16] all the glory of Kedar[^17] will come to an end.
כִּי־כֹ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֲדֹנָ֖י אֵלָ֑י בְּע֤וֹד שָׁנָה֙ כִּשְׁנֵ֣י שָׂכִ֔יר וְכָלָ֖ה כָּל־כְּב֥וֹד קֵדָֽר׃
The bows of Kedar's warriors that remain will be few." For Yahweh, the God of Israel, has spoken.
וּשְׁאָ֧ר מִסְפַּר־קֶ֛שֶׁת גִּבּוֹרֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־קֵדָ֖ר יִמְעָ֑טוּ כִּ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל דִּבֵּֽר׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *massa*. See 13:1. Also in verses 11 and 13.
n.2: Hebrew *midbar-yam*. The oracle concerns Babylon (verse 9), which lay near the marshes at the head of the Persian Gulf, a region the Assyrians called "the Sealand". The Septuagint reads only "the wilderness".
n.3: The dry southern region of Judah.
n.4: Elam and Media, peoples to the east of Babylon (11:11; 13:17).
n.5: Literally "all her groaning", that is, the groaning Babylon has caused, or perhaps Babylon's own groaning.
n.6: Literally "my loins".
n.7: Or "they set the watch". The meaning of the Hebrew phrase *tsafoh ha-tsafit* is uncertain.
n.8: Literally "And a lion called out". The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) reads "And the lookout called out".
n.9: Or "my lord". Hebrew *Adonai*.
n.10: Compare Revelation 14:8; 18:2.
n.11: Literally "my threshed one and son of my threshing floor": Israel, beaten and sifted by its enemies.
n.12: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.13: *Dumah*, "silence", is an oasis in northern Arabia (Genesis 25:14). Here it may also be a play on *Edom*, since Seir is the mountain country of Edom. The Septuagint reads "Idumea", that is, Edom.
n.14: The verbs "ask" and "come" are in forms close to Aramaic, perhaps imitating the speech of the questioner.
n.15: Or "An oracle in the steppe". Hebrew *ba'rav*. Dedan and Tema were oasis towns of northern Arabia.
n.16: Literally "like the years of a hired worker", that is, exactly (16:14).
n.17: A tribe of the Arabian desert (Genesis 25:13; Psalm 120:5).

v: An oracle[^1] concerning the Valley of Vision:[^2] What is the matter with you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops,
מַשָּׂ֖א גֵּ֣יא חִזָּי֑וֹן מַה־לָּ֣ךְ אֵפ֔וֹא כִּֽי־עָלִ֥ית כֻּלָּ֖ךְ לַגַּגּֽוֹת׃
you city full of noise, you town of tumult and celebration? Your slain were not slain by the sword, nor did they die in battle.
תְּשֻׁא֣וֹת ׀ מְלֵאָ֗ה עִ֚יר הֽוֹמִיָּ֔ה קִרְיָ֖ה עַלִּיזָ֑ה חֲלָלַ֙יִךְ֙ לֹ֣א חַלְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶב וְלֹ֖א מֵתֵ֥י מִלְחָמָֽה׃
All your rulers fled together; they were captured without a bow being drawn.[^3] All of you who were found were captured together, though they had fled far away.
כָּל־קְצִינַ֥יִךְ נָֽדְדוּ־יַ֖חַד מִקֶּ֣שֶׁת אֻסָּ֑רוּ כָּל־נִמְצָאַ֙יִךְ֙ אֻסְּר֣וּ יַחְדָּ֔ו מֵרָח֖וֹק בָּרָֽחוּ׃
Therefore I said, "Look away from me; let me weep bitterly. Do not try to comfort me over the destruction of my dear people."[^4]
עַל־כֵּ֥ן אָמַ֛רְתִּי שְׁע֥וּ מִנִּ֖י אֲמָרֵ֣ר בַּבֶּ֑כִי אַל־תָּאִ֣יצוּ לְנַֽחֲמֵ֔נִי עַל־שֹׁ֖ד בַּת־עַמִּֽי׃
For the Lord Yahweh of Armies[^5] has a day of tumult, trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision, of battering down walls and of crying out to the mountain.[^6]
כִּ֣י יוֹם֩ מְהוּמָ֨ה וּמְבוּסָ֜ה וּמְבוּכָ֗ה לַֽאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּגֵ֣יא חִזָּי֑וֹן מְקַרְקַ֥ר קִ֖ר וְשׁ֥וֹעַ אֶל־הָהָֽר׃
Elam took up the quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir uncovered the shield.[^7]
וְעֵילָם֙ נָשָׂ֣א אַשְׁפָּ֔ה בְּרֶ֥כֶב אָדָ֖ם פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וְקִ֥יר עֵרָ֖ה מָגֵֽן׃
Your choicest valleys were full of chariots, and the horsemen took their positions at the gate.
וַיְהִ֥י מִבְחַר־עֲמָקַ֖יִךְ מָ֣לְאוּ רָ֑כֶב וְהַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים שֹׁ֖ת שָׁ֥תוּ הַשָּֽׁעְרָה׃
He removed the covering of Judah.[^8] On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest.[^9]
וַיְגַ֕ל אֵ֖ת מָסַ֣ךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַתַּבֵּט֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא אֶל־נֶ֖שֶׁק בֵּ֥ית הַיָּֽעַר׃
You saw that the breaches in the walls of the City of David were many, and you collected the waters of the Lower Pool.
וְאֵ֨ת בְּקִיעֵ֧י עִיר־דָּוִ֛ד רְאִיתֶ֖ם כִּי־רָ֑בּוּ וַֽתְּקַבְּצ֔וּ אֶת־מֵ֥י הַבְּרֵכָ֖ה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָֽה׃
You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore houses down to strengthen the wall.
וְאֶת־בָּתֵּ֥י יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם סְפַרְתֶּ֑ם וַתִּתְֿצוּ֙ הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים לְבַצֵּ֖ר הַחוֹמָֽה׃
You made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the Old Pool.[^10] But you did not look to the one who made it, or consider the one who planned it long ago.
וּמִקְוָ֣ה ׀ עֲשִׂיתֶ֗ם בֵּ֚ין הַחֹ֣מֹתַ֔יִם לְמֵ֖י הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הַיְשָׁנָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א הִבַּטְתֶּם֙ אֶל־עֹשֶׂ֔יהָ וְיֹצְרָ֥הּ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לֹ֥א רְאִיתֶֽם׃
On that day the Lord Yahweh of Armies called for weeping and mourning, for shaving the head and putting on sackcloth.
וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא לִבְכִי֙ וּלְמִסְפֵּ֔ד וּלְקָרְחָ֖ה וְלַחֲגֹ֥ר שָֽׂק׃
But look, there was joy and celebration, killing cattle and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"[^11]
וְהִנֵּ֣ה ׀ שָׂשׂ֣וֹן וְשִׂמְחָ֗ה הָרֹ֤ג ׀ בָּקָר֙ וְשָׁחֹ֣ט צֹ֔אן אָכֹ֥ל בָּשָׂ֖ר וְשָׁת֣וֹת יָ֑יִן אָכ֣וֹל וְשָׁת֔וֹ כִּ֥י מָחָ֖ר נָמֽוּת׃
Yahweh of Armies revealed himself in my hearing: Surely this guilt will not be atoned for you until you die, says the Lord Yahweh of Armies.
וְנִגְלָ֥ה בְאָזְנָ֖י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אִם־יְ֠כֻפַּר הֶעָוֺ֨ן הַזֶּ֤ה לָכֶם֙ עַד־תְּמֻת֔וּן אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ פ
This is what the Lord Yahweh of Armies says: Go, go to this steward, to Shebna, who is in charge of the palace:[^12]
כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת לֶךְ־בֹּא֙ אֶל־הַסֹּכֵ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה עַל־שֶׁבְנָ֖א אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־הַבָּֽיִת׃
What right do you have here, and whom do you have here, that you have cut out a tomb for yourself here, cutting out a tomb on the height, carving a resting place for himself in the rock?[^13]
מַה־לְּךָ֥ פֹה֙ וּמִ֣י לְךָ֣ פֹ֔ה כִּֽי־חָצַ֧בְתָּ לְּךָ֛ פֹּ֖ה קָ֑בֶר חֹצְבִ֤י מָרוֹם֙ קִבְר֔וֹ חֹקְקִ֥י בַסֶּ֖לַע מִשְׁכָּ֥ן לֽוֹ׃
Look, Yahweh is about to hurl you away violently, you strong man, and grasp you firmly.[^14]
הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ מְטַלְטֶלְךָ֔ טַלְטֵלָ֖ה גָּ֑בֶר וְעֹטְךָ֖ עָטֹֽה׃
He will roll you up tightly like a ball and throw you into a wide land. There you will die, and there your splendid chariots will be, you disgrace to your master's house!
צָנ֤וֹף יִצְנָפְךָ֙ צְנֵפָ֔ה כַּדּ֕וּר אֶל־אֶ֖רֶץ רַחֲבַ֣ת יָדָ֑יִם שָׁ֣מָּה תָמ֗וּת וְשָׁ֙מָּה֙ מַרְכְּב֣וֹת כְּבוֹדֶ֔ךָ קְל֖וֹן בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃
I will thrust you from your office, and he will pull you down from your position.
וַהֲדַפְתִּ֖יךָ מִמַּצָּבֶ֑ךָ וּמִמַּעֲמָֽדְךָ֖ יֶהֶרְסֶֽךָ׃
On that day I will call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּֽהוּ׃
I will clothe him with your robe and fasten your sash around him, and I will hand your authority over to him. He will be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
וְהִלְבַּשְׁתִּ֣יו כֻּתָּנְתֶּ֗ךָ וְאַבְנֵֽטְךָ֙ אֲחַזְּקֶ֔נּוּ וּמֶֽמְשֶׁלְתְּךָ֖ אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיָד֑וֹ וְהָיָ֥ה לְאָ֛ב לְיוֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם וּלְבֵ֥ית יְהוּדָֽה׃
I will place on his shoulder the key of the house of David. What he opens, no one will shut, and what he shuts, no one will open.[^15]
וְנָתַתִּ֛י מַפְתֵּ֥חַ בֵּית־דָּוִ֖ד עַל־שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וּפָתַח֙ וְאֵ֣ין סֹגֵ֔ר וְסָגַ֖ר וְאֵ֥ין פֹּתֵֽחַ׃
I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will become a seat of honor for his father's house.[^16]
וּתְקַעְתִּ֥יו יָתֵ֖ד בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן וְהָיָ֛ה לְכִסֵּ֥א כָב֖וֹד לְבֵ֥ית אָבִֽיו׃
They will hang on him all the weight[^17] of his father's house, offspring and offshoots, all the small vessels, from bowls to all the jars.
וְתָל֨וּ עָלָ֜יו כֹּ֣ל ׀ כְּב֣וֹד בֵּית־אָבִ֗יו הַצֶּֽאֱצָאִים֙ וְהַצְּפִע֔וֹת כֹּ֖ל כְּלֵ֣י הַקָּטָ֑ן מִכְּלֵי֙ הָֽאַגָּנ֔וֹת וְעַ֖ד כָּל־כְּלֵ֥י הַנְּבָלִֽים׃
On that day, declares Yahweh of Armies, the peg driven into a firm place will give way. It will be cut down and fall, and the load[^18] hanging on it will be cut off. For Yahweh has spoken.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת תָּמוּשׁ֙ הַיָּתֵ֔ד הַתְּקוּעָ֖ה בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן וְנִגְדְּעָ֣ה וְנָפְלָ֗ה וְנִכְרַת֙ הַמַּשָּׂ֣א אֲשֶׁר־עָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *massa*. See 13:1.
n.2: A name for Jerusalem, perhaps from a valley near the city where the prophet saw visions.
n.3: Literally "without the bow".
n.4: Literally "the daughter of my people", a tender name for the people pictured as a young woman.
n.5: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.6: Hebrew *meqarqar qir*, a phrase of uncertain meaning that echoes its own sounds. Perhaps "a shouting of 'Qir!'".
n.7: Kir, a region in Mesopotamia from which the Arameans came (Amos 9:7). Elam and Kir supplied troops to the Assyrian army.
n.8: Or "the defenses of Judah were stripped away".
n.9: The House of the Forest of Lebanon, a hall built by Solomon, named for its cedar pillars, where weapons were kept (1 Kings 7:2; 10:17).
n.10: Compare Hezekiah's work on Jerusalem's water supply before the Assyrian siege (2 Kings 20:20; 2 Chronicles 32:2–5, 30).
n.11: Paul quotes these words in 1 Corinthians 15:32.
n.12: Literally "who is over the house", the title of the king's chief minister. Shebna appears as secretary, with Eliakim in this office, in 36:3.
n.13: Literally "for himself". The Hebrew moves from "you" to "he".
n.14: Or "and wrap you up tightly". The meaning of verses 17–18 is uncertain in places.
n.15: Revelation 3:7 echoes this verse.
n.16: Literally "a throne of glory".
n.17: Hebrew *kavod*, "glory, weight".
n.18: Hebrew *massa*, the word translated "oracle" in verse 1.

v: An oracle[^1] concerning Tyre: Wail, you ships of Tarshish![^2] For Tyre is destroyed, without house or harbor.[^3] From the land of Cyprus[^4] the news has reached them.[^5]
מַשָּׂ֖א צֹ֑ר הֵילִ֣ילוּ ׀ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־שֻׁדַּ֤ד מִבַּ֙יִת֙ מִבּ֔וֹא מֵאֶ֥רֶץ כִּתִּ֖ים נִגְלָה־לָֽמוֹ׃
Be silent, you who live on the coast, you merchants of Sidon, whom the seafarers have made rich.[^6]
דֹּ֖מּוּ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי אִ֑י סֹחֵ֥ר צִיד֛וֹן עֹבֵ֥ר יָ֖ם מִלְאֽוּךְ׃
On the great waters came the grain of Shihor;[^7] the harvest of the Nile was her revenue, and she became the marketplace of the nations.
וּבְמַ֤יִם רַבִּים֙ זֶ֣רַע שִׁחֹ֔ר קְצִ֥יר יְא֖וֹר תְּבֽוּאָתָ֑הּ וַתְּהִ֖י סְחַ֥ר גּוֹיִֽם׃
Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea: "I have not been in labor or given birth; I have not raised young men or brought up young women."
בּ֣וֹשִׁי צִיד֔וֹן כִּֽי־אָמַ֣ר יָ֔ם מָע֥וֹז הַיָּ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹֽא־חַ֣לְתִּי וְלֹֽא־יָלַ֗דְתִּי וְלֹ֥א גִדַּ֛לְתִּי בַּחוּרִ֖ים רוֹמַ֥מְתִּי בְתוּלֽוֹת׃
When the report reaches Egypt, they will be in anguish at the report about Tyre.
כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־שֵׁ֖מַע לְמִצְרָ֑יִם יָחִ֖ילוּ כְּשֵׁ֥מַע צֹֽר׃
Cross over to Tarshish! Wail, you who live on the coast!
עִבְר֖וּ תַּרְשִׁ֑ישָׁה הֵילִ֖ילוּ יֹ֥שְׁבֵי אִֽי׃
Is this your joyful city,[^8] whose origin is from days of old, whose feet carried her to settle in distant places?
הֲזֹ֥את לָכֶ֖ם עַלִּיזָ֑ה מִֽימֵי־קֶ֤דֶם קַדְמָתָהּ֙ יֹבִל֣וּהָ רַגְלֶ֔יהָ מֵֽרָח֖וֹק לָגֽוּר׃
Who has planned this against Tyre, the giver of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traders[^9] are the honored of the earth?
מִ֚י יָעַ֣ץ זֹ֔את עַל־צֹ֖ר הַמַּֽעֲטִירָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר סֹחֲרֶ֙יה֙ שָׂרִ֔ים כִּנְעָנֶ֖יהָ נִכְבַדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃
Yahweh of Armies[^10] has planned it, to defile the pride of all glory and to humble all the honored of the earth.
יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת יְעָצָ֑הּ לְחַלֵּל֙ גְּא֣וֹן כָּל־צְבִ֔י לְהָקֵ֖ל כָּל־נִכְבַּדֵּי־אָֽרֶץ׃
Go through your land as the Nile does, Daughter Tarshish; there is no longer any restraint.[^11]
עִבְרִ֥י אַרְצֵ֖ךְ כַּיְאֹ֑ר בַּת־תַּרְשִׁ֕ישׁ אֵ֖ין מֵ֥זַח עֽוֹד׃
He has stretched out his hand over the sea and made kingdoms tremble. Yahweh has given orders concerning Canaan[^12] to destroy its strongholds.
יָדוֹ֙ נָטָ֣ה עַל־הַיָּ֔ם הִרְגִּ֖יז מַמְלָכ֑וֹת יְהוָה֙ צִוָּ֣ה אֶל־כְּנַ֔עַן לַשְׁמִ֖ד מָעֻזְנֶֽיהָ׃
He said, "You will no longer celebrate, you oppressed virgin Daughter Sidon! Get up, cross over to Cyprus; even there you will find no rest."
וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֥יפִי ע֖וֹד לַעְל֑וֹז הַֽמְעֻשָּׁקָ֞ה בְּתוּלַ֣ת בַּת־צִיד֗וֹן *כתיים **כִּתִּים֙ ק֣וּמִי עֲבֹ֔רִי גַּם־שָׁ֖ם לֹא־יָנ֥וּחַֽ לָֽךְ׃
Look at the land of the Chaldeans! This is the people that is no more. Assyria assigned it to desert creatures. They set up their siege towers; they stripped its palaces bare and made it a ruin.[^13]
הֵ֣ן ׀ אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה אַשּׁ֖וּר יְסָדָ֣הּ לְצִיִּ֑ים הֵקִ֣ימוּ *בחיניו **בַחוּנָ֗יו עֹרְרוּ֙ אַרְמְנוֹתֶ֔יהָ שָׂמָ֖הּ לְמַפֵּלָֽה׃
Wail, you ships of Tarshish, for your fortress is destroyed!
הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד מָעֻזְּכֶֽן׃ ס
On that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the lifetime of one king.[^14] At the end of seventy years it will be with Tyre as in the song about the prostitute:
וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְנִשְׁכַּ֤חַת צֹר֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה כִּימֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶחָ֑ד מִקֵּ֞ץ שִׁבְעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לְצֹ֔ר כְּשִׁירַ֖ת הַזּוֹנָֽה׃
"Take a lyre, go around the city, you forgotten prostitute! Play skillfully, sing many songs, so that you will be remembered."
קְחִ֥י כִנּ֛וֹר סֹ֥בִּי עִ֖יר זוֹנָ֣ה נִשְׁכָּחָ֑ה הֵיטִ֤יבִי נַגֵּן֙ הַרְבִּי־שִׁ֔יר לְמַ֖עַן תִּזָּכֵֽרִי׃
At the end of seventy years Yahweh will come to Tyre.[^15] She will return to her fees[^16] and will prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.
וְהָיָ֞ה מִקֵּ֣ץ ׀ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה יִפְקֹ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־צֹ֔ר וְשָׁבָ֖ה לְאֶתְנַנָּ֑ה וְזָֽנְתָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃

But her profit and her fees will be holy to Yahweh. They will not be stored up or hoarded, but her profit will go to those who live in Yahweh's presence, so that they may eat their fill and wear fine clothes.[^17]
וְהָיָ֨ה סַחְרָ֜הּ וְאֶתְנַנָּ֗הּ קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א יֵֽאָצֵ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יֵֽחָסֵ֑ן כִּ֣י לַיֹּשְׁבִ֞ים לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה סַחְרָ֔הּ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל לְשָׂבְעָ֖ה וְלִמְכַסֶּ֥ה עָתִֽיק׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *massa*. See 13:1.
n.2: Large seagoing ships, of the kind that sailed to Tarshish, a distant port in the west, perhaps in Spain (2:16). Also in verse 14.
n.3: Literally "it is destroyed, from house, from entering". The meaning is uncertain.
n.4: Hebrew *Kittim*, the people of Cyprus, later used of other peoples of the west. Also in verse 12.
n.5: Literally "it has been revealed to them".
n.6: Literally "who cross the sea have filled you".
n.7: An arm of the Nile in the eastern Delta, here standing for the Nile.
n.8: Literally "Is this for you the exultant one?"
n.9: Literally "her Canaanites". The Canaanites of the coast, the Phoenicians, were known as traders, so *Canaanite* came to mean "merchant".
n.10: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.11: Or "there is no longer a harbor". Hebrew *mezach*, perhaps "belt" or "dockyard". The meaning of the verse is uncertain.
n.12: Here Phoenicia, the coastal land of Tyre and Sidon.
n.13: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. It seems to point to the fate of Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, as a warning to Tyre.
n.14: Literally "like the days of one king", a normal human lifetime (Psalm 90:10).
n.15: Or "will visit". Hebrew *paqad*, to come to someone to deal with them, in blessing or in punishment.
n.16: Hebrew *etnan*, a prostitute's pay, here an image for Tyre's trade. Also in verse 18.
n.17: Literally "for a stately covering".

v: Look, Yahweh[^1] is about to empty the earth and lay it waste.[^2] He will twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants.
הִנֵּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בּוֹקֵ֥ק הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבֽוֹלְקָ֑הּ וְעִוָּ֣ה פָנֶ֔יהָ וְהֵפִ֖יץ יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ׃
It will be the same for people and priest, for servant and master, for maid and mistress, for buyer and seller, for lender and borrower, for creditor and debtor.
וְהָיָ֤ה כָעָם֙ כַּכֹּהֵ֔ן כַּעֶ֙בֶד֙ כַּֽאדֹנָ֔יו כַּשִּׁפְחָ֖ה כַּגְּבִרְתָּ֑הּ כַּקּוֹנֶה֙ כַּמּוֹכֵ֔ר כַּמַּלְוֶה֙ כַּלֹּוֶ֔ה כַּנֹּשֶׁ֕ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר נֹשֶׁ֥א בֽוֹ׃
The earth will be utterly emptied and utterly plundered, for Yahweh has spoken this word.
הִבּ֧וֹק ׀ תִּבּ֛וֹק הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהִבּ֣וֹז ׀ תִּבּ֑וֹז כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
The earth dries up[^3] and withers; the world languishes and withers; the highest of the people of the earth languish.
אָבְלָ֤ה נָֽבְלָה֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֻמְלְלָ֥ה נָבְלָ֖ה תֵּבֵ֑ל אֻמְלָ֖לוּ מְר֥וֹם עַם־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
The earth is defiled under its inhabitants, for they have broken the laws, violated the decree and broken the everlasting covenant.[^4]
וְהָאָ֥רֶץ חָנְפָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ כִּֽי־עָבְר֤וּ תוֹרֹת֙ חָ֣לְפוּ חֹ֔ק הֵפֵ֖רוּ בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃
Therefore a curse devours the earth, and its people bear their guilt. Therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned up,[^5] and few people are left.
עַל־כֵּ֗ן אָלָה֙ אָ֣כְלָה אֶ֔רֶץ וַֽיֶּאְשְׁמ֖וּ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ עַל־כֵּ֗ן חָרוּ֙ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי אֶ֔רֶץ וְנִשְׁאַ֥ר אֱנ֖וֹשׁ מִזְעָֽר׃
The new wine dries up; the vine languishes. All the merrymakers groan.
אָבַ֥ל תִּיר֖וֹשׁ אֻמְלְלָה־גָ֑פֶן נֶאֶנְח֖וּ כָּל־שִׂמְחֵי־לֵֽב׃
The joyful sound of tambourines has stopped; the noise of the revelers has ended; the joyful sound of the lyre has stopped.
שָׁבַת֙ מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ תֻּפִּ֔ים חָדַ֖ל שְׁא֣וֹן עַלִּיזִ֑ים שָׁבַ֖ת מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ כִּנּֽוֹר׃
They no longer drink wine with a song; beer is bitter to those who drink it.
בַּשִּׁ֖יר לֹ֣א יִשְׁתּוּ־יָ֑יִן יֵמַ֥ר שֵׁכָ֖ר לְשֹׁתָֽיו׃
The city of chaos[^6] is broken down; every house is shut up so that no one can enter.
נִשְׁבְּרָ֖ה קִרְיַת־תֹּ֑הוּ סֻגַּ֥ר כָּל־בַּ֖יִת מִבּֽוֹא׃
In the streets there is an outcry over wine; all joy has turned to gloom; the gladness of the earth has gone into exile.
צְוָחָ֥ה עַל־הַיַּ֖יִן בַּֽחוּצ֑וֹת עָֽרְבָה֙ כָּל־שִׂמְחָ֔ה גָּלָ֖ה מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Desolation is left in the city, and its gate is battered to ruins.
נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּעִ֖יר שַׁמָּ֑ה וּשְׁאִיָּ֖ה יֻכַּת־שָֽׁעַר׃
For so it will be in the middle of the earth, among the peoples: as when an olive tree is beaten, as at the gleaning when the grape harvest is over.
כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה יִהְיֶ֛ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָֽעַמִּ֑ים כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת כְּעוֹלֵלֹ֖ת אִם־כָּלָ֥ה בָצִֽיר׃
They raise their voices and shout for joy; they cry out from the west[^7] over the majesty of Yahweh.
הֵ֛מָּה יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם יָרֹ֑נּוּ בִּגְא֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה צָהֲל֖וּ מִיָּֽם׃
Therefore in the east[^8] give glory to Yahweh; in the coastlands of the sea, give glory to the name of Yahweh, the God of Israel.
עַל־כֵּ֥ן בָּאֻרִ֖ים כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה בְּאִיֵּ֣י הַיָּ֔ם שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס
From the ends of the earth we hear songs: "Glory[^9] to the Righteous One!" But I said, "I waste away, I waste away![^10] Woe is me! The traitors betray; with treachery the traitors betray!"[^11]
מִכְּנַ֨ף הָאָ֜רֶץ זְמִרֹ֤ת שָׁמַ֙עְנוּ֙ צְבִ֣י לַצַּדִּ֔יק וָאֹמַ֛ר רָזִי־לִ֥י רָֽזִי־לִ֖י א֣וֹי לִ֑י בֹּגְדִ֣ים בָּגָ֔דוּ וּבֶ֥גֶד בּוֹגְדִ֖ים בָּגָֽדוּ׃
Terror and pit and snare are upon you, you who live on the earth![^12]
פַּ֥חַד וָפַ֖חַת וָפָ֑ח עָלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

Whoever flees at the sound of terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare. For the windows of heaven are opened,[^13] and the foundations of the earth shake.
וֽ͏ְ֠הָיָה הַנָּ֞ס מִקּ֤וֹל הַפַּ֙חַד֙ יִפֹּ֣ל אֶל־הַפַּ֔חַת וְהָֽעוֹלֶה֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַפַּ֔חַת יִלָּכֵ֖ד בַּפָּ֑ח כִּֽי־אֲרֻבּ֤וֹת מִמָּרוֹם֙ נִפְתָּ֔חוּ וַֽיִּרְעֲשׁ֖וּ מ֥וֹסְדֵי אָֽרֶץ׃
The earth is utterly broken; the earth is split apart; the earth is violently shaken.
רֹ֥עָה הִֽתְרֹעֲעָ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ פּ֤וֹר הִֽתְפּוֹרְרָה֙ אֶ֔רֶץ מ֥וֹט הִֽתְמוֹטְטָ֖ה אָֽרֶץ׃
The earth staggers like a drunkard; it sways like a hut.[^14] Its rebellion lies heavy on it; it falls and will not rise again.
נ֣וֹעַ תָּנ֤וּעַ אֶ֙רֶץ֙ כַּשִּׁכּ֔וֹר וְהִֽתְנוֹדְדָ֖ה כַּמְּלוּנָ֑ה וְכָבַ֤ד עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ פִּשְׁעָ֔הּ וְנָפְלָ֖ה וְלֹא־תֹסִ֥יף קֽוּם׃ ס
On that day Yahweh will punish the host of heaven in heaven,[^15] and the kings of the earth on the earth.
וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִפְקֹ֧ד יְהוָ֛ה עַל־צְבָ֥א הַמָּר֖וֹם בַּמָּר֑וֹם וְעַל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
They will be gathered together like prisoners in a pit; they will be shut up in a prison, and after many days they will be punished.[^16]
וְאֻסְּפ֨וּ אֲסֵפָ֤ה אַסִּיר֙ עַל־בּ֔וֹר וְסֻגְּר֖וּ עַל־מַסְגֵּ֑ר וּמֵרֹ֥ב יָמִ֖ים יִפָּקֵֽדוּ׃
The moon will be ashamed and the sun abashed,[^17] for Yahweh of Armies[^18] will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and his glory will be before his elders.[^19]
וְחָֽפְרָה֙ הַלְּבָנָ֔ה וּבוֹשָׁ֖ה הַֽחַמָּ֑ה כִּֽי־מָלַ֞ךְ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת בְּהַ֤ר צִיּוֹן֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְנֶ֥גֶד זְקֵנָ֖יו כָּבֽוֹד׃ פ

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. Chapters 24–27 are often called the "Isaiah Apocalypse": poems about the judgment of the whole earth and the final triumph of God.
n.2: A play on sounds: *boqeq … u-voleqah*, "empty … and lay waste". Similar sound-plays run through verses 3, 4, 16, 17 and 19.
n.3: Or "mourns". Hebrew *avlah*, also in verse 7.
n.4: Perhaps the covenant with Noah and all living things (Genesis 9:16). *Laws* is Hebrew *torot*, "instructions"; *decree* is *choq*.
n.5: Or "dwindle". The meaning of the Hebrew verb is uncertain.
n.6: Hebrew *tohu*, the word for the "formless" earth in Genesis 1:2. The city is not named.
n.7: Literally "from the sea", the Mediterranean, to the west of Israel.
n.8: Hebrew *ba'urim*, perhaps "in the regions of light", where the sun rises. The meaning is uncertain.
n.9: Or "Beauty". Hebrew *tsevi*.
n.10: Hebrew *razi li*, a phrase of uncertain meaning, perhaps "leanness to me". The Vulgate reads "My secret is mine".
n.11: A play on words: *bogdim bagadu u-veged bogdim bagadu*.
n.12: A play on sounds: *pachad va-pachat va-fach*. Jeremiah 48:43–44 repeats verses 17–18.
n.13: As in the flood (Genesis 7:11).
n.14: A watchman's hut in a field (1:8).
n.15: Literally "the army of the height in the height": the heavenly powers, perhaps the stars, or the beings thought to rule the nations.
n.16: Or "visited". Hebrew *paqad* (verse 21).
n.17: Hebrew *levanah*, "the white one", and *chammah*, "the hot one", poetic names for the moon and the sun.
n.18: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.19: Literally "and before his elders, glory". Compare the elders who saw the God of Israel on Mount Sinai (Exodus 24:9–11).
