v: Yahweh,[^1] you are my God; I will exalt you; I will praise your name. For you have done wonderful things, plans formed long ago, faithful and sure.[^2]
יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהַי֙ אַתָּ֔ה אֲרֽוֹמִמְךָ֙ אוֹדֶ֣ה שִׁמְךָ֔ כִּ֥י עָשִׂ֖יתָ פֶּ֑לֶא עֵצ֥וֹת מֵֽרָח֖וֹק אֱמ֥וּנָה אֹֽמֶן׃
For you have made the city a heap of rubble, the fortified town a ruin. The palace of foreigners is a city no more; it will never be rebuilt.
כִּ֣י שַׂ֤מְתָּ מֵעִיר֙ לַגָּ֔ל קִרְיָ֥ה בְצוּרָ֖ה לְמַפֵּלָ֑ה אַרְמ֤וֹן זָרִים֙ מֵעִ֔יר לְעוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א יִבָּנֶֽה׃
Therefore a strong people will honor you; the city of ruthless nations will fear you.
עַל־כֵּ֖ן יְכַבְּד֣וּךָ עַם־עָ֑ז קִרְיַ֛ת גּוֹיִ֥ם עָרִיצִ֖ים יִירָאֽוּךָ׃
For you have been a refuge for the poor, a refuge for the needy in their distress, a shelter from the storm and a shade from the heat. For the breath of the ruthless is like a storm against a wall.
כִּֽי־הָיִ֨יתָ מָע֥וֹז לַדָּ֛ל מָע֥וֹז לָאֶבְי֖וֹן בַּצַּר־ל֑וֹ מַחְסֶ֤ה מִזֶּ֙רֶם֙ צֵ֣ל מֵחֹ֔רֶב כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ עָרִיצִ֖ים כְּזֶ֥רֶם קִֽיר׃
Like heat in a dry land, you subdue the uproar of foreigners. As heat is cooled by the shade of a cloud, so the song of the ruthless is silenced.
כְּחֹ֣רֶב בְּצָי֔וֹן שְׁא֥וֹן זָרִ֖ים תַּכְנִ֑יעַ חֹ֚רֶב בְּצֵ֣ל עָ֔ב זְמִ֥יר עָֽרִיצִ֖ים יַעֲנֶֽה׃ פ
On this mountain Yahweh of Armies[^3] will prepare for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of aged wine,[^4] of rich food full of marrow, of aged wine well refined.
וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת לְכָל־הָֽעַמִּים֙ בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה מִשְׁתֵּ֥ה שְׁמָנִ֖ים מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה שְׁמָרִ֑ים שְׁמָנִים֙ מְמֻ֣חָיִ֔ם שְׁמָרִ֖ים מְזֻקָּקִֽים׃
On this mountain he will swallow up the shroud that covers all peoples, the sheet that is spread over all nations.
וּבִלַּע֙ בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה פְּנֵֽי־הַלּ֥וֹט ׀ הַלּ֖וֹט עַל־כָּל־הָֽעַמִּ֑ים וְהַמַּסֵּכָ֥ה הַנְּסוּכָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִֽם׃
He will swallow up death forever.[^5] The Lord Yahweh will wipe away the tears from every face and remove the disgrace of his people from all the earth. For Yahweh has spoken.
בִּלַּ֤ע הַמָּ֙וֶת֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וּמָחָ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה דִּמְעָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל כָּל־פָּנִ֑ים וְחֶרְפַּ֣ת עַמּ֗וֹ יָסִיר֙ מֵעַ֣ל כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ פ
On that day they will say, "Look, this is our God; we waited for him, and he has saved us. This is Yahweh; we waited for him. Let us rejoice and be glad in his salvation."
וְאָמַר֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא הִנֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֥ינוּ זֶ֛ה קִוִּ֥ינוּ ל֖וֹ וְיֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נוּ זֶ֤ה יְהוָה֙ קִוִּ֣ינוּ ל֔וֹ נָגִ֥ילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָ֖ה בִּישׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃
For the hand of Yahweh will rest on this mountain. But Moab will be trampled down where he stands, as straw is trampled down in a dung pit.[^6]
כִּֽי־תָנ֥וּחַ יַד־יְהוָ֖ה בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְנָדוֹ֤[t]שׁ מוֹאָב֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו כְּהִדּ֥וּשׁ מַתְבֵּ֖ן *במי **בְּמ֥וֹ מַדְמֵנָֽה׃
He will spread out his hands in it, as a swimmer spreads out his hands to swim, but he will bring down his pride, for all the skill of his hands.[^7]
וּפֵרַ֤שׂ יָדָיו֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְפָרֵ֥שׂ הַשֹּׂחֶ֖ה לִשְׂח֑וֹת וְהִשְׁפִּיל֙ גַּֽאֲוָת֔וֹ עִ֖ם אָרְבּ֥וֹת יָדָֽיו׃
The high fortress of your walls he will bring down, lay low and cast to the ground, to the dust.
וּמִבְצַ֞ר מִשְׂגַּ֣ב חוֹמֹתֶ֗יךָ הֵשַׁ֥ח הִשְׁפִּ֛יל הִגִּ֥יעַ לָאָ֖רֶץ עַד־עָפָֽר׃ ס

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *emunah omen*, two words from the root *aman*, "be firm" (7:9).
n.3: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.4: Literally "of lees", wine left to mature on its sediment. Also later in the verse.
n.5: Or "in victory". Hebrew *lanetsach*. Paul quotes this line in 1 Corinthians 15:54, "Death has been swallowed up in victory". Revelation 7:17 and 21:4 echo the next line.
n.6: The Hebrew text is written "in the water of a dung pit" but read "in a dung pit". *Dung pit* (*madmenah*) sounds like Madmen, a town of Moab (Jeremiah 48:2).
n.7: *He* in the first line is probably Moab, and in the second Yahweh. *Skill* (Hebrew *arbot*) is uncertain; perhaps "the tricks" or "the strokes" of his hands.

v: On that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: "We have a strong city; he sets up salvation as its walls and ramparts.[^1]
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר־הַזֶּ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה עִ֣יר עָז־לָ֔נוּ יְשׁוּעָ֥ה יָשִׁ֖ית חוֹמ֥וֹת וָחֵֽל׃
Open the gates, so that the righteous nation may enter, the nation that keeps faith.
פִּתְח֖וּ שְׁעָרִ֑ים וְיָבֹ֥א גוֹי־צַדִּ֖יק שֹׁמֵ֥ר אֱמֻנִֽים׃
You keep in perfect peace[^2] the one whose mind is steadfast,[^3] because he trusts in you.
יֵ֣צֶר סָמ֔וּךְ תִּצֹּ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם ׀ שָׁל֑וֹם כִּ֥י בְךָ֖ בָּטֽוּחַ׃
Trust in Yahweh[^4] forever, for in Yah, Yahweh,[^5] you have an everlasting Rock.
בִּטְח֥וּ בַֽיהוָ֖ה עֲדֵי־עַ֑ד כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה צ֖וּר עוֹלָמִֽים׃
For he has brought down those who live on high, the lofty city. He lays it low, lays it low to the ground, and casts it down to the dust.
כִּ֤י הֵשַׁח֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י מָר֔וֹם קִרְיָ֖ה נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה יַשְׁפִּילֶ֤נָּה יַשְׁפִּילָהּ֙ עַד־אֶ֔רֶץ יַגִּיעֶ֖נָּה עַד־עָפָֽר׃
The foot tramples it, the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy."
תִּרְמְסֶ֖נָּה רָ֑גֶל רַגְלֵ֥י עָנִ֖י פַּעֲמֵ֥י דַלִּֽים׃
The path of the righteous is level; you, the Upright One, make smooth the way of the righteous.[^6]
אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים יָשָׁ֕ר מַעְגַּ֥ל צַדִּ֖יק תְּפַלֵּֽס׃
Yes, Yahweh, in the path of your judgments we wait for you. Your name and your renown are the desire of our soul.
אַ֣ף אֹ֧רַח מִשְׁפָּטֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה קִוִּינ֑וּךָ לְשִׁמְךָ֥ וּֽלְזִכְרְךָ֖ תַּאֲוַת־נָֽפֶשׁ׃
My soul longs for you in the night; yes, my spirit within me seeks you at dawn. For when your judgments come upon the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
נַפְשִׁ֤י אִוִּיתִ֙יךָ֙ בַּלַּ֔יְלָה אַף־רוּחִ֥י בְקִרְבִּ֖י אֲשַֽׁחֲרֶ֑ךָּ כִּ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר מִשְׁפָּטֶ֙יךָ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ צֶ֥דֶק לָמְד֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃
If the wicked are shown favor, they do not learn righteousness. In a land of honesty they act unjustly and do not see the majesty of Yahweh.
יֻחַ֤ן רָשָׁע֙ בַּל־לָמַ֣ד צֶ֔דֶק בְּאֶ֥רֶץ נְכֹח֖וֹת יְעַוֵּ֑ל וּבַל־יִרְאֶ֖ה גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה׃ ס
Yahweh, your hand is lifted up, but they do not see it. Let them see your zeal for your people and be ashamed; let the fire meant for your enemies consume them.
יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖ בַּל־יֶחֱזָי֑וּן יֶחֱז֤וּ וְיֵבֹ֙שׁוּ֙ קִנְאַת־עָ֔ם אַף־אֵ֖שׁ צָרֶ֥יךָ תֹאכְלֵֽם׃ ס
Yahweh, you will establish peace for us; indeed, all that we have done, you have done for us.
יְהוָ֕ה תִּשְׁפֹּ֥ת שָׁל֖וֹם לָ֑נוּ כִּ֛י גַּ֥ם כָּֽל־מַעֲשֵׂ֖ינוּ פָּעַ֥לְתָּ לָּֽנוּ׃
Yahweh our God, other lords besides you have ruled over us, but your name alone do we honor.[^7]
יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ בְּעָל֥וּנוּ אֲדֹנִ֖ים זֽוּלָתֶ֑ךָ לְבַד־בְּךָ֖ נַזְכִּ֥יר שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
The dead do not live; the shades[^8] do not rise. That is why you punished them and destroyed them, and wiped out all memory of them.
מֵתִים֙ בַּל־יִחְי֔וּ רְפָאִ֖ים בַּל־יָקֻ֑מוּ לָכֵ֤ן פָּקַ֙דְתָּ֙ וַתַּשְׁמִידֵ֔ם וַתְּאַבֵּ֥ד כָּל־זֵ֖כֶר לָֽמוֹ׃
You have enlarged the nation, Yahweh; you have enlarged the nation; you are glorified. You have extended all the borders of the land.
יָסַ֤פְתָּ לַגּוֹי֙ יְהוָ֔ה יָסַ֥פְתָּ לַגּ֖וֹי נִכְבָּ֑דְתָּ רִחַ֖קְתָּ כָּל־קַצְוֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
Yahweh, in distress they came looking for you; they poured out a whispered prayer when your discipline was on them.[^9]
יְהוָ֖ה בַּצַּ֣ר פְּקָד֑וּךָ צָק֣וּן לַ֔חַשׁ מוּסָרְךָ֖ לָֽמוֹ׃
As a pregnant woman about to give birth writhes and cries out in her pains, so were we because of you, Yahweh.
כְּמ֤וֹ הָרָה֙ תַּקְרִ֣יב לָלֶ֔דֶת תָּחִ֥יל תִּזְעַ֖ק בַּחֲבָלֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן הָיִ֥ינוּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה׃
We were pregnant, we writhed, but we gave birth only to wind. We have not brought salvation to the earth, and no inhabitants of the world have been born.[^10]
הָרִ֣ינוּ חַ֔לְנוּ כְּמ֖וֹ יָלַ֣דְנוּ ר֑וּחַ יְשׁוּעֹת֙ בַּל־נַ֣עֲשֶׂה אֶ֔רֶץ וּבַֽל־יִפְּל֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃
Your dead will live; my dead bodies will rise.[^11] Wake up and shout for joy, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is a dew of light,[^12] and the earth will give birth to the shades.[^13]
יִֽחְי֣וּ מֵתֶ֔יךָ נְבֵלָתִ֖י יְקוּמ֑וּן הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר כִּ֣י טַ֤ל אוֹרֹת֙ טַלֶּ֔ךָ וָאָ֖רֶץ רְפָאִ֥ים תַּפִּֽיל׃ ס
Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your door behind you.[^14] Hide for a little while, until the wrath has passed by.
לֵ֤ךְ עַמִּי֙ בֹּ֣א בַחֲדָרֶ֔יךָ וּֽסְגֹ֥ר *דלתיך **דְּלָתְךָ֖ בַּעֲדֶ֑ךָ חֲבִ֥י כִמְעַט־רֶ֖גַע עַד־*יעבור־**יַעֲבָר־זָֽעַם׃
For look, Yahweh is coming out from his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their guilt. The earth will uncover the blood shed on it and will no longer cover its slain.
כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֹצֵ֣א מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ לִפְקֹ֛ד עֲוֺ֥ן יֹֽשֵׁב־הָאָ֖רֶץ עָלָ֑יו וְגִלְּתָ֤ה הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֶת־דָּמֶ֔יהָ וְלֹֽא־תְכַסֶּ֥ה ע֖וֹד עַל־הֲרוּגֶֽיהָ׃ ס

n.1: Literally "salvation he sets up, walls and rampart". The song may end at verse 6; the prayer that follows runs to verse 19.
n.2: Literally "peace, peace". Hebrew *shalom shalom*, doubled for emphasis.
n.3: Hebrew *yetser*, "what is formed": the mind, its purpose and inclination.
n.4: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.5: Hebrew *Yah YHWH*. *Yah* is a short form of the name Yahweh (12:2).
n.6: Or "the path of the righteous is level; you make level the way of the righteous". Hebrew *yashar* can be a title, "Upright One", or mean "level".
n.7: Literally "only by you do we call your name to mind".
n.8: Hebrew *repha'im*, the spirits of the dead (14:9). Also in verse 19.
n.9: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. *Came looking for you* is Hebrew *peqadukha*, perhaps "they missed you".
n.10: Literally "have not fallen", that is, have not been born.
n.11: Literally "my corpse", a collective: the dead of the speaker's own people.
n.12: Or "a dew of herbs". Hebrew *orot* can mean "lights" or "plants" (2 Kings 4:39).
n.13: This verse is often read, with Daniel 12:2, as a promise that the dead will rise. Others take it as an image of the nation's revival, as in Ezekiel 37.
n.14: The Hebrew text is written "your doors" but read "your door".

v: On that day Yahweh[^1] will punish with his sword, hard and great and strong, Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the twisting serpent, and he will kill the dragon[^2] that is in the sea.[^3]

בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָה֩ בְּחַרְב֨וֹ הַקָּשָׁ֜ה וְהַגְּדוֹלָ֣ה וְהֽ͏ַחֲזָקָ֗ה עַ֤ל לִוְיָתָן֙ נָחָ֣שׁ בָּרִ֔חַ וְעַל֙ לִוְיָתָ֔ן נָחָ֖שׁ עֲקַלָּת֑וֹן וְהָרַ֥ג אֶת־הַתַּנִּ֖ין אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּיָּֽם׃ ס
On that day sing of a delightful vineyard:
בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ־לָֽהּ׃
I, Yahweh, am its keeper; I water it every moment. So that no one may harm it, I guard it night and day.
אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ לִרְגָעִ֖ים אַשְׁקֶ֑נָּה פֶּ֚ן יִפְקֹ֣ד עָלֶ֔יהָ לַ֥יְלָה וָי֖וֹם אֶצֳּרֶֽנָּה׃
I have no anger. If only there were briers and thorns to fight against! I would march against them; I would burn them all together.
חֵמָ֖ה אֵ֣ין לִ֑י מִֽי־יִתְּנֵ֜נִי שָׁמִ֥יר שַׁ֙יִת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה אֶפְשְׂעָ֥ה בָ֖הּ אֲצִיתֶ֥נָּה יָּֽחַד׃
Or else let them take hold of my protection; let them make peace with me; yes, let them make peace with me.
א֚וֹ יַחֲזֵ֣ק בְּמָעוּזִּ֔י יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה שָׁל֖וֹם לִ֑י שָׁל֖וֹם יֽ͏ַעֲשֶׂה־לִּֽי׃
In days to come[^4] Jacob will take root; Israel will blossom and sprout, and fill the face of the world with fruit.
הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב יָצִ֥יץ וּפָרַ֖ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּמָלְא֥וּ פְנֵי־תֵבֵ֖ל תְּנוּבָֽה׃ ס
Has he struck him as he struck those who struck him? Has he been killed as those who killed him were killed?[^5]
הַכְּמַכַּ֥ת מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ אִם־כְּהֶ֥רֶג הֲרֻגָ֖יו הֹרָֽג׃
By driving her away, by sending her off, you contended with her.[^6] He removed her with his fierce wind on the day of the east wind.
בְּסַּאסְּאָ֖ה בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה הָגָ֛ה בְּרוּח֥וֹ הַקָּשָׁ֖ה בְּי֥וֹם קָדִֽים׃

Therefore by this the guilt of Jacob will be atoned for, and this will be the full fruit of the removal of his sin: when he makes all the altar stones like chalk stones crushed to pieces, no Asherah poles[^7] or incense altars will be left standing.
לָכֵ֗ן בְּזֹאת֙ יְכֻפַּ֣ר עֲוֺֽן־יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְזֶ֕ה כָּל־פְּרִ֖י הָסִ֣ר חַטָּאת֑וֹ בְּשׂוּמ֣וֹ ׀ כָּל־אַבְנֵ֣י מִזְבֵּ֗חַ כְּאַבְנֵי־גִר֙ מְנֻפָּצ֔וֹת לֹֽא־יָקֻ֥מוּ אֲשֵׁרִ֖ים וְחַמָּנִֽים׃
For the fortified city is desolate, a settlement abandoned and deserted like the wilderness. There the calf grazes, there it lies down and strips its branches.
כִּ֣י עִ֤יר בְּצוּרָה֙ בָּדָ֔ד נָוֶ֕ה מְשֻׁלָּ֥ח וְנֶעֱזָ֖ב כַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר שָׁ֣ם יִרְעֶ֥ה עֵ֛גֶל וְשָׁ֥ם יִרְבָּ֖ץ וְכִלָּ֥ה סְעִפֶֽיהָ׃

When its twigs are dry, they are broken off; women come and make fires with them. For this is a people without understanding; therefore their Maker will have no compassion on them, and the one who formed them will show them no favor.
בִּיבֹ֤שׁ קְצִירָהּ֙ תִּשָּׁבַ֔רְנָה נָשִׁ֕ים בָּא֖וֹת מְאִיר֣וֹת אוֹתָ֑הּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א עַם־בִּינוֹת֙ ה֔וּא עַל־כֵּן֙ לֹֽא־יְרַחֲמֶ֣נּוּ עֹשֵׂ֔הוּ וְיֹצְר֖וֹ לֹ֥א יְחֻנֶּֽנּוּ׃ ס
On that day Yahweh will thresh from the flowing Euphrates[^8] to the Wadi of Egypt,[^9] and you will be gathered up one by one, people of Israel.
וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יַחְבֹּ֧ט יְהוָ֛ה מִשִּׁבֹּ֥לֶת הַנָּהָ֖ר עַד־נַ֣חַל מִצְרָ֑יִם וְאַתֶּ֧ם תְּלֻקְּט֛וּ לְאַחַ֥ד אֶחָ֖ד בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס

On that day a great ram's horn[^10] will be blown, and those who were perishing in the land of Assyria and those who were scattered in the land of Egypt will come and worship Yahweh on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִתָּקַע֮ בְּשׁוֹפָ֣ר גָּדוֹל֒ וּבָ֗אוּ הָאֹֽבְדִים֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אַשּׁ֔וּר וְהַנִדָּחִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהִשְׁתַּחֲו֧וּ לַיהוָ֛ה בְּהַ֥ר הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *tannin*, a sea monster or serpent (51:9; Genesis 1:21).
n.3: Leviathan is a sea monster, a picture of the forces of chaos that God overcomes (Psalm 74:13–14; Job 3:8). Older Canaanite poems from Ugarit describe the monster Litan in almost the same words: "the fleeing serpent, the twisting serpent".
n.4: Literally "Those who come". Or "In the coming days".
n.5: Israel has been struck, but not destroyed as its enemies were.
n.6: Hebrew *be-sa'se'ah*, a word found only here, perhaps "by measure" or "by driving away". *Her* is Israel, pictured as a woman sent away.
n.7: Hebrew *asherim*: wooden poles or trees that were symbols of the goddess Asherah. The *incense altars* (*chammanim*) are as in 17:8.
n.8: Literally "from the flowing stream of the River". Hebrew *shibbolet* can mean "flowing stream" or "ear of grain", a play on the image of threshing.
n.9: The Wadi el-Arish, the southwestern border of the promised land.
n.10: Hebrew *shofar*, a trumpet made from a ram's horn.

v: Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim,[^1] to the fading flower of its glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley,[^2] of those overcome by wine!
ה֗וֹי עֲטֶ֤רֶת גֵּאוּת֙ שִׁכֹּרֵ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְצִ֥יץ נֹבֵ֖ל צְבִ֣י תִפְאַרְתּ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֛ר עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ גֵּֽיא־שְׁמָנִ֖ים הֲל֥וּמֵי יָֽיִן׃
Look, the Lord has one who is mighty and strong. Like a storm of hail, a destroying wind, like a storm of mighty, flooding waters, he will throw it down to the ground with his hand.
הִנֵּ֨ה חָזָ֤ק וְאַמִּץ֙ לַֽאדֹנָ֔י כְּזֶ֥רֶם בָּרָ֖ד שַׂ֣עַר קָ֑טֶב כְּ֠זֶרֶם מַ֣יִם כַּבִּירִ֥ים שֹׁטְפִ֛ים הִנִּ֥יחַ לָאָ֖רֶץ בְּיָֽד׃
The proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trampled underfoot.
בְּרַגְלַ֖יִם תֵּֽרָמַ֑סְנָה עֲטֶ֥רֶת גֵּא֖וּת שִׁכּוֹרֵ֥י אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

And the fading flower of its glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, will be like a fig that ripens before the summer harvest: as soon as someone sees it, he swallows it while it is still in his hand.
וְֽהָ֨יְתָ֜ה צִיצַ֤ת נֹבֵל֙ צְבִ֣י תִפְאַרְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־רֹ֖אשׁ גֵּ֣יא שְׁמָנִ֑ים כְּבִכּוּרָהּ֙ בְּטֶ֣רֶם קַ֔יִץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִרְאֶ֤ה הָֽרֹאֶה֙ אוֹתָ֔הּ בְּעוֹדָ֥הּ בְּכַפּ֖וֹ יִבְלָעֶֽנָּה׃ ס
On that day Yahweh of Armies[^3] will be a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty for the remnant of his people,
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לַעֲטֶ֣רֶת צְבִ֔י וְלִצְפִירַ֖ת תִּפְאָרָ֑ה לִשְׁאָ֖ר עַמּֽוֹ׃
a spirit of justice for the one who sits in judgment, and strength for those who turn back the battle at the gate.
וּלְר֖וּחַ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט לַיּוֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־הַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְלִ֨גְבוּרָ֔ה מְשִׁיבֵ֥י מִלְחָמָ֖ה שָֽׁעְרָה׃ ס

But these too reel from wine and stagger from beer: priest and prophet reel from beer; they are swallowed up by wine; they stagger from beer; they reel when they see visions; they stumble when they give judgment.
וְגַם־אֵ֙לֶּה֙ בַּיַּ֣יִן שָׁג֔וּ וּבַשֵּׁכָ֖ר תָּע֑וּ כֹּהֵ֣ן וְנָבִיא֩ שָׁג֨וּ בַשֵּׁכָ֜ר נִבְלְע֣וּ מִן־הַיַּ֗יִן תָּעוּ֙ מִן־הַשֵּׁכָ֔ר שָׁגוּ֙ בָּֽרֹאֶ֔ה פָּק֖וּ פְּלִילִיָּֽה׃
For all the tables are covered with vomit; no place is without filth.
כִּ֚י כָּל־שֻׁלְחָנ֔וֹת מָלְא֖וּ קִ֣יא צֹאָ֑ה בְּלִ֖י מָקֽוֹם׃ ס
Whom is he trying to teach? To whom is he explaining his message? To children just weaned from milk, just taken from the breast?[^4]
אֶת־מִי֙ יוֹרֶ֣ה דֵעָ֔ה וְאֶת־מִ֖י יָבִ֣ין שְׁמוּעָ֑ה גְּמוּלֵי֙ מֵֽחָלָ֔ב עַתִּיקֵ֖י מִשָּׁדָֽיִם׃
For it is *tsav la-tsav, tsav la-tsav, qav la-qav, qav la-qav*, a little here, a little there.[^5]
כִּ֣י צַ֤ו לָצָו֙ צַ֣ו לָצָ֔ו קַ֥ו לָקָ֖ו קַ֣ו לָקָ֑ו זְעֵ֥יר שָׁ֖ם זְעֵ֥יר שָֽׁם׃
Very well, then: with stammering lips and in a foreign tongue he will speak to this people,[^6]
כִּ֚י בְּלַעֲגֵ֣י שָׂפָ֔ה וּבְלָשׁ֖וֹן אַחֶ֑רֶת יְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃
to whom he said, "This is the place of rest; give rest to the weary; this is the place of repose." But they would not listen.
אֲשֶׁ֣ר ׀ אָמַ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם זֹ֤את הַמְּנוּחָה֙ הָנִ֣יחוּ לֶֽעָיֵ֔ף וְזֹ֖את הַמַּרְגֵּעָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א אָב֖וּא שְׁמֽוֹעַ׃

So the word of Yahweh will be to them *tsav la-tsav, tsav la-tsav, qav la-qav, qav la-qav*, a little here, a little there, so that they will go and fall backward, be broken, be snared and be captured.
וְהָיָ֨ה לָהֶ֜ם דְּבַר־יְהוָ֗ה צַ֣ו לָצָ֞ו צַ֤ו לָצָו֙ קַ֤ו לָקָו֙ קַ֣ו לָקָ֔ו זְעֵ֥יר שָׁ֖ם זְעֵ֣יר שָׁ֑ם לְמַ֨עַן יֵלְכ֜וּ וְכָשְׁל֤וּ אָחוֹר֙ וְנִשְׁבָּ֔רוּ וְנוֹקְשׁ֖וּ וְנִלְכָּֽדוּ׃ פ
Therefore hear the word of Yahweh, you scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem![^7]
לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן מֹֽשְׁלֵי֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃

For you have said, "We have made a covenant with death,[^8] and with Sheol[^9] we have made an agreement. When the overwhelming scourge passes through,[^10] it will not reach us, for we have made lies our refuge and hidden ourselves in falsehood."

כִּ֣י אֲמַרְתֶּ֗ם כָּרַ֤תְנֽוּ בְרִית֙ אֶת־מָ֔וֶת וְעִם־שְׁא֖וֹל עָשִׂ֣ינוּ חֹזֶ֑ה *שיט **שׁ֣וֹט שׁוֹטֵ֤ף כִּֽי־*עבר **יֽ͏ַעֲבֹר֙ לֹ֣א יְבוֹאֵ֔נוּ כִּ֣י שַׂ֧מְנוּ כָזָ֛ב מַחְסֵ֖נוּ וּבַשֶּׁ֥קֶר נִסְתָּֽרְנוּ׃ ס
Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Look, I am laying in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a firm foundation.[^11] Whoever trusts will not panic.[^12]
לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֛י יִסַּ֥ד בְּצִיּ֖וֹן אָ֑בֶן אֶ֣בֶן בֹּ֜חַן פִּנַּ֤ת יִקְרַת֙ מוּסָ֣ד מוּסָּ֔ד הַֽמַּאֲמִ֖ין לֹ֥א יָחִֽישׁ׃
I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line. Hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and water will flood the hiding place.
וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י מִשְׁפָּט֙ לְקָ֔ו וּצְדָקָ֖ה לְמִשְׁקָ֑לֶת וְיָעָ֤ה בָרָד֙ מַחְסֵ֣ה כָזָ֔ב וְסֵ֥תֶר מַ֖יִם יִשְׁטֹֽפוּ׃
Your covenant with death will be annulled,[^13] and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled down by it.
וְכֻפַּ֤ר בְּרִֽיתְכֶם֙ אֶת־מָ֔וֶת וְחָזוּתְכֶ֥ם אֶת־שְׁא֖וֹל לֹ֣א תָק֑וּם שׁ֤וֹט שׁוֹטֵף֙ כִּ֣י יַֽעֲבֹ֔ר וִהְיִ֥יתֶם ל֖וֹ לְמִרְמָֽס׃
As often as it passes through, it will take you; morning after morning it will pass through, by day and by night. To understand the message will be sheer terror.
מִדֵּ֤י עָבְרוֹ֙ יִקַּ֣ח אֶתְכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־בַבֹּ֧קֶר בַּבֹּ֛קֶר יַעֲבֹ֖ר בַּיּ֣וֹם וּבַלָּ֑יְלָה וְהָיָ֥ה רַק־זְוָעָ֖ה הָבִ֥ין שְׁמוּעָֽה׃
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too narrow to wrap around you.
כִּֽי־קָצַ֥ר הַמַּצָּ֖ע מֵֽהִשְׂתָּרֵ֑עַ וְהַמַסֵּכָ֥ה צָ֖רָה כְּהִתְכַּנֵּֽס׃
For Yahweh will rise up as at Mount Perazim; he will rage as in the valley of Gibeon,[^14] to do his work, his strange work, and to perform his task, his alien task.
כִּ֤י כְהַר־פְּרָצִים֙ יָק֣וּם יְהוָ֔ה כְּעֵ֖מֶק בְּגִבְע֣וֹן יִרְגָּ֑ז לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ זָ֣ר מַעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ וְלַֽעֲבֹד֙ עֲבֹ֣דָת֔וֹ נָכְרִיָּ֖ה עֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃
So now, stop your scoffing, or your chains will be made heavier. For I have heard from the Lord Yahweh of Armies a decree of destruction against the whole land.[^15]
וְעַתָּה֙ אַל־תִּתְלוֹצָ֔צוּ פֶּֽן־יֶחְזְק֖וּ מֽוֹסְרֵיכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־כָלָ֨ה וְנֶחֱרָצָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי מֵאֵ֨ת אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת עַל־כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Listen and hear my voice; pay attention and hear what I say.
הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי׃
Does the plowman plow all day to plant seed? Does he keep on breaking up and harrowing his ground?
הֲכֹ֣ל הַיּ֔וֹם יַחֲרֹ֥שׁ הַחֹרֵ֖שׁ לִזְרֹ֑עַ יְפַתַּ֥ח וִֽיַשַׂדֵּ֖ד אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃
When he has leveled its surface, does he not scatter dill and sow cumin? Does he not put wheat in rows, barley in its place, and spelt at its border?[^16]
הֲלוֹא֙ אִם־שִׁוָּ֣ה פָנֶ֔יהָ וְהֵפִ֥יץ קֶ֖צַח וְכַמֹּ֣ן יִזְרֹ֑ק וְשָׂ֨ם חִטָּ֤ה שׂוֹרָה֙ וּשְׂעֹרָ֣ה נִסְמָ֔ן וְכֻסֶּ֖מֶת גְּבֻלָתֽוֹ׃
His God instructs him and teaches him the right way.[^17]
וְיִסְּר֥וֹ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט אֱלֹהָ֥יו יוֹרֶֽנּוּ׃
Dill is not threshed with a threshing sledge, and a cartwheel is not rolled over cumin. Dill is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
כִּ֣י לֹ֤א בֶֽחָרוּץ֙ י֣וּדַשׁ קֶ֔צַח וְאוֹפַ֣ן עֲגָלָ֔ה עַל־כַּמֹּ֖ן יוּסָּ֑ב כִּ֧י בַמַּטֶּ֛ה יֵחָ֥בֶט קֶ֖צַח וְכַמֹּ֥ן בַּשָּֽׁבֶט׃
Grain for bread is crushed, but not endlessly; he does not keep threshing it forever. He drives the wheel of his cart and his horses over it, but he does not crush it.
לֶ֣חֶם יוּדָ֔ק כִּ֛י לֹ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח אָד֣וֹשׁ יְדוּשֶׁ֑נּוּ וְ֠הָמַם גִּלְגַּ֧ל עֶגְלָת֛וֹ וּפָרָשָׁ֖יו לֹֽא־יְדֻקֶּֽנּוּ׃
This also comes from Yahweh of Armies. His counsel is wonderful, and his wisdom is great.[^18]
גַּם־זֹ֕את מֵעִ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת יָצָ֑אָה הִפְלִ֣יא עֵצָ֔ה הִגְדִּ֖יל תּוּשִׁיָּֽה׃ ס

n.1: Samaria, capital of the northern kingdom (Ephraim), stood on a hill above a fertile valley like a crown or garland on a drinker's head. It fell to Assyria in 722 BC.
n.2: Literally "the valley of fatness". Also in verse 4.
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.4: Verses 9–10 are probably the words of the drunken priests and prophets, mocking Isaiah's teaching as fit only for small children.
n.5: The Hebrew is a string of short sounds, perhaps baby talk, or the drunken mockery of a teacher. It may also be understood as "command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line", since *tsav* may come from the word for "command" and *qav* means "measuring line" (verse 17). Some think of the letters *tsade* and *qof* recited by children learning the alphabet. Also in verse 13.
n.6: The foreign speech of Assyrian soldiers. Paul quotes verses 11–12 in 1 Corinthians 14:21.
n.7: Or "you scoffers who make proverbs for this people". Hebrew *moshle* can mean "rulers" or "speakers of sayings".
n.8: Hebrew *mavet*. In Canaanite stories *Mot*, "Death", was also the name of a god of the underworld.
n.9: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead. Also in verse 18. *Agreement* is literally "vision" or "seer" (*chozeh*), perhaps a pact made through a seer.
n.10: The Hebrew text is written "passed" but read "passes".
n.11: Literally "Look, I have laid". The form of the Hebrew verb is unusual.
n.12: Or "will not be in a hurry". The Septuagint reads "will not be put to shame", and Romans 9:33; 10:11 and 1 Peter 2:6 quote the verse in that form.
n.13: Literally "covered over", the verb used for atonement, here perhaps "wiped out".
n.14: Where David defeated the Philistines (2 Samuel 5:20, 25; 1 Chronicles 14:16), and where Yahweh fought for Joshua at Gibeon (Joshua 10:10–14).
n.15: Or "against the whole earth". Compare 10:23.
n.16: The words translated *in rows* and *in its place* are uncertain.
n.17: Literally "for judgment", that is, the proper way to do things.
n.18: Hebrew *tushiyyah*, practical wisdom that brings success.

v: Woe to Ariel, Ariel,[^1] the city where David camped! Add year to year; let the festivals run their round.
ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל קִרְיַ֖ת חָנָ֣ה דָוִ֑ד סְפ֥וּ שָׁנָ֛ה עַל־שָׁנָ֖ה חַגִּ֥ים יִנְקֹֽפוּ׃
Yet I will bring distress on Ariel. There will be mourning and lamenting,[^2] and she will be to me like an altar hearth.[^3]
וַהֲצִיק֖וֹתִי לַֽאֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְהָיְתָ֤ה תַֽאֲנִיָּה֙ וַֽאֲנִיָּ֔ה וְהָ֥יְתָה לִּ֖י כַּאֲרִיאֵֽל׃
I will camp against you all around;[^4] I will besiege you with towers and set up siege works against you.
וְחָנִ֥יתִי כַדּ֖וּר עָלָ֑יִךְ וְצַרְתִּ֤י עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ מֻצָּ֔ב וַהֲקֽ͏ִימֹתִ֥י עָלַ֖יִךְ מְצֻרֹֽת׃
Brought low, you will speak from the ground, and your words will come muffled from the dust. Your voice will come from the ground like a ghost's,[^5] and your words will whisper from the dust.
וְשָׁפַלְתְּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ תְּדַבֵּ֔רִי וּמֵֽעָפָ֖ר תִּשַּׁ֣ח אִמְרָתֵ֑ךְ וְֽ֠הָיָה כְּא֤וֹב מֵאֶ֙רֶץ֙ קוֹלֵ֔ךְ וּמֵעָפָ֖ר אִמְרָתֵ֥ךְ תְּצַפְצֵֽף׃
But the horde of your foes[^6] will be like fine dust, the horde of the ruthless like chaff blowing away. Suddenly, in an instant,
וְהָיָ֛ה כְּאָבָ֥ק דַּ֖ק הֲמ֣וֹן זָרָ֑יִךְ וּכְמֹ֤ץ עֹבֵר֙ הֲמ֣וֹן עָֽרִיצִ֔ים וְהָיָ֖ה לְפֶ֥תַע פִּתְאֹֽם׃
you will be visited by Yahweh of Armies[^7] with thunder and earthquake and great noise, with whirlwind and storm and the flame of a devouring fire.
מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד בְּרַ֥עַם וּבְרַ֖עַשׁ וְק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל סוּפָה֙ וּסְעָרָ֔ה וְלַ֖הַב אֵ֥שׁ אוֹכֵלָֽה׃
The horde of all the nations that fight against Ariel, all who attack her and her stronghold and bring distress on her, will be like a dream, a vision in the night.
וְהָיָ֗ה כַּֽחֲלוֹם֙ חֲז֣וֹן לַ֔יְלָה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־אֲרִיאֵ֑ל וְכָל־צֹבֶ֙יהָ֙ וּמְצֹ֣דָתָ֔הּ וְהַמְּצִיקִ֖ים לָֽהּ׃

It will be as when a hungry man dreams that he is eating, but he wakes up, and his hunger is not satisfied, or as when a thirsty man dreams that he is drinking, but he wakes up faint, and his thirst is not quenched.[^8] So it will be with the horde of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion.

וְהָיָ֡ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יַחֲלֹ֨ם הָרָעֵ֜ב וְהִנֵּ֣ה אוֹכֵ֗ל וְהֵקִיץ֮ וְרֵיקָ֣ה נַפְשׁוֹ֒ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר יַחֲלֹ֤ם הַצָּמֵא֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה שֹׁתֶ֔ה וְהֵקִיץ֙ וְהִנֵּ֣ה עָיֵ֔ף וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ שׁוֹקֵקָ֑ה כֵּ֣ן יִֽהְיֶ֗ה הֲמוֹן֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַצֹּבְאִ֖ים עַל־הַ֥ר צִיּֽוֹן׃ ס
Be stunned and stay stunned; blind yourselves and be blind! Be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not with beer![^9]
הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתּֽ͏ַעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ שָֽׁכְר֣וּ וְלֹא־יַ֔יִן נָע֖וּ וְלֹ֥א שֵׁכָֽר׃
For Yahweh has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes, the prophets, and covered your heads, the seers.[^10]
כִּֽי־נָסַ֨ךְ עֲלֵיכֶ֤ם יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ תַּרְדֵּמָ֔ה וַיְעַצֵּ֖ם אֶת־עֵֽינֵיכֶ֑ם אֶת־הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים וְאֶת־רָאשֵׁיכֶ֥ם הַחֹזִ֖ים כִּסָּֽה׃
For you this whole vision has become like the words of a sealed scroll. When they give it to someone who can read[^11] and say, "Read this, please," he answers, "I cannot, for it is sealed."
וַתְּהִ֨י לָכֶ֜ם חָז֣וּת הַכֹּ֗ל כְּדִבְרֵי֮ הַסֵּ֣פֶר הֶֽחָתוּם֒ אֲשֶֽׁר־יִתְּנ֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־יוֹדֵ֥עַ *הספר **סֵ֛פֶר לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־זֶ֑ה וְאָמַר֙ לֹ֣א אוּכַ֔ל כִּ֥י חָת֖וּם הֽוּא׃
Or when they give the scroll to someone who cannot read and say, "Read this, please," he answers, "I cannot read."
וְנִתַּ֣ן הַסֵּ֗פֶר עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יָדַ֥ע סֵ֛פֶר לֵאמֹ֖ר קְרָ֣א נָא־זֶ֑ה וְאָמַ֕ר לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי סֵֽפֶר׃ ס
The Lord said: Because this people draw near with their mouth and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their fear of me is a human command learned by rote,[^12]
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י יַ֚עַן כִּ֤י נִגַּשׁ֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה בְּפִ֤יו וּבִשְׂפָתָיו֙ כִּבְּד֔וּנִי וְלִבּ֖וֹ רִחַ֣ק מִמֶּ֑נִּי וַתְּהִ֤י יִרְאָתָם֙ אֹתִ֔י מִצְוַ֥ת אֲנָשִׁ֖ים מְלֻמָּדָֽה׃
therefore, look, I will again do amazing things with this people, wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of their wise will perish, and the understanding of their discerning will vanish.[^13]
לָכֵ֗ן הִנְנִ֥י יוֹסִ֛ף לְהַפְלִ֥יא אֶת־הָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה הַפְלֵ֣א וָפֶ֑לֶא וְאָֽבְדָה֙ חָכְמַ֣ת חֲכָמָ֔יו וּבִינַ֥ת נְבֹנָ֖יו תִּסְתַּתָּֽר׃ ס
Woe to those who go to great depths to hide their plans from Yahweh, whose deeds are done in the dark, and who say, "Who sees us? Who knows us?"
ה֛וֹי הַמַּעֲמִיקִ֥ים מֵֽיהוָ֖ה לַסְתִּ֣ר עֵצָ֑ה וְהָיָ֤ה בְמַחְשָׁךְ֙ מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֥י רֹאֵ֖נוּ וּמִ֥י יוֹדְעֵֽנוּ׃

How you turn things upside down! Should the potter be thought of as the clay? Should what is made say of its maker, "He did not make me"? Should the pot say of the potter, "He has no understanding"?[^14]
הַ֨פְכְּכֶ֔ם אִם־כְּחֹ֥מֶר הַיֹּצֵ֖ר יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב כִּֽי־יֹאמַ֨ר מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה לְעֹשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ לֹ֣א עָשָׂ֔נִי וְיֵ֛צֶר אָמַ֥ר לְיוֹצְר֖וֹ לֹ֥א הֵבִֽין׃
In a very little while, will not Lebanon be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be thought of as a forest?[^15]
הֲלוֹא־עוֹד֙ מְעַ֣ט מִזְעָ֔ר וְשָׁ֥ב לְבָנ֖וֹן לַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב׃
On that day the deaf will hear the words of a scroll, and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
וְשָׁמְע֧וּ בַיּוֹם־הַה֛וּא הַחֵרְשִׁ֖ים דִּבְרֵי־סֵ֑פֶר וּמֵאֹ֣פֶל וּמֵחֹ֔שֶׁךְ עֵינֵ֥י עִוְרִ֖ים תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃
The humble will again rejoice in Yahweh, and the poorest of people will exult in the Holy One of Israel.
וְיָסְפ֧וּ עֲנָוִ֛ים בַּֽיהוָ֖ה שִׂמְחָ֑ה וְאֶבְיוֹנֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יָגִֽילוּ׃
For the ruthless will be gone, the scoffer will come to an end, and all who watch for a chance to do evil will be cut off,
כִּֽי־אָפֵ֥ס עָרִ֖יץ וְכָ֣לָה לֵ֑ץ וְנִכְרְת֖וּ כָּל־שֹׁ֥קְדֵי אָֽוֶן׃
those who make a person guilty with a word,[^16] who lay a trap for the one who argues for justice at the gate,[^17] and with empty claims[^18] turn aside the innocent.
מַחֲטִיאֵ֤י אָדָם֙ בְּדָבָ֔ר וְלַמּוֹכִ֥יחַ בַּשַּׁ֖עַר יְקֹשׁ֑וּן וַיַּטּ֥וּ בַתֹּ֖הוּ צַדִּֽיק׃ ס
Therefore this is what Yahweh, who redeemed Abraham, says to the house of Jacob: Jacob will no longer be ashamed; his face will no longer grow pale.
לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּדָ֖ה אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם לֹֽא־עַתָּ֤ה יֵבוֹשׁ֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְלֹ֥א עַתָּ֖ה פָּנָ֥יו יֶחֱוָֽרוּ׃
For when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in his midst, they will treat my name as holy. They will treat the Holy One of Jacob as holy and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
כִּ֣י בִ֠רְאֹתוֹ יְלָדָ֞יו מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדַ֛י בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ יַקְדִּ֣ישֽׁוּ שְׁמִ֑י וְהִקְדִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ אֶת־קְד֣וֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְאֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יַעֲרִֽיצוּ׃
Those who go astray in spirit will gain understanding, and those who grumble will accept instruction.
וְיָדְע֥וּ תֹֽעֵי־ר֖וּחַ בִּינָ֑ה וְרוֹגְנִ֖ים יִלְמְדוּ־לֶֽקַח׃

n.1: A name for Jerusalem. Hebrew *ari'el* can mean "lion of God", but in Ezekiel 43:15–16 it is the "altar hearth" where sacrifices were burned (verse 2).
n.2: A play on sounds: *ta'aniyyah va-aniyyah*.
n.3: Hebrew *ari'el*. Jerusalem will become like the place of burning on the altar.
n.4: Literally "like a circle". The Septuagint reads "like David", whose camp is named in verse 1.
n.5: Hebrew *ov*, the spirit of a dead person called up by a medium (8:19), thought to speak in a faint whisper.
n.6: Literally "your strangers".
n.7: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.8: Literally "his *nephesh* is empty … his *nephesh* is longing". Hebrew *nephesh* here means "throat, appetite".
n.9: Plays on sounds: *hitmahmehu u-temahu, hishta'ash'u va-sho'u*.
n.10: *The prophets* and *the seers* may explain what *your eyes* and *your heads* mean.
n.11: Literally "who knows writing". The Hebrew text is written "who knows the scroll" but read "who knows writing".
n.12: Literally "a commandment of human beings, taught". Jesus quotes verse 13 in Mark 7:6–7 and Matthew 15:8–9, following the Septuagint: "They worship me in vain, teaching human rules as if they were doctrines."
n.13: Paul quotes the last part of this verse in 1 Corinthians 1:19, following the Septuagint.
n.14: Compare 45:9 and Romans 9:20.
n.15: Hebrew *karmel*, "garden land, orchard" (10:18). The great forest will become farmland, and farmland will grow wild, a reversal of the present order.
n.16: Or "who condemn a person in a lawsuit". Hebrew *davar* means "word" or "case".
n.17: The town gate was where cases were heard and judged.
n.18: Hebrew *tohu*, "emptiness" (24:10).

v: Woe to the rebellious children, declares Yahweh,[^1] who carry out plans that are not mine, and make an alliance,[^2] but not by my Spirit,[^3] heaping sin on sin,
ה֣וֹי בָּנִ֤ים סֽוֹרְרִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת עֵצָה֙ וְלֹ֣א מִנִּ֔י וְלִנְסֹ֥ךְ מַסֵּכָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א רוּחִ֑י לְמַ֛עַן סְפ֥וֹת חַטָּ֖את עַל־חַטָּֽאת׃
who set out to go down to Egypt without asking my advice,[^4] to take refuge in Pharaoh's protection and to shelter in Egypt's shade!
הַהֹלְכִים֙ לָרֶ֣דֶת מִצְרַ֔יִם וּפִ֖י לֹ֣א שָׁאָ֑לוּ לָעוֹז֙ בְּמָע֣וֹז פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלַחְס֖וֹת בְּצֵ֥ל מִצְרָֽיִם׃
But Pharaoh's protection will be your shame, and shelter in Egypt's shade your disgrace.
וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם מָע֥וֹז פַּרְעֹ֖ה לְבֹ֑שֶׁת וְהֶחָס֥וּת בְּצֵל־מִצְרַ֖יִם לִכְלִמָּֽה׃
For though his officials are in Zoan and his envoys have reached Hanes,[^5]
כִּֽי־הָי֥וּ בְצֹ֖עַן שָׂרָ֑יו וּמַלְאָכָ֖יו חָנֵ֥ס יַגִּֽיעוּ׃
everyone will be put to shame[^6] because of a people who cannot help them, who bring neither help nor benefit, but only shame and disgrace.
כֹּ֣ל *הבאיש **הֹבִ֔ישׁ עַל־עַ֖ם לֹא־יוֹעִ֣ילוּ לָ֑מוֹ לֹ֤א לְעֵ֙זֶר֙ וְלֹ֣א לְהוֹעִ֔יל כִּ֥י לְבֹ֖שֶׁת וְגַם־לְחֶרְפָּֽה׃ ס

An oracle[^7] concerning the animals of the Negev:[^8] Through a land of trouble and distress, of lioness and lion, of viper and flying serpent,[^9] they carry their wealth on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people that cannot help them.

מַשָּׂ֖א בַּהֲמ֣וֹת נֶ֑גֶב בְּאֶרֶץ֩ צָרָ֨ה וְצוּקָ֜ה לָבִ֧יא וָלַ֣יִשׁ מֵהֶ֗ם אֶפְעֶה֙ וְשָׂרָ֣ף מְעוֹפֵ֔ף יִשְׂאוּ֩ עַל־כֶּ֨תֶף עֲיָרִ֜ים חֵֽילֵהֶ֗ם וְעַל־דַּבֶּ֤שֶׁת גְּמַלִּים֙ אֽוֹצְרֹתָ֔ם עַל־עַ֖ם לֹ֥א יוֹעִֽילוּ׃
Egypt's help is worthless and empty. Therefore I have called her "Rahab, who sits still."[^10]
וּמִצְרַ֕יִם הֶ֥בֶל וָרִ֖יק יַעְזֹ֑רוּ לָכֵן֙ קָרָ֣אתִי לָזֹ֔את רַ֥הַב הֵ֖ם שָֽׁבֶת׃
Now go, write it on a tablet in their presence, and inscribe it in a scroll, so that it may be there for the time to come, forever and ever.[^11]
עַתָּ֗ה בּ֣וֹא כָתְבָ֥הּ עַל־ל֛וּחַ אִתָּ֖ם וְעַל־סֵ֣פֶר חֻקָּ֑הּ וּתְהִי֙ לְי֣וֹם אַחֲר֔וֹן לָעַ֖ד עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
For they are a rebellious people, lying children, children unwilling to listen to the instruction[^12] of Yahweh,
כִּ֣י עַ֤ם מְרִי֙ ה֔וּא בָּנִ֖ים כֶּחָשִׁ֑ים בָּנִ֕ים לֹֽא־אָב֥וּ שְׁמ֖וֹעַ תּוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃
who say to the seers, "Do not see!" and to the prophets, "Do not prophesy to us what is right! Tell us smooth things; prophesy illusions!
אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמְר֤וּ לָֽרֹאִים֙ לֹ֣א תִרְא֔וּ וְלַ֣חֹזִ֔ים לֹ֥א תֶחֱזוּ־לָ֖נוּ נְכֹח֑וֹת דַּבְּרוּ־לָ֣נוּ חֲלָק֔וֹת חֲז֖וּ מַהֲתַלּֽוֹת׃
Get out of the way; turn aside from the path; stop confronting us with the Holy One of Israel!"[^13]
ס֚וּרוּ מִנֵּי־דֶ֔רֶךְ הַטּ֖וּ מִנֵּי־אֹ֑רַח הַשְׁבִּ֥יתוּ מִפָּנֵ֖ינוּ אֶת־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס
Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says: Because you have rejected this word and trusted in oppression and deceit, and relied on them,
לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַ֥עַן מָֽאָסְכֶ֖ם בַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַֽתִּבְטְחוּ֙ בְּעֹ֣שֶׁק וְנָל֔וֹז וַתִּֽשָּׁעֲנ֖וּ עָלָֽיו׃
this guilt will be for you like a breach in a high wall, bulging out and about to fall, whose collapse comes suddenly, in an instant.
לָכֵ֗ן יִֽהְיֶ֤ה לָכֶם֙ הֶעָוֺ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה כְּפֶ֣רֶץ נֹפֵ֔ל נִבְעֶ֖ה בְּחוֹמָ֣ה נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־פִּתְאֹ֥ם לְפֶ֖תַע יָב֥וֹא שִׁבְרָֽהּ׃
It will break like a potter's jar, smashed so ruthlessly that among its pieces not a fragment is found to take fire from a hearth or to scoop water from a cistern.
וּ֠שְׁבָרָהּ כְּשֵׁ֨בֶר נֵ֧בֶל יוֹצְרִ֛ים כָּת֖וּת לֹ֣א יַחְמֹ֑ל וְלֹֽא־יִמָּצֵ֤א בִמְכִתָּתוֹ֙ חֶ֔רֶשׂ לַחְתּ֥וֹת אֵשׁ֙ מִיָּק֔וּד וְלַחְשֹׂ֥ף מַ֖יִם מִגֶּֽבֶא׃ פ
For this is what the Lord Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, says: In returning and rest you will be saved; in quietness and trust will be your strength. But you were not willing.
כִּ֣י כֹֽה־אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּשׁוּבָ֤ה וָנַ֙חַת֙ תִּוָּ֣שֵׁע֔וּן בְּהַשְׁקֵט֙ וּבְבִטְחָ֔ה תִּהְיֶ֖ה גְּבֽוּרַתְכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֖א אֲבִיתֶֽם׃
You said, "No! We will flee on horses." So you will flee! "We will ride on swift horses." So your pursuers will be swift![^14]
וַתֹּ֨אמְר֥וּ לֹא־כִ֛י עַל־ס֥וּס נָנ֖וּס עַל־כֵּ֣ן תְּנוּס֑וּן וְעַל־קַ֣ל נִרְכָּ֔ב עַל־כֵּ֖ן יִקַּ֥לּוּ רֹדְפֵיכֶֽם׃
A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will all flee, until you are left like a flagpole on a mountaintop, like a signal flag on a hill.
אֶ֣לֶף אֶחָ֗ד מִפְּנֵי֙ גַּעֲרַ֣ת אֶחָ֔ד מִפְּנֵ֛י גַּעֲרַ֥ת חֲמִשָּׁ֖ה תָּנֻ֑סוּ עַ֣ד אִם־נוֹתַרְתֶּ֗ם כַּתֹּ֙רֶן֙ עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֔ר וְכַנֵּ֖ס עַל־הַגִּבְעָֽה׃
Therefore Yahweh waits to be gracious to you; therefore he rises to show you compassion. For Yahweh is a God of justice. Happy are all who wait for him![^15]
וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽחֲנַנְכֶ֔ם וְלָכֵ֥ן יָר֖וּם לְרַֽחֶמְכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אֱלֹהֵ֤י מִשְׁפָּט֙ יְהוָ֔ה אַשְׁרֵ֖י כָּל־ח֥וֹכֵי לֽוֹ׃ ס
You people in Zion, who live in Jerusalem,[^16] you will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your cry; as soon as he hears it, he will answer you.
כִּי־עַ֛ם בְּצִיּ֥וֹן יֵשֵׁ֖ב בִּירֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם בָּכ֣וֹ לֹֽא־תִבְכֶּ֗ה חָנ֤וֹן יָחְנְךָ֙ לְק֣וֹל זַעֲקֶ֔ךָ כְּשָׁמְעָת֖וֹ עָנָֽךְ׃
Though the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your teacher[^17] will no longer hide himself, but your eyes will see your teacher.
וְנָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֧ם אֲדֹנָ֛י לֶ֥חֶם צָ֖ר וּמַ֣יִם לָ֑חַץ וְלֹֽא־יִכָּנֵ֥ף עוֹד֙ מוֹרֶ֔יךָ וְהָי֥וּ עֵינֶ֖יךָ רֹא֥וֹת אֶת־מוֹרֶֽיךָ׃
Your ears will hear a word behind you: "This is the way; walk in it," whenever you turn to the right or to the left.
וְאָזְנֶ֙יךָ֙ תִּשְׁמַ֣עְנָה דָבָ֔ר מֵֽאַחֲרֶ֖יךָ לֵאמֹ֑ר זֶ֤ה הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ לְכ֣וּ ב֔וֹ כִּ֥י תַאֲמִ֖ינוּ וְכִ֥י תַשְׂמְאִֽילוּ׃
Then you will defile your silver-plated idols and your gold-covered images. You will throw them away like a menstrual cloth and say to them, "Get out!"
וְטִמֵּאתֶ֗ם אֶת־צִפּוּי֙ פְּסִילֵ֣י כַסְפֶּ֔ךָ וְאֶת־אֲפֻדַּ֖ת מַסֵּכַ֣ת זְהָבֶ֑ךָ תִּזְרֵם֙ כְּמ֣וֹ דָוָ֔ה צֵ֖א תֹּ֥אמַר לֽוֹ׃
He will give rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and the bread that the ground produces will be rich and plentiful. On that day your cattle will graze in broad pastures.
וְנָתַן֩ מְטַ֨ר זַרְעֲךָ֜ אֲשֶׁר־תִּזְרַ֣ע אֶת־הָאֲדָמָ֗ה וְלֶ֙חֶם֙ תְּבוּאַ֣ת הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה דָשֵׁ֖ן וְשָׁמֵ֑ן יִרְעֶ֥ה מִקְנֶ֛יךָ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כַּ֥ר נִרְחָֽב׃
The oxen and donkeys that work the ground will eat seasoned fodder, winnowed with shovel and fork.
וְהָאֲלָפִ֣ים וְהָעֲיָרִ֗ים עֹֽבְדֵי֙ הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה בְּלִ֥יל חָמִ֖יץ יֹאכֵ֑לוּ אֲשֶׁר־זֹרֶ֥ה בָרַ֖חַת וּבַמִּזְרֶֽה׃
On every high mountain and on every lofty hill there will be streams flowing with water, on the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ עַל־כָּל־הַ֣ר גָּבֹ֗הַ וְעַל֙ כָּל־גִּבְעָ֣ה נִשָּׂאָ֔ה פְּלָגִ֖ים יִבְלֵי־מָ֑יִם בְּיוֹם֙ הֶ֣רֶג רָ֔ב בִּנְפֹ֖ל מִגְדָּלִֽים׃

The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, on the day Yahweh binds up the wounds of his people and heals the bruises from his blows.
וְהָיָ֤ה אֽוֹר־הַלְּבָנָה֙ כְּא֣וֹר הַֽחַמָּ֔ה וְא֤וֹר הַֽחַמָּה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שִׁבְעָתַ֔יִם כְּא֖וֹר שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים בְּי֗וֹם חֲבֹ֤שׁ יְהוָה֙ אֶת־שֶׁ֣בֶר עַמּ֔וֹ וּמַ֥חַץ מַכָּת֖וֹ יִרְפָּֽא׃ ס
Look, the name of Yahweh comes from far away, burning with his anger, in thick, rising smoke.[^18] His lips are full of fury, and his tongue is like a devouring fire.
הִנֵּ֤ה שֵׁם־יְהוָה֙ בָּ֣א מִמֶּרְחָ֔ק בֹּעֵ֣ר אַפּ֔וֹ וְכֹ֖בֶד מַשָּׂאָ֑ה שְׂפָתָיו֙ מָ֣לְאוּ זַ֔עַם וּלְשׁוֹנ֖וֹ כְּאֵ֥שׁ אֹכָֽלֶת׃
His breath[^19] is like a flooding torrent that rises up to the neck, to sift the nations in the sieve of destruction, and to put in the jaws of the peoples a bridle that leads them astray.
וְרוּח֞וֹ כְּנַ֤חַל שׁוֹטֵף֙ עַד־צַוָּ֣אר יֶֽחֱצֶ֔ה לַהֲנָפָ֥ה גוֹיִ֖ם בְּנָ֣פַת שָׁ֑וְא וְרֶ֣סֶן מַתְעֶ֔ה עַ֖ל לְחָיֵ֥י עַמִּֽים׃
You will have a song as on the night when a festival is kept holy, and gladness of heart as when people go up with the flute to the mountain of Yahweh, to the Rock of Israel.
הַשִּׁיר֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם כְּלֵ֖יל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ־חָ֑ג וְשִׂמְחַ֣ת לֵבָ֗ב כַּֽהוֹלֵךְ֙ בֶּֽחָלִ֔יל לָב֥וֹא בְהַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־צ֥וּר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Yahweh will make his majestic voice heard and show his arm coming down, in raging anger and the flame of a devouring fire, with cloudburst and storm and hailstones.
וְהִשְׁמִ֨יעַ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ה֣וֹד קוֹל֗וֹ וְנַ֤חַת זְרוֹעוֹ֙ יַרְאֶ֔ה בְּזַ֣עַף אַ֔ף וְלַ֖הַב אֵ֣שׁ אוֹכֵלָ֑ה נֶ֥פֶץ וָזֶ֖רֶם וְאֶ֥בֶן בָּרָֽד׃
For at the voice of Yahweh Assyria will be shattered, when he strikes with the rod.
כִּֽי־מִקּ֥וֹל יְהוָ֖ה יֵחַ֣ת אַשּׁ֑וּר בַּשֵּׁ֖בֶט יַכֶּֽה׃
Every stroke of the appointed rod that Yahweh lays on him will be to the sound of tambourines and lyres, as he fights against them[^20] in battle with brandished arm.
וְהָיָ֗ה כֹּ֚ל מַֽעֲבַר֙ מַטֵּ֣ה מֽוּסָדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנִ֤יחַ יְהוָה֙ עָלָ֔יו בְּתֻפִּ֖ים וּבְכִנֹּר֑וֹת וּבְמִלְחֲמ֥וֹת תְּנוּפָ֖ה נִלְחַם־*בה **בָּֽם׃

For a Topheth[^21] has long been prepared; it has been made ready for the king.[^22] Its fire pit has been made deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of Yahweh, like a stream of sulfur, sets it ablaze.
כִּֽי־עָר֤וּךְ מֵֽאֶתְמוּל֙ תָּפְתֶּ֔ה גַּם־*הוא **הִ֛יא לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הוּכָ֖ן הֶעְמִ֣יק הִרְחִ֑ב מְדֻרָתָ֗הּ אֵ֤שׁ וְעֵצִים֙ הַרְבֵּ֔ה נִשְׁמַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ כְּנַ֣חַל גָּפְרִ֔ית בֹּעֲרָ֖ה בָּֽהּ׃ ס

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "pour out a drink offering", perhaps to seal a treaty, or "weave a web".
n.3: Or "not by my spirit". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.4: Literally "and have not asked my mouth".
n.5: Probably Heracleopolis, a city in Egypt south of Memphis. *Zoan* is Tanis in the Nile Delta (19:11).
n.6: The Hebrew text is written "Everyone has made a stench" but read "Everyone has been put to shame".
n.7: Hebrew *massa*. See 13:1.
n.8: The dry region south of Judah, through which envoys traveled to Egypt with gifts.
n.9: Hebrew *saraf*, as in 14:29.
n.10: *Rahab*, "arrogance, storming", is the name of a sea monster, a picture of chaos (51:9; Job 26:12), used also as a name for Egypt (Psalm 87:4). *Who sits still* may mean "the do-nothing". The Hebrew phrase is difficult.
n.11: The vowel points read "forever" (*la'ad*). The same consonants can be read "as a witness" (*le'ed*).
n.12: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching, law".
n.13: Literally "make the Holy One of Israel cease from before us".
n.14: A play on words: *nanus*, "we will flee" (on horses, *sus*), and *qal*, "swift", with *yiqqallu*, "will be swift".
n.15: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".
n.16: Or "For a people will live in Zion, in Jerusalem".
n.17: Or "your teachers". The Hebrew form can be singular or plural. Also later in the verse.
n.18: Literally "and heavy is the lifting up". Hebrew *massa'ah*, related to *massa* (verse 6), here perhaps rising smoke.
n.19: Or "His spirit". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.20: The Hebrew text is written "against her" but read "against them".
n.21: Hebrew *tofteh*, a form of *Topheth*, the burning place in the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem where children were sacrificed (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31).
n.22: Hebrew *melekh*, "king", perhaps also a play on *Molekh* (Molech), the god to whom children were burned there (Leviticus 18:21; 2 Kings 23:10).

v: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in chariots because they are many and in horsemen because they are very strong, but do not look to the Holy One of Israel or seek Yahweh![^1]

ה֣וֹי הַיֹּרְדִ֤ים מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לְעֶזְרָ֔ה עַל־סוּסִ֖ים יִשָּׁעֵ֑נוּ וַיִּבְטְח֨וּ עַל־רֶ֜כֶב כִּ֣י רָ֗ב וְעַ֤ל פָּֽרָשִׁים֙ כִּֽי־עָצְמ֣וּ מְאֹ֔ד וְלֹ֤א שָׁעוּ֙ עַל־קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֶת־יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א דָרָֽשׁוּ׃
Yet he too is wise and brings disaster; he does not take back his words. He will rise up against the house of evildoers and against the helpers of those who do wrong.
וְגַם־ה֤וּא חָכָם֙ וַיָּ֣בֵא רָ֔ע וְאֶת־דְּבָרָ֖יו לֹ֣א הֵסִ֑יר וְקָם֙ עַל־בֵּ֣ית מְרֵעִ֔ים וְעַל־עֶזְרַ֖ת פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

The Egyptians are human beings and not God;[^2] their horses are flesh and not spirit. When Yahweh stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble and the one who is helped will fall; they will all perish together.
וּמִצְרַ֤יִם אָדָם֙ וְֽלֹא־אֵ֔ל וְסוּסֵיהֶ֥ם בָּשָׂ֖ר וְלֹא־ר֑וּחַ וַֽיהוָ֞ה יַטֶּ֣ה יָד֗וֹ וְכָשַׁ֤ל עוֹזֵר֙ וְנָפַ֣ל עָזֻ֔ר וְיַחְדָּ֖ו כֻּלָּ֥ם יִכְלָיֽוּן׃ ס

For this is what Yahweh has said to me: As a lion or a young lion growls over its prey, and though a whole band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their shouting or daunted by their noise, so Yahweh of Armies[^3] will come down to wage war on Mount Zion and on its hill.[^4]

כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר־יְהוָ֣ה ׀ אֵלַ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶהְגֶּה֩ הָאַרְיֵ֨ה וְהַכְּפִ֜יר עַל־טַרְפּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִקָּרֵ֤א עָלָיו֙ מְלֹ֣א רֹעִ֔ים מִקּוֹלָם֙ לֹ֣א יֵחָ֔ת וּמֵֽהֲמוֹנָ֖ם לֹ֣א יַֽעֲנֶ֑ה כֵּ֗ן יֵרֵד֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לִצְבֹּ֥א עַל־הַר־צִיּ֖וֹן וְעַל־גִּבְעָתָֽהּ׃
Like birds hovering overhead, so Yahweh of Armies will shield Jerusalem; he will shield and rescue it, pass over and deliver it.[^5]
כְּצִפֳּרִ֣ים עָפ֔וֹת כֵּ֗ן יָגֵ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת עַל־יְרֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם גָּנ֥וֹן וְהִצִּ֖יל פָּסֹ֥חַ וְהִמְלִֽיט׃
Return to the one against whom the Israelites have so deeply rebelled.
שׁ֗וּבוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֛ר הֶעְמִ֥יקוּ סָרָ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
For on that day each of you will reject your idols of silver and your idols of gold, which your hands have made for you in sin.[^6]
כִּ֚י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִמְאָס֗וּן אִ֚ישׁ אֱלִילֵ֣י כַסְפּ֔וֹ וֶאֱלִילֵ֖י זְהָב֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם יְדֵיכֶ֖ם חֵֽטְא׃
Assyria will fall by a sword not of man; a sword not of a human being will devour him. He will flee from the sword,[^7] and his young men will be put to forced labor.
וְנָפַ֤ל אַשּׁוּר֙ בְּחֶ֣רֶב לֹא־אִ֔ישׁ וְחֶ֥רֶב לֹֽא־אָדָ֖ם תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֑נּוּ וְנָ֥ס לוֹ֙ מִפְּנֵי־חֶ֔רֶב וּבַחוּרָ֖יו לָמַ֥ס יִהְיֽוּ׃
His rock will pass away in terror,[^8] and his officers will be dismayed at the signal flag,[^9] declares Yahweh, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
וְסַלְעוֹ֙ מִמָּג֣וֹר יַֽעֲב֔וֹר וְחַתּ֥וּ מִנֵּ֖ס שָׂרָ֑יו נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־א֥וּר לוֹ֙ בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וְתַנּ֥וּר ל֖וֹ בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ ס

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *el*, "God, a god".
n.3: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. *To wage war* (*litsbo*) comes from the same root.
n.4: Or "against Mount Zion". The Hebrew can mean either; verse 5 shows Yahweh protecting the city.
n.5: Hebrew *pasoach*, the verb of the Passover, when Yahweh "passed over" the houses of Israel (Exodus 12:13, 23, 27).
n.6: Literally "which your hands have made for you, a sin".
n.7: Literally "he will flee for himself from before the sword".
n.8: Perhaps his stronghold, or his king. Hebrew *sal'o*, "his rock".
n.9: Or "will desert the standard".

v: Look, a king will reign in righteousness, and rulers will rule with justice.
הֵ֥ן לְצֶ֖דֶק יִמְלָךְ־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּלְשָׂרִ֖ים לְמִשְׁפָּ֥ט יָשֹֽׂרוּ׃
Each of them will be like a shelter from the wind and a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shade of a great rock in a weary land.
וְהָיָה־אִ֥ישׁ כְּמַֽחֲבֵא־ר֖וּחַ וְסֵ֣תֶר זָ֑רֶם כְּפַלְגֵי־מַ֣יִם בְּצָי֔וֹן כְּצֵ֥ל סֶֽלַע־כָּבֵ֖ד בְּאֶ֥רֶץ עֲיֵפָֽה׃
Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed,[^1] and the ears of those who hear will listen.
וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁעֶ֖ינָה עֵינֵ֣י רֹאִ֑ים וְאָזְנֵ֥י שֹׁמְעִ֖ים תִּקְשַֽׁבְנָה׃
The mind of the rash will understand and know, and the tongue of those who stammer will speak quickly and clearly.
וּלְבַ֥ב נִמְהָרִ֖ים יָבִ֣ין לָדָ֑עַת וּלְשׁ֣וֹן עִלְּגִ֔ים תְּמַהֵ֖ר לְדַבֵּ֥ר צָחֽוֹת׃
The fool will no longer be called noble, and the scoundrel will no longer be called honorable.[^2]
לֹֽא־יִקָּרֵ֥א ע֛וֹד לְנָבָ֖ל נָדִ֑יב וּלְכִילַ֕י לֹ֥א יֵֽאָמֵ֖ר שֽׁוֹעַ׃
For the fool speaks folly, and his mind plots evil: to practice godlessness, to spread error about Yahweh,[^3] to leave the hungry empty and to deprive the thirsty of drink.
כִּ֤י נָבָל֙ נְבָלָ֣ה יְדַבֵּ֔ר וְלִבּ֖וֹ יַעֲשֶׂה־אָ֑וֶן לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת חֹ֗נֶף וּלְדַבֵּ֤ר אֶל־יְהוָה֙ תּוֹעָ֔ה לְהָרִיק֙ נֶ֣פֶשׁ רָעֵ֔ב וּמַשְׁקֶ֥ה צָמֵ֖א יַחְסִֽיר׃
The scoundrel's ways are evil;[^4] he devises wicked schemes to ruin the poor[^5] with lies, even when the needy plead their just cause.
וְכֵלַ֖י כֵּלָ֣יו רָעִ֑ים ה֚וּא זִמּ֣וֹת יָעָ֔ץ לְחַבֵּ֤ל *ענוים **עֲנִיִּים֙ בְּאִמְרֵי־שֶׁ֔קֶר וּבְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶבְי֖וֹן מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
But the noble person makes noble plans, and by noble deeds he stands.
וְנָדִ֖יב נְדִיב֣וֹת יָעָ֑ץ וְה֖וּא עַל־נְדִיב֥וֹת יָקֽוּם׃ פ
You women who are at ease, rise up and hear my voice! You daughters who feel secure, listen to what I say!
נָשִׁים֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת קֹ֖מְנָה שְׁמַ֣עְנָה קוֹלִ֑י בָּנוֹת֙ בֹּֽטח֔וֹת הַאְזֵ֖נָּה אִמְרָתִֽי׃
In little more than a year[^6] you who feel secure will tremble, for the grape harvest will fail, and the harvest of fruit will not come.
יָמִים֙ עַל־שָׁנָ֔ה תִּרְגַּ֖זְנָה בֹּֽטְח֑וֹת כִּ֚י כָּלָ֣ה בָצִ֔יר אֹ֖סֶף בְּלִ֥י יָבֽוֹא׃
Tremble, you women who are at ease! Shudder, you who feel secure! Strip off your clothes, stand bare, and put sackcloth around your waists.
חִרְדוּ֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת רְגָ֖זָה בֹּֽטְח֑וֹת פְּשֹׁ֣טָֽה וְעֹ֔רָה וַחֲג֖וֹרָה עַל־חֲלָצָֽיִם׃
Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine,[^7]
עַל־שָׁדַ֖יִם סֹֽפְדִ֑ים עַל־שְׂדֵי־חֶ֕מֶד עַל־גֶּ֖פֶן פֹּרִיָּֽה׃
for the soil of my people, where thorns and briers grow up, yes, for all the houses of joy in the joyful city.
עַ֚ל אַדְמַ֣ת עַמִּ֔י ק֥וֹץ שָׁמִ֖יר תַּֽעֲלֶ֑ה כִּ֚י עַל־כָּל־בָּתֵּ֣י מָשׂ֔וֹשׂ קִרְיָ֖ה עַלִּיזָֽה׃
For the palace is abandoned, the busy city deserted. The hill[^8] and the watchtower will become caves forever, the delight of wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks,
כִּֽי־אַרְמ֣וֹן נֻטָּ֔שׁ הֲמ֥וֹן עִ֖יר עֻזָּ֑ב עֹ֣פֶל וָבַ֜חַן הָיָ֨ה בְעַ֤ד מְעָרוֹת֙ עַד־עוֹלָ֔ם מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ פְּרָאִ֖ים מִרְעֵ֥ה עֲדָרִֽים׃
until the Spirit[^9] is poured out on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is thought of as a forest.[^10]
עַד־יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה עָלֵ֛ינוּ ר֖וּחַ מִמָּר֑וֹם וְהָיָ֤ה מִדְבָּר֙ לַכַּרְמֶ֔ל *וכרמל **וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב׃
Then justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will live in the fruitful field.
וְשָׁכַ֥ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בַּכַּרְמֶ֥ל תֵּשֵֽׁב׃
The work of righteousness will be peace, and the effect of righteousness will be quietness and confidence forever.
וְהָיָ֛ה מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הַצְּדָקָ֖ה שָׁל֑וֹם וַֽעֲבֹדַת֙ הַצְּדָקָ֔ה הַשְׁקֵ֥ט וָבֶ֖טַח עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃
My people will live in a peaceful home, in secure dwellings and in undisturbed resting places.
וְיָשַׁ֥ב עַמִּ֖י בִּנְוֵ֣ה שָׁל֑וֹם וּֽבְמִשְׁכְּנוֹת֙ מִבְטַחִ֔ים וּבִמְנוּחֹ֖ת שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת׃
But hail will fall when the forest comes down, and the city will be utterly laid low.[^11]
וּבָרַ֖ד בְּרֶ֣דֶת הַיָּ֑עַר וּבַשִּׁפְלָ֖ה תִּשְׁפַּ֥ל הָעִֽיר׃
Happy are you[^12] who sow beside every stream, who let the ox and the donkey range free!
אַשְׁרֵיכֶ֕ם זֹרְעֵ֖י עַל־כָּל־מָ֑יִם מְשַׁלְּחֵ֥י רֶֽגֶל־הַשּׁ֖וֹר וְהַחֲמֽוֹר׃ ס

n.1: Or "will no longer be dim". The Hebrew verb may come from *sha'ah*, "look", or from *sha'a*, "be smeared shut" (6:10).
n.2: Hebrew *kilai*, a rare word, perhaps "cheat, swindler". Also in verse 7.
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: A play on sounds: *kelai kelav*, "the scoundrel, his tools".
n.5: The Hebrew text is written "the humble" but read "the poor".
n.6: Literally "days upon a year".
n.7: Literally "beating upon breasts". Hebrew *shadayim*, "breasts", sounds like *sede*, "fields".
n.8: Hebrew *ophel*, "hill, mound", also the name of the fortified hill of Jerusalem south of the temple (2 Chronicles 27:3).
n.9: Or "a spirit". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.10: Hebrew *karmel*, "garden land, orchard" (29:17). The Hebrew text is written "and a fruitful field" but read "and the fruitful field". Also in verse 16.
n.11: A play on sounds: *u-varad be-redet ha-ya'ar*, "and it will hail when the forest comes down". The meaning of the verse is uncertain.
n.12: Hebrew *ashrei*: happy, fortunate; traditionally "blessed".

v: Woe to you, destroyer, you who have not been destroyed, you traitor, whom no one has betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you have done with betraying,[^1] they will betray you.
ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א שָׁד֔וּד וּבוֹגֵ֖ד וְלֹא־בָ֣גְדוּ ב֑וֹ כַּהֲתִֽמְךָ֤ שׁוֹדֵד֙ תּוּשַּׁ֔ד כַּנְּלֹתְךָ֥ לִבְגֹּ֖ד יִבְגְּדוּ־בָֽךְ׃ ס
Yahweh,[^2] be gracious to us; we wait for you. Be their strength[^3] every morning, our salvation in time of distress.
יְהוָ֥ה חָנֵּ֖נוּ לְךָ֣ קִוִּ֑ינוּ הֱיֵ֤ה זְרֹעָם֙ לַבְּקָרִ֔ים אַף־יְשׁוּעָתֵ֖נוּ בְּעֵ֥ת צָרָֽה׃
At the sound of the tumult, peoples flee; when you rise up, nations scatter.
מִקּ֣וֹל הָמ֔וֹן נָדְד֖וּ עַמִּ֑ים מֵר֣וֹמְמֻתֶ֔ךָ נָפְצ֖וּ גּוֹיִֽם׃
Your plunder is gathered as the caterpillar gathers; as locusts swarm, people swarm over it.
וְאֻסַּ֣ף שְׁלַלְכֶ֔ם אֹ֖סֶף הֶֽחָסִ֑יל כְּמַשַּׁ֥ק גֵּבִ֖ים שׁוֹקֵ֥ק בּֽוֹ׃
Yahweh is exalted, for he dwells on high; he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
נִשְׂגָּ֣ב יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י שֹׁכֵ֖ן מָר֑וֹם מִלֵּ֣א צִיּ֔וֹן מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃
He will be the stability of your times, a wealth of salvation, of wisdom and knowledge. The fear of Yahweh is Zion's treasure.[^4]
וְהָיָה֙ אֱמוּנַ֣ת עִתֶּ֔יךָ חֹ֥סֶן יְשׁוּעֹ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת וָדָ֑עַת יִרְאַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה הִ֥יא אוֹצָרֽוֹ׃ ס
Look, their heroes[^5] cry out in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם צָעֲק֖וּ חֻ֑צָה מַלְאֲכֵ֣י שָׁל֔וֹם מַ֖ר יִבְכָּיֽוּן׃
The highways are deserted; no one travels the roads. He has broken the treaty and despised the cities;[^6] he has no regard for anyone.
נָשַׁ֣מּוּ מְסִלּ֔וֹת שָׁבַ֖ת עֹבֵ֣ר אֹ֑רַח הֵפֵ֤ר בְּרִית֙ מָאַ֣ס עָרִ֔ים לֹ֥א חָשַׁ֖ב אֱנֽוֹשׁ׃
The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and withers. Sharon is like the Arabah,[^7] and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
אָבַ֤ל אֻמְלְלָה֙ אָ֔רֶץ הֶחְפִּ֥יר לְבָנ֖וֹן קָמַ֑ל הָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרוֹן֙ כָּֽעֲרָבָ֔ה וְנֹעֵ֥ר בָּשָׁ֖ן וְכַרְמֶֽל׃
Now I will arise, says Yahweh; now I will lift myself up; now I will be exalted.
עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ אֵֽרוֹמָ֔ם עַתָּ֖ה אֶנָּשֵֽׂא׃
You conceive chaff and give birth to straw; your breath[^8] is a fire that will consume you.
תַּהֲר֥וּ חֲשַׁ֖שׁ תֵּ֣לְדוּ קַ֑שׁ רוּחֲכֶ֕ם אֵ֖שׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶֽם׃
The peoples will be burned to lime, like cut thorns set on fire.
וְהָי֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים מִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת שִׂ֑יד קוֹצִ֥ים כְּסוּחִ֖ים בָּאֵ֥שׁ יִצַּֽתּוּ׃ ס
Hear, you who are far away, what I have done; and you who are near, acknowledge my might.
שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי וּדְע֥וּ קְרוֹבִ֖ים גְּבֻרָתִֽי׃
The sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling has seized the godless: "Who of us can live with the devouring fire? Who of us can live with everlasting burning?"
פָּחֲד֤וּ בְצִיּוֹן֙ חַטָּאִ֔ים אָחֲזָ֥ה רְעָדָ֖ה חֲנֵפִ֑ים מִ֣י ׀ יָג֣וּר לָ֗נוּ אֵ֚שׁ אוֹכֵלָ֔ה מִי־יָג֥וּר לָ֖נוּ מוֹקְדֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃

The one who walks in righteousness and speaks what is right, who rejects gain from extortion, who shakes his hands so that they hold no bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed and shuts his eyes from looking at evil,[^9]
הֹלֵ֣ךְ צְדָק֔וֹת וְדֹבֵ֖ר מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים מֹאֵ֞ס בְּבֶ֣צַע מַעֲשַׁקּ֗וֹת נֹעֵ֤ר כַּפָּיו֙ מִתְּמֹ֣ךְ בַּשֹּׁ֔חַד אֹטֵ֤ם אָזְנוֹ֙ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ דָּמִ֔ים וְעֹצֵ֥ם עֵינָ֖יו מֵרְא֥וֹת בְּרֽ͏ָע׃
he will dwell on the heights; his refuge will be the fortress of the rocks. His bread will be given him; his water will not fail.
ה֚וּא מְרוֹמִ֣ים יִשְׁכֹּ֔ן מְצָד֥וֹת סְלָעִ֖ים מִשְׂגַּבּ֑וֹ לַחְמ֣וֹ נִתָּ֔ן מֵימָ֖יו נֶאֱמָנִֽים׃
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty; they will see a land that stretches far away.
מֶ֥לֶךְ בְּיָפְי֖וֹ תֶּחֱזֶ֣ינָה עֵינֶ֑יךָ תִּרְאֶ֖ינָה אֶ֥רֶץ מַרְחַקִּֽים׃
Your mind will think back on the terror: "Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed the tribute? Where is the one who counted the towers?"[^10]
לִבְּךָ֖ יֶהְגֶּ֣ה אֵימָ֑ה אַיֵּ֤ה סֹפֵר֙ אַיֵּ֣ה שֹׁקֵ֔ל אַיֵּ֖ה סֹפֵ֥ר אֶת־הַמִּגְדָּלִֽים׃
You will no longer see the insolent people,[^11] a people of speech too obscure to understand, with a stammering tongue that no one can make sense of.
אֶת־עַ֥ם נוֹעָ֖ז לֹ֣א תִרְאֶ֑ה עַ֣ם עִמְקֵ֤י שָׂפָה֙ מִשְּׁמ֔וֹעַ נִלְעַ֥ג לָשׁ֖וֹן אֵ֥ין בִּינָֽה׃
Look at Zion, the city of our festivals! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful dwelling, a tent that will not be moved, whose stakes will never be pulled up and none of whose ropes will be broken.
חֲזֵ֣ה צִיּ֔וֹן קִרְיַ֖ת מֽוֹעֲדֵ֑נוּ עֵינֶיךָ֩ תִרְאֶ֨ינָה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם נָוֶ֣ה שַׁאֲנָ֗ן אֹ֤הֶל בַּל־יִצְעָן֙ בַּל־יִסַּ֤ע יְתֵֽדֹתָיו֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וְכָל־חֲבָלָ֖יו בַּל־יִנָּתֵֽקוּ׃
But there Yahweh will be majestic for us, a place of rivers and broad streams, where no galley with oars will go, and no mighty ship will pass.
כִּ֣י אִם־שָׁ֞ם אַדִּ֤יר יְהוָה֙ לָ֔נוּ מְקוֹם־נְהָרִ֥ים יְאֹרִ֖ים רַחֲבֵ֣י יָדָ֑יִם בַּל־תֵּ֤לֶךְ בּוֹ֙ אֳנִי־שַׁ֔יִט וְצִ֥י אַדִּ֖יר לֹ֥א יַעַבְרֶֽנּוּ׃
For Yahweh is our judge, Yahweh is our lawgiver, Yahweh is our king; he will save us.
כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֔נוּ יְהוָ֖ה מְחֹקְקֵ֑נוּ יְהוָ֥ה מַלְכֵּ֖נוּ ה֥וּא יוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ׃
Your ropes hang loose; they cannot hold the mast firm in its place or spread the sail.[^12] Then plunder in abundance will be divided; even the lame will carry off the spoil.
נִטְּשׁ֖וּ חֲבָלָ֑יִךְ בַּל־יְחַזְּק֤וּ כֵן־תָּרְנָם֙ בַּל־פָּ֣רְשׂוּ נֵ֔ס אָ֣ז חֻלַּ֤ק עַֽד־שָׁלָל֙ מַרְבֶּ֔ה פִּסְחִ֖ים בָּ֥זְזוּ בַֽז׃
No one who lives there will say, "I am sick"; the people who live there will be forgiven their guilt.
וּבַל־יֹאמַ֥ר שָׁכֵ֖ן חָלִ֑יתִי הָעָ֛ם הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב בָּ֖הּ נְשֻׂ֥א עָוֺֽן׃

n.1: Hebrew *ka-nelotkha*, a word found only here, probably "when you have finished".
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "their arm". The prayer moves from "us" to "them" and back.
n.4: Literally "his treasure".
n.5: Hebrew *er'ellam*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "their heroes" or "their messengers".
n.6: The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) reads "despised the witnesses", a difference of one similar letter.
n.7: *Sharon*, *Bashan* and *Carmel* were fertile, wooded regions. The *Arabah* is the dry rift valley around the Jordan and the Dead Sea.
n.8: Or "your spirit". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.9: Compare the questions and answers of Psalms 15 and 24:3–6.
n.10: Officials of the enemy who counted and weighed the tribute and surveyed the city's defenses. Paul echoes this verse in 1 Corinthians 1:20.
n.11: Hebrew *no'az*, a word found only here, perhaps "fierce" or "insolent".
n.12: *Your* is feminine singular, perhaps addressing the enemy pictured as a disabled ship.

v: Come near, you nations, and hear! Pay attention, you peoples! Let the earth hear, and all that fills it, the world and all that comes from it.[^1]
קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ תִּשְׁמַ֤ע הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ וּמְלֹאָ֔הּ תֵּבֵ֖ל וְכָל־צֶאֱצָאֶֽיהָ׃
For Yahweh[^2] is angry with all the nations and furious with all their armies. He has devoted them to destruction;[^3] he has handed them over to slaughter.
כִּ֣י קֶ֤צֶף לַֽיהוָה֙ עַל־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְחֵמָ֖ה עַל־כָּל־צְבָאָ֑ם הֶחֱרִימָ֖ם נְתָנָ֥ם לַטָּֽבַח׃
Their slain will be thrown out, and the stench of their corpses will rise. The mountains will melt with their blood.
וְחַלְלֵיהֶ֣ם יֻשְׁלָ֔כוּ וּפִגְרֵיהֶ֖ם יַעֲלֶ֣ה בָאְשָׁ֑ם וְנָמַ֥סּוּ הָרִ֖ים מִדָּמָֽם׃

All the army of the heavens[^4] will rot away, and the heavens will be rolled up like a scroll. All their army will wither, as a leaf withers and falls from the vine, like a withered fig from the fig tree.[^5]
וְנָמַ֙קּוּ֙ כָּל־צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנָגֹ֥לּוּ כַסֵּ֖פֶר הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְכָל־צְבָאָ֣ם יִבּ֔וֹל כִּנְבֹ֤ל עָלֶה֙ מִגֶּ֔פֶן וּכְנֹבֶ֖לֶת מִתְּאֵנָֽה׃
For my sword has drunk its fill in the heavens. Look, it comes down on Edom,[^6] on the people I have devoted to destruction, to judge them.
כִּֽי־רִוְּתָ֥ה בַשָּׁמַ֖יִם חַרְבִּ֑י הִנֵּה֙ עַל־אֱד֣וֹם תֵּרֵ֔ד וְעַל־עַ֥ם חֶרְמִ֖י לְמִשְׁפָּֽט׃

Yahweh has a sword; it is filled with blood. It is gorged with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For Yahweh has a sacrifice in Bozrah[^7] and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
חֶ֣רֶב לַיהוָ֞ה מָלְאָ֥ה דָם֙ הֻדַּ֣שְׁנָה מֵחֵ֔לֶב מִדַּ֤ם כָּרִים֙ וְעַתּוּדִ֔ים מֵחֵ֖לֶב כִּלְי֣וֹת אֵילִ֑ים כִּ֣י זֶ֤בַח לַֽיהוָה֙ בְּבָצְרָ֔ה וְטֶ֥בַח גָּד֖וֹל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃
Wild oxen[^8] will go down with them, and young bulls with the mighty steers. Their land will drink its fill of blood, and their soil will be gorged with fat.
וְיָרְד֤וּ רְאֵמִים֙ עִמָּ֔ם וּפָרִ֖ים עִם־אַבִּירִ֑ים וְרִוְּתָ֤ה אַרְצָם֙ מִדָּ֔ם וַעֲפָרָ֖ם מֵחֵ֥לֶב יְדֻשָּֽׁן׃
For Yahweh has a day of vengeance, a year of repayment, to uphold the cause of Zion.[^9]
כִּ֛י י֥וֹם נָקָ֖ם לַֽיהוָ֑ה שְׁנַ֥ת שִׁלּוּמִ֖ים לְרִ֥יב צִיּֽוֹן׃
Edom's streams will be turned into pitch, and its soil into sulfur; its land will become burning pitch.[^10]
וְנֶהֶפְכ֤וּ נְחָלֶ֙יהָ֙ לְזֶ֔פֶת וַעֲפָרָ֖הּ לְגָפְרִ֑ית וְהָיְתָ֣ה אַרְצָ֔הּ לְזֶ֖פֶת בֹּעֵרָֽה׃
Night and day it will not be quenched; its smoke will go up forever.[^11] From generation to generation it will lie in ruins; forever and ever no one will pass through it.
לַ֤יְלָה וְיוֹמָם֙ לֹ֣א תִכְבֶּ֔ה לְעוֹלָ֖ם יַעֲלֶ֣ה עֲשָׁנָ֑הּ מִדּ֤וֹר לָדוֹר֙ תֶּחֱרָ֔ב לְנֵ֣צַח נְצָחִ֔ים אֵ֥ין עֹבֵ֖ר בָּֽהּ׃
The pelican and the owl[^12] will possess it; the great owl and the raven will live there. He will stretch over it the measuring line of chaos and the plumb line of emptiness.[^13]
וִירֵשׁ֙וּהָ֙ קָאַ֣ת וְקִפּ֔וֹד וְיַנְשׁ֥וֹף וְעֹרֵ֖ב יִשְׁכְּנוּ־בָ֑הּ וְנָטָ֥ה עָלֶ֛יהָ קַֽו־תֹ֖הוּ וְאַבְנֵי־בֹֽהוּ׃
Its nobles will have nothing there to call a kingdom, and all its princes will come to nothing.[^14]
חֹרֶ֥יהָ וְאֵֽין־שָׁ֖ם מְלוּכָ֣ה יִקְרָ֑אוּ וְכָל־שָׂרֶ֖יהָ יִ֥הְיוּ אָֽפֶס׃
Thorns will grow up in its fortresses, nettles and thistles in its strongholds. It will be a haunt for jackals, a home[^15] for ostriches.
וְעָלְתָ֤ה אַרְמְנֹתֶ֙יהָ֙ סִירִ֔ים קִמּ֥וֹשׂ וָח֖וֹחַ בְּמִבְצָרֶ֑יהָ וְהָיְתָה֙ נְוֵ֣ה תַנִּ֔ים חָצִ֖יר לִבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה׃
Desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and the wild goat will call to its fellow.[^16] There too the night creature[^17] will settle and find for herself a place to rest.
וּפָגְשׁ֤וּ צִיִּים֙ אֶת־אִיִּ֔ים וְשָׂעִ֖יר עַל־רֵעֵ֣הוּ יִקְרָ֑א אַךְ־שָׁם֙ הִרְגִּ֣יעָה לִּילִ֔ית וּמָצְאָ֥ה לָ֖הּ מָנֽוֹחַ׃
There the owl[^18] will nest and lay eggs; it will hatch them and gather its young in its shade. There too the kites will gather, each one with its mate.
שָׁ֣מָּה קִנְּנָ֤ה קִפּוֹז֙ וַתְּמַלֵּ֔ט וּבָקְעָ֖ה וְדָגְרָ֣ה בְצִלָּ֑הּ אַךְ־שָׁ֛ם נִקְבְּצ֥וּ דַיּ֖וֹת אִשָּׁ֥ה רְעוּתָֽהּ׃
Search in the scroll of Yahweh, and read: Not one of these will be missing; none will be without its mate. For it is my mouth that has commanded it, and his Spirit that has gathered them.[^19]
דִּרְשׁ֨וּ מֵֽעַל־סֵ֤פֶר יְהוָה֙ וּֽקְרָ֔אוּ אַחַ֤ת מֵהֵ֙נָּה֙ לֹ֣א נֶעְדָּ֔רָה אִשָּׁ֥ה רְעוּתָ֖הּ לֹ֣א פָקָ֑דוּ כִּֽי־פִי֙ ה֣וּא צִוָּ֔ה וְרוּח֖וֹ ה֥וּא קִבְּצָֽן׃
He has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided the land among them with the measuring line. They will possess it forever; they will live in it from generation to generation.
וְהֽוּא־הִפִּ֤יל לָהֶן֙ גּוֹרָ֔ל וְיָד֛וֹ חִלְּקַ֥תָּה לָהֶ֖ם בַּקָּ֑ו עַד־עוֹלָם֙ יִֽירָשׁ֔וּהָ לְד֥וֹר וָד֖וֹר יִשְׁכְּנוּ־בָֽהּ׃ ס

n.1: Or "all its offspring". Hebrew *tse'etsa'im*, what comes out of the earth: its plants, or the living things it brings forth.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *hecherim*, "devote to destruction": to give over to God by destroying completely (11:15). Also in verse 5, "the people I have devoted to destruction".
n.4: Hebrew *tseva ha-shamayim*, the sun, moon and stars, pictured as an army. *Tseva* is the word for the nations' *armies* in verse 2.
n.5: Revelation 6:13–14 echoes this verse; compare Mark 13:25.
n.6: The land south and east of the Dead Sea, whose people were descended from Esau, Jacob's brother (Genesis 36). Edom was often Israel's enemy, and here it stands for all the nations hostile to Zion (compare 63:1–6).
n.7: The chief city of Edom (63:1).
n.8: Hebrew *re'emim*, traditionally "unicorns". The oxen and bulls of this verse may stand for Edom's leaders and warriors.
n.9: Or "for Zion's cause", that is, to take up Zion's case against her enemies.
n.10: The burning pitch and sulfur recall the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24).
n.11: Revelation 14:11 and 19:3 echo this line.
n.12: Hebrew *qa'at*, perhaps a pelican or a kind of owl (Leviticus 11:18; Psalm 102:7), and *qippod*, perhaps an owl or a hedgehog (14:23). The identification of many of the creatures in verses 11–15 is uncertain.
n.13: Literally "the line of *tohu* and the stones of *bohu*", the words used in Genesis 1:2 for the earth before creation, "formless and empty". The builder's tools are used to undo the land. The *stones* are the weights of a plumb line.
n.14: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "Its nobles, and there is no kingdom there they will call, and all its princes will be nothing."
n.15: Hebrew *chatsir*, usually "grass", but here probably a form of *chatser*, "courtyard, dwelling".
n.16: *Desert creatures*, *hyenas* and *wild goats* are named also in 13:21–22. *Wild goat* is Hebrew *sa'ir*, "hairy one", perhaps a goat-demon thought to haunt ruins (13:21; Leviticus 17:7).
n.17: Hebrew *lilit*, found only here. It may be a night bird, or the name of a female demon of the night known from Mesopotamian texts and later Jewish tradition as Lilith.
n.18: Hebrew *qippoz*, found only here, perhaps an owl or a kind of snake.
n.19: Literally "For my mouth, it has commanded, and his Spirit, he has gathered them." The Hebrew moves from "my" to "his". *Spirit* is Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, wind, breath".

v: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad; the desert[^1] will rejoice and blossom like the crocus.[^2]
יְשֻׂשׂ֥וּם מִדְבָּ֖ר וְצִיָּ֑ה וְתָגֵ֧ל עֲרָבָ֛ה וְתִפְרַ֖ח כַּחֲבַצָּֽלֶת׃

It will blossom abundantly and rejoice, yes, rejoice with shouts of joy. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon.[^3] They will see the glory of Yahweh,[^4] the splendor of our God.
פָּרֹ֨חַ תִּפְרַ֜ח וְתָגֵ֗ל אַ֚ף גִּילַ֣ת וְרַנֵּ֔ן כְּב֤וֹד הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ נִתַּן־לָ֔הּ הֲדַ֥ר הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל וְהַשָּׁר֑וֹן הֵ֛מָּה יִרְא֥וּ כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה הֲדַ֥ר אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ ס
Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the knees that give way.[^5]
חַזְּק֖וּ יָדַ֣יִם רָפ֑וֹת וּבִרְכַּ֥יִם כֹּשְׁל֖וֹת אַמֵּֽצוּ׃
Say to those whose hearts are anxious, "Be strong, do not be afraid. Look, your God will come with vengeance; with the recompense of God he will come and save you."
אִמְרוּ֙ לְנִמְהֲרֵי־לֵ֔ב חִזְק֖וּ אַל־תִּירָ֑אוּ הִנֵּ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ נָקָ֣ם יָב֔וֹא גְּמ֣וּל אֱלֹהִ֔ים ה֥וּא יָב֖וֹא וְיֹשַׁעֲכֶֽם׃
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
אָ֥ז תִּפָּקַ֖חְנָה עֵינֵ֣י עִוְרִ֑ים וְאָזְנֵ֥י חֵרְשִׁ֖ים תִּפָּתַֽחְנָה׃
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will shout for joy.[^6] For water will burst out in the wilderness and streams in the desert.
אָ֣ז יְדַלֵּ֤ג כָּֽאַיָּל֙ פִּסֵּ֔חַ וְתָרֹ֖ן לְשׁ֣וֹן אִלֵּ֑ם כִּֽי־נִבְקְע֤וּ בַמִּדְבָּר֙ מַ֔יִם וּנְחָלִ֖ים בָּעֲרָבָֽה׃
The burning sand[^7] will become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water. In the haunts where jackals lay, grass will become reeds and papyrus.[^8]
וְהָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרָב֙ לַאֲגַ֔ם וְצִמָּא֖וֹן לְמַבּ֣וּעֵי מָ֑יִם בִּנְוֵ֤ה תַנִּים֙ רִבְצָ֔הּ חָצִ֖יר לְקָנֶ֥ה וָגֹֽמֶא׃
A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel on it; it will be for those who walk that way, and fools will not wander onto it.[^9]
וְהָיָה־שָׁ֞ם מַסְל֣וּל וָדֶ֗רֶךְ וְדֶ֤רֶךְ הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ יִקָּ֣רֵא לָ֔הּ לֹֽא־יַעַבְרֶ֥נּוּ טָמֵ֖א וְהוּא־לָ֑מוֹ הֹלֵ֥ךְ דֶּ֛רֶךְ וֶאֱוִילִ֖ים לֹ֥א יִתְעֽוּ׃
No lion will be there, and no ravenous beast will go up on it; they will not be found there. But the redeemed[^10] will walk there.
לֹא־יִהְיֶ֨ה שָׁ֜ם אַרְיֵ֗ה וּפְרִ֤יץ חַיּוֹת֙ בַּֽל־יַעֲלֶ֔נָּה לֹ֥א תִמָּצֵ֖א שָׁ֑ם וְהָלְכ֖וּ גְּאוּלִֽים׃
Those whom Yahweh has ransomed will return and come to Zion with singing. Everlasting joy will be on their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.[^11]
וּפְדוּיֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה יְשֻׁב֗וּן וּבָ֤אוּ צִיּוֹן֙ בְּרִנָּ֔ה וְשִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם עַל־רֹאשָׁ֑ם שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יַשִּׂ֔יגוּ וְנָ֖סוּ יָג֥וֹן וַאֲנָחָֽה׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *aravah*, the dry steppe, and also the name of the rift valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea (Deuteronomy 1:1). Also in verse 6.
n.2: Hebrew *chavatselet*, a meadow flower, perhaps a crocus or an asphodel; traditionally "rose" (Song of Songs 2:1).
n.3: Lebanon was famous for its cedars, and Carmel and Sharon, on the coast of Israel, for their woods and pastures (33:9).
n.4: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.5: Hebrews 12:12 echoes this verse.
n.6: Jesus' answer to John the Baptist in Matthew 11:5 and Luke 7:22 echoes verses 5–6.
n.7: Hebrew *sharav*, "scorching heat", perhaps the shimmering heat of the desert or a mirage (49:10).
n.8: Literally "In the haunt of jackals, its resting place, grass for reed and papyrus." Or "grass and reeds and papyrus". The meaning is uncertain.
n.9: Or "it will be for them; whoever walks that way, even fools, will not go astray". The Hebrew is difficult.
n.10: Hebrew *ge'ulim*, those whom Yahweh has rescued as next of kin (41:14).
n.11: Verse 10 is repeated in 51:11.

v: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.[^1]
וַיְהִ֡י בְּאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ עָלָ֞ה סַנְחֵרִ֤יב מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁוּר֙ עַ֣ל כָּל־עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה הַבְּצֻר֖וֹת וַֽיִּתְפְּשֵֽׂם׃
The king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh[^2] with a large army from Lachish[^3] to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. He stood by the channel of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field.[^4]

וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֣וּר ׀ אֶת־רַב־שָׁקֵ֨ה מִלָּכִ֧ישׁ יְרוּשָׁלַ֛͏ְמָה אֶל־הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּחֵ֣יל כָּבֵ֑ד וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֗ד בִּתְעָלַת֙ הַבְּרֵכָ֣ה הָעֶלְיוֹנָ֔ה בִּמְסִלַּ֖ת שְׂדֵ֥ה כוֹבֵֽס׃
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator,[^5] Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder,[^6] went out to him.
וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֵלָ֛יו אֶלְיָקִ֥ים בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַבָּ֑יִת וְשֶׁבְנָא֙ הַסֹּפֵ֔ר וְיוֹאָ֥ח בֶּן־אָסָ֖ף הַמַּזְכִּֽיר׃
The Rabshakeh said to them, "Tell Hezekiah, 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence of yours? What are you trusting in?
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה אִמְרוּ־נָ֖א אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר מָ֧ה הַבִּטָח֛וֹן הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּטָֽחְתָּ׃
I say that your strategy and strength for war are mere words.[^7] Now, on whom are you relying, that you have rebelled against me?
אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ אַךְ־דְּבַר־שְׂפָתַ֔יִם עֵצָ֥ה וּגְבוּרָ֖ה לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ עַל־מִ֣י בָטַ֔חְתָּ כִּ֥י מָרַ֖דְתָּ בִּֽי׃
Look, you are relying on Egypt, that broken reed of a staff, which goes into the hand of anyone who leans on it and pierces it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is to all who rely on him.

הִנֵּ֣ה בָטַ֡חְתָּ עַל־מִשְׁעֶנֶת֩ הַקָּנֶ֨ה הָרָצ֤וּץ הַזֶּה֙ עַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִסָּמֵ֥ךְ אִישׁ֙ עָלָ֔יו וּבָ֥א בְכַפּ֖וֹ וּנְקָבָ֑הּ כֵּ֚ן פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֔יִם לְכָֽל־הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים עָלָֽיו׃

But if you say to me, "We are trusting in Yahweh[^8] our God," isn't he the one whose high places[^9] and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship before this altar"?[^10]

וְכִי־תֹאמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י אֶל־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ בָּטָ֑חְנוּ הֲלוֹא־ה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵסִ֤יר חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶת־בָּמֹתָ֣יו וְאֶת־מִזְבְּחֹתָ֔יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לִֽיהוּדָה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִפְנֵ֛י הַמִּזְבֵּ֥חַ הַזֶּ֖ה תִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֽוּ׃
So now, make a wager with my master, the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able to put riders on them!
וְעַתָּה֙ הִתְעָ֣רֶב נָ֔א אֶת־אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לְךָ֙ אַלְפַּ֣יִם סוּסִ֔ים אִם־תּוּכַ֕ל לָ֥תֶת לְךָ֖ רֹכְבִ֥ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
How then can you drive back even one officer,[^11] one of the least of my master's servants, when you rely on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
וְאֵ֣יךְ תָּשִׁ֗יב אֵ֠ת פְּנֵ֨י פַחַ֥ת אַחַ֛ד עַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י הַקְטַנִּ֑ים וַתִּבְטַ֤ח לְךָ֙ עַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם לְרֶ֖כֶב וּלְפָרָשִֽׁים׃
And besides, have I come up against this land to destroy it without Yahweh? Yahweh himself said to me, "Go up against this land and destroy it."'"[^12]
וְעַתָּה֙ הֲמִבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עָלִ֛יתִי עַל־הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את לְהַשְׁחִיתָ֑הּ יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י עֲלֵ֛ה אֶל־הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את וְהַשְׁחִיתָֽהּ׃

Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic,[^13] for we understand it. Do not speak to us in the language of Judah[^14] in the hearing of the people on the wall."

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶלְיָקִים֩ וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א וְיוֹאָ֜ח אֶל־רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה דַּבֶּר־נָ֤א אֶל־עֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲרָמִ֔ית כִּ֥י שֹׁמְעִ֖ים אֲנָ֑חְנוּ וְאַל־תְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלֵ֙ינוּ֙ יְהוּדִ֔ית בְּאָזְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַחוֹמָֽה׃

But the Rabshakeh said, "Was it to your master and to you that my master sent me to speak these words? Wasn't it to the men sitting on the wall, who, like you, will have to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?"[^15]

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר רַב־שָׁקֵ֗ה הַאֶ֨ל אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ וְאֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲדֹנִ֔י לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲלֹ֣א עַל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ עַל־הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת־*חראיהם **צוֹאָתָ֗ם וְלִשְׁתּ֛וֹת אֶת־*שיניהם **מֵימֵ֥י **רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם עִמָּכֶֽם׃
Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in the language of Judah. He said, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ רַב־שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְקוֹל־גָּד֖וֹל יְהוּדִ֑ית וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְע֗וּ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הַגָּד֖וֹל מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃
This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to rescue you.[^16]
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אַל־יַשִּׁ֥א לָכֶ֖ם חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ כִּ֥י לֹֽא־יוּכַ֖ל לְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶֽם׃
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in Yahweh by saying, 'Yahweh will surely rescue us; this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'
וְאַל־יַבְטַ֨ח אֶתְכֶ֤ם חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר הַצֵּ֥ל יַצִּילֵ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me[^17] and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and each of you will drink water from his own cistern,
אַֽל־תִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ ס כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר עֲשֽׂוּ־אִתִּ֤י בְרָכָה֙ וּצְא֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וְאִכְל֤וּ אִישׁ־גַּפְנוֹ֙ וְאִ֣ישׁ תְּאֵנָת֔וֹ וּשְׁת֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ מֵי־בוֹרֽוֹ׃
until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.[^18]
עַד־בֹּאִ֕י וְלָקַחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּאַרְצְכֶ֑ם אֶ֤רֶץ דָּגָן֙ וְתִיר֔וֹשׁ אֶ֥רֶץ לֶ֖חֶם וּכְרָמִֽים׃
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, 'Yahweh will rescue us.' Has any of the gods of the nations rescued his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
פֶּן־יַסִּ֨ית אֶתְכֶ֤ם חִזְקִיָּ֙הוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֖ה יַצִּילֵ֑נוּ הַהִצִּ֜ילוּ אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־אַרְצ֔וֹ מִיַּ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim?[^19] Did they rescue Samaria from my hand?
אַיֵּ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י חֲמָת֙ וְאַרְפָּ֔ד אַיֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י סְפַרְוָ֑יִם וְכִֽי־הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־שֹׁמְר֖וֹן מִיָּדִֽי׃
Who among all the gods of these lands has rescued his land from my hand, that Yahweh should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?"
מִ֗י בְּכָל־אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָֽאֲרָצוֹת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־הִצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־אַרְצָ֖ם מִיָּדִ֑י כִּֽי־יַצִּ֧יל יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם מִיָּדִֽי׃
But they kept silent and did not answer him a word,[^20] for the king had commanded, "Do not answer him."
וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ וְלֹֽא־עָנ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ דָּבָ֑ר כִּֽי־מִצְוַ֨ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הִ֛יא לֵאמֹ֖ר לֹ֥א תַעֲנֻֽהוּ׃

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they told him the words of the Rabshakeh.

וַיָּבֹ֣א אֶלְיָקִ֣ים בֶּן־חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ אֲשֶׁר־עַל־הַ֠בַּיִת וְשֶׁבְנָ֨א הַסּוֹפֵ֜ר וְיוֹאָ֨ח בֶּן־אָסָ֧ף הַמַּזְכִּ֛יר אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י רַב שָׁקֵֽה׃ ס

n.1: In 701 BC. Chapters 36–39 are also found, with small differences, in 2 Kings 18:13–20:19, and parts of the story are told in 2 Chronicles 32. Where the Hebrew is the same, the English here follows the translation of 2 Kings. 2 Kings 18:14–16, Hezekiah's payment of tribute to Sennacherib, is not in Isaiah, and Hezekiah's psalm (38:9–20) is not in Kings.
n.2: Hebrew *rav-shaqeh*, from the Assyrian title *rab shaqe*, "chief cupbearer", a high official who here speaks for the king. Also in verses 4, 11–13 and 22. 2 Kings 18:17 says that the Tartan (the commander-in-chief) and the Rab-saris (the chief official) were sent with him.
n.3: A fortified city of Judah about 30 miles (50 km) southwest of Jerusalem, which Sennacherib was besieging.
n.4: Traditionally "the Fuller's Field", a field outside the city where cloth was washed and bleached. It is the place where Isaiah met Ahaz (7:3).
n.5: Literally "who was over the house", the title of the king's chief minister (22:15, 20–22). Also in verse 22.
n.6: Hebrew *mazkir*, "one who brings to remembrance": a senior royal official, perhaps the king's herald or the keeper of records. Also in verse 22.
n.7: Literally "I say: only a word of lips, counsel and strength for war." 2 Kings 18:20 reads "You say", that is, "You think that mere words are strategy and strength for war."
n.8: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.9: Hebrew *bamot*: places of worship, often on hilltops.
n.10: 2 Kings 18:22 reads "before this altar in Jerusalem".
