I myself have stirred him up in righteousness,[^13] and I will make all his ways straight. He will rebuild my city and set my exiles free, not for a price or a bribe, says Yahweh of Armies.[^14]
אָנֹכִי֙ הַעִירֹתִ֣הֽוּ בְצֶ֔דֶק וְכָל־דְּרָכָ֖יו אֲיַשֵּׁ֑ר הֽוּא־יִבְנֶ֤ה עִירִי֙ וְגָלוּתִ֣י יְשַׁלֵּ֔חַ לֹ֤א בִמְחִיר֙ וְלֹ֣א בְשֹׁ֔חַד אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ פ

This is what Yahweh says: The wealth of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush, and the Sabeans,[^15] men of great height, will come over to you and be yours.[^16] They will walk behind you, coming over in chains. They will bow down to you and plead with you:[^17] "Surely God is with you, and there is no other; there is no other god."

כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה יְגִ֨יעַ מִצְרַ֥יִם וּֽסְחַר־כּוּשׁ֮ וּסְבָאִים֮ אַנְשֵׁ֣י מִדָּה֒ עָלַ֤יִךְ יַעֲבֹ֙רוּ֙ וְלָ֣ךְ יִֽהְי֔וּ אַחֲרַ֣יִךְ יֵלֵ֔כוּ בַּזִּקִּ֖ים יַעֲבֹ֑רוּ וְאֵלַ֤יִךְ יִֽשְׁתַּחֲוּוּ֙ אֵלַ֣יִךְ יִתְפַּלָּ֔לוּ אַ֣ךְ בָּ֥ךְ אֵ֛ל וְאֵ֥ין ע֖וֹד אֶ֥פֶס אֱלֹהִֽים׃
Truly you are a God who hides himself, the God of Israel, the Savior.[^18]
אָכֵ֕ן אַתָּ֖ה אֵ֣ל מִסְתַּתֵּ֑ר אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃
They will be put to shame and disgraced, all of them; the makers of idols go off together in disgrace.
בּ֥וֹשׁוּ וְגַֽם־נִכְלְמ֖וּ כֻּלָּ֑ם יַחְדָּו֙ הָלְכ֣וּ בַכְּלִמָּ֔ה חָרָשֵׁ֖י צִירִֽים׃
But Israel is saved by Yahweh with an everlasting salvation. You will not be put to shame or disgraced, to ages everlasting.
יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נוֹשַׁ֣ע בַּיהוָ֔ה תְּשׁוּעַ֖ת עוֹלָמִ֑ים לֹא־תֵבֹ֥שׁוּ וְלֹא־תִכָּלְמ֖וּ עַד־ע֥וֹלְמֵי עַֽד׃ פ

For this is what Yahweh says, who created the heavens (he is God), who formed the earth and made it (he established it; he did not create it to be empty,[^19] but formed it to be inhabited): I am Yahweh, and there is no other.
כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר־יְ֠הוָה בּוֹרֵ֨א הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים יֹצֵ֨ר הָאָ֤רֶץ וְעֹשָׂהּ֙ ה֣וּא כֽוֹנְנָ֔הּ לֹא־תֹ֥הוּ בְרָאָ֖הּ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת יְצָרָ֑הּ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וְאֵ֥ין עֽוֹד׃
I did not speak in secret, somewhere in a land of darkness. I did not say to the offspring of Jacob, "Seek me in vain." I, Yahweh, speak what is right; I declare what is true.[^20]
לֹ֧א בַסֵּ֣תֶר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי בִּמְקוֹם֙ אֶ֣רֶץ חֹ֔שֶׁךְ לֹ֥א אָמַ֛רְתִּי לְזֶ֥רַע יַעֲקֹ֖ב תֹּ֣הוּ בַקְּשׁ֑וּנִי אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ דֹּבֵ֣ר צֶ֔דֶק מַגִּ֖יד מֵישָׁרִֽים׃
Gather together and come; draw near together, you survivors of the nations! They have no knowledge, those who carry around their wooden idols and keep praying to a god who cannot save.
הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וָבֹ֛אוּ הִֽתְנַגְּשׁ֥וּ יַחְדָּ֖ו פְּלִיטֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם לֹ֣א יָדְע֗וּ הַנֹּֽשְׂאִים֙ אֶת־עֵ֣ץ פִּסְלָ֔ם וּמִתְפַּלְלִ֔ים אֶל־אֵ֖ל לֹ֥א יוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

Declare it and present your case; let them take counsel together. Who announced this long ago, who declared it from of old? Was it not I, Yahweh? There is no other god apart from me, a righteous God and a Savior; there is none besides me.

הַגִּ֣ידוּ וְהַגִּ֔ישׁוּ אַ֥ף יִֽוָּעֲצ֖וּ יַחְדָּ֑ו מִ֣י הִשְׁמִיעַ֩ זֹ֨את מִקֶּ֜דֶם מֵאָ֣ז הִגִּידָ֗הּ הֲל֨וֹא אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ וְאֵֽין־ע֤וֹד אֱלֹהִים֙ מִבַּלְעָדַ֔י אֵֽל־צַדִּ֣יק וּמוֹשִׁ֔יעַ אַ֖יִן זוּלָתִֽי׃
Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other.
פְּנוּ־אֵלַ֥י וְהִוָּשְׁע֖וּ כָּל־אַפְסֵי־אָ֑רֶץ כִּ֥י אֲנִי־אֵ֖ל וְאֵ֥ין עֽוֹד׃
By myself I have sworn; a word has gone out from my mouth in righteousness, and it will not turn back: To me every knee will bow, every tongue will swear allegiance.[^21]
בִּ֣י נִשְׁבַּ֔עְתִּי יָצָ֨א מִפִּ֧י צְדָקָ֛ה דָּבָ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יָשׁ֑וּב כִּי־לִי֙ תִּכְרַ֣ע כָּל־בֶּ֔רֶךְ תִּשָּׁבַ֖ע כָּל־לָשֽׁוֹן׃
"Only in Yahweh," it will be said of me,[^22] "are righteousness and strength."[^23] All who raged against him will come to him and be put to shame.
אַ֧ךְ בַּיהוָ֛ה לִ֥י אָמַ֖ר צְדָק֣וֹת וָעֹ֑ז עָדָיו֙ יָב֣וֹא וְיֵבֹ֔שׁוּ כֹּ֖ל הַנֶּחֱרִ֥ים בּֽוֹ׃
In Yahweh all the offspring of Israel will be found righteous[^24] and will glory.
בַּיהוָ֛ה יִצְדְּק֥וּ וְיִֽתְהַלְל֖וּ כָּל־זֶ֥רַע יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *meshicho*, "his anointed one" (*mashiach*), the title of Israel's kings (1 Samuel 24:7; Psalm 2:2) and the source of the word "Messiah". Only here is it given to a foreign king. The text does not say that Cyrus was anointed with oil: Yahweh has chosen and appointed him for a task, as a king was set apart by anointing.
n.3: Literally "to loosen the loins of kings", that is, to ungird them, taking off the belts that held their weapons. Yahweh will "gird" Cyrus in verse 5.
n.4: Hebrew *hadurim*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "swellings" or "rough places". The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) and the Septuagint read "mountains".
n.5: Literally "I will gird you" (verse 1).
n.6: Hebrew *shalom*, "peace, well-being", and *ra'*, "evil, harm, disaster". The verse sets Yahweh over all that happens, good and bad.
n.7: Hebrew *tsedeq* and, later in the verse, *tsedaqah*, here God's saving order, which puts things right. Or "victory", "deliverance".
n.8: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning, used by the prophets to announce disaster (see 1:4). Also in verse 10.
n.9: Hebrew *yotser*, "former, potter", from the verb translated "form" in verses 7 and 18. Also later in this verse, "the one who forms it".
n.10: Literally "and your work: He has no hands". The pot is made to criticize its potter. Compare 29:16; Jeremiah 18:6; Romans 9:20–21.
n.11: Literally "The things to come, ask me! Concerning my children and concerning the work of my hands, command me!", perhaps said with irony.
n.12: The stars, pictured as an army (40:26).
n.13: Hebrew *tsedeq*, here God's right and saving purpose (41:2). *Him* is Cyrus.
n.14: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.15: The people of Seba (43:3), far to the south.
n.16: *You* is feminine singular in this verse: Zion is addressed as a woman.
n.17: Literally "pray to you".
n.18: The speaker may be the nations of verse 14, or the prophet.
n.19: Hebrew *tohu*, "formless, empty" (Genesis 1:2). In verse 19, "in vain" is the same word.
n.20: Literally "I speak righteousness; I declare what is upright".
n.21: Romans 14:11 quotes this verse, and Philippians 2:10–11 echoes it, following the Septuagint: "every tongue will confess to God".
n.22: Literally "Only in Yahweh, he has said to me" or "of me". The Hebrew is difficult.

v: Bel bows down; Nebo stoops.[^1] Their idols are loaded on animals and cattle. The things you used to carry in procession are loaded as a burden[^2] on weary animals.
כָּרַ֥ע בֵּל֙ קֹרֵ֣ס נְב֔וֹ הָיוּ֙ עֲצַבֵּיהֶ֔ם לַחַיָּ֖ה וְלַבְּהֵמָ֑ה נְשֻׂאֹתֵיכֶ֣ם עֲמוּס֔וֹת מַשָּׂ֖א לַעֲיֵפָֽה׃
They stoop and bow down together; they cannot rescue the burden. They themselves[^3] go into captivity.
קָרְס֤וּ כָֽרְעוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו לֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ מַלֵּ֣ט מַשָּׂ֑א וְנַפְשָׁ֖ם בַּשְּׁבִ֥י הָלָֽכָה׃ ס
Listen to me, house of Jacob, all the remnant of the house of Israel, you whom I have carried since birth, whom I have borne since you were in the womb.[^4]
שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְכָל־שְׁאֵרִ֖ית בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הַֽעֲמֻסִים֙ מִנִּי־בֶ֔טֶן הַנְּשֻׂאִ֖ים מִנִּי־רָֽחַם׃
Even to your old age I am he,[^5] and to your gray hairs I will carry you. I have made you, and I will bear you; I will carry you and rescue you.
וְעַד־זִקְנָה֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא וְעַד־שֵ[c]יבָ֖ה אֲנִ֣י אֶסְבֹּ֑ל אֲנִ֤י עָשִׂ֙יתִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אֶשָּׂ֔א וַאֲנִ֥י אֶסְבֹּ֖ל וַאֲמַלֵּֽט׃ ס
To whom will you compare me and make me equal? With whom will you liken me, that we may be alike?
לְמִ֥י תְדַמְי֖וּנִי וְתַשְׁו֑וּ וְתַמְשִׁל֖וּנִי וְנִדְמֶֽה׃
Those who pour out gold from the bag and weigh out silver on the scale hire a goldsmith, and he makes it into a god; they bow down and worship it.
הַזָּלִ֤ים זָהָב֙ מִכִּ֔יס וְכֶ֖סֶף בַּקָּנֶ֣ה יִשְׁקֹ֑לוּ יִשְׂכְּר֤וּ צוֹרֵף֙ וְיַעֲשֵׂ֣הוּ אֵ֔ל יִסְגְּד֖וּ אַף־יִֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃

They lift it to their shoulders and carry it; they set it in its place, and it stands there; it cannot move from its place. Even when someone cries out to it, it does not answer; it cannot save anyone from his trouble.
יִ֠שָּׂאֻהוּ עַל־כָּתֵ֨ף יִסְבְּלֻ֜הוּ וְיַנִּיחֻ֤הוּ תַחְתָּיו֙ וְיַֽעֲמֹ֔ד מִמְּקוֹמ֖וֹ לֹ֣א יָמִ֑ישׁ אַף־יִצְעַ֤ק אֵלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲנֶ֔ה מִצָּרָת֖וֹ לֹ֥א יוֹשִׁיעֶֽנּוּ׃ ס
Remember this and stand firm;[^6] take it to heart, you rebels.
זִכְרוּ־זֹ֖את וְהִתְאֹשָׁ֑שׁוּ הָשִׁ֥יבוּ פוֹשְׁעִ֖ים עַל־לֵֽב׃
Remember the former things of long ago, for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like me.
זִכְר֥וּ רִאשֹׁנ֖וֹת מֵעוֹלָ֑ם כִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֥י אֵל֙ וְאֵ֣ין ע֔וֹד אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְאֶ֥פֶס כָּמֽוֹנִי׃
I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times what has not yet been done. I say, "My plan will stand, and I will do all that I please."
מַגִּ֤יד מֵֽרֵאשִׁית֙ אַחֲרִ֔ית וּמִקֶּ֖דֶם אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־נַעֲשׂ֑וּ אֹמֵר֙ עֲצָתִ֣י תָק֔וּם וְכָל־חֶפְצִ֖י אֶעֱשֶֽׂה׃
I call a bird of prey from the east, the man of my plan[^7] from a far country. I have spoken, and I will bring it about; I have planned it, and I will do it.
קֹרֵ֤א מִמִּזְרָח֙ עַ֔יִט מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָ֖ק אִ֣ישׁ *עצתו **עֲצָתִ֑י אַף־דִּבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ אַף־אֲבִיאֶ֔נָּה יָצַ֖רְתִּי אַף־אֶעֱשֶֽׂנָּה׃ ס
Listen to me, you stubborn of heart,[^8] who are far from righteousness.
שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֖י אַבִּ֣ירֵי לֵ֑ב הָרְחוֹקִ֖ים מִצְּדָקָֽה׃
I am bringing my righteousness near; it is not far off, and my salvation will not be delayed. I will give salvation in Zion, and my glory to Israel.[^9]
קֵרַ֤בְתִּי צִדְקָתִי֙ לֹ֣א תִרְחָ֔ק וּתְשׁוּעָתִ֖י לֹ֣א תְאַחֵ֑ר וְנָתַתִּ֤י בְצִיּוֹן֙ תְּשׁוּעָ֔ה לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תִּפְאַרְתִּֽי׃ ס

n.1: *Bel*, "lord", is a title of Marduk, the chief god of Babylon; *Nebo* (Nabu), his son, was the god of writing and wisdom. Their images were carried in procession at the New Year festival. Here they are carried off on pack animals as the city falls.
n.2: Hebrew *massa*, the word translated "oracle" in 13:1. Also in verse 2.
n.3: Literally "their *nephesh*".
n.4: Babylon's gods must be carried by their worshipers (verses 1 and 7), but Yahweh has carried his people since their birth.
n.5: Hebrew *ani hu* (41:4).
n.6: Hebrew *hit'oshashu*, a word found only here, perhaps "take courage" or "show yourselves men". The meaning is uncertain.
n.7: The Hebrew text is written "his plan" but read "my plan". The *bird of prey* and the man are Cyrus (44:28; 45:1).
n.8: Literally "you mighty of heart".
n.9: Or "I will give salvation in Zion to Israel, my glory".

v: Go down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter Babylon![^1] Sit on the ground without a throne, daughter of the Chaldeans![^2] For you will no longer be called tender and delicate.
רְדִ֣י ׀ וּשְׁבִ֣י עַל־עָפָ֗ר בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־בָּבֶ֔ל שְׁבִי־לָאָ֥רֶץ אֵין־כִּסֵּ֖א בַּת־כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כִּ֣י לֹ֤א תוֹסִ֙יפִי֙ יִקְרְאוּ־לָ֔ךְ רַכָּ֖ה וַעֲנֻגָּֽה׃
Take millstones and grind flour.[^3] Remove your veil; strip off your skirt; bare your legs and wade through the rivers.
קְחִ֥י רֵחַ֖יִם וְטַ֣חֲנִי קָ֑מַח גַּלִּ֨י צַמָּתֵ֧ךְ חֶשְׂפִּי־שֹׁ֛בֶל גַּלִּי־שׁ֖וֹק עִבְרִ֥י נְהָרֽוֹת׃
Your nakedness will be exposed; your shame will be seen. I will take vengeance, and I will spare no one.[^4]
תִּגָּל֙ עֶרְוָתֵ֔ךְ גַּ֥ם תֵּרָאֶ֖ה חֶרְפָּתֵ֑ךְ נָקָ֣ם אֶקָּ֔ח וְלֹ֥א אֶפְגַּ֖ע אָדָֽם׃ ס
Our Redeemer, whose name is Yahweh of Armies,[^5] is the Holy One of Israel.[^6]
גֹּאֲלֵ֕נוּ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ קְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
Sit in silence and go into darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, for you will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms.[^7]
שְׁבִ֥י דוּמָ֛ם וּבֹ֥אִי בַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ בַּת־כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כִּ֣י לֹ֤א תוֹסִ֙יפִי֙ יִקְרְאוּ־לָ֔ךְ גְּבֶ֖רֶת מַמְלָכֽוֹת׃
I was angry with my people; I profaned my inheritance and handed them over to you. You showed them no mercy; even on the old you made your yoke very heavy.
קָצַ֣פְתִּי עַל־עַמִּ֗י חִלַּ֙לְתִּי֙ נַחֲלָתִ֔י וָאֶתְּנֵ֖ם בְּיָדֵ֑ךְ לֹא־שַׂ֤מְתְּ לָהֶם֙ רַחֲמִ֔ים עַל־זָקֵ֕ן הִכְבַּ֥דְתְּ עֻלֵּ֖ךְ מְאֹֽד׃
You said, "I will be queen forever." You did not take these things to heart or think about how it would end.
וַתֹּ֣אמְרִ֔י לְעוֹלָ֖ם אֶהְיֶ֣ה גְבָ֑רֶת עַ֣ד לֹא־שַׂ֥מְתְּ אֵ֙לֶּה֙ עַל־לִבֵּ֔ךְ לֹ֥א זָכַ֖רְתְּ אַחֲרִיתָֽהּ׃ ס
So now hear this, you lover of pleasure, who sit secure, who say in your heart, "I am, and there is no one besides me.[^8] I will never sit as a widow or know the loss of children."
וְעַתָּ֞ה שִׁמְעִי־זֹ֤את עֲדִינָה֙ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת לָבֶ֔טַח הָאֹֽמְרָה֙ בִּלְבָ֔בָהּ אֲנִ֖י וְאַפְסִ֣י ע֑וֹד לֹ֤א אֵשֵׁב֙ אַלְמָנָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א אֵדַ֖ע שְׁכֽוֹל׃
Both of these will come on you in a moment, in a single day: loss of children and widowhood. They will come on you in full measure, in spite of your many sorceries and the great power of your spells.
וְתָבֹאנָה֩ לָּ֨ךְ שְׁתֵּי־אֵ֥לֶּה רֶ֛גַע בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד שְׁכ֣וֹל וְאַלְמֹ֑ן כְּתֻמָּם֙ בָּ֣אוּ עָלַ֔יִךְ בְּרֹ֣ב כְּשָׁפַ֔יִךְ בְּעָצְמַ֥ת חֲבָרַ֖יִךְ מְאֹֽד׃
You trusted in your wickedness; you said, "No one sees me." Your wisdom and your knowledge led you astray, and you said in your heart, "I am, and there is no one besides me."
וַתִּבְטְחִ֣י בְרָעָתֵ֗ךְ אָמַרְתְּ֙ אֵ֣ין רֹאָ֔נִי חָכְמָתֵ֥ךְ וְדַעְתֵּ֖ךְ הִ֣יא שׁוֹבְבָ֑תֶךְ וַתֹּאמְרִ֣י בְלִבֵּ֔ךְ אֲנִ֖י וְאַפְסִ֥י עֽוֹד׃

But disaster[^9] will come on you, and you will not know how to charm it away.[^10] Ruin will fall on you that you cannot buy off;[^11] catastrophe will come on you suddenly, which you do not foresee.
וּבָ֧א עָלַ֣יִךְ רָעָ֗ה לֹ֤א תֵדְעִי֙ שַׁחְרָ֔הּ וְתִפֹּ֤ל עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ הֹוָ֔ה לֹ֥א תוּכְלִ֖י כַּפְּרָ֑הּ וְתָבֹ֨א עָלַ֧יִךְ פִּתְאֹ֛ם שׁוֹאָ֖ה לֹ֥א תֵדָֽעִי׃
Keep on, then, with your spells and your many sorceries, which you have labored at since your youth. Perhaps you will succeed; perhaps you will cause terror.
עִמְדִי־נָ֤א בַחֲבָרַ֙יִךְ֙ וּבְרֹ֣ב כְּשָׁפַ֔יִךְ בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָגַ֖עַתְּ מִנְּעוּרָ֑יִךְ אוּלַ֛י תּוּכְלִ֥י הוֹעִ֖יל אוּלַ֥י תַּעֲרֽוֹצִי׃
You are worn out by all your counsel. Let them stand up and save you, those who divide up the heavens,[^12] who gaze at the stars, who make known at each new moon what is coming on you.
נִלְאֵ֖ית בְּרֹ֣ב עֲצָתָ֑יִךְ יַעַמְדוּ־נָ֨א וְיוֹשִׁיעֻ֜ךְ *הברו **הֹבְרֵ֣י שָׁמַ֗יִם הַֽחֹזִים֙ בַּכּ֣וֹכָבִ֔ים מֽוֹדִיעִם֙ לֶחֳדָשִׁ֔ים מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָבֹ֖אוּ עָלָֽיִךְ׃
Look, they are like straw; the fire burns them up. They cannot save themselves[^13] from the power of the flame. This is no coal to warm oneself by, no fire to sit in front of!
הִנֵּ֨ה הָי֤וּ כְקַשׁ֙ אֵ֣שׁ שְׂרָפָ֔תַם לֹֽא־יַצִּ֥ילוּ אֶת־נַפְשָׁ֖ם מִיַּ֣ד לֶֽהָבָ֑ה אֵין־גַּחֶ֣לֶת לַחְמָ֔ם א֖וּר לָשֶׁ֥בֶת נֶגְדּֽוֹ׃
That is what they are to you, those you have labored with, those who have traded with you since your youth. Each one wanders off his own way; there is no one to save you.
כֵּ֥ן הָיוּ־לָ֖ךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָגָ֑עַתְּ סֹחֲרַ֣יִךְ מִנְּעוּרַ֗יִךְ אִ֤ישׁ לְעֶבְרוֹ֙ תָּע֔וּ אֵ֖ין מוֹשִׁיעֵֽךְ׃ ס

n.1: A poetic name for the city of Babylon and its people, pictured as a young woman (compare "Daughter Zion", 1:8). *You* is feminine singular throughout this chapter.
n.2: The people of southern Babylonia, whose kings ruled the Babylonian empire (13:19).
n.3: Grinding grain with a hand mill was the work of slave women (Exodus 11:5). The once delicate lady must now work and cross rivers on the way into captivity.
n.4: Literally "I will not meet a human being", perhaps "no one will stand in my way" or "I will not spare anyone".
n.5: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.6: This verse may be a cry of praise by Israel, breaking into Yahweh's words. *Redeemer* is Hebrew *go'el* (41:14).
n.7: Hebrew *geveret*, "mistress, lady", the woman who rules a household or a queen mother. Also in verse 7.
n.8: Babylon's boast takes up the words Yahweh uses of himself (45:5–6, 18, 21). Zephaniah 2:15 puts the same words in the mouth of Nineveh, and Revelation 18:7–8 echoes verses 7–9.
n.9: Hebrew *ra'ah*, "evil, disaster", the same word as *wickedness* in verse 10.
n.10: Hebrew *shachrah*, perhaps "to charm it away" or "its dawning": "you will not know when it is coming".
n.11: Hebrew *kapper*, "atone, appease, ransom", the word used in 6:7 for atonement.
n.12: Hebrew *hovre shamayim*, probably astrologers who divide the sky into regions to read the stars.
n.13: Literally "their *nephesh*".

v: Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and have come from the waters of Judah,[^1] you who swear by the name of Yahweh[^2] and invoke the God of Israel, but not in truth or righteousness.

שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֣את בֵּֽית־יַעֲקֹ֗ב הַנִּקְרָאִים֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִמֵּ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יָצָ֑אוּ הַֽנִּשְׁבָּעִ֣ים ׀ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה וּבֵאלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יַזְכִּ֔ירוּ לֹ֥א בֶאֱמֶ֖ת וְלֹ֥א בִצְדָקָֽה׃
For they call themselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel; Yahweh of Armies[^3] is his name.
כִּֽי־מֵעִ֤יר הַקֹּ֙דֶשׁ֙ נִקְרָ֔אוּ וְעַל־אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִסְמָ֑כוּ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ ס
The former things I declared long ago; they went out from my mouth, and I announced them. Then suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
הָרִֽאשֹׁנוֹת֙ מֵאָ֣ז הִגַּ֔דְתִּי וּמִפִּ֥י יָצְא֖וּ וְאַשְׁמִיעֵ֑ם פִּתְאֹ֥ם עָשִׂ֖יתִי וַתָּבֹֽאנָה׃
Because I knew that you are stubborn, your neck an iron sinew and your forehead bronze,
מִדַּעְתִּ֕י כִּ֥י קָשֶׁ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וְגִ֤יד בַּרְזֶל֙ עָרְפֶּ֔ךָ וּמִצְחֲךָ֖ נְחוּשָֽׁה׃
I declared them to you long ago; before they came to pass I announced them to you, so that you could not say, "My idol did them; my carved image and my cast image commanded them."
וָאַגִּ֤יד לְךָ֙ מֵאָ֔ז בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֑יךָ פֶּן־תֹּאמַר֙ עָצְבִּ֣י עָשָׂ֔ם וּפִסְלִ֥י וְנִסְכִּ֖י צִוָּֽם׃
You have heard it; now see it all.[^4] Will you not declare it? From now on I announce to you new things, hidden things that you have not known.
שָׁמַ֤עְתָּֽ חֲזֵה֙ כֻּלָּ֔הּ וְאַתֶּ֖ם הֲל֣וֹא תַגִּ֑ידוּ הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֤יךָ חֲדָשׁוֹת֙ מֵעַ֔תָּה וּנְצֻר֖וֹת וְלֹ֥א יְדַעְתָּֽם׃
They are created now, not long ago; before today you have not heard of them, so that you could not say, "Look, I knew them."
עַתָּ֤ה נִבְרְאוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מֵאָ֔ז וְלִפְנֵי־י֖וֹם וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתָּ֑ם פֶּן־תֹּאמַ֖ר הִנֵּ֥ה יְדַעְתִּֽין׃
You have never heard, you have never known; from of old your ear has not been opened. For I knew that you would surely act treacherously, and that you were called a rebel from birth.[^5]
גַּ֣ם לֹֽא־שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ גַּ֚ם לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתָּ גַּ֕ם מֵאָ֖ז לֹא־פִתְּחָ֣ה אָזְנֶ֑ךָ כִּ֤י יָדַ֙עְתִּי֙ בָּג֣וֹד תִּבְגּ֔וֹד וּפֹשֵׁ֥עַ מִבֶּ֖טֶן קֹ֥רָא לָֽךְ׃
For the sake of my name I hold back my anger; for the sake of my praise I restrain it for you, so as not to cut you off.
לְמַ֤עַן שְׁמִי֙ אַאֲרִ֣יךְ אַפִּ֔י וּתְהִלָּתִ֖י אֶחֱטָם־לָ֑ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הַכְרִיתֶֽךָ׃
Look, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.[^6]
הִנֵּ֥ה צְרַפְתִּ֖יךָ וְלֹ֣א בְכָ֑סֶף בְּחַרְתִּ֖יךָ בְּכ֥וּר עֹֽנִי׃
For my own sake, for my own sake, I do it; for how can my name be profaned?[^7] I will not give my glory to another.
לְמַעֲנִ֧י לְמַעֲנִ֛י אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה כִּ֣י אֵ֣יךְ יֵחָ֑ל וּכְבוֹדִ֖י לְאַחֵ֥ר לֹֽא־אֶתֵּֽן׃ ס
Listen to me, Jacob, Israel whom I called: I am he;[^8] I am the first, and I am also the last.
שְׁמַ֤ע אֵלַי֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מְקֹרָאִ֑י אֲנִי־הוּא֙ אֲנִ֣י רִאשׁ֔וֹן אַ֖ף אֲנִ֥י אַחֲרֽוֹן׃
My own hand laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand spread out the heavens. When I call to them, they stand up together.
אַף־יָדִי֙ יָ֣סְדָה אֶ֔רֶץ וִֽימִינִ֖י טִפְּחָ֣ה שָׁמָ֑יִם קֹרֵ֥א אֲנִ֛י אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יַעַמְד֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃
Gather, all of you, and listen! Who among them declared these things? The one Yahweh loves will carry out his purpose against Babylon, and his arm will be against the Chaldeans.[^9]
הִקָּבְצ֤וּ כֻלְּכֶם֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔עוּ מִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם הִגִּ֣יד אֶת־אֵ֑לֶּה יְהוָ֣ה אֲהֵב֔וֹ יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה חֶפְצוֹ֙ בְּבָבֶ֔ל וּזְרֹע֖וֹ כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
I, I have spoken; I have called him. I have brought him, and he will succeed in his way.
אֲנִ֥י אֲנִ֛י דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי אַף־קְרָאתִ֑יו הֲבִיאֹתִ֖יו וְהִצְלִ֥יחַ דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃
Come near to me and hear this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it came to be, I have been there. And now the Lord Yahweh has sent me, and his Spirit.[^10]
קִרְב֧וּ אֵלַ֣י שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֗את לֹ֤א מֵרֹאשׁ֙ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי מֵעֵ֥ת הֱיוֹתָ֖הּ שָׁ֣ם אָ֑נִי וְעַתָּ֗ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה שְׁלָחַ֖נִי וְרוּחֽוֹ׃ פ
This is what Yahweh says, your Redeemer,[^11] the Holy One of Israel: I am Yahweh your God, who teaches you what is for your good, who leads you in the way you should go.
כֹּֽה־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְךָ֖ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲנִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ מְלַמֶּדְךָ֣ לְהוֹעִ֔יל מַדְרִֽיכֲךָ֖ בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ תֵּלֵֽךְ׃
If only you had paid attention to my commands! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
ל֥וּא הִקְשַׁ֖בְתָּ לְמִצְוֺתָ֑י וַיְהִ֤י כַנָּהָר֙ שְׁלוֹמֶ֔ךָ וְצִדְקָתְךָ֖ כְּגַלֵּ֥י הַיָּֽם׃
Your offspring would have been like the sand, and your descendants like its grains. Their name would never be cut off or destroyed from before me.
וַיְהִ֤י כַחוֹל֙ זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וְצֶאֱצָאֵ֥י מֵעֶ֖יךָ כִּמְעֹתָ֑יו לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֧ת וְֽלֹא־יִשָּׁמֵ֛ד שְׁמ֖וֹ מִלְּפָנָֽי׃
Go out from Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With a shout of joy declare this, proclaim it, send it out to the end of the earth. Say, "Yahweh has redeemed his servant Jacob!"
צְא֣וּ מִבָּבֶל֮ בִּרְח֣וּ מִכַּשְׂדִּים֒ בְּק֣וֹל רִנָּ֗ה הַגִּ֤ידוּ הַשְׁמִ֙יעוּ֙ זֹ֔את הוֹצִיא֖וּהָ עַד־קְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ אִמְר֕וּ גָּאַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה עַבְדּ֥וֹ יַעֲקֹֽב׃
They did not thirst when he led them through the deserts. He made water flow for them from the rock; he split the rock, and the water gushed out.[^12]
וְלֹ֣א צָמְא֗וּ בָּחֳרָבוֹת֙ הֽוֹלִיכָ֔ם מַ֥יִם מִצּ֖וּר הִזִּ֣יל לָ֑מוֹ וַיִּ֨בְקַע־צ֔וּר וַיָּזֻ֖בוּ מָֽיִם׃
There is no peace, says Yahweh, for the wicked.[^13]
אֵ֣ין שָׁל֔וֹם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָרְשָׁעִֽים׃ ס

n.1: Literally "from the waters of Judah", perhaps "from the spring of Judah", the source of the family. Some scholars read *mimme'e*, "from the body of Judah", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.4: Literally "You have heard; see all of it".
n.5: Literally "from the womb".
n.6: Or "I have tested you". The Hebrew verb *bachar*, "choose", has the sense "test" in later Hebrew and Aramaic. The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) reads "I have tested you".
n.7: Literally "how can it be profaned?"
n.8: Hebrew *ani hu* (41:4).
n.9: Or "and his arm will be on the Chaldeans". Literally "and his arm Chaldeans". *The one Yahweh loves* is Cyrus (verse 15; 45:1).
n.10: Or "the Lord Yahweh and his Spirit have sent me", or "the Lord Yahweh has sent me with his Spirit". Here a new speaker, the prophet or the servant, speaks of being sent (compare 49:1–6; 61:1). *Spirit* is Hebrew *ruach*.
n.11: Hebrew *go'el* (41:14).
n.12: As in the wilderness after the exodus (Exodus 17:6; Numbers 20:11).
n.13: This line is repeated in 57:21. Each closes a section of chapters 40–66.

v: Listen to me, you coastlands;[^1] pay attention, you peoples far away! Yahweh[^2] called me before I was born; from my mother's body he named me.[^3]
שִׁמְע֤וּ אִיִּים֙ אֵלַ֔י וְהַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ לְאֻמִּ֖ים מֵרָח֑וֹק יְהוָה֙ מִבֶּ֣טֶן קְרָאָ֔נִי מִמְּעֵ֥י אִמִּ֖י הִזְכִּ֥יר שְׁמִֽי׃
He made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand he hid me. He made me a polished arrow; in his quiver he concealed me.[^4]
וַיָּ֤שֶׂם פִּי֙ כְּחֶ֣רֶב חַדָּ֔ה בְּצֵ֥ל יָד֖וֹ הֶחְבִּיאָ֑נִי וַיְשִׂימֵ֙נִי֙ לְחֵ֣ץ בָּר֔וּר בְּאַשְׁפָּת֖וֹ הִסְתִּירָֽנִי׃
He said to me, "You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will show my glory."[^5]
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֖י עַבְדִּי־אָ֑תָּה יִשְׂרָאֵ֕ל אֲשֶׁר־בְּךָ֖ אֶתְפָּאָֽר׃
But I said, "I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for nothing and emptiness. Yet surely my cause[^6] is with Yahweh, and my reward with my God."
וַאֲנִ֤י אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ לְרִ֣יק יָגַ֔עְתִּי לְתֹ֥הוּ וְהֶ֖בֶל כֹּחִ֣י כִלֵּ֑יתִי אָכֵן֙ מִשְׁפָּטִ֣י אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וּפְעֻלָּתִ֖י אֶת־אֱלֹהָֽי׃

And now Yahweh says, he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him, so that Israel might be gathered to him[^7] (for I am honored in the eyes of Yahweh, and my God has become my strength),
וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה יֹצְרִ֤י מִבֶּ֙טֶן֙ לְעֶ֣בֶד ל֔וֹ לְשׁוֹבֵ֤ב יַֽעֲקֹב֙ אֵלָ֔יו וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל *לא **ל֣וֹ יֵאָסֵ֑ף וְאֶכָּבֵד֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וֵאלֹהַ֖י הָיָ֥ה עֻזִּֽי׃

he says, "It is too small a thing for you to be my servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob and bring back the survivors of Israel. I will also make you a light for the nations, so that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth."[^8]

וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָקֵ֨ל מִֽהְיוֹתְךָ֥ לִי֙ עֶ֔בֶד לְהָקִים֙ אֶת־שִׁבְטֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב *ונצירי **וּנְצוּרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהָשִׁ֑יב וּנְתַתִּ֙יךָ֙ לְא֣וֹר גּוֹיִ֔ם לִֽהְי֥וֹת יְשׁוּעָתִ֖י עַד־קְצֵ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃ ס

This is what Yahweh says, the Redeemer[^9] of Israel and his Holy One, to the one who is deeply despised,[^10] abhorred by the nation, the servant of rulers: Kings will see and rise up; princes will bow down, because of Yahweh, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.

כֹּ֣ה אָֽמַר־יְהוָה֩ גֹּאֵ֨ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל קְדוֹשׁ֗וֹ לִבְזֹה־נֶ֜פֶשׁ לִמְתָ֤עֵֽב גּוֹי֙ לְעֶ֣בֶד מֹשְׁלִ֔ים מְלָכִים֙ יִרְא֣וּ וָקָ֔מוּ שָׂרִ֖ים וְיִֽשְׁתַּחֲוּ֑וּ לְמַ֤עַן יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נֶאֱמָ֔ן קְדֹ֥שׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיִּבְחָרֶֽךָּ׃

This is what Yahweh says: In a time of favor I have answered you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you.[^11] I will keep you and make you a covenant for the people,[^12] to restore the land and to give out again the desolate inheritances,
כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה בְּעֵ֤ת רָצוֹן֙ עֲנִיתִ֔יךָ וּבְי֥וֹם יְשׁוּעָ֖ה עֲזַרְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֶצָּרְךָ֗ וְאֶתֶּנְךָ֙ לִבְרִ֣ית עָ֔ם לְהָקִ֣ים אֶ֔רֶץ לְהַנְחִ֖יל נְחָל֥וֹת שֹׁמֵמֽוֹת׃
saying to the prisoners, "Come out," and to those in darkness, "Show yourselves." They will graze along the roads, and their pasture will be on all the bare heights.
לֵאמֹ֤ר לַֽאֲסוּרִים֙ צֵ֔אוּ לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּחֹ֖שֶׁךְ הִגָּל֑וּ עַל־דְּרָכִ֣ים יִרְע֔וּ וּבְכָל־שְׁפָיִ֖ים מַרְעִיתָֽם׃
They will not hunger or thirst; the scorching heat and the sun will not strike them. For he who has compassion on them will lead them and guide them to springs of water.[^13]
לֹ֤א יִרְעָ֙בוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִצְמָ֔אוּ וְלֹא־יַכֵּ֥ם שָׁרָ֖ב וָשָׁ֑מֶשׁ כִּי־מְרַחֲמָ֣ם יְנַהֲגֵ֔ם וְעַל־מַבּ֥וּעֵי מַ֖יִם יְנַהֲלֵֽם׃
I will make all my mountains into a road, and my highways will be raised up.
וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י כָל־הָרַ֖י לַדָּ֑רֶךְ וּמְסִלֹּתַ֖י יְרֻמֽוּן׃
Look, these will come from far away; look, these from the north and from the west,[^14] and these from the land of Sinim.[^15]
הִנֵּה־אֵ֕לֶּה מֵרָח֖וֹק יָבֹ֑אוּ וְהִֽנֵּה־אֵ֙לֶּה֙ מִצָּפ֣וֹן וּמִיָּ֔ם וְאֵ֖לֶּה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ סִינִֽים׃
Shout for joy, you heavens! Rejoice, you earth! Break into song, you mountains! For Yahweh has comforted his people and will have compassion on his afflicted ones.
רָנּ֤וּ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְגִ֣ילִי אָ֔רֶץ *יפצחו **וּפִצְח֥וּ הָרִ֖ים רִנָּ֑ה כִּֽי־נִחַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ וַעֲנִיָּ֖ו יְרַחֵֽם׃ ס
But Zion said, "Yahweh has abandoned me; the Lord has forgotten me."
וַתֹּ֥אמֶר צִיּ֖וֹן עֲזָבַ֣נִי יְהוָ֑ה וַאדֹנָ֖י שְׁכֵחָֽנִי׃
Can a woman forget her nursing child, or have no compassion on the son of her womb? Even if these forget, I will not forget you.[^16]
הֲתִשְׁכַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ עוּלָ֔הּ מֵרַחֵ֖ם בֶּן־בִּטְנָ֑הּ גַּם־אֵ֣לֶּה תִשְׁכַּ֔חְנָה וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֥א אֶשְׁכָּחֵֽךְ׃
Look, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are always before me.
הֵ֥ן עַל־כַּפַּ֖יִם חַקֹּתִ֑יךְ חוֹמֹתַ֥יִךְ נֶגְדִּ֖י תָּמִֽיד׃
Your children hurry back;[^17] those who destroyed you and laid you waste go away from you.
מִֽהֲר֖וּ בָּנָ֑יִךְ מְהָֽרְסַ֥יִךְ וּמַחֲרִבַ֖יִךְ מִמֵּ֥ךְ יֵצֵֽאוּ׃
Lift up your eyes and look around: they all gather and come to you. As surely as I live, declares Yahweh, you will put them all on like jewelry; you will tie them on as a bride does.
שְׂאִֽי־סָבִ֤יב עֵינַ֙יִךְ֙ וּרְאִ֔י כֻּלָּ֖ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ בָֽאוּ־לָ֑ךְ חַי־אָ֣נִי נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ כָּעֲדִ֣י תִלְבָּ֔שִׁי וּֽתְקַשְּׁרִ֖ים כַּכַּלָּֽה׃
For your ruins and your desolate places and your devastated land—now you will be too small for your inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far away.
כִּ֤י חָרְבֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ וְשֹׁ֣מְמֹתַ֔יִךְ וְאֶ֖רֶץ הֲרִֽסֻתֵ֑יךְ כִּ֤י עַתָּה֙ תֵּצְרִ֣י מִיּוֹשֵׁ֔ב וְרָחֲק֖וּ מְבַלְּעָֽיִךְ׃
The children born in your time of bereavement will yet say in your hearing, "This place is too cramped for me; make room for me to live."
ע֚וֹד יֹאמְר֣וּ בְאָזְנַ֔יִךְ בְּנֵ֖י שִׁכֻּלָ֑יִךְ צַר־לִ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם גְּשָׁה־לִּ֥י וְאֵשֵֽׁבָה׃
Then you will say in your heart, "Who bore me these? I was bereaved and barren, exiled and turned away. Who brought these up? Look, I was left all alone; where have these come from?"
וְאָמַ֣רְתְּ בִּלְבָבֵ֗ךְ מִ֤י יָֽלַד־לִי֙ אֶת־אֵ֔לֶּה וַאֲנִ֥י שְׁכוּלָ֖ה וְגַלְמוּדָ֑ה גֹּלָ֣ה ׀ וְסוּרָ֗ה וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ מִ֣י גִדֵּ֔ל הֵ֤ן אֲנִי֙ נִשְׁאַ֣רְתִּי לְבַדִּ֔י אֵ֖לֶּה אֵיפֹ֥ה הֵֽם׃ פ

This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Look, I will lift up my hand to the nations and raise my signal flag to the peoples. They will bring your sons in their arms,[^18] and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders.
כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אֶשָּׂ֤א אֶל־גּוֹיִם֙ יָדִ֔י וְאֶל־עַמִּ֖ים אָרִ֣ים נִסִּ֑י וְהֵבִ֤יאוּ בָנַ֙יִךְ֙ בְּחֹ֔צֶן וּבְנֹתַ֖יִךְ עַל־כָּתֵ֥ף תִּנָּשֶֽׂאנָה׃

Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am Yahweh; those who hope in me will not be put to shame.

וְהָי֨וּ מְלָכִ֜ים אֹֽמְנַ֗יִךְ וְשָׂרֽוֹתֵיהֶם֙ מֵינִ֣יקֹתַ֔יִךְ אַפַּ֗יִם אֶ֚רֶץ יִשְׁתַּ֣חֲווּ לָ֔ךְ וַעֲפַ֥ר רַגְלַ֖יִךְ יְלַחֵ֑כוּ וְיָדַ֙עַתְּ֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יֵבֹ֖שׁוּ קֹוָֽי׃ ס
Can plunder be taken from a warrior, or captives be rescued from a righteous one?[^19]
הֲיֻקַּ֥ח מִגִּבּ֖וֹר מַלְק֑וֹחַ וְאִם־שְׁבִ֥י צַדִּ֖יק יִמָּלֵֽט׃

But this is what Yahweh says: Even the captives of the warrior will be taken, and the plunder of the tyrant will be rescued. I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children.
כִּי־כֹ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה גַּם־שְׁבִ֤י גִבּוֹר֙ יֻקָּ֔ח וּמַלְק֥וֹחַ עָרִ֖יץ יִמָּלֵ֑ט וְאֶת־יְרִיבֵךְ֙ אָנֹכִ֣י אָרִ֔יב וְאֶת־בָּנַ֖יִךְ אָנֹכִ֥י אוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh, and they will be drunk on their own blood as on new wine. Then all people[^20] will know that I, Yahweh, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.[^21]
וְהַאֲכַלְתִּ֤י אֶת־מוֹנַ֙יִךְ֙ אֶת־בְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְכֶעָסִ֖יס דָּמָ֣ם יִשְׁכָּר֑וּן וְיָדְע֣וּ כָל־בָּשָׂ֗ר כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ מֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֔ךְ וְגֹאֲלֵ֖ךְ אֲבִ֥יר יַעֲקֹֽב׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *iyyim*, the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean (11:11), and in these chapters the most distant lands. Verses 1–13 are the second of the servant passages (see 42:1). In verses 1–6 the servant himself speaks.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "from the womb he called me; from the inner parts of my mother he made mention of my name". Compare Jeremiah 1:5; Galatians 1:15.
n.4: The sword and the arrow are kept ready and hidden until the time to use them. Revelation 1:16 and 2:12 echo the first line.
n.5: Here the servant is named *Israel*, as in 41:8 and 44:1–2. Yet in verses 5–6 he has a task toward Jacob and Israel. Some have taken him to be the true Israel, the faithful within the people; others an individual who embodies Israel. *Show my glory* is Hebrew *etpa'ar*, "I will be glorified" or "I will glory".
n.6: Hebrew *mishpat*, "justice, right, judgment". *Reward* is literally "wage".
n.7: The Hebrew text is written "and Israel is not gathered" but read "and Israel to him is gathered". The two words for "not" and "to him" sound alike (*lo*).
n.8: Literally "to be my salvation to the end of the earth", that is, "so that you may be my salvation" or "so that my salvation may be". Acts 13:47 quotes this sentence from the Septuagint, and Simeon's words in Luke 2:32 echo it.
n.9: Hebrew *go'el* (41:14). Also in verse 26.
n.10: Literally "to one despised of *nephesh*". Or "to the one whom people despise".
n.11: 2 Corinthians 6:2 quotes this sentence from the Septuagint: "At an acceptable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I helped you."
n.12: Hebrew *berit am* (42:6).
n.13: Revelation 7:16–17 echoes this verse.
n.14: Literally "from the sea", the Mediterranean, to the west of Israel.
n.15: An unknown land. The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) reads *Sewenim*, that is, Syene (modern Aswan) in southern Egypt (Ezekiel 29:10), where there was a colony of Jews in the Persian period.
n.16: *You* is feminine singular in verses 15–26: Zion is addressed as a woman and a mother.
n.17: The same consonants can be read *bonayikh*, "your builders", the reading of the Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a).
n.18: Literally "in their bosom", the fold of the garment over the chest.
n.19: The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) reads "from a tyrant", as in verse 25.
n.21: Hebrew *avir ya'aqov*, a title of God (Genesis 49:24; Isaiah 1:24; 60:16).

v: This is what Yahweh[^1] says: Where is your mother's certificate of divorce, with which I sent her away?[^2] Or to which of my creditors did I sell you? Look, it was for your sins that you were sold, and for your rebellious acts that your mother was sent away.

כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣י זֶ֠ה סֵ֣פֶר כְּרִית֤וּת אִמְּכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שִׁלַּחְתִּ֔יהָ א֚וֹ מִ֣י מִנּוֹשַׁ֔י אֲשֶׁר־מָכַ֥רְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם ל֑וֹ הֵ֤ן בַּעֲוֺנֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ נִמְכַּרְתֶּ֔ם וּבְפִשְׁעֵיכֶ֖ם שֻׁלְּחָ֥ה אִמְּכֶֽם׃

Why was there no one when I came? Why was there no one to answer when I called? Is my hand too short to redeem?[^3] Have I no power to rescue? Look, with a rebuke I dry up the sea; I turn rivers into a wilderness. Their fish rot for lack of water and die of thirst.

מַדּ֨וּעַ בָּ֜אתִי וְאֵ֣ין אִ֗ישׁ קָרָֽאתִי֮ וְאֵ֣ין עוֹנֶה֒ הֲקָצ֨וֹר קָצְרָ֤ה יָדִי֙ מִפְּד֔וּת וְאִם־אֵֽין־בִּ֥י כֹ֖חַ לְהַצִּ֑יל הֵ֣ן בְּגַעֲרָתִ֞י אַחֲרִ֣יב יָ֗ם אָשִׂ֤ים נְהָרוֹת֙ מִדְבָּ֔ר תִּבְאַ֤שׁ דְּגָתָם֙ מֵאֵ֣ין מַ֔יִם וְתָמֹ֖ת בַּצָּמָֽא׃
I clothe the heavens with darkness and make sackcloth their covering.
אַלְבִּ֥ישׁ שָׁמַ֖יִם קַדְר֑וּת וְשַׂ֖ק אָשִׂ֥ים כְּסוּתָֽם׃ ס

The Lord Yahweh has given me the tongue of one who is taught,[^4] so that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word.[^5] Morning by morning he wakens, he wakens my ear to listen like one who is taught.
אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה נָ֤תַן לִי֙ לְשׁ֣וֹן לִמּוּדִ֔ים לָדַ֛עַת לָע֥וּת אֶת־יָעֵ֖ף דָּבָ֑ר יָעִ֣יר ׀ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֗קֶר יָעִ֥יר לִי֙ אֹ֔זֶן לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ כַּלִּמּוּדִֽים׃
The Lord Yahweh has opened my ear, and I did not rebel; I did not turn back.
אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ פָּתַֽח־לִ֣י אֹ֔זֶן וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֣א מָרִ֑יתִי אָח֖וֹר לֹ֥א נְסוּגֹֽתִי׃
I gave my back to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who pulled out my beard. I did not hide my face from insults and spitting.[^6]
גֵּוִי֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לְמַכִּ֔ים וּלְחָיַ֖י לְמֹֽרְטִ֑ים פָּנַי֙ לֹ֣א הִסְתַּ֔רְתִּי מִכְּלִמּ֖וֹת וָרֹֽק׃
But the Lord Yahweh helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced. Therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I will not be put to shame.
וַאדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ יַֽעֲזָר־לִ֔י עַל־כֵּ֖ן לֹ֣א נִכְלָ֑מְתִּי עַל־כֵּ֞ן שַׂ֤מְתִּי פָנַי֙ כַּֽחַלָּמִ֔ישׁ וָאֵדַ֖ע כִּי־לֹ֥א אֵבֽוֹשׁ׃
He who proves me right is near.[^7] Who will bring charges against me? Let us stand up together. Who is my accuser?[^8] Let him come near me.
קָרוֹב֙ מַצְדִּיקִ֔י מִֽי־יָרִ֥יב אִתִּ֖י נַ֣עַמְדָה יָּ֑חַד מִֽי־בַ֥עַל מִשְׁפָּטִ֖י יִגַּ֥שׁ אֵלָֽי׃
Look, the Lord Yahweh helps me; who will declare me guilty? Look, they will all wear out like a garment; the moth will eat them up.
הֵ֣ן אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ יַֽעֲזָר־לִ֔י מִי־ה֖וּא יַרְשִׁיעֵ֑נִי הֵ֤ן כֻּלָּם֙ כַּבֶּ֣גֶד יִבְל֔וּ עָ֖שׁ יֹאכְלֵֽם׃
Who among you fears Yahweh and obeys the voice of his servant? Whoever walks in darkness and has no light, let him trust in the name of Yahweh and rely on his God.
מִ֤י בָכֶם֙ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֔ה שֹׁמֵ֖עַ בְּק֣וֹל עַבְדּ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר ׀ הָלַ֣ךְ חֲשֵׁכִ֗ים וְאֵ֥ין נֹ֙גַהּ֙ ל֔וֹ יִבְטַח֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וְיִשָּׁעֵ֖ן בֵּאלֹהָֽיו׃

But look, all of you who kindle a fire, who arm yourselves with burning arrows,[^9] walk in the light of your fire and among the burning arrows you have lit! This is what you will receive from my hand: you will lie down in torment.
הֵ֧ן כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם קֹ֥דְחֵי אֵ֖שׁ מְאַזְּרֵ֣י זִיק֑וֹת לְכ֣וּ ׀ בְּא֣וּר אֶשְׁכֶ֗ם וּבְזִיקוֹת֙ בִּֽעַרְתֶּ֔ם מִיָּדִי֙ הָיְתָה־זֹּ֣את לָכֶ֔ם לְמַעֲצֵבָ֖ה תִּשְׁכָּבֽוּן׃ פ

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: A husband who divorced his wife gave her a written certificate (Deuteronomy 24:1; Jeremiah 3:8). Yahweh has given Zion, the mother, no such certificate, and he has not sold her children to pay a debt (compare 2 Kings 4:1). Their exile is not a final break.
n.3: Hebrew *padah*, "ransom, redeem".
n.4: Hebrew *limmudim*, "those who are taught, disciples" (8:16). Also later in this verse. Verses 4–11 are the third of the servant passages (see 42:1). The speaker is not named, but verse 10 calls him "his servant".
n.5: Hebrew *la'ut*, a word found only here, of uncertain meaning, perhaps "to help" or "to answer".
n.6: Compare the treatment of Jesus in Matthew 26:67; Mark 14:65 and 15:19.
n.7: Hebrew *matsdiq*, "one who declares in the right, vindicates", a term from the law court. Romans 8:33–34 echoes verses 8–9.
n.8: Literally "Who is the lord of my judgment?", that is, the one who brings a case against me.
n.9: Or "firebrands". Hebrew *ziqot*, perhaps flaming arrows or sparks. *Arm yourselves* is literally "gird yourselves".

v: Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek Yahweh:[^1] Look to the rock from which you were cut and to the quarry from which you were dug.[^2]
שִׁמְע֥וּ אֵלַ֛י רֹ֥דְפֵי צֶ֖דֶק מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הַבִּ֙יטוּ֙ אֶל־צ֣וּר חֻצַּבְתֶּ֔ם וְאֶל־מַקֶּ֥בֶת בּ֖וֹר נֻקַּרְתֶּֽם׃
Look to your ancestor Abraham[^3] and to Sarah who gave birth to you. For he was only one when I called him, and I blessed him and made him many.
הַבִּ֙יטוּ֙ אֶל־אַבְרָהָ֣ם אֲבִיכֶ֔ם וְאֶל־שָׂרָ֖ה תְּחוֹלֶלְכֶ֑ם כִּי־אֶחָ֣ד קְרָאתִ֔יו וַאֲבָרְכֵ֖הוּ וְאַרְבֵּֽהוּ׃ ס

For Yahweh will comfort Zion; he will comfort all her ruins. He will make her wilderness like Eden, her desert like the garden of Yahweh. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of singing.
כִּֽי־נִחַ֨ם יְהוָ֜ה צִיּ֗וֹן נִחַם֙ כָּל־חָרְבֹתֶ֔יהָ וַיָּ֤שֶׂם מִדְבָּרָהּ֙ כְּעֵ֔דֶן וְעַרְבָתָ֖הּ כְּגַן־יְהוָ֑ה שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יִמָּ֣צֵא בָ֔הּ תּוֹדָ֖ה וְק֥וֹל זִמְרָֽה׃ ס
Pay attention to me, my people; listen to me, my nation. For instruction[^4] will go out from me, and I will set my justice as a light for the peoples.[^5]
הַקְשִׁ֤יבוּ אֵלַי֙ עַמִּ֔י וּלְאוּמִּ֖י אֵלַ֣י הַאֲזִ֑ינוּ כִּ֤י תוֹרָה֙ מֵאִתִּ֣י תֵצֵ֔א וּמִשְׁפָּטִ֔י לְא֥וֹר עַמִּ֖ים אַרְגִּֽיעַ׃
My righteousness draws near; my salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples. The coastlands[^6] will hope in me and wait for my arm.
קָר֤וֹב צִדְקִי֙ יָצָ֣א יִשְׁעִ֔י וּזְרֹעַ֖י עַמִּ֣ים יִשְׁפֹּ֑טוּ אֵלַי֙ אִיִּ֣ים יְקַוּ֔וּ וְאֶל־זְרֹעִ֖י יְיַחֵלֽוּן׃

Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look at the earth beneath. For the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will die like gnats.[^7] But my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness will never fail.

שְׂאוּ֩ לַשָּׁמַ֨יִם עֵֽינֵיכֶ֜ם וְֽהַבִּ֧יטוּ אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ מִתַּ֗חַת כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֜יִם כֶּעָשָׁ֤ן נִמְלָ֙חוּ֙ וְהָאָ֙רֶץ֙ כַּבֶּ֣גֶד תִּבְלֶ֔ה וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כְּמוֹ־כֵ֣ן יְמוּת֑וּן וִישֽׁוּעָתִי֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְצִדְקָתִ֖י לֹ֥א תֵחָֽת׃ ס
Listen to me, you who know what is right, you people who have my instruction in your hearts. Do not fear the reproach of mere mortals, or be dismayed by their insults.
שִׁמְע֤וּ אֵלַי֙ יֹ֣דְעֵי צֶ֔דֶק עַ֖ם תּוֹרָתִ֣י בְלִבָּ֑ם אַל־תִּֽירְאוּ֙ חֶרְפַּ֣ת אֱנ֔וֹשׁ וּמִגִּדֻּפֹתָ֖ם אַל־תֵּחָֽתּוּ׃
For the moth will eat them like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation through all generations.
כִּ֤י כַבֶּ֙גֶד֙ יֹאכְלֵ֣ם עָ֔שׁ וְכַצֶּ֖מֶר יֹאכְלֵ֣ם סָ֑ס וְצִדְקָתִי֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וִישׁוּעָתִ֖י לְד֥וֹר דּוֹרִֽים׃ ס
Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of Yahweh! Awake, as in days of old, in generations long ago. Was it not you who cut Rahab to pieces,[^8] who pierced the dragon?[^9]
עוּרִ֨י עוּרִ֤י לִבְשִׁי־עֹז֙ זְר֣וֹעַ יְהוָ֔ה ע֚וּרִי כִּ֣ימֵי קֶ֔דֶם דֹּר֖וֹת עוֹלָמִ֑ים הֲל֥וֹא אַתְּ־הִ֛יא הַמַּחְצֶ֥בֶת רַ֖הַב מְחוֹלֶ֥לֶת תַּנִּֽין׃
Was it not you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a road for the redeemed to cross?[^10]
הֲל֤וֹא אַתְּ־הִיא֙ הַמַּחֲרֶ֣בֶת יָ֔ם מֵ֖י תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֑ה הַשָּׂ֙מָה֙ מַֽעֲמַקֵּי־יָ֔ם דֶּ֖רֶךְ לַעֲבֹ֥ר גְּאוּלִֽים׃
Those whom Yahweh has ransomed will return and come to Zion with singing. Everlasting joy will be on their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.[^11]
וּפְדוּיֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה יְשׁוּב֗וּן וּבָ֤אוּ צִיּוֹן֙ בְּרִנָּ֔ה וְשִׂמְחַ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם עַל־רֹאשָׁ֑ם שָׂשׂ֤וֹן וְשִׂמְחָה֙ יַשִּׂיג֔וּן נָ֖סוּ יָג֥וֹן וַאֲנָחָֽה׃ ס
I, I am he[^12] who comforts you. Who are you that you are afraid of mortals who die, of human beings who are made like grass?
אָנֹכִ֧י אָנֹכִ֛י ה֖וּא מְנַחֶמְכֶ֑ם מִֽי־אַ֤תְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ מֵאֱנ֣וֹשׁ יָמ֔וּת וּמִבֶּן־אָדָ֖ם חָצִ֥יר יִנָּתֵֽן׃

You have forgotten Yahweh your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth. You live in constant fear all day long because of the fury of the oppressor, as he prepares to destroy. But where is the fury of the oppressor?
וַתִּשְׁכַּ֞ח יְהוָ֣ה עֹשֶׂ֗ךָ נוֹטֶ֣ה שָׁמַיִם֮ וְיֹסֵ֣ד אָרֶץ֒ וַתְּפַחֵ֨ד תָּמִ֜יד כָּל־הַיּ֗וֹם מִפְּנֵי֙ חֲמַ֣ת הַמֵּצִ֔יק כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר כּוֹנֵ֖ן לְהַשְׁחִ֑ית וְאַיֵּ֖ה חֲמַ֥ת הַמֵּצִֽיק׃
The one bowed down in chains[^13] will soon be set free. He will not die and go down to the Pit,[^14] and he will not lack bread.
מִהַ֥ר צֹעֶ֖ה לְהִפָּתֵ֑חַ וְלֹא־יָמ֣וּת לַשַּׁ֔חַת וְלֹ֥א יֶחְסַ֖ר לַחְמֽוֹ׃
For I am Yahweh your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar.[^15] Yahweh of Armies[^16] is his name.
וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ רֹגַ֣ע הַיָּ֔ם וַיֶּהֱמ֖וּ גַּלָּ֑יו יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃
I have put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hand, to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Zion, "You are my people."
וָאָשִׂ֤ים דְּבָרַי֙ בְּפִ֔יךָ וּבְצֵ֥ל יָדִ֖י כִּסִּיתִ֑יךָ לִנְטֹ֤עַ שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְלִיסֹ֣ד אָ֔רֶץ וְלֵאמֹ֥ר לְצִיּ֖וֹן עַמִּי־אָֽתָּה׃ ס
Wake up, wake up! Stand up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of Yahweh the cup of his fury, you who have drained to the dregs the bowl, the cup that makes people stagger.[^17]
הִתְעוֹרְרִ֣י הִֽתְעוֹרְרִ֗י ק֚וּמִי יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁתִ֛ית מִיַּ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־כּ֣וֹס חֲמָת֑וֹ אֶת־קֻבַּ֜עַת כּ֧וֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָ֛ה שָׁתִ֖ית מָצִֽית׃
There is no one to guide her among all the children she bore; there is no one to take her by the hand among all the children she brought up.
אֵין־מְנַהֵ֣ל לָ֔הּ מִכָּל־בָּנִ֖ים יָלָ֑דָה וְאֵ֤ין מַחֲזִיק֙ בְּיָדָ֔הּ מִכָּל־בָּנִ֖ים גִּדֵּֽלָה׃
These two things have happened to you (who will grieve with you?): ruin and destruction, famine and sword. How can I comfort you?[^18]
שְׁתַּ֤יִם הֵ֙נָּה֙ קֹֽרְאֹתַ֔יִךְ מִ֖י יָנ֣וּד לָ֑ךְ הַשֹּׁ֧ד וְהַשֶּׁ֛בֶר וְהָרָעָ֥ב וְהַחֶ֖רֶב מִ֥י אֲנַחֲמֵֽךְ׃
Your children have fainted; they lie at the head of every street like an antelope caught in a net. They are full of the fury of Yahweh, the rebuke of your God.
בָּנַ֜יִךְ עֻלְּפ֥וּ שָׁכְב֛וּ בְּרֹ֥אשׁ כָּל־חוּצ֖וֹת כְּת֣וֹא מִכְמָ֑ר הַֽמְלֵאִ֥ים חֲמַת־יְהוָ֖ה גַּעֲרַ֥ת אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃
Therefore hear this, you afflicted one, drunk, but not with wine.
לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְעִי־נָ֥א זֹ֖את עֲנִיָּ֑ה וּשְׁכֻרַ֖ת וְלֹ֥א מִיָּֽיִן׃ ס

This is what your Lord, Yahweh, says, your God, who defends his people: Look, I have taken from your hand the cup that makes people stagger, the bowl, the cup of my fury. You will never drink it again.
כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנַ֣יִךְ יְהוָ֗ה וֵאלֹהַ֙יִךְ֙ יָרִ֣יב עַמּ֔וֹ הִנֵּ֥ה לָקַ֛חְתִּי מִיָּדֵ֖ךְ אֶת־כּ֣וֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָ֑ה אֶת־קֻבַּ֙עַת֙ כּ֣וֹס חֲמָתִ֔י לֹא־תוֹסִ֥יפִי לִשְׁתּוֹתָ֖הּ עֽוֹד׃
I will put it into the hands of your tormentors, who said to you,[^19] "Bow down, so that we may walk over you." And you made your back like the ground, like a street for them to walk over.
וְשַׂמְתִּ֙יהָ֙ בְּיַד־מוֹגַ֔יִךְ אֲשֶׁר־אָמְר֥וּ לְנַפְשֵׁ֖ךְ שְׁחִ֣י וְנַעֲבֹ֑רָה וַתָּשִׂ֤ימִי כָאָ֙רֶץ֙ גֵּוֵ֔ךְ וְכַח֖וּץ לַעֹבְרִֽים׃ ס

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "to the hollow of the pit from which you were dug". The rock and the quarry are Abraham and Sarah (verse 2).
n.3: Literally "Abraham your father".
n.4: Hebrew *torah*, "instruction, teaching, law". Also in verse 7.
n.5: Hebrew *argia*, perhaps "I will establish" or "in a moment", joined to the next verse.
n.6: Hebrew *iyyim*, the islands and coasts of the Mediterranean (11:11), and in these chapters the most distant lands.
n.7: Hebrew *kemo-khen*, perhaps "like gnats" (*ken*) or "in the same way".
n.8: Hebrew *Rahav*, a sea monster, a figure of the chaos that God overcame (Job 9:13; 26:12; Psalm 89:11, 89:10 in most English Bibles), and a poetic name for Egypt (30:7; Psalm 87:4). It is not the Rahab of Joshua 2, whose name is spelled differently in Hebrew.
n.9: Hebrew *tannin*, "sea monster, dragon" (27:1). The defeat of the monsters of the sea is joined in verse 10 with the crossing of the Red Sea.
n.10: Hebrew *ge'ulim*, those whom Yahweh has rescued as next of kin (41:14).
n.11: Verse 11 repeats 35:10.
n.12: Hebrew *ani hu* (41:4). *You* is plural, then feminine singular ("Who are you"), then masculine singular in verse 13.
n.13: Hebrew *tso'eh*, "one who stoops", perhaps a prisoner bent under his chains.
n.14: Hebrew *shachat*, "pit, grave", the world of the dead.
n.15: Or "who stills the sea when its waves roar". The same line is found in Jeremiah 31:35.
n.16: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.17: Literally "the bowl of the cup of reeling you have drunk, you have drained". The cup stands for the judgment God gives his people to drink (Jeremiah 25:15–17; Psalm 75:9, 75:8 in most English Bibles).
n.18: Literally "Who, I will comfort you?" The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) and the Septuagint read "Who will comfort you?"
n.19: Literally "to your *nephesh*".

v: Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion! Put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city! For the uncircumcised and the unclean will never enter you again.
עוּרִ֥י עוּרִ֛י לִבְשִׁ֥י עֻזֵּ֖ךְ צִיּ֑וֹן לִבְשִׁ֣י ׀ בִּגְדֵ֣י תִפְאַרְתֵּ֗ךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ עִ֣יר הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ כִּ֣י לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֛יף יָבֹא־בָ֥ךְ ע֖וֹד עָרֵ֥ל וְטָמֵֽא׃
Shake yourself free from the dust; rise up and take your seat, Jerusalem![^1] Loose the bonds from your neck,[^2] captive Daughter Zion!
הִתְנַעֲרִ֧י מֵעָפָ֛ר ק֥וּמִי שְּׁבִ֖י יְרֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם *התפתחו **הִֽתְפַּתְּחִי֙ מוֹסרֵ֣י צַוָּארֵ֔ךְ שְׁבִיָּ֖ה בַּת־צִיּֽוֹן׃ ס
For this is what Yahweh[^3] says: You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without silver.
כִּֽי־כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה חִנָּ֖ם נִמְכַּרְתֶּ֑ם וְלֹ֥א בְכֶ֖סֶף תִּגָּאֵֽלוּ׃
For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: At first my people went down to Egypt to live there as foreigners; then Assyria oppressed them for nothing.
כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה מִצְרַ֛יִם יָֽרַד־עַמִּ֥י בָרִֽאשֹׁנָ֖ה לָג֣וּר שָׁ֑ם וְאַשּׁ֖וּר בְּאֶ֥פֶס עֲשָׁקֽוֹ׃
And now what do I have here?[^4] declares Yahweh. For my people have been taken away for nothing. Their rulers wail,[^5] declares Yahweh, and all day long my name is continually despised.[^6]
וְעַתָּ֤ה *מי־*לי־**מַה־**לִּי־פֹה֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־לֻקַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖י חִנָּ֑ם *משלו **מֹשְׁלָ֤יו יְהֵילִ֙ילוּ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְתָמִ֥יד כָּל־הַיּ֖וֹם שְׁמִ֥י מִנֹּאָּֽץ׃
Therefore my people will know my name; therefore on that day they will know that I am he[^7] who speaks: Here I am.
לָכֵ֛ן יֵדַ֥ע עַמִּ֖י שְׁמִ֑י לָכֵן֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כִּֽי־אֲנִי־ה֥וּא הַֽמְדַבֵּ֖ר הִנֵּֽנִי׃

How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the one who brings good news,[^8] who proclaims peace, who brings good news of good things, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"[^9]
מַה־נָּאו֨וּ עַל־הֶהָרִ֜ים רַגְלֵ֣י מְבַשֵּׂ֗ר מַשְׁמִ֧יעַ שָׁל֛וֹם מְבַשֵּׂ֥ר ט֖וֹב מַשְׁמִ֣יעַ יְשׁוּעָ֑ה אֹמֵ֥ר לְצִיּ֖וֹן מָלַ֥ךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃
Listen! Your watchmen raise their voices; together they shout for joy. For with their own eyes[^10] they will see Yahweh return to Zion.
ק֥וֹל צֹפַ֛יִךְ נָ֥שְׂאוּ ק֖וֹל יַחְדָּ֣ו יְרַנֵּ֑נוּ כִּ֣י עַ֤יִן בְּעַ֙יִן֙ יִרְא֔וּ בְּשׁ֥וּב יְהוָ֖ה צִיּֽוֹן׃
Break into singing together, you ruins of Jerusalem! For Yahweh has comforted his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem.
פִּצְח֤וּ רַנְּנוּ֙ יַחְדָּ֔ו חָרְב֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם כִּֽי־נִחַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ עַמּ֔וֹ גָּאַ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Yahweh has bared his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
חָשַׂ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶת־זְר֣וֹעַ קָדְשׁ֔וֹ לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְרָאוּ֙ כָּל־אַפְסֵי־אָ֔רֶץ אֵ֖ת יְשׁוּעַ֥ת אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ ס
Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch nothing unclean. Go out from the middle of her; purify yourselves, you who carry the vessels of Yahweh.[^11]
ס֤וּרוּ ס֙וּרוּ֙ צְא֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם טָמֵ֖א אַל־תִּגָּ֑עוּ צְא֣וּ מִתּוֹכָ֔הּ הִבָּ֕רוּ נֹשְׂאֵ֖י כְּלֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
But you will not go out in haste or leave in flight.[^12] For Yahweh will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear guard.
כִּ֣י לֹ֤א בְחִפָּזוֹן֙ תֵּצֵ֔אוּ וּבִמְנוּסָ֖ה לֹ֣א תֵלֵכ֑וּן כִּֽי־הֹלֵ֤ךְ לִפְנֵיכֶם֙ יְהוָ֔ה וּמְאַסִּפְכֶ֖ם אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס
Look, my servant will act wisely;[^13] he will be raised and lifted up and greatly exalted.[^14]
הִנֵּ֥ה יַשְׂכִּ֖יל עַבְדִּ֑י יָר֧וּם וְנִשָּׂ֛א וְגָבַ֖הּ מְאֹֽד׃
Just as many were appalled at you,[^15] so disfigured was his appearance, beyond that of any man, and his form beyond that of human beings,[^16]
כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁמְמ֤וּ עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ רַבִּ֔ים כֵּן־מִשְׁחַ֥ת מֵאִ֖ישׁ מַרְאֵ֑הוּ וְתֹאֲר֖וֹ מִבְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃
so he will sprinkle many nations.[^17] Kings will shut their mouths because of him. For what they were not told, they will see, and what they have not heard, they will understand.[^18]
כֵּ֤ן יַזֶּה֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים עָלָ֛יו יִקְפְּצ֥וּ מְלָכִ֖ים פִּיהֶ֑ם כִּ֠י אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־סֻפַּ֤ר לָהֶם֙ רָא֔וּ וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־שָׁמְע֖וּ הִתְבּוֹנָֽנוּ׃

n.1: Hebrew *shevi*, "sit", that is, sit enthroned. The same Hebrew word can mean "captivity", and many translate "rise up, captive Jerusalem", matching "captive Daughter Zion" at the end of the verse.
n.2: The Hebrew text is written "the bonds of your neck have come loose" but read "Loose the bonds from your neck".
n.3: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.4: The Hebrew text is written "Who do I have here?" but read "What do I have here?"
n.5: Or "Their rulers boast" or "mock". Hebrew *yehelilu*.
n.6: Romans 2:24 quotes this line from the Septuagint: "Because of you my name is despised among the nations."
n.7: Hebrew *ani hu* (41:4).
n.8: Hebrew *mevasser*, from *basar*, "bring good news" (40:9). Also later in this verse. Romans 10:15 quotes the first part of this verse.
n.9: Or "Your God has become king!" Hebrew *malakh*, as in "Yahweh reigns!" (Psalm 93:1; 96:10; 97:1; 99:1).
n.10: Literally "eye to eye".
n.11: The vessels of the temple, which Nebuchadnezzar had carried off to Babylon (Ezra 1:7–11). 2 Corinthians 6:17 quotes this verse.
n.12: Unlike the exodus from Egypt, when Israel left in haste (Exodus 12:11; Deuteronomy 16:3).
n.13: Or "will prosper". Hebrew *yaskil* means both "act with insight" and "succeed". 52:13–53:12 is the fourth of the servant passages (see 42:1). The Aramaic Targum begins "Look, my servant the anointed one (Messiah) will prosper", but it applies the suffering in the passage to Israel and the nations rather than to the Messiah. In the New Testament the passage is applied to the suffering and death of Jesus, and many Jewish interpreters have understood the servant as Israel, the righteous within Israel, or the prophet.
n.14: Literally "he will be high and lifted up and very lofty". The words "high and lifted up" are used of Yahweh on his throne in 6:1 and 57:15.
n.15: The Syriac and the Aramaic Targum read "at him". The Hebrew moves between "you" and "him".
n.16: Hebrew *mishchat*, a word found only here, probably "disfigurement". The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a) has *mashachti*, which may be read "I anointed". The meaning of verses 14–15 is uncertain in places.
n.17: Hebrew *yazzeh*, "he will sprinkle", the verb used for the priest's sprinkling of blood or water to cleanse (Leviticus 4:6; 16:14; Numbers 19:18). The Septuagint reads "so many nations will marvel at him".
n.18: Romans 15:21 quotes the end of this verse from the Septuagint.

v: Who has believed what we have heard?[^1] And to whom has the arm of Yahweh[^2] been revealed?
מִ֥י הֶאֱמִ֖ין לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ וּזְר֥וֹעַ יְהוָ֖ה עַל־מִ֥י נִגְלָֽתָה׃
He grew up before him like a young plant, like a root out of dry ground. He had no form or majesty that we should look at him, no appearance that we should desire him.
וַיַּ֨עַל כַּיּוֹנֵ֜ק לְפָנָ֗יו וְכַשֹּׁ֙רֶשׁ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צִיָּ֔ה לֹא־תֹ֥אַר ל֖וֹ וְלֹ֣א הָדָ֑ר וְנִרְאֵ֥הוּ וְלֹֽא־מַרְאֶ֖ה וְנֶחְמְדֵֽהוּ׃
He was despised and rejected by others,[^3] a man of pains, who knew what sickness was.[^4] Like one from whom people hide their faces,[^5] he was despised, and we held him in no regard.
נִבְזֶה֙ וַחֲדַ֣ל אִישִׁ֔ים אִ֥ישׁ מַכְאֹב֖וֹת וִיד֣וּעַ חֹ֑לִי וּכְמַסְתֵּ֤ר פָּנִים֙ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ נִבְזֶ֖ה וְלֹ֥א חֲשַׁבְנֻֽהוּ׃
Surely he has carried our sicknesses and borne our pains.[^6] Yet we thought of him as stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
אָכֵ֤ן חֳלָיֵ֙נוּ֙ ה֣וּא נָשָׂ֔א וּמַכְאֹבֵ֖ינוּ סְבָלָ֑ם וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ חֲשַׁבְנֻ֔הוּ נָג֛וּעַ מֻכֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים וּמְעֻנֶּֽה׃
But he was pierced[^7] for our rebellious acts; he was crushed for our wrongdoings. The punishment that brought us peace[^8] was on him, and by his wounds[^9] we are healed.
וְהוּא֙ מְחֹלָ֣ל מִפְּשָׁעֵ֔נוּ מְדֻכָּ֖א מֵעֲוֺנֹתֵ֑ינוּ מוּסַ֤ר שְׁלוֹמֵ֙נוּ֙ עָלָ֔יו וּבַחֲבֻרָת֖וֹ נִרְפָּא־לָֽנוּ׃
We all, like sheep, have gone astray; we have each turned to his own way. And Yahweh has laid on him the guilt of us all.[^10]
כֻּלָּ֙נוּ֙ כַּצֹּ֣אן תָּעִ֔ינוּ אִ֥ישׁ לְדַרְכּ֖וֹ פָּנִ֑ינוּ וַֽיהוָה֙ הִפְגִּ֣יעַ בּ֔וֹ אֵ֖ת עֲוֺ֥ן כֻּלָּֽנוּ׃

He was oppressed, and he let himself be afflicted,[^11] yet he did not open his mouth. Like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that is silent before its shearers, he did not open his mouth.[^12]
נִגַּ֨שׂ וְה֣וּא נַעֲנֶה֮ וְלֹ֣א יִפְתַּח־פִּיו֒ כַּשֶּׂה֙ לַטֶּ֣בַח יוּבָ֔ל וּכְרָחֵ֕ל לִפְנֵ֥י גֹזְזֶ֖יהָ נֶאֱלָ֑מָה וְלֹ֥א יִפְתַּ֖ח פִּֽיו׃
By oppression and judgment he was taken away.[^13] And who of his generation considered[^14] that he was cut off from the land of the living, struck down for the rebellion of my people?[^15]
מֵעֹ֤צֶר וּמִמִּשְׁפָּט֙ לֻקָּ֔ח וְאֶת־דּוֹר֖וֹ מִ֣י יְשׂוֹחֵ֑חַ כִּ֤י נִגְזַר֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֔ים מִפֶּ֥שַׁע עַמִּ֖י נֶ֥גַע לָֽמוֹ׃
They made his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death,[^16] although he had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth.[^17]
וַיִּתֵּ֤ן אֶת־רְשָׁעִים֙ קִבְר֔וֹ וְאֶת־עָשִׁ֖יר בְּמֹתָ֑יו עַ֚ל לֹא־חָמָ֣ס עָשָׂ֔ה וְלֹ֥א מִרְמָ֖ה בְּפִֽיו׃
Yet it was Yahweh's will to crush him; he made him sick. When you make his life a guilt offering,[^18] he will see offspring and prolong his days, and the will of Yahweh will prosper in his hand.
וַיהוָ֞ה חָפֵ֤ץ דַּכְּאוֹ֙ הֶֽחֱלִ֔י אִם־תָּשִׂ֤ים אָשָׁם֙ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ יִרְאֶ֥ה זֶ֖רַע יַאֲרִ֣יךְ יָמִ֑ים וְחֵ֥פֶץ יְהוָ֖ה בְּיָד֥וֹ יִצְלָֽח׃
Out of the anguish of his soul he will see[^19] and be satisfied. By his knowledge[^20] my righteous servant will make many righteous,[^21] and he will bear their wrongdoings.
מֵעֲמַ֤ל נַפְשׁוֹ֙ יִרְאֶ֣ה יִשְׂבָּ֔ע בְּדַעְתּ֗וֹ יַצְדִּ֥יק צַדִּ֛יק עַבְדִּ֖י לָֽרַבִּ֑ים וַעֲוֺנֹתָ֖ם ה֥וּא יִסְבֹּֽל׃

Therefore I will give him a portion among the many,[^22] and he will divide the plunder with the strong, because he poured out his life to death and was counted among the rebels.[^23] Yet he bore the sin of many and made intercession for the rebels.[^24]

לָכֵ֞ן אֲחַלֶּק־ל֣וֹ בָרַבִּ֗ים וְאֶת־עֲצוּמִים֮ יְחַלֵּ֣ק שָׁלָל֒ תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶעֱרָ֤ה לַמָּ֙וֶת֙ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ וְאֶת־פֹּשְׁעִ֖ים נִמְנָ֑ה וְהוּא֙ חֵטְא־רַבִּ֣ים נָשָׂ֔א וְלַפֹּשְׁעִ֖ים יַפְגִּֽיעַ׃ ס

n.1: Or "our message", that is, the message we bring. Hebrew *shemu'ah*, "what is heard, report". John 12:38 and Romans 10:16 quote this verse from the Septuagint: "Lord, who has believed our message?" The speakers in verses 1–10 are not named: the nations and kings of 52:15, or Israel, or the prophet with those who share his view.
n.2: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.3: Literally "lacking men", that is, abandoned by people, or "the lowest of men".
n.4: Literally "a man of pains, knowing sickness". Traditionally "a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief". Hebrew *choli*, "sickness", as in verse 4.
n.5: Or "Like one who hides his face from us", as a leper covered his face (Leviticus 13:45).
n.6: Matthew 8:17 quotes this line, applying it to Jesus' healing of the sick: "He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases."
n.7: Or "wounded". Hebrew *mecholal*, from the verb "pierce".
n.8: Literally "The discipline of our peace". Hebrew *musar*, "discipline, correction, chastisement"; *shalom*, "peace, well-being, wholeness".
n.9: Hebrew *chabburah*, "wound, welt, bruise" (1:6). 1 Peter 2:24–25 echoes verses 5–6.
n.10: Literally "has caused to fall on him the guilt of us all". The same verb is translated "made intercession" in verse 12.
n.11: Or "he humbled himself". Hebrew *na'aneh*.
n.12: Acts 8:32–33 quotes verses 7–8 from the Septuagint: "Like a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he does not open his mouth. In his humiliation justice was denied him. Who can describe his generation? For his life is taken away from the earth." Philip begins from this passage to tell the Ethiopian official the good news about Jesus (Acts 8:35).
n.13: Or "Without restraint and without justice he was taken away", or "From prison and from judgment he was taken away". Hebrew *otser* means "restraint, oppression" or "custody".
n.14: Or "And who could speak of his descendants?" or "Who could think about his fate?" Hebrew *dor* means "generation", the people living at one time, or perhaps "fate, dwelling". The Hebrew of this line is difficult.
n.15: Literally "for the rebellion of my people, a blow to them" (or "to him"). The Septuagint reads "for the lawless acts of my people he was led to death".
n.16: Literally "in his deaths". *They made* is literally "he gave" or "one gave". The *rich* stand in parallel with the *wicked*, perhaps as oppressors. Compare the burial of Jesus in the tomb of Joseph of Arimathea, a rich man (Matthew 27:57–60).
n.17: 1 Peter 2:22 quotes this line.
n.18: Or "When his life makes a guilt offering". The Hebrew verb can mean "you make" or "it makes". Hebrew *asham*, the guilt offering (Leviticus 5:14–26, 5:14–6:7 in most English Bibles), also called the reparation offering, which made up for a wrong done. *Life* is Hebrew *nephesh*, also in verses 11–12.
n.19: The Great Isaiah Scroll from Qumran (1QIsa-a), two other Isaiah scrolls from Qumran and the Septuagint read "he will see light".
n.20: Or "By knowing him", that is, by the knowledge others gain of him.
n.21: Hebrew *yatsdiq*, "make righteous, declare righteous, bring justice to" (50:8). *Many* (Hebrew *rabbim*) is repeated from 52:14–15 and is found again twice in verse 12.
n.22: Or "among the great". Hebrew *rabbim*, "many" or "great". *The strong* (Hebrew *atsumim*) may also mean "the numerous".
n.23: Luke 22:37 quotes this line, which Jesus applies to himself. *Poured out* is literally "laid bare".
n.24: Or "and intervened for the rebels". Hebrew *yafgia*, the verb translated "laid on him" in verse 6.

v: Sing, barren woman, you who have not given birth! Break into song and shout, you who have not been in labor! For the children of the desolate woman will be more than the children of the married woman, says Yahweh.[^1]
רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה פִּצְחִ֨י רִנָּ֤ה וְצַהֲלִי֙ לֹא־חָ֔לָה כִּֽי־רַבִּ֧ים בְּֽנֵי־שׁוֹמֵמָ֛ה מִבְּנֵ֥י בְעוּלָ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
Enlarge the place of your tent; let the curtains of your dwellings be stretched out; do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your stakes.
הַרְחִ֣יבִי ׀ מְק֣וֹם אָהֳלֵ֗ךְ וִירִיע֧וֹת מִשְׁכְּנוֹתַ֛יִךְ יַטּ֖וּ אַל־תַּחְשֹׂ֑כִי הַאֲרִ֙יכִי֙ מֵֽיתָרַ֔יִךְ וִיתֵדֹתַ֖יִךְ חַזֵּֽקִי׃
For you will spread out to the right and to the left. Your offspring will possess the nations and will settle the desolate cities.
כִּי־יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹ֖אול תִּפְרֹ֑צִי וְזַרְעֵךְ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם יִירָ֔שׁ וְעָרִ֥ים נְשַׁמּ֖וֹת יוֹשִֽׁיבוּ׃

Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; do not be disgraced, for you will not be humiliated. You will forget the shame of your youth, and you will no longer remember the disgrace of your widowhood.
אַל־תִּֽירְאִי֙ כִּי־לֹ֣א תֵב֔וֹשִׁי וְאַל־תִּכָּלְמִ֖י כִּ֣י לֹ֣א תַחְפִּ֑ירִי כִּ֣י בֹ֤שֶׁת עֲלוּמַ֙יִךְ֙ תִּשְׁכָּ֔חִי וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת אַלְמְנוּתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֥א תִזְכְּרִי־עֽוֹד׃
For your husband[^2] is your Maker; Yahweh of Armies[^3] is his name. Your Redeemer[^4] is the Holy One of Israel; he is called the God of all the earth.
כִּ֤י בֹעֲלַ֙יִךְ֙ עֹשַׂ֔יִךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ וְגֹֽאֲלֵךְ֙ קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֱלֹהֵ֥י כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ יִקָּרֵֽא׃
For Yahweh has called you back like a wife abandoned and grieved in spirit, like a wife married in her youth who has been rejected, says your God.
כִּֽי־כְאִשָּׁ֧ה עֲזוּבָ֛ה וַעֲצ֥וּבַת ר֖וּחַ קְרָאָ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֧שֶׁת נְעוּרִ֛ים כִּ֥י תִמָּאֵ֖ס אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ׃
For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you.
בְּרֶ֥גַע קָטֹ֖ן עֲזַבְתִּ֑יךְ וּבְרַחֲמִ֥ים גְּדֹלִ֖ים אֲקַבְּצֵֽךְ׃
In a flood of anger[^5] I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting faithful love[^6] I will have compassion on you, says Yahweh, your Redeemer.
בְּשֶׁ֣צֶף קֶ֗צֶף הִסְתַּ֨רְתִּי פָנַ֥י רֶ֙גַע֙ מִמֵּ֔ךְ וּבְחֶ֥סֶד עוֹלָ֖ם רִֽחַמְתִּ֑יךְ אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ ס
For this is like the waters of Noah to me:[^7] as I swore that the waters of Noah would never again pass over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.
כִּי־מֵ֥י נֹ֙חַ֙ זֹ֣את לִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבַּ֗עְתִּי מֵעֲבֹ֥ר מֵי־נֹ֛חַ ע֖וֹד עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כֵּ֥ן נִשְׁבַּ֛עְתִּי מִקְּצֹ֥ף עָלַ֖יִךְ וּמִגְּעָר־בָּֽךְ׃
For the mountains may depart and the hills be shaken, but my faithful love will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be shaken, says Yahweh, who has compassion on you.
כִּ֤י הֶֽהָרִים֙ יָמ֔וּשׁוּ וְהַגְּבָע֖וֹת תְּמוּטֶ֑נָה וְחַסְדִּ֞י מֵאִתֵּ֣ךְ לֹֽא־יָמ֗וּשׁ וּבְרִ֤ית שְׁלוֹמִי֙ לֹ֣א תָמ֔וּט אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃ ס
Afflicted one, storm-tossed and not comforted, look, I will set your stones in black mortar[^8] and lay your foundations with sapphires.[^9]
עֲנִיָּ֥ה סֹעֲרָ֖ה לֹ֣א נֻחָ֑מָה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַרְבִּ֤יץ בַּפּוּךְ֙ אֲבָנַ֔יִךְ וִיסַדְתִּ֖יךְ בַּסַּפִּירִֽים׃
I will make your battlements of rubies, your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.[^10]
וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י כַּֽדְכֹד֙ שִׁמְשֹׁתַ֔יִךְ וּשְׁעָרַ֖יִךְ לְאַבְנֵ֣י אֶקְדָּ֑ח וְכָל־גְּבוּלֵ֖ךְ לְאַבְנֵי־חֵֽפֶץ׃
All your children will be taught by Yahweh,[^11] and great will be the peace of your children.
וְכָל־בָּנַ֖יִךְ לִמּוּדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְרַ֖ב שְׁל֥וֹם בָּנָֽיִךְ׃
You will be established in righteousness. You will be far from oppression, for you will have nothing to fear, and from terror, for it will not come near you.
בִּצְדָקָ֖ה תִּכּוֹנָ֑נִי רַחֲקִ֤י מֵעֹ֙שֶׁק֙ כִּֽי־לֹ֣א תִירָ֔אִי וּמִ֨מְּחִתָּ֔ה כִּ֥י לֹֽא־תִקְרַ֖ב אֵלָֽיִךְ׃
If anyone stirs up trouble,[^12] it will not be from me; whoever stirs up trouble against you will fall because of you.
הֵ֣ן גּ֥וֹר יָג֛וּר אֶ֖פֶס מֵֽאוֹתִ֑י מִי־גָ֥ר אִתָּ֖ךְ עָלַ֥יִךְ יִפּֽוֹל׃
Look, I have created the smith who blows on the coals and produces a weapon fit for its work. I have also created the destroyer to wreak havoc.
*הן **הִנֵּ֤ה אָֽנֹכִי֙ בָּרָ֣אתִי חָרָ֔שׁ נֹפֵ֙חַ֙ בְּאֵ֣שׁ פֶּחָ֔ם וּמוֹצִ֥יא כְלִ֖י לְמַעֲשֵׂ֑הוּ וְאָנֹכִ֛י בָּרָ֥אתִי מַשְׁחִ֖ית לְחַבֵּֽל׃

No weapon forged against you will succeed, and you will refute every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the heritage of the servants of Yahweh,[^13] and their vindication[^14] comes from me, declares Yahweh.
כָּל־כְּלִ֞י יוּצַ֤ר עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ לֹ֣א יִצְלָ֔ח וְכָל־לָשׁ֛וֹן תָּֽקוּם־אִתָּ֥ךְ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט תַּרְשִׁ֑יעִי זֹ֡את נַחֲלַת֩ עַבְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה וְצִדְקָתָ֛ם מֵאִתִּ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles. *You* is feminine singular in this chapter: Zion is addressed as a wife and mother. Galatians 4:27 quotes this verse.
n.2: Hebrew *bo'alayikh*, "your husband, your master", from *ba'al*, "lord, owner, husband".
n.3: *Yahweh of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.4: Hebrew *go'el* (41:14). Also in verse 8.
n.5: Hebrew *shetsef qetsef*, a sound play found only here. *Shetsef* probably means "flood" or "surge".
n.6: Hebrew *chesed*: loyal, faithful love. Also in verse 10.
n.7: Literally "For the waters of Noah this is to me". Yahweh's oath after the flood is in Genesis 8:21–22 and 9:11.
n.8: Hebrew *pukh*, the black paint women used around their eyes (2 Kings 9:30), here perhaps a dark mortar that sets off the stones.
n.9: Probably lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone (Exodus 24:10). The precious stones of verses 11–12 cannot all be identified with certainty. Revelation 21:18–21 echoes these verses.
n.10: *Battlements* is literally "suns", perhaps shields or pinnacles that shine in the sun; *rubies* is Hebrew *kadkod*; *sparkling jewels* is *avne eqdach*, "stones of fire", perhaps garnets or beryl; *walls* is literally "border".
n.11: Literally "will be disciples of Yahweh" (50:4). John 6:45 quotes this line.
n.12: Hebrew *gur*, "stir up strife". The same word can mean "live as a foreigner".
n.13: From here to the end of the book, Yahweh's servants are plural: those in Israel who are faithful to him (56:6; 63:17; 65:8–15; 66:14).
n.14: Hebrew *tsedaqah*, "righteousness", here the right that Yahweh upholds for them.

v: Come,[^1] all you who are thirsty, come to the waters! And you who have no money, come, buy grain and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost.
ה֤וֹי כָּל־צָמֵא֙ לְכ֣וּ לַמַּ֔יִם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵֽין־ל֖וֹ כָּ֑סֶף לְכ֤וּ שִׁבְרוּ֙ וֶֽאֱכֹ֔לוּ וּלְכ֣וּ שִׁבְר֗וּ בְּלוֹא־כֶ֛סֶף וּבְל֥וֹא מְחִ֖יר יַ֥יִן וְחָלָֽב׃
Why do you spend money on what is not bread, and your earnings on what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and eat what is good, and you will delight in rich food.[^2]
לָ֤מָּה תִשְׁקְלוּ־כֶ֙סֶף֙ בְּֽלוֹא־לֶ֔חֶם וִיגִיעֲכֶ֖ם בְּל֣וֹא לְשָׂבְעָ֑ה שִׁמְע֨וּ שָׁמ֤וֹעַ אֵלַי֙ וְאִכְלוּ־ט֔וֹב וְתִתְעַנַּ֥ג בַּדֶּ֖שֶׁן נַפְשְׁכֶֽם׃
Turn your ear and come to me; listen, so that you may live. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, my faithful love promised to David.[^3]
הַטּ֤וּ אָזְנְכֶם֙ וּלְכ֣וּ אֵלַ֔י שִׁמְע֖וּ וּתְחִ֣י נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וְאֶכְרְתָ֤ה לָכֶם֙ בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֔ם חַֽסְדֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד הַנֶּאֱמָנִֽים׃
Look, I made him a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander for the peoples.
הֵ֛ן עֵ֥ד לְאוּמִּ֖ים נְתַתִּ֑יו נָגִ֥יד וּמְצַוֵּ֖ה לְאֻמִּֽים׃
Look, you will call a nation you do not know, and a nation that does not know you will run to you, because of Yahweh[^4] your God, the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
הֵ֣ן גּ֤וֹי לֹֽא־תֵדַע֙ תִּקְרָ֔א וְג֥וֹי לֹֽא־יְדָע֖וּךָ אֵלֶ֣יךָ יָר֑וּצוּ לְמַ֙עַן֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֥י פֵאֲרָֽךְ׃ ס
Seek Yahweh while he may be found; call on him while he is near.
דִּרְשׁ֥וּ יְהוָ֖ה בְּהִמָּצְא֑וֹ קְרָאֻ֖הוּ בִּֽהְיוֹת֥וֹ קָרֽוֹב׃
Let the wicked abandon his way, and the evildoer his thoughts. Let him turn back to Yahweh, and he will have compassion on him, to our God, for he will freely forgive.
יַעֲזֹ֤ב רָשָׁע֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אָ֖וֶן מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֑יו וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וִֽירַחֲמֵ֔הוּ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כִּֽי־יַרְבֶּ֥ה לִסְלֽוֹחַ׃
For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways, declares Yahweh.
כִּ֣י לֹ֤א מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי֙ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם דְּרָכָ֑י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃
For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
כִּֽי־גָבְה֥וּ שָׁמַ֖יִם מֵאָ֑רֶץ כֵּ֣ן גָּבְה֤וּ דְרָכַי֙ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֔ם וּמַחְשְׁבֹתַ֖י מִמַּחְשְׁבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
For as the rain and the snow come down from the heavens and do not return there without watering the earth and making it bear and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
כִּ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵרֵד֩ הַגֶּ֨שֶׁם וְהַשֶּׁ֜לֶג מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם וְשָׁ֙מָּה֙ לֹ֣א יָשׁ֔וּב כִּ֚י אִם־הִרְוָ֣ה אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהוֹלִידָ֖הּ וְהִצְמִיחָ֑הּ וְנָ֤תַן זֶ֙רַע֙ לַזֹּרֵ֔עַ וְלֶ֖חֶם לָאֹכֵֽל׃
so will my word be that goes out from my mouth: it will not return to me empty, without accomplishing what I desire and succeeding in the purpose for which I sent it.
כֵּ֣ן יִֽהְיֶ֤ה דְבָרִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵצֵ֣א מִפִּ֔י לֹֽא־יָשׁ֥וּב אֵלַ֖י רֵיקָ֑ם כִּ֤י אִם־עָשָׂה֙ אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפַ֔צְתִּי וְהִצְלִ֖יחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁלַחְתִּֽיו׃
For you will go out with joy and be led out in peace. The mountains and the hills will break into singing before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
כִּֽי־בְשִׂמְחָ֣ה תֵצֵ֔אוּ וּבְשָׁל֖וֹם תּֽוּבָל֑וּן הֶהָרִ֣ים וְהַגְּבָע֗וֹת יִפְצְח֤וּ לִפְנֵיכֶם֙ רִנָּ֔ה וְכָל־עֲצֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה יִמְחֲאוּ־כָֽף׃
Instead of the thornbush the juniper will grow, and instead of the brier the myrtle will grow. This will make a name for Yahweh, an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.
תַּ֤חַת הַֽנַּעֲצוּץ֙ יַעֲלֶ֣ה בְר֔וֹשׁ *תחת **וְתַ֥חַת הַסִּרְפַּ֖ד יַעֲלֶ֣ה הֲדַ֑ס וְהָיָ֤ה לַֽיהוָה֙ לְשֵׁ֔ם לְא֥וֹת עוֹלָ֖ם לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *hoy*, usually "Woe to" (1:4). Here it is a call for attention, like the cry of a seller in the market.
n.2: Literally "and your *nephesh* will delight in fatness". Also in verse 3, "so that your *nephesh* may live".
n.3: Literally "the sure faithful acts (*chesed*) of David", the lasting love Yahweh promised to David and his house (2 Samuel 7:15–16; Psalm 89:2–5, 29, 89:1–4, 28 in most English Bibles). Acts 13:34 quotes these words from the Septuagint: "I will give you the holy and sure things of David."
n.4: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.

v: This is what Yahweh[^1] says: Keep justice and do what is right,[^2] for my salvation is about to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שִׁמְר֥וּ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וַעֲשׂ֣וּ צְדָקָ֑ה כִּֽי־קְרוֹבָ֤ה יְשֽׁוּעָתִי֙ לָב֔וֹא וְצִדְקָתִ֖י לְהִגָּלֽוֹת׃
Blessed is the person who does this, the human being who holds fast to it, who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.
אַשְׁרֵ֤י אֱנוֹשׁ֙ יַעֲשֶׂה־זֹּ֔את וּבֶן־אָדָ֖ם יַחֲזִ֣יק בָּ֑הּ שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ וְשֹׁמֵ֥ר יָד֖וֹ מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת כָּל־רָֽע׃ ס
Let no foreigner who has joined himself to Yahweh say, "Yahweh will surely separate me from his people." And let no eunuch say, "Look, I am only a dry tree."[^3]
וְאַל־יֹאמַ֣ר בֶּן־הַנֵּכָ֗ר הַנִּלְוָ֤ה אֶל־יְהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַבְדֵּ֧ל יַבְדִּילַ֛נִי יְהוָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל עַמּ֑וֹ וְאַל־יֹאמַר֙ הַסָּרִ֔יס הֵ֥ן אֲנִ֖י עֵ֥ץ יָבֵֽשׁ׃ ס
For this is what Yahweh says: To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, who choose what pleases me and hold fast to my covenant,
כִּי־כֹ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לַסָּֽרִיסִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִשְׁמְרוּ֙ אֶת־שַׁבְּתוֹתַ֔י וּבָֽחֲר֖וּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑צְתִּי וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי׃
I will give within my house and within my walls a memorial and a name[^4] better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not be cut off.
וְנָתַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֜ם בְּבֵיתִ֤י וּבְחֽוֹמֹתַי֙ יָ֣ד וָשֵׁ֔ם ט֖וֹב מִבָּנִ֣ים וּמִבָּנ֑וֹת שֵׁ֤ם עוֹלָם֙ אֶתֶּן־ל֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵֽת׃ ס
And the foreigners who join themselves to Yahweh to serve him, to love the name of Yahweh, and to be his servants, all who keep the Sabbath without profaning it and hold fast to my covenant,
וּבְנֵ֣י הַנֵּכָ֗ר הַנִּלְוִ֤ים עַל־יְהוָה֙ לְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ וּֽלְאַהֲבָה֙ אֶת־שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה לִהְי֥וֹת ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִ֑ים כָּל־שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי׃

I will bring to my holy mountain and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.[^5]
וַהֲבִיאוֹתִ֞ים אֶל־הַ֣ר קָדְשִׁ֗י וְשִׂמַּחְתִּים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית תְּפִלָּתִ֔י עוֹלֹתֵיהֶ֧ם וְזִבְחֵיהֶ֛ם לְרָצ֖וֹן עַֽל־מִזְבְּחִ֑י כִּ֣י בֵיתִ֔י בֵּית־תְּפִלָּ֥ה יִקָּרֵ֖א לְכָל־הָעַמִּֽים׃
The Lord Yahweh declares, he who gathers the outcasts of Israel: I will gather still others to them besides those already gathered.
נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה מְקַבֵּ֖ץ נִדְחֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ע֛וֹד אֲקַבֵּ֥ץ עָלָ֖יו לְנִקְבָּצָֽיו׃
All you wild animals of the field, come and devour, all you wild animals in the forest!
כֹּ֖ל חַיְת֣וֹ שָׂדָ֑י אֵתָ֕יוּ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל כָּל־חַיְת֖וֹ בַּיָּֽעַר׃ ס
Its watchmen[^6] are blind; none of them knows anything. They are all mute dogs that cannot bark. They lie around dreaming;[^7] they love to sleep.
*צפו **צֹפָ֞יו עִוְרִ֤ים כֻּלָּם֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ כֻּלָּם֙ כְּלָבִ֣ים אִלְּמִ֔ים לֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ לִנְבֹּ֑חַ הֹזִים֙ שֹֽׁכְבִ֔ים אֹהֲבֵ֖י לָנֽוּם׃

The dogs have a mighty appetite;[^8] they never know when they have had enough. And they are shepherds who have no understanding. They have all turned to their own way, each to his own gain, every one of them.
וְהַכְּלָבִ֣ים עַזֵּי־נֶ֗פֶשׁ לֹ֤א יָֽדְעוּ֙ שָׂבְעָ֔ה וְהֵ֣מָּה רֹעִ֔ים לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ הָבִ֑ין כֻּלָּם֙ לְדַרְכָּ֣ם פָּנ֔וּ אִ֥ישׁ לְבִצְע֖וֹ מִקָּצֵֽהוּ׃
"Come," they say, "let me get wine, and let us fill ourselves with beer! Tomorrow will be like today, only far better!"
אֵתָ֥יוּ אֶקְחָה־יַ֖יִן וְנִסְבְּאָ֣ה שֵׁכָ֑ר וְהָיָ֤ה כָזֶה֙ י֣וֹם מָחָ֔ר גָּד֖וֹל יֶ֥תֶר מְאֹֽד׃

n.1: *Yahweh*: God's personal name (Hebrew YHWH), traditionally rendered "the LORD" in English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *tsedaqah*, the word translated "righteousness" later in the verse.
n.3: The law shut men who had been castrated, and some foreigners, out of the assembly of Yahweh (Deuteronomy 23:2–4, 23:1–3 in most English Bibles). A eunuch could have no children to carry on his name.
n.4: Hebrew *yad va-shem*, literally "a hand and a name": a monument that keeps a name alive (2 Samuel 18:18). *Them* in the next sentence is literally "him", each one of them.
n.5: Jesus quotes this line in Mark 11:17 when he drives the traders out of the temple courts.
n.6: The leaders of Israel. *Its* is literally "his", Israel's.
n.7: Hebrew *hozim*, a word found only here, perhaps "dreaming" or "panting".
n.8: Literally "are strong of *nephesh*".

v: The righteous one perishes, and no one takes it to heart. The faithful[^1] are taken away, and no one understands that the righteous one is taken away from the evil to come.[^2]
הַצַּדִּ֣יק אָבָ֔ד וְאֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ שָׂ֣ם עַל־לֵ֑ב וְאַנְשֵׁי־חֶ֤סֶד נֶֽאֱסָפִים֙ בְּאֵ֣ין מֵבִ֔ין כִּֽי־מִפְּנֵ֥י הָרָעָ֖ה נֶאֱסַ֥ף הַצַּדִּֽיק׃
He enters into peace; they rest on their beds,[^3] all who walk uprightly.
יָב֣וֹא שָׁל֔וֹם יָנ֖וּחוּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם הֹלֵ֖ךְ נְכֹחֽוֹ׃
But you, come here, you children of a sorceress, offspring of an adulterer and a prostitute!
וְאַתֶּ֥ם קִרְבוּ־הֵ֖נָּה בְּנֵ֣י עֹנְנָ֑ה זֶ֥רַע מְנָאֵ֖ף וַתִּזְנֶֽה׃
Whom are you mocking? At whom do you open your mouth wide and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of rebellion, offspring of deceit?
עַל־מִי֙ תִּתְעַנָּ֔גוּ עַל־מִ֛י תַּרְחִ֥יבוּ פֶ֖ה תַּאֲרִ֣יכוּ לָשׁ֑וֹן הֲלֽוֹא־אַתֶּ֥ם יִלְדֵי־פֶ֖שַׁע זֶ֥רַע שָֽׁקֶר׃
You inflame yourselves among the oaks,[^4] under every green tree; you slaughter children in the ravines, under the clefts of the rocks.[^5]
הַנֵּֽחָמִים֙ בָּֽאֵלִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת כָּל־עֵ֣ץ רַעֲנָ֑ן שֹׁחֲטֵ֤י הַיְלָדִים֙ בַּנְּחָלִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת סְעִפֵ֥י הַסְּלָעִֽים׃

Among the smooth stones of the ravine is your portion;[^6] they, they are your lot. To them you have poured out drink offerings and brought up grain offerings.[^7] Should I relent because of these things?
בְּחַלְּקֵי־נַ֣חַל חֶלְקֵ֔ךְ הֵ֥ם הֵ֖ם גּוֹרָלֵ֑ךְ גַּם־לָהֶ֞ם שָׁפַ֥כְתְּ נֶ֙סֶךְ֙ הֶעֱלִ֣ית מִנְחָ֔ה הַ֥עַל אֵ֖לֶּה אֶנָּחֵֽם׃
On a high and lofty mountain you have made your bed; there too you went up to offer sacrifice.
עַ֤ל הַר־גָּבֹ֙הַּ֙ וְנִשָּׂ֔א שַׂ֖מְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבֵ֑ךְ גַּם־שָׁ֥ם עָלִ֖ית לִזְבֹּ֥חַ זָֽבַח׃

Behind the door and the doorpost you have set up your sign.[^8] For, deserting me, you uncovered your bed, climbed up into it and opened it wide. You made a bargain for yourself with them; you loved their bed; you gazed on their nakedness.[^9]
וְאַחַ֤ר הַדֶּ֙לֶת֙ וְהַמְּזוּזָ֔ה שַׂ֖מְתְּ זִכְרוֹנֵ֑ךְ כִּ֣י מֵאִתִּ֞י גִּלִּ֣ית וַֽתַּעֲלִ֗י הִרְחַ֤בְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבֵךְ֙ וַתִּכְרָת־לָ֣ךְ מֵהֶ֔ם אָהַ֥בְתְּ מִשְׁכָּבָ֖ם יָ֥ד חָזִֽית׃
You went to the king[^10] with oil and gave him many perfumes. You sent your envoys far away; you sent them down even to Sheol.[^11]
וַתָּשֻׁ֤רִי לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן וַתַּרְבִּ֖י רִקֻּחָ֑יִךְ וַתְּשַׁלְּחִ֤י צִרַ֙יִךְ֙ עַד־מֵ֣רָחֹ֔ק וַתַּשְׁפִּ֖ילִי עַד־שְׁאֽוֹל׃
You were wearied by your many journeys, but you did not say, "It is hopeless." You found new strength,[^12] so you did not grow faint.
בְּרֹ֤ב דַּרְכֵּךְ֙ יָגַ֔עַתְּ לֹ֥א אָמַ֖רְתְּ נוֹאָ֑שׁ חַיַּ֤ת יָדֵךְ֙ מָצָ֔את עַל־כֵּ֖ן לֹ֥א חָלִֽית׃
Whom did you dread and fear, that you lied, and did not remember me or take it to heart? Is it not because I have kept silent, and for a long time, that you do not fear me?
וְאֶת־מִ֞י דָּאַ֤גְתְּ וַתִּֽירְאִי֙ כִּ֣י תְכַזֵּ֔בִי וְאוֹתִי֙ לֹ֣א זָכַ֔רְתְּ לֹא־שַׂ֖מְתְּ עַל־לִבֵּ֑ךְ הֲלֹ֨א אֲנִ֤י מַחְשֶׁה֙ וּמֵ֣עֹלָ֔ם וְאוֹתִ֖י לֹ֥א תִירָֽאִי׃
I will expose your righteousness and your deeds,[^13] and they will not help you.
אֲנִ֥י אַגִּ֖יד צִדְקָתֵ֑ךְ וְאֶֽת־מַעֲשַׂ֖יִךְ וְלֹ֥א יוֹעִילֽוּךְ׃

When you cry out, let your collection of idols[^14] save you! The wind will carry them all off; a breath will take them away. But whoever takes refuge in me will inherit the land and possess my holy mountain.
בְּזַֽעֲקֵךְ֙ יַצִּילֻ֣ךְ קִבּוּצַ֔יִךְ וְאֶת־כֻּלָּ֥ם יִשָּׂא־ר֖וּחַ יִקַּח־הָ֑בֶל וְהַחוֹסֶ֥ה בִי֙ יִנְחַל־אֶ֔רֶץ וְיִירַ֖שׁ הַר־קָדְשִֽׁי׃
And it will be said, "Build it up, build it up, prepare the road! Remove every obstacle from the way of my people."
וְאָמַ֥ר סֹֽלּוּ־סֹ֖לּוּ פַּנּוּ־דָ֑רֶךְ הָרִ֥ימוּ מִכְשׁ֖וֹל מִדֶּ֥רֶךְ עַמִּֽי׃ ס
